docs.title: RadHarmony
docs.text:
RadHarmony gives many public radiology datasets (chest X-ray, CT and MRI) and many foundation models one interface.

A harmonizer reads the source files of a dataset and makes one harmonized table. A dataset class gives samples with the same keys for every dataset. An evaluator (probe, zero-shot, fine-tune, segmentation or report generation) takes any dataset and the encoder of a backbone recipe. It gives the same result table for all of them. Report generation takes a report generator in place of an encoder. So you can test one encoder on many datasets, or many encoders on one dataset, with no code for each pair.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
This block runs a linear probe with RAD-DINO features on Montgomery County CXR (138 chest X-rays, a TB label), with 5 folds. Your first benchmark in 10 minutes runs it step by step.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import LinearProbeEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/", transform=transform, output_cls=True, cache_dir=None
)
ev = LinearProbeEvaluator(encoder, dataset=ds, n_folds=5, output_dir="outputs/first_benchmark")
results = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(results)  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
print(results.groupby("label")["auroc"].mean().round(3).to_dict())
# {'macro_average': 0.971, 'tuberculosis': 0.971}

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text:
This page records the design choices of RadHarmony and the reason for each choice. Use it to answer the question "is this a bug, or is it how we want it?".

  • Contributors: read it before you add a dataset, a backbone or an evaluator.
  • Review agents: compare the code with these decisions. If no decision covers a behavior and you cannot tell if it is a bug, write an open question (see the review briefs). Do not guess the intent.

Related pages: Concepts shows how the layers work. The file eval/RULES.md in the repo has the review rules (J-xx) and the lesson checks (L-xxx). The folder docs/proposals/ has the design drafts.

docs.title: How to read an entry
docs.text:
Each decision has an ID (D-xx) and these lines:

  • Status:
  • Decided means that a maintainer chose it. The entry names the person and date, or the file that records it.
  • Decided, planned means that a maintainer chose it, but the feature is not built yet. Do not report the missing feature as a bug.
  • Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm means that an agent chose its recommended option. This was in the fix stage that started on 2026-11-01, and for Q-9 to Q-20 and the draft rules of the 2026-11-02 review. Frank Li asked for it both times. Treat it as decided until Frank Li confirms or changes it.
  • From the code means that the code does it today, but no maintainer has confirmed it yet. Treat it as the intent until a maintainer confirms or changes it.
  • Open means that a maintainer has not decided yet. The entry gives the question, what the code does today, the options and the evidence (a command and its output, or a file and line). It has no "Known gaps" line. Do not report the behavior as a bug. When a maintainer decides, the status changes, and the ID stays the same.
  • Checked by: the review rule, lesson or test that checks it, or "none".
  • Known gaps: places where the code breaks the decision today, one line each, with the finding ID. A gap is a bug to fix, not a reason to change the decision. An ID (for example V-H1-23) always names the same finding, in every run. reports/eval/index.json gives its run folder. The index and the folder are local only (not in git). "No ID" means that a maintainer found the gap by reading the code, and no report has it yet. Some gaps have more details in eval/TODO.md, section 2. /fix removes a gap when it fixes it. A gap whose fix needs a base-code change names its strict xfail test, if one exists.
  • Open part: a detail of a decided entry that is not decided yet. It gives the question, an example and the options.
  • Notes: facts that help, but that are not gaps.
  • Related: other entries about the same topic.

An ID never changes. A new decision gets the next free D- number, and it goes in the section where it belongs. So the numbers in a section are not in order. Use the index to find an ID.

Words on this page:

  • Table: the harmonized_df that a harmonizer makes.
  • Harmonizer: a class that reads the source files and makes the table.
  • Dataset class: a class that reads the table and gives samples (ds[i]).
  • Official split: a train, validation or test set that the dataset authors provide.
  • Bootstrap sample: one draw, with replacement, from the test set.
  • Open question: a behavior that no decision covers. A review agent writes it in its report (Q- ID). A maintainer decides it, or it becomes an entry with the status "Open".
  • Open part: a detail of a decided entry that is not decided yet. For example, D-29 had one until 2026-10-30: which threshold zero-shot uses.

docs.title: D-01 One table is the contract
docs.text:
harmonize() returns the table as one pandas DataFrame. After harmonize(), no class reads the source CSV or JSON files again. The dataset classes, the app and the evaluators read only the table.

  • Required columns: patient_id, study_id, image_path.
  • Optional columns: series_id, view_position, mask_path, bbox, bbox_labels, report, age_years, sex, the label columns, the regression columns (REG_COLS) and the extra columns (EXTRA_OUTPUT_COLS).
  • Planned optional columns (D-31): study_date, study_time and visit_number. They are NaN when the source has no value.

Why: one format lets a dataset class, a probe or the app work with every dataset.

  • Status: From the code (_select_harmonized_columns in radharmony/harmonizer/base.py).
  • Checked by: J-02.
  • Source IDs: study_id keeps the study ID of the source, also when the source gives one ID to 2 patients. The harmonizer then warns. Code that groups by study uses (patient_id, study_id), as D-31 does. Example: BRAX keeps the AccessionNumber, and 2 of its 23,276 values belong to 2 patients each. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, V-H1-9). The other option was the BRAX Study_<UID> folder name (23,278 values, 1 patient each). PadChest also warns since 2026-11-03: 1 StudyID belongs to 2 patients (V-H2-32). Both use warn_shared_study_ids in radharmony/harmonizer/_ids.py. Checked by: tests/test_padchest.py.
  • MedPMC answer: the release index has no caption, so the caption comes from our tag table (scripts/build_medpmc_tags.py). With no tag table, answer is None in every row, and the harmonizer warns. The images still work. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, V-H1-27). The other options were an error, and an error with a new argument to turn it off. Checked by tests/test_harmonizer_data.py::test_medpmc_without_tag_table_warns_that_answer_is_empty.
  • MedPMC include_multipanel=False: a specialty filter drops the multipanel rows, because their tag comes from the caption of the whole figure. Without a specialty filter, the flag does nothing. Example: the multipanel radiology rows go from 513,709 to 0. Before 2026-11-03, the flag did nothing, because the tag table has no contains_specialty column. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-H1-47). The other options were to drop the flag, and to drop every multipanel row also with no specialty filter. Checked by: tests/test_medpmc.py::test_include_multipanel_false_gives_a_panel_level_set.
  • MIMIC IDs: every harmonizer on MIMIC images writes patient_id and study_id as digits, the official MIMIC IDs (for example 10003502, not p10003502). So a join across these datasets works. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-12 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other option was the source form of each dataset, on its wiki page. Since 2026-11-01, GEMeX VQA and MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA write digits (Q-12). The study_ids= and patient_ids= filters of MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA accept both forms. Checked by: tests/test_harmonizer_id_filter.py::test_mimic_ext_qba_ids_are_digits_and_question_id_names_one_row and ::test_gemex_vqa_ids_are_digits.
  • VQA row id: the question_id of MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA is <study_id>_<source question_id>, because the source id is a template name that repeats in every study (V-H1-30). Example: 50037760_D01_describe_finding_015. Decided (Frank Li confirmed on 2026-11-02 the choice of the agent of 2026-11-01). The other option was the source id with a separate row number.
  • VQA row id of CheXinstruct VQA: unique_id of the compiled JSON. The MIMIC-CXR-VQA processor shuffles the train questions with no seed, so scripts/compile_chexinstruct_vqa.py seeds random (--seed, default 0). 2 runs with the same seed then give the same file. The JSON on the NAS came from a run with no seed, and it stays. A new run gives the same 701,458 questions, answers, images and splits. Only the unique_id and the order of the MIMIC-CXR-VQA train rows change, and the qa_pair of the closed questions. The harmonizer does not read qa_pair. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04). The other options were a seed and a new NAS file, and no seed. Checked by: tests/test_scripts.py::test_compile_chexinstruct_vqa_seed_gives_the_same_file.
  • 3-D view_position: the name of the nearest plane ("axial", "coronal" or "sagittal"), from the DICOM ImageOrientationPatient. The vector goes in the extra column image_orientation. Example: CT-RATE. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, V-H1-28). The other options were the vector only, and the plane name with no vector column.
  • Checked by (3-D view_position): tests/test_harmonizer_data.py::test_ct_rate_view_position_is_the_nearest_plane and ::test_ct_rate_orientation_count_on_nas.
  • Known gaps (3-D view_position): 3 harmonizers do not read ImageOrientationPatient, so their tables have no view_position. They are RSNA 2022 cervical spine, RSNA 2023 abdominal trauma and RSNA PE detection. The DICOM headers have the tag. Found in the 6c rewrite of the wiki pages (2026-11-04). The fix is in their own harmonizers, not in base code.
  • RSNA 2024 lumbar spine follows the 3-D rule: view_position is "axial" or "sagittal". The series description ("Axial T2", "Sagittal T1", "Sagittal T2/STIR") goes to the column series_description. series_filter reads that column, with the same values as before. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-18 of the 2026-10-31 review), with a note from Frank Li: revisit this later. The other option was an exception for datasets with a description. Known gap: view_position holds the description today (Q-18). The description agrees with the orientation in 300 of 300 random series.
  • 2-D view_position: one shared name list, as for sex (D-26). The names are PA, AP and LATERAL, and NaN means unknown (for example a blank, Unknown, UNK, N/A or EXCLUDE). A source with AP or PA gives AP or PA, not Frontal. Any other source value (for example an oblique view or AP_horizontal) keeps its raw value in upper case. One base step does the mapping. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-13 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other option was the raw values of each source, listed on each wiki page.
  • 2-D view_position step: _build_view_position_names in radharmony/harmonizer/base.py (base code, approved by Frank Li on 2026-11-02). L, LL, RL and LAT give LATERAL, POSTERO_ANTERIOR gives PA, ANTERO_POSTERIOR gives AP, and the text None gives NaN. A class with VIEW_POSITION_NAMES = False keeps its own names: CT-RATE and RSNA 2024 lumbar (3-D plane or series names) and Emory CXR DICOM. Checked by: tests/test_view_position.py. On 2026-11-02 the real counts matched the source, for example BRAX LATERAL = 9,052 L + 1,340 RL. A table saved before 2026-11-02 keeps its old names until harmonize() runs again.
  • Notes (2-D view_position step): since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li, ANTERO_POSTERIOR gives AP and the text None gives NaN (V-H2-43). Before, they gave ANTERO_POSTERIOR and NONE. The ReXGradient train JSON has 1 ANTERO_POSTERIOR view and 2 text None views. Checked by: tests/test_view_position.py::test_unknown_strings_give_nan_and_an_opt_out_class_keeps_them.
  • CheXpert, CheXpert Plus and CheXphoto view_position: a frontal image with LL or RL in AP/PA gives NaN, because AP or PA is unknown. CheXpert train has 17 such images. This follows the Emory rule of Q-14. Decided (Frank Li confirmed on 2026-11-02 the choice of the agent). The other options were LATERAL from the shared table, and the source value LL or RL.
  • Known gaps (2-D view_position): these harmonizers write FRONTAL where the source has AP or PA (Q-13). CheXlocalize val has AP or PA in its CSV for 202 images. SIIM-ACR PTX writes Frontal for all images, but 200 of 200 sampled DICOM files have ViewPosition PA or AP. The fixes are in their own harmonizers, not in base code.
  • MIMIC-CXR (DICOM) view_position: only with dicom_base_dir. The harmonizer then reads the DICOM tag ViewPosition of each file, which is slow (377,110 files for all splits). Without it, the harmonized table has no view_position. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-03, found in the 6c rewrite of the wiki page). The other options were to read the DICOM files in base_image_dir, and to take the view from the MIMIC-CXR-JPG metadata file. Before, the docstring said that dicom_base_dir falls back to base_image_dir, but the code never did. Checked by: tests/test_mimic_cxr.py::test_no_dicom_base_dir_gives_no_view_position.
  • MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA view_position: img.view_position of the question's image in image_metadata.parquet, with the shared names. With no image_metadata.parquet, the harmonizer warns and the table has no view_position. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04, found in the 6c rewrite of the wiki page). The other option was no change. In q1M of A_frontal, the table and the source both give AP for 613,324 questions and PA for 386,676. Checked by: tests/test_mimic_ext_cxr_qba.py::test_view_position_comes_from_the_image_metadata and ::test_no_image_metadata_warns_and_gives_no_view_position.
  • Notes (OpenI view): since 2026-11-02, OpenI corrects the figure number with the DICOM tag (V-H2-40). The tag wins when it is AP or a lateral tag. A PA tag counts only on F1, because many lateral images also have PA. The 1,313 F1 images with no tag stay FRONTAL. Checked by: tests/test_harmonizer_data.py::test_openi_view_takes_the_dicom_tag_when_it_names_ap_or_a_lateral and ::test_openi_view_reads_the_dicom_tag.
  • 2-D view_position from the DICOM tag: a release can have no view column. Then the harmonizer reads the DICOM ViewPosition tag, as D-06 does for age and sex. Example: RSNA Pneumonia Kaggle has no view column, but in 300 of its DICOM files the tag is PA (166) or AP (134). Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-02, Q-18 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were a view from a CSV only, and the tag only for datasets that a benchmark filters by view. Since 2026-11-03, RSNA Pneumonia Kaggle train and test read the tag. They read it with the sex and the age, in one header pass (extra_tags of add_patient_tags in radharmony/harmonizer/_dicom_tags.py). A real run gave train PA 14,511 and AP 12,173 (26,684 images), and test PA 1,618 and AP 1,382. Checked by: tests/test_rsna_pneumonia_kaggle.py::test_train_view_position_comes_from_the_dicom_tag and ::test_test_view_position_comes_from_the_dicom_tag.
  • Size columns: the BRAX extra columns rows and columns give the DICOM size from the source metadata, also in the PNG variant. Example: 2752 x 2232 in the table, but the PNG is 1261 x 1024. The BRAX wiki page says so. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-02, Q-10 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were the names dicom_rows and dicom_columns, and the PNG size in the PNG variant. Notes: since 2026-11-03, docs/wiki/reference/datasets/cxr-labels/brax.md says it (Q-10).
  • Emory CXR view_position: when the Frontal column and the DICOM ViewPosition tag disagree, Frontal wins, because it is more accurate (Frank Li). Frontal = 0 gives LATERAL. Frontal = 1 with ViewPosition Lateral gives NaN, because AP or PA is unknown. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-14 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other options were NaN for every conflict, and both columns as in the source. Exception: Frontal = 0 with ViewPosition AP (2,202 images) gives NaN. In 24 random images of this group, 9 are upright frontal and 11 are decubitus (AP with the patient on the side). 3 are lateral, and 1 is unclear. So LATERAL is wrong for most of them. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-01). The other options were AP and LATERAL. Since the Q-13 step (2026-11-02), the lateral name is LATERAL. The rule is for the PNG classes only. Emory CXR DICOM keeps ViewPosition as in the source (Frank Li, 2026-11-01). Checked by: tests/test_emory_cxr.py::test_view_position_follows_frontal. Notes: a sample of 4 images for each conflict group on 2026-10-31. Frontal=0 with PA: 4 lateral. Frontal=1 with Lateral: 4 frontal. Before 2026-11-01, view_position came from ViewPosition only, so a PA filter kept 45,687 lateral images (Q-14).
  • Notes (CT-RATE): a real run on 2026-10-30 checked the 47,149 train volumes. 47,111 are axial, 14 coronal and 12 sagittal. 12 more are tilted more than 8° from a plane (5 near axial, 5 near coronal, 2 near sagittal). All 3,039 volumes of the validation split are axial.

docs.title: D-02 Harmonize first, then filter
docs.text:
Run harmonize() on the full dataset. Then filter the table with pandas. The study_ids= and patient_ids= arguments only make harmonize() faster on a big dataset. They must give the same rows as a filter after harmonize().

df = h.harmonize()
df = df[df["view_position"] == "PA"]

Why: a filter on an image property (view, mask present) must see every image row.

  • Status: From the code (BaseHarmonizer.harmonize docstring).
  • Checked by: tests/test_harmonizer_id_filter.py::test_study_ids_filter_matches_filter_after, ::test_mimic_ext_qba_id_filter_matches_filter_after, tests/test_siim_acr_ptx.py::test_id_filter_gives_the_rows_of_a_filter_after, L-008 and L-014.
  • No matching study: a study id that no row has gives 0 rows with the columns of the full table, not an error. A split class gets such an id when the study is in another split. Checked by: tests/test_official_splits.py::test_a_study_of_no_row_gives_an_empty_table and the no_study check of tests/fixtures/harmonizer_contract.py (L-014).
  • Notes (no matching study): before 2026-11-01, CheXlocalize, CheXpert Plus and MIMIC-CXR-JPG raised an error (V-H1-38).
  • VQA harmonizers: only MIMICExtCXRQBAHarmonizer gets study_ids= and patient_ids=, before its slow qa.zip step. The other VQA harmonizers have no filter. Filter their table with pandas after harmonize(). Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30), option (c). The other options were (a) a filter for all 7 VQA harmonizers (a base-code change in base_vqa.py) and (b) no VQA filter. Findings: V-H2-11, V-H1-16 and V-H3-10.
  • Notes: a real run on 2026-10-29 timed the full VQA harmonize(). VQA-RAD train took 0.0 s, CheXinstruct VQA train 6.0 s and MedPMC (11.1 million rows) 16.6 s. MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA (208,316 studies) did not finish in 25 minutes, because it opens 1 file in qa.zip for each study. With max_studies=1000 it took 10.3 s. With study_ids= of 3 studies, it took 2.8 s (since 2026-10-30).
  • A filter argument of a dataset class also filters a given table (harmonized_df=, harmonizer= or harmonizer_path=). Example: RSNA 2024 lumbar series_filter, in the train and the test class. Before 2026-11-03, the test class kept all series of a given table (V-D-32). Checked by: tests/test_rsna_2024_lumbar_spine.py::test_series_filter_applies_to_a_given_table.
  • VQA and caption classes: since 2026-11-04, the filters of ROCO, ROCOv2, MedPMC and CheXinstruct VQA also filter a given table. Each harmonizer has one filter_table() that its harmonize() and the dataset class both use. Before, a given table kept every row: ROCOv2TestDataset(modalities=["ct"]) gave 3,615 rows from the source files, but 9,927 rows with harmonized_df=. A split class with a given table keeps only its split, when the table has a split column. A MedPMC filter whose column the given table does not have raises ValueError. Arguments that only change how harmonize() makes a column (ROCOv2 manual_concepts_only, MedPMC tags_path) do not change a given table. Checked by: tests/test_vqa_filters.py.
  • ROCO radiology_only: the dataset default is None. None gives True when the class harmonizes. On a given table, True keeps only the radiology rows, and None and False keep every row. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04). The other options were the default True that also filters a given table, and no filter on a given table at all. With the default True, a saved table with radiology_only=False loses its non-radiology rows.
  • Local lists that are not in the release: a harmonizer does not use them, and the table keeps their rows. The dataset wiki page names the files, so a user can filter with them. Example: the CT-RATE folder has tables/no_chest_train.txt (752 volumes) and tables/no_chest_valid.txt (37 volumes). Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-02, Q-13 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were to drop these volumes by default, and a flag column such as has_chest. Since 2026-11-03, the CT-RATE wiki page names the files and shows a filter. On the valid split, the filter removes the 37 listed volumes of 3,039.
  • Missing image files: a harmonizer keeps a row whose image file is not on disk. When it can check the disk quickly, it warns with the count of its own table, and the user calls verify_images() to drop the rows. Example: the NAS copy of CheXpert Plus has no folder for 12,471 of 223,228 train rows and 5 of 234 valid rows. The same table then comes from every copy of a release. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-H1-7, V-D-17). The other option was to drop these rows in harmonize(). Checked by: tests/test_chexpert_plus.py::test_missing_patient_folders_warn and ::test_a_split_class_counts_the_missing_folders_of_its_own_split.
  • Notes (missing image files): before 2026-11-03, a CheXpert Plus split class counted the rows of both splits. Example: 12,476 of 223,462 rows for valid (V-H1-45).
  • Related: D-31.

docs.title: D-03 One row per image
docs.text:
A harmonizer returns one row per image. A harmonizer can return one row per study, series or volume instead. In that case, its docstring and its wiki page say so.

Some source files have one line per box or per mask region (for example SIIM-ACR). The harmonizer's own code joins these lines into one line per image. The base merges raise a ValueError when a source file has more than one line for a key. This applies to labels, view position, masks, boxes and reports.

Why: an image row keeps every image property, and a study or patient table can be built from it.

  • Status: From the code. The rule for a repeated key: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-29, V-H2-17).
  • Checked by: J-02, tests/test_harmonizer_merge.py (also ::test_a_repeated_report_key_raises), and tests/test_dataset_stats.py::test_one_row_per_image for the datasets with expected_stats.
  • Notes (report merge): since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li, the base _build_report() also raises on a repeated key (V-H2-31). Before, 2 report lines for one study gave 2 rows for each image of the study. Only MIMIC-CXR uses this step, and its report list has 0 repeated keys in 227,835 lines.
  • Emory CXR: its own code reads the report and label CSVs, which can have 2 different lines for one study. A blank report template (only "REPORT", spaces and underscores) counts as no report. When a study has another row, the code drops the blank report row and a label row with only No Finding = 1. For the other conflicts, the first row stays, with a warning. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, V-H1-12). The other options were the first row with a warning, and NaN for every conflict.
  • An image of the source list with no annotation file: the harmonizer leaves it out of the table and warns with the count. Example: 2 images of the Chest ImaGenome silver valid.csv have no scene graph file. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-H1-37). The other options were a row with no boxes, and an error. Checked by: tests/test_chest_imagenome.py::test_silver_warns_about_images_with_no_scene_graph.
  • Notes (Chest ImaGenome): since 2026-11-03, the same rule holds for an image with no DICOM header with Rows and Columns in base_image_dir. A box needs the image size (D-07), so the harmonizer leaves the image out and warns with the count. Before, it gave no warning. Checked by: tests/test_chest_imagenome.py::test_gold_warns_about_an_image_with_no_readable_size and ::test_silver_warns_about_an_image_with_no_readable_size.
  • Checked by (Emory): tests/test_harmonizer_data.py::test_emory_prefers_the_real_row_of_a_study and ::test_emory_conflicting_duplicate_rows_on_nas (8 label and 17 report conflicts left on 2026-10-30).
  • Notes (Emory): a real run on 2026-10-30 found 151 studies with 2 report rows. 134 had a blank template and a real report, and 17 had 2 real reports. 75 studies had 2 label rows. 67 of them had a "No Finding only" row, and 65 of these also had a blank template. The first row was the blank template for 68 reports, and the "No Finding only" row for 32 label rows.
  • Related: D-31.

docs.title: D-31 Study and patient tables come from the image table
docs.text:
The image table stays the only source. One function builds the other levels from it:

df = h.harmonize()                      # image level
df = df[df["view_position"] == "PA"]    # filter at image level first
study_df = to_level(df, "study")        # one row per study
patient_df = to_level(df, "patient")    # one row per patient

harmonize() does not take a level= argument. Every table also gets the columns study_date, study_time and visit_number (D-01). The rules for each column are in docs/proposals/harmonized_df_levels_and_visits.md.

Why: a filter on an image property must run before the grouping (D-02). One function works for every harmonizer and for saved and filtered tables.

  • Status: Decided, planned (Frank Li, 2026-10-28). We build it after the new evaluation pipeline is done and the code findings are fixed.
  • Checked by: none.
  • Related: D-01, D-02, D-03.

docs.title: D-04 Image paths are relative to base_image_dir
docs.text:
image_path is relative to base_image_dir. base_image_dir is the deepest folder that is the same for every image. For example, for /data/cxr14/images_001/a.png and /data/cxr14/images_002/b.png, base_image_dir is /data/cxr14 and image_path is images_001/a.png.

When the dataset authors provide separate train and test folders, each official split class takes its own folder. For example, VinDr-CXR uses train/ and test/.

A dataset with images from several sources keeps image_path relative to the folder of its source, with a data_source column. The dataset class joins the folder of each source when it loads (for example source_image_dirs of CheXinstruct VQA). image_path holds a relative path, with one exception: the copy step (see "Exception (copy step)" below). A mask_path that a harmonizer writes is also absolute (see the last line of this entry).

Why: the user gives one folder, and the same table works on any computer.

  • Status: From the code (.claude/skills/add-dataset/SKILL.md, "base_image_dir Convention"). The rule for several sources: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-11 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other option was absolute paths for CheXinstruct VQA, as an exception.
  • Checked by: the harmonizer contract (L-008, since 2026-11-03), on 11 fake datasets in CI and on the datasets with expected_stats in the full run. The proof that the check fails on an absolute path is tests/test_harmonizer_contract.py::test_contract_finds_an_absolute_image_path. Also tests/test_harmonizer_data.py::test_ms_cxr_t_base_image_dir_is_the_files_folder (MS-CXR-T only), tests/test_save_load.py::test_verify_images_needs_the_image_folder_for_relative_paths and ::test_series_verify_images_follows_d04 (the 4 3-D harmonizers whose image_path is a series folder), and tests/test_vqa_base.py::test_verify_images_needs_the_image_folder_for_relative_paths (VQA).
  • Notes (CheXinstruct VQA): before 2026-11-01, it wrote an absolute image_path in all 21,296 test rows, and base_image_dir was None (Q-11). Checked by: tests/test_official_splits.py::test_chexinstruct_image_path_is_relative and ::test_chexinstruct_dataset_joins_the_folder_of_each_source. A table or harmonizer that an older version saved has absolute paths. The dataset class makes them relative to the folder first (::test_chexinstruct_dataset_loads_an_old_table_and_a_harmonizer_object).
  • Exception (copy step): after harmonize(preprocess_output_dir=...), image_path is the path of the copy below preprocess_output_dir. It is absolute when that folder is absolute, for example /data/out/a.png.nii. Base code approved by Frank Li on 2026-11-03: with no base_image_dir in the call, the copy step reads from h.base_image_dir, as verify_images() does. Before, h.harmonize(preprocess_output_dir=..., preprocessor=...) read from the current folder and raised "N of N images failed". Keeping the copy paths relative was the other option: rejected because it needs a new attribute for the folder of the copies. The mask step (harmonize(mask_output_dir=...)) uses the same default since 2026-11-03 (base code approved by Frank Li). Checked by: tests/test_harmonizer_preprocess.py::test_copy_step_reads_from_the_folder_of_the_harmonizer and ::test_mask_step_reads_from_the_folder_of_the_harmonizer.
  • Notes: since 2026-10-29 (approved by Frank Li), the base docstrings say that image_path is relative. verify_images() takes self.base_image_dir when the harmonizer has it. With relative paths and no folder, it raises a ValueError. Before, it dropped every row, for example 138 of 138 Montgomery rows (V-H2-23, V-H1-22). Since 2026-11-01, the verify_images() overrides of RSNA 2024 lumbar, RSNA PE, RSNA 2023 abdominal trauma and RSNA 2022 cervical follow the same rule. Before, lumbar dropped all 6,294 rows although base_image_dir was set (V-H3-22). Since 2026-11-02 (base code approved by Frank Li), BaseVQAHarmonizer.verify_images() follows it too. Before, the ROCOv2 harmonizer had no folder, so a default call dropped every row (V-H2-28). Since 2026-11-03, Shenzhen, VinDr-PCXR and SIIM-ACR PTX use their own folder argument (base_dir or dicom_dir) as the default. Before, a default call raised the ValueError (V-H3-36). Checked by: tests/test_verify_images.py.
  • Dataset classes: since 2026-11-04 (base code approved by Frank Li), verify_images() of a dataset class follows the same rule. BaseRadiologicalDataset, BaseVQADataset and all 7 overrides call one helper, _require_image_folder in radharmony/dataset/base.py. Before, a dataset class with relative paths and no base_image_dir dropped every row. Example: CheXpertDataset(harmonized_df=df). CheXinstruct VQA with several source_image_dirs has no single folder, so its own verify_images() joins the folder of the data_source of each row. Before, it dropped every row. Checked by: tests/test_verify_images.py.
  • RAD-ChestCT folder name: the harmonizer takes base_image_dir=, as the other harmonizers and configs/data_paths.json do. The old name image_base_dir= still works, and 2 different folders raise ValueError. Before 2026-11-03, image_base_dir= was the only name, so verify_images() with defaults raised ValueError (V-H2-33). Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-H2-33). The other option was an override of verify_images() that reads image_base_dir. Checked by: tests/test_radchestct.py.
  • Exception (mask files that a harmonizer writes): their mask_path is absolute. The harmonizer writes them to an output folder that the user picks, and the dataset class joins base_image_dir to image_path only. This is the case for Montgomery, Shenzhen, QaTa-COV19 and MedSeg COVID CT. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-H1-50). The other option was a path relative to base_image_dir, with a change of the join step and of the 4 harmonizers. A move of the output folder needs a new harmonize().

docs.title: D-35 infer_path looks only in exact places, and missing data raises FileNotFoundError
docs.text:
When the user does not give a source file, infer_path (radharmony/utils/infer.py) looks for it only in these places, in this order:

  1. The path that the user gives. If the user gives a path that does not exist, it raises FileNotFoundError with that path.
  2. base_dir/<name>.
  3. parent/<name>, where parent is the folder above base_dir.

It does not walk folders. A dataset class whose file is in another folder puts the sub folder in the name. Example: VinDr-CXR looks for annotations/image_labels_train.csv in parent.

Why: a folder walk can take a file of another dataset with the same name. On 2026-10-29, the CheXphoto classes took ranzcr-clip-catheter-line-classification/train.csv, because the CheXphoto folder could not be read. A folder walk can also search all of / when a folder is missing, so 2 doc blocks timed out.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-29), option (a). Frank Li chose it over (b), a shorter folder walk, and (c), no change. Findings: V-A-19, V-P-13 and V-P-8.
  • Checked by: tests/test_official_splits.py::test_infer_path_candidate_order_and_sub_path, ::test_infer_path_looks_only_in_exact_places, ::test_infer_path_raises_for_a_user_path_that_does_not_exist, ::test_infer_path_required_names_the_file_and_the_places, ::test_a_class_with_no_data_names_the_missing_file, ::test_a_class_names_its_second_missing_file, ::test_a_test_split_class_does_not_need_the_train_files, ::test_a_test_class_names_the_argument_of_a_wrong_path, ::test_an_asked_output_needs_its_file, ::test_ranzcr_mask_without_the_annotation_file_names_it, ::test_mimic_cxr_metadata_file_is_not_the_record_list, ::test_chexpert_plus_finds_its_files_2_folders_up_and_takes_impression_fixed, ::test_a_class_with_an_empty_image_folder_names_the_folder and ::test_roco_with_no_split_folder_raises_and_a_missing_one_warns. Also tests/test_roco.py::test_roco_split_with_no_captions_file_warns_and_names_it and ::test_roco_with_no_captions_file_at_all_raises (V-H2-45).
  • Missing file: when a class does not find a required file, it raises FileNotFoundError. The message names the file and the places it looked, for example train_image_level.csv is not in <base_dir> or <parent>. Pass image_csv_path=<path>. Then the doc block runner reports "blocked, needs data". Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other options were the old ValueErrors with a new runner rule, and no change.
  • File for one output: a file that a class reads for only one output is required when the user asks for that output. Example: MIMIC-CXR with output_cls=True and no mimic-cxr-2.0.0-chexpert.csv raises FileNotFoundError. Before, the sample had no cls key and no warning. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31). The other options were a warning and no key, and no change.
  • Empty image folder: a class with no index file (a CSV or JSON that lists the images) lists the images in its folder. It raises FileNotFoundError when it finds no image, and the message names the folder and the file type. Example: No <study>/<series>/*.dcm file in <dir>. montgomery_cxr, siim_acr_ptx_test and siim_covid19_test got this on 2026-10-31. Before, they crashed with an AttributeError or a KeyError. shenzhen_cxr, qata_cov19, ranzcr_clip_test and rsna_bone_age_test already did it. Since 2026-11-03, rsna_pneumonia_kaggle_test does it too (V-H3-28). Its parent folder, as an old docstring said, gave a KeyError before (V-H3-5). Checked by: tests/test_rsna_pneumonia_kaggle.py::test_test_folder_with_no_dicom_names_the_folder. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31). The other options were 0 samples with a warning, and no change.
  • Known gaps: the file-for-one-output rule is checked only for MIMIC-CXR, MIMIC-CXR-JPG, RSNA Pneumonia Kaggle, CheXpert Plus, RANZCR CLiP, Montgomery, Shenzhen and CheXlocalize. The other classes were not scanned for it (no ID).
  • Notes (Shenzhen, CheXlocalize): since 2026-11-03, a call for masks raises FileNotFoundError that names the missing file. For Shenzhen, it is the Annotations-2/masks/ folder, when the table has a TB image. For CheXlocalize, it is gt_segmentations_*.json. Before, Shenzhen kept only the normal images, and CheXlocalize raised "No mask_path column found" in harmonize(). Found in the 6c rewrite of the wiki pages. Checked by: tests/test_harmonizer_preprocess.py::test_shenzhen_masks_with_no_mask_folder_raise and tests/test_chexlocalize.py::test_output_mask_with_no_mask_file_raises.
  • Notes (Montgomery): since 2026-11-03, a call for masks with no ManualMask/ raises FileNotFoundError that names the folder. Before, it raised a ValueError, and the wiki said the rows were dropped (V-H2-36). Checked by: tests/test_montgomery_cxr.py::test_masks_without_manual_mask_folder_name_it.
  • Notes: a real run on 2026-10-29 built 70 registry keys with only base_image_dir (119 searches). 6 found the given path, 14 found the file in base_dir and 63 in parent. 24 found it in a sibling folder, and 2 (CheXlocalize) in an uncle folder. 10 found nothing. Each search took 0.6 s or less.
  • Notes (fix): on 2026-10-30, infer_path looks only in the 2 exact places. 6 datasets put the sub folder in the file name: VinDr-CXR annotations/, RAD-ChestCT tables/, Emory CXR TABLES/, ReXGradient download/metadata/, CheXlocalize ../CheXlocalize/ and CheXpert Plus ../. CheXpert Plus walked up 4 folders before 2026-10-31. A scan of the 103 registry keys with only base_image_dir found the same files as before. Only CheXphoto changed: its folder is restricted, so it raises now. Before, it took the RANZCR train.csv. On 2026-10-30, 14 dataset classes got required=True, and ROCO got its own FileNotFoundError when it finds no split folder. On 2026-10-31, 15 more classes got required=True. Before, 18 of their keys gave the pandas error "Invalid file path or buffer object type". Examples are chestxray14_bbox, the MIMIC-CXR and MS-CXR keys, RANZCR CLiP and the RSNA 2022 and 2023 keys. The 4 CheXInstruct keys gave a TypeError, and 5 keys gave another ValueError. A test-split class does not require the train files. 5 classes set _TRAIN_FILES_REQUIRED = False. The RSNA 2022, 2023 and PE test classes pass their test file as csv_path. A scan on 2026-10-31 built every registry key with an empty image folder and called get_datasets(). 112 of the 128 keys raise FileNotFoundError (the 4 ROCO keys take base_dir, not base_image_dir). 14 keys raise a ValueError that names an argument to pass, for example annotation_dir (Chest ImaGenome). The 2 QaTa-COV19 split keys say that the folder must be in Train Set/ or Test Set/. On 2026-11-03, CheXpertValidDataset got required=True for valid.csv. Before, it took the train.csv search of CheXpertDataset when valid.csv was missing (V-A-34). Checked by tests/test_app.py::test_chexpert_valid_without_valid_csv_is_an_error.
  • Related: D-04, D-21.

docs.title: D-05 Labels
docs.text:
• Label columns are in LABEL_COLS, with snake_case names.
  • Name a label after the finding, not after the way the source codes it. Example: Montgomery and Shenzhen both give tuberculosis. Some datasets still use different names for one finding, for example ChestX-ray14 effusion and CheXpert pleural_effusion. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-05).
  • The label columns are sorted alphabetically by their snake_case names. BaseHarmonizer.harmonize sorts them. The cls vector uses the same order.
  • In cls, a label keeps the CheXpert-style source codes: 1 (positive), 0 (negative), -1 (uncertain) and NaN (not mentioned, or unknown). The probes use only 0 and 1, so they skip -1 and NaN. drop_uncertain=True drops the rows with -1. A harmonizer can keep raw grades, for example the TAIX-Ray grades 0 to 4. Then its dataset class maps them to 0 and 1.
  • Not mentioned (CheXpert, CheXpert Plus, MIMIC-CXR and MIMIC-CXR-JPG): the argument not_mentioned sets a blank label. "negative" (the default) gives 0, as most CheXpert papers do. "nan" keeps NaN, so the probes skip it. Example: Pleural Other is blank in 97% of the CheXpert train rows.
  • A regression target goes in REG_COLS, not in LABEL_COLS.
  • Each dataset wiki page gives the policy for uncertain and blank labels. For example, CheXpert maps a blank to 0 and keeps -1.
  • A row for which the labeler gave no label at all (an empty label list) gets NaN in every label. It is unknown, not negative. Example: 777 PadChest rows have the raw Labels value [''], and their reports name findings such as scoliosis. The probes skip NaN, so these rows do not count as negatives. A CheXpert-style row with every label blank is such a row, also with not_mentioned="negative". Example: 4,857 MIMIC-CXR-JPG train rows. Before 2026-11-02 they got 0 in every label (V-H1-41).
  • A source value that a harmonizer splits into one-hot columns gets NaN in all of these columns when the value is blank. Example: a blank RSNA 2024 lumbar severity gives NaN in normal_mild, moderate and severe, not 0 in all 3.
  • A class that a source does not annotate gets NaN, not 0. Example: the MedSeg dataset2 masks have only the values 0, 1 and 2, so pleural_effusion is NaN in its 829 rows. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-02, Q-12 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other option was 0 with the current wiki line.
  • A trigger word sets only its own finding. Example: the OpenI MeSH term Lung/hypoinflation does not set atelectasis. 189 of the 504 OpenI studies with atelectasis = 1 have only this term. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-02, Q-15 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were to keep the trigger with a wiki line, and a separate hypoinflation column.
  • Notes (MedSeg, since 2026-11-03): dataset2 gives NaN in pleural_effusion, because its masks have no class 3 (Q-12). Checked by: tests/test_harmonizer_data.py::test_medseg_dataset2_pleural_effusion_is_nan.
  • Notes (2026-11-02): OpenI no longer maps lung/hypoinflation to atelectasis (Q-15). Its reports with only the MeSH term "No Indexing", or with no term, get NaN in every label (V-H2-41).
  • Notes (2026-11-05): the Montgomery label tb became tuberculosis, the same name as Shenzhen and the public RadHarmony repo. Decided by Frank Li. The other option was to keep tb. A saved Montgomery table with tb has no tuberculosis column. With output_cls=True, the dataset class warns that the label column is missing, and a sample raises RuntimeError. Harmonize such a table again. Checked by (the label names only): tests/test_montgomery_cxr.py::test_label_is_tuberculosis.

Why: a probe can use the label columns of any dataset without code for that dataset.

  • Status: From the code. The codes in cls (-1 uncertain, NaN not mentioned): Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-4 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other options were 1, 0 and NaN only (-1 becomes NaN), and -1 as an exception for 3 classes. The empty-label-list rule: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-15 of the same review). The other options were to drop the rows, and to keep them with all labels 0. The one-hot rule: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-17 of the same review). The other option was 0 in all columns, with a wiki line. The not_mentioned rule: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-01, follow-up of Q-4). The other options were always 0 and always NaN. 73% of the CheXpert train label cells are blank, so NaN as the default would train each probe on the mentioned rows only.
  • Checked by: J-04, tests/test_label_order.py, L-008, and tests/test_harmonizer_data.py::test_padchest_empty_label_list_is_nan and ::test_rsna_2024_lumbar_blank_severity_is_nan (since 2026-11-01, Q-15 and Q-17), and ::test_chexpert_codes_follow_d05, ::test_mimic_jpg_keeps_uncertain_as_minus_one, ::test_chexpert_not_mentioned_nan_keeps_the_blank and ::test_every_chexpert_style_harmonizer_follows_d05 (Q-4). For V-H1-41: ::test_chexpert_codes_keep_nan_for_a_row_with_no_label and ::test_a_row_with_no_label_at_all_is_nan_by_default. For OpenI (Q-15, V-H2-41): ::test_openi_mesh_terms_match_whole_words and ::test_openi_no_indexing_gives_nan_in_every_label.
  • Notes (Q-4): before 2026-11-01, CheXpert, CheXpert Plus, MIMIC-CXR and MIMIC-CXR-JPG mapped -1 to NaN. So cls lost the difference between "uncertain" and "not mentioned" (Q-4, V-H1-34). Now they share chexpert_codes in radharmony/harmonizer/_labels.py, with the MIMIC-CXR-JPG labeled test class. With the defaults, the table is the same as before. BRAX ("raw"), Emory CXR and the MIMIC-CXR-JPG labeled test kept -1 already.
  • Related: D-08, D-30.

docs.title: D-44 A "stable" finding is present
docs.text:
In the phase-grounding labels (docs/wiki/explanation/phase-grounding.md), "stable X" means that finding X is still there and has not changed. So X is present. With no severity word, X gets the default severity 2.

Example: "stable cardiomegaly" gives heart_size 2.

Why: a score of 0 would call a present finding absent.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-22 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other options were no default for a "stable" finding (score 0), and a separate rule for "stable X".
  • Checked by: none.
  • Known gaps: the doc calls the score "reasonable" and gives no reason (R-docs-18 of the 2026-10-31 review).
  • Known gaps (script): the label script (extract_mimic_labels.py of the phase-grounding project, outside this repo) has "stable" in its grade-0 word list. So "Stable cardiomegaly." gives heart_size 0, and the labels parquet does not follow D-44 yet. Found on 2026-11-04 in the 6c rewrite. Frank Li kept D-44 (2026-11-04): the owner of the script changes it and makes the parquet again (eval/TODO.md). The other options were to change D-44 to 0, and to leave the question open.
  • Related: D-05.

docs.title: D-48 CheXpert Plus labels come from impression_fixed.json
docs.text:
The CheXpert Plus harmonizers take their labels from impression_fixed.json, not from report_fixed.json. Both files are in the release folder, with the same image paths in the same order.

Why: the labels in report_fixed.json do not follow the image. A check with pandas only, joined by image path, gave these numbers on 2026-11-02:

  • P(Cardiomegaly=1) is 0.16 when CheXpert v1 says 1, and 0.16 when it does not. With impression_fixed.json, it is 0.90 and 0.03.
  • The images of one study share one report, so they must share labels. In report_fixed.json, 31,377 of the 33,973 studies with 2 or more images give their images different labels. In impression_fixed.json, 380 do.

CheXpert v1 also takes its labels from the impression.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-02, Q-7 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were to keep report_fixed.json with a wiki warning, and to leave the question open.
  • Checked by: tests/test_chexpert_plus.py::test_every_chexpert_plus_key_reads_the_labels_of_the_impression, tests/test_official_splits.py::test_chexpert_plus_finds_its_files_2_folders_up_and_takes_impression_fixed, and the CheXpert Plus expected_stats in tests/test_dataset_stats.py (full run, real data).
  • Notes: since 2026-11-03, the dataset class, the app and configs/data_paths.json take impression_fixed.json (Q-7). The CheXpert Plus rows with no label go from 3,673 to 12 (V-H1-41). With the default drop_uncertain=True, train has 143,343 images (134,623 before) and valid has 165 (145 before). All CheXpert Plus benchmark results must run again.
  • Related: D-05, D-35.

docs.title: D-51 A MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA answer holds the main answer only
docs.text:
The answer column of MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA holds only the texts of the main_answer entries. The texts of details and related_information stay in answer_struct.

Example: 421,565 of the 1,000,000 q1M questions also have a details or related_information text. Their answer does not hold it.

Why: answer is the short answer that a VQA metric compares. The extra texts make it long.

  • Status: Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-02, Q-14 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other option was to keep all top-level texts with a wiki line.
  • Checked by: tests/test_mimic_ext_cxr_qba.py::test_answer_holds_only_the_main_answer_texts.
  • Notes: before 2026-11-03, answer joined all top-level texts (Q-14), and the wiki said that it joins the texts of the annotators (V-H1-43).
  • Notes: a question whose main_answer text is empty gets answer "". A check of 2,000 studies (371,228 questions) in qa.zip on 2026-11-03 found 57 such questions with a related_information text. Before, their answer was that text.
  • Related: D-02.

docs.title: D-06 Age in years
docs.text:
Every harmonizer whose source has the age of the patient gives the column age_years. It is a float in years. A harmonizer declares the source column and its unit with AGE_SOURCE_COL and AGE_SOURCE_UNIT. The code never guesses the unit from the size of the numbers.

DICOM tags: if the age or the sex is only in the DICOM headers, the harmonizer reads the tags PatientAge and PatientSex. A missing or empty tag gives NaN. The docstring and the wiki page say that these values come from the DICOM tags, not from the official release of the dataset.

Why: datasets store age in days, months, years or DICOM age strings. A guess fails on child cohorts.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-28). The unit rule is from the code (comment on AGE_SOURCE_COL in radharmony/harmonizer/base.py).
  • Checked by: L-001 (tests/test_lessons.py), tests/test_dicom_tags.py, tests/test_sex_column.py, and tests/test_dataset_stats.py for the datasets with expected_stats.
  • Age groups: when the source gives only an age group, age_years is the low edge of the group. BRAX gives 5-year groups (0, 5, ..., 80) and 85 or more, so 85 or more gives 85. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other option was NaN for 85 or more (2,299 of 40,967 images). The same rule gives 90 for the 90+ of RSNA 2023 abdominal trauma (90 patients, V-H3-32).
  • Chest ImaGenome silver: age_years is the low edge of the scene-graph age_decile, and sex comes from its gender. The release writes the group 10-20 as 20-Oct, because a spreadsheet read it as a date, so 20-Oct gives 10. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-H1-35). The other option was NaN for 20-Oct (551 of 23,951 valid images). Checked by: tests/test_chest_imagenome.py::test_silver_gives_sex_and_the_low_edge_of_the_age_group.
  • Range: an age below 0 or above 130 years gives NaN (radharmony/harmonizer/_age.py). These values are errors in the source. Example: ChestX-ray14 has 16 images with an age from 148 to 414. Patient 5567 is 412 at the first visit and 53 at the next. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other option was to keep the raw value.
  • VinDr-CXR: a DICOM PatientAge of 0 (000Y or 000D) gives NaN, because it means "unknown". The tags give age 0 for 905 train and 269 test images, but only 2 to 12 images for each age from 2 to 17. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). This rule is for VinDr-CXR only. A child dataset such as VinDr-PCXR can have real newborns. The other options were NaN for age 0 in every DICOM dataset, and no change.
  • TAIX-Ray: Age 0 days gives age_years 0.0, because these are real newborns. The number of images falls smoothly over the first days (day 0: 55, day 1: 44, day 2: 36, day 3: 23). The same patients have later images at an older age. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-19 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other option was NaN for age 0, as in VinDr-CXR.
  • CheXpert demographics workbook: its AGE_AT_CXR is one age per patient, so the table does not take it. age_years comes from the Age of each image in the CSV. Before, the column age held the workbook age on every image, wrong by more than 1 year for 16,169 of 137,783 rows (V-H1-40). Decided (Frank Li confirmed on 2026-11-02 the choice of the agent of 2026-11-01). The other option was the workbook age under another column name.
  • Birth year: when the source has only the birth year and the study date, age_years is the study year minus the birth year. The age can be 1 year too high. PadChest has PatientBirth and StudyDate_DICOM, and the PatientAge of PadChest-GR uses the same formula. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other options were no age, and the year difference minus 0.5.
  • Checked by (the 3 rules above): tests/test_harmonizer_data.py::test_brax_age_group_85_or_more_gives_85, tests/test_dicom_tags.py::test_vindr_cxr_age_0_is_unknown and tests/test_age_units.py::test_padchest_age_is_study_year_minus_birth_year.
  • Known gaps: MR-RATE gives no age_years, because nobody has checked the unit of its column Patient'sAge. The data is restricted (no ID).
  • Notes: a real run on 2026-10-30 gave PadChest an age for 157,601 of its 157,607 rows, from 0 to 105 (median 62). VinDr-CXR train has ages from 2 to 124, and test from 4 to 90.
  • Notes (since 2026-11-03): VinDr-PCXR reads PatientAge and PatientSex from its DICOM headers (V-H3-31). The paper says every patient is under 10. The tags give 72 train and 14 test images an age over 10, up to 45 and 51. The table keeps the tag value. RSNA 2023 abdominal trauma reads Age and Sex from train_demographics_2024.csv (V-H3-32). Both have expected_stats with sex and age (L-021).
  • Related: D-26.

docs.title: D-26 One sex column
docs.text:
Every harmonizer that has the sex of the patient gives one column sex. Its values are "M", "F" or NaN. NaN means unknown or other, for example the DICOM value O. The source column can stay as an extra column. A sex that is only in the DICOM headers follows the DICOM rule of D-06. RSNA Bone Age also keeps sex_female (0 or 1), because bone-age models use it as a number.

Why: a user can compare or filter by sex across datasets without code for each dataset.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-28). Method: each harmonizer declares SEX_SOURCE_COL, and one base step next to _build_age_years maps the values with one shared table. The change to radharmony/harmonizer/base.py (base code) was approved by Frank Li on 2026-10-28. It was built on the same day. On 2026-10-29, Frank Li approved one more base-code change: a dataset and save() never use sex and age_years as labels.
  • Checked by: tests/test_sex_column.py, tests/test_dicom_tags.py, tests/test_padchest_gr.py::test_sex_comes_from_patient_sex_dicom, and tests/test_dataset_stats.py for the datasets with expected_stats.
  • CheXpert: sex comes from the CSV column Sex, on every row. It does not depend on demographics_path. The workbook column GENDER differs for 3 patients (patient51668, patient54170 and patient54565, 1 image each). Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other options were the workbook when it is given, and NaN when the 2 files differ.
  • Related: D-06.

docs.title: D-07 Box format
docs.text:
A box is [dim0_min, dim0_max, dim1_min, dim1_max], row first. For a 2-D image this is [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max]. A 3-D box adds dim2_min, dim2_max. The values are fractions in [0, 1] of the size of the image file that image_path points to. Each min is less than its max. bbox_labels has one label for each box, in the same order.

A harmonizer clips each box to the image. It drops a box with no area left, with its bbox_labels and bbox_findings entries. Examples: a source box with x1 == x2, or a box past the image edge. It warns with the number of dropped boxes. When a box in ds[i] has a NaN or inf value, the transform raises a ValueError (MONAI wraps it in a RuntimeError).

Why: the first axis of a numpy array is the row. So img[y0:y1, x0:x1] uses the box in its own order.

  • Status: From the code (docs/wiki/get-started/concepts.md, "Box order"). The clip, drop and ValueError rules: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other options were the ValueError rule only, and no written rule.
  • Checked by: J-03, L-015, tests/test_bbox_axis_alignment.py, tests/test_harmonizer_boxes.py (with ::test_chest_imagenome_gold_drops_boxes_with_no_area, ::test_chest_imagenome_silver_drops_boxes_with_no_area, ::test_vindr_cxr_train_box_is_clipped_to_the_image, ::test_clip_boxes_follows_d07 and ::test_every_box_harmonizer_clips_its_boxes), tests/test_padchest_gr.py::test_a_box_past_the_edge_is_clipped_and_a_box_with_no_area_is_dropped, tests/test_ms_cxr.py::test_box_values_are_python_floats_and_survive_a_csv_round_trip, tests/test_transforms.py::test_box_that_is_not_finite_raises and ::test_a_table_read_back_from_csv_gives_the_same_boxes.
  • Notes (value type): MS-CXR boxes hold Python floats since 2026-11-03. Before, they held numpy floats, so a CSV export wrote np.float64(...) text that json.loads cannot read (V-H2-35).
  • Labels with no class in the source: RSNA 2022 cervical spine boxes get the label fracture, one for each box. The source CSV marks fracture boxes, but it gives no class or vertebra. Decided (Frank Li confirmed on 2026-11-02 the choice of the agent of 2026-11-01, V-H3-23). The other option was no bbox_labels column.
  • Notes: a real run on 2026-10-30 checked the readable box datasets. Chest ImaGenome dropped 1,528 of the silver train boxes and 6 of the gold boxes. The other 8 datasets had no box outside [0, 1], with no area or not finite. The VinDr-CXR train clip moves 3 boxes that start outside the image (since 2026-10-30, D-36). On 2026-11-02, NODE21, ChestX-Det10 and VinDr-PCXR became readable. All their source boxes are inside [0, 1], with an area, and finite. They are 1,476 boxes in NODE21, 8,339 in ChestX-Det10 and 6,171 in VinDr-PCXR. Each image has one label per box. PadChest-GR is still restricted, and RSNA Pneumonia (adjudicated) is not on the NAS.
  • PadChest-GR extra boxes (extra_bbox): the same clip and drop rule as bbox. Decided (Frank Li confirmed on 2026-11-02 the choice of the agent of 2026-11-01, R-code-17). The other option was no check, because the extra boxes do not reach ds[i].
  • keep_negatives=False of NODE21 and ChestX-Det10 drops the images with no finding in the source. An image keeps its row when the clip step drops its only box.
  • A finding on a region with no box: the harmonizer keeps it out of the boxes and warns with the count. The dataset wiki page says so. Example: Chest ImaGenome gold has 227 positive findings (181 images) on the region "mediastinum", but its gold box file has only "upper mediastinum". Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-02, Q-8 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were the "upper mediastinum" box, a column for findings with no box, and to leave the question open. Checked by: tests/test_chest_imagenome.py::test_gold_warns_about_findings_on_a_region_with_no_box (since 2026-11-03).
  • Inverted source box (a min greater than its max): the harmonizer drops it with the warning above. It does not swap the corners. Example: 22 of the 25,989 Chest ImaGenome gold boxes are inverted. Their median IoU with the automatic box of the same region is 0.0, and the normal boxes give 1.0. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-02, Q-9 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were to keep the swap, and to drop only the boxes far from the automatic box. Checked by: tests/test_chest_imagenome.py::test_gold_drops_an_inverted_box_with_the_d07_warning. Since 2026-11-03, the gold table has 25,961 boxes (28 dropped), not 25,983.
  • bbox_labels use snake case in every harmonizer, as the label columns do (D-05). Example: VinDr-PCXR writes Cardiomegaly, but VinDr-CXR writes cardiomegaly. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-02, Q-17 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were the source names on each wiki page, and no rule. The shared step is box_label in radharmony/harmonizer/_bbox.py (lower case, a space gives _, a / stays as in nodule/mass). PadChest-GR joins the snake case labels of one sentence with " + ". Checked by: the box_labels check of tests/fixtures/harmonizer_contract.py (L-008, also on real data in the full run).
  • Notes (Q-17, since 2026-11-03): VinDr-PCXR (Cardiomegaly), MS-CXR (Pleural Effusion), Chest ImaGenome (right lung) and PadChest-GR (vascular redistribution) changed to snake case. The other box harmonizers already wrote snake case. A table saved before 2026-11-03 keeps the old names until harmonize() runs again.
  • A source box that gives no box in the table warns with the count, also when the file of the image cannot be read. Example: VinDr-PCXR with an unreadable DICOM file (R-code-19 of the 2026-10-31 review). Another example is an RSNA 2024 lumbar point on a series that cannot be read (R-code-20). A third is a lumbar point on a second GDCM sub-series of the series folder (V-H3-33). The 3-D loader reads only the first sub-series. Checked by: tests/test_vindr_pcxr.py::test_an_unreadable_dicom_of_a_boxed_image_warns, tests/test_rsna_2024_lumbar_spine.py::test_points_on_a_second_sub_series_warn_with_the_count, ::test_a_series_that_cannot_be_read_warns, and L-020 (no silent except in radharmony/harmonizer/). Notes: a real run of RSNA 2024 lumbar train on 2026-11-03 gave 48,541 boxes. 151 of the 48,692 points are not on the loaded volume. All series were read, so these points are on a second sub-series.
  • No image folder for a box that needs the image size from a DICOM header: the harmonizer warns and gives no box. This is the same as for a file that cannot be read. Example: VinDr-CXR train and test with bbox_csv_path and no base_image_dir. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-H3-35). The other option was a ValueError, as RSNA 2024 lumbar raises. Checked by: tests/test_vindr_cxr.py::test_boxes_with_no_image_folder_warn. A real run gave the same 8,328 train and 2,697 test boxes as before with the folder.
  • RSNA 2022 cervical spine writes bbox and bbox_labels as JSON text, as NODE21 does. So a table saved with to_csv loads back with output_bbox=True (V-H3-34). Before 2026-11-03, a Python list became ['fracture'], which is not JSON. At that time, the fix was in the harmonizer, not in the base parser. Checked by: tests/test_rsna_2022_cervical_spine.py::test_a_table_read_back_from_csv_gives_the_boxes.
  • Notes (since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li): the box step of the transform also reads a Python list text, with ast.literal_eval (never eval). So the table of any box harmonizer, saved with to_csv and read back, works with output_bbox=True (V-D-33). Example: a VinDr-CXR bbox_labels is ['calcification', 'cardiomegaly'] in the CSV. Before, it raised JSONDecodeError. Checked by: tests/test_transforms.py::test_a_table_read_back_from_csv_gives_the_same_boxes.
  • RSNA 2022 cervical bbox_epsilon: the in-plane box comes from the source width and height, so the argument has no effect. A value gives a warning. The argument stays, so a harmonizer saved before 2026-11-03 still loads, with this warning. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-H3-24). The other option was a box of a fixed size from bbox_epsilon. Checked by: tests/test_rsna_2022_cervical_spine.py::test_the_in_plane_box_comes_from_the_source_size.
  • Notes (one clip step): since 2026-11-01, all 15 box harmonizers use clip_boxes or clip_box in radharmony/harmonizer/_bbox.py (R-code-17). Before, Chest ImaGenome and VinDr-CXR train clipped and dropped. SIIM-COVID19, VinDr-PCXR and the RSNA 2022 and 2024 spine harmonizers only clipped, and PadChest-GR raised ValueError. A real run gave the same box columns before and after the change for 11 readable datasets. They are Chest ImaGenome gold and silver, ChestX-ray14, MS-CXR, RAD-ChestCT, RSNA 2022 cervical, RSNA 2024 lumbar, RSNA Pneumonia (Kaggle), SIIM-COVID19, and VinDr-CXR test and train.
  • Related: D-28 (the box in ds[i]).

docs.title: D-36 Boxes of several readers are grouped by overlap
docs.text:
When 2 or more readers draw boxes on one image, the harmonizer groups the boxes of one class that overlap (IoU > 0.5) into one lesion. It keeps a lesion that 2 or more readers drew. The box of the lesion is the mean of the boxes in its group.

Example: VinDr-CXR train, image 03e6ecfa6f6fb33dfeac6ca4f9b459c9, class Nodule/Mass. 3 readers drew 55 boxes (28, 24 and 3). They form 40 groups, and 14 of them have boxes of 2 or more readers. So the table has 14 boxes.

Why: the mean of all boxes of a class is on no real lesion when a reader draws more than 1 box. In VinDr-CXR train this is true for 2,179 of the 9,016 (image, class) pairs. Only in 96 of these 2,179 pairs (4%) is the mean box near a raw box (IoU > 0.5).

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-29), option (c). The other options: (a) all 28,800 raw boxes, (b) weighted boxes fusion with the package ensemble_boxes, (d) no change. Findings: V-H3-4.
  • Checked by: tests/test_harmonizer_boxes.py::test_vindr_cxr_train_groups_the_boxes_of_readers_by_overlap, and tests/test_dataset_stats.py for VinDr-CXR train (8,328 boxes on 4,167 images, from the raw CSV).
  • Notes: the VinDr-CXR test set has 1 agreed set of boxes (no rad_id), so it needs no merge. Weighted boxes fusion also groups boxes by overlap. With human boxes of equal weight, it gives about the same boxes.
  • Related: D-07, D-28.

docs.title: D-08 Save and load give the same table
docs.text:
After h.save(path) and load_from_saved(path), pandas.testing.assert_frame_equal passes on harmonized_df, and LABEL_COLS has the same items in the same order.

Why: a saved harmonizer lets you skip a slow harmonize, so it must not change the data.

  • Status: From the code. The label rule after harmonizer_path= and harmonized_df=: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-02).
  • Checked by: J-02, tests/test_save_load.py (for example test_label_order_is_the_same_after_load and test_no_labels_stay_no_labels_after_load), L-008, and tests/test_dataset_stats.py::test_saved_table_matches_harmonize for the datasets with expected_stats.
  • Dataset load: the dataset class of a key loads its own saved harmonizer with harmonizer_path=. It is not empty, its image paths are in the table, and its label columns are the harmonizer's. Checked by: the harmonizer_path and harmonizer_path_labels checks of tests/fixtures/harmonizer_contract.py, in the full run only (tests/test_dataset_stats.py, L-014). In CI: tests/test_save_load.py (test_dataset_takes_only_the_declared_labels and test_harmonized_df_takes_no_extra_columns_as_labels).
  • Label columns: after harmonizer_path= or harmonizer=, the declared labels of the harmonizer (get_label_cols(), in snake case) that are in the table. The other columns, for example age or bbox_labels, are not labels. With harmonized_df= or set_harmonized_df(), a class with empty LABEL_COLS takes the declared labels of its _HARMONIZER_CLS (in snake case) that are in the table.
  • Notes: Frank Li approved these 2 base-code changes on 2026-11-02. Before them, the dataset class took every column that is not a standard column as a label. Of the 41 real image keys, 16 got wrong label columns after harmonizer_path=, and the 6 TAIX-Ray keys raised an error. With harmonized_df=, 11 of the 12 keys with no declared labels got labels, for example age_months (the regression target) in RSNA Bone Age. The RANZCR test table has no extra columns.
  • Related: D-05, D-24.

docs.title: D-24 harmonized_df equals the last harmonize() result
docs.text:
After df = h.harmonize(), pandas.testing.assert_frame_equal(df, h.harmonized_df) passes. This applies to every harmonizer, including the official split classes. A harmonizer that removes rows (for example, to keep one split) removes them from self.df too. self.df is the source of h.harmonized_df.

Why: save(), harmonizer= and harmonizer_path= read h.harmonized_df. They must give the same rows as harmonize().

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-28).
  • Checked by: tests/test_dataset_stats.py::test_saved_table_matches_harmonize for the datasets with expected_stats, and L-008 (tests/test_harmonizer_contract.py in CI on 11 fake datasets, tests/test_dataset_stats.py::test_harmonizer_contract in the full run). Also tests/test_mrrate.py::test_a_filter_with_no_series_gives_an_empty_harmonized_table. Before 2026-11-03, an MR-RATE filter with no series gave the raw metadata table, and harmonized_df raised KeyError (V-H2-30).
  • Related: D-08, D-09.

docs.title: D-30 A harmonizer changes steps, not harmonize()
docs.text:
A harmonizer overrides only the _build_* steps and a _read_source() step that reads the source files and returns the table. It overrides harmonize() only to take an option (for example drop_uncertain) or to add steps after the base steps. Such an override calls super().harmonize().

Why: when the base harmonize() gets a fix, every harmonizer gets it. A copy of the base steps does not.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-28). The base step _read_source() was approved on 2026-10-29. Its default reads csv_path. Since 2026-11-03 (plan 6b, merges refactor-r1 to r4), every harmonizer uses the base steps. Since 2026-11-03, the VQA base also has its own steps, _read_source() and _build_vqa_columns() (base code approved by Frank Li). 8 classes still override harmonize(), and each calls super().harmonize(). MIMIC-CXR, MIMIC-CXR-JPG, CheXpert Plus and PadChest take drop_uncertain (and, except PadChest, not_mentioned). MIMIC-CXR-JPG test sets the default drop_uncertain=False. CheXpert takes both options and adds a step after. CT-RATE and _KeepSplitMixin add a step after.
  • Split classes: _KeepSplitMixin removes the rows of the other splits in _read_source(), before the base steps. So preprocess_output_dir and sample_n see only the split. Before 2026-11-03, it removed them after harmonize(). Then the image copies held all splits, and sample_n could give 0 rows. Checked by: tests/test_official_splits.py::test_keep_split_mixin_samples_and_copies_only_its_own_split (TAIX-Ray, CheXpert Plus and MS-CXR).
  • Checked by: L-022, tests/test_lessons.py::test_l022_every_harmonize_override_calls_the_base_steps. On 4f7a98e, the commit before the change, it fails and names the 45 classes that copied the base steps (for example BRAX and ChestX-Det10). J-12 checks for other copied code.
  • Notes (image copies of an override): since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li (V-H2-27). A harmonize() override can skip the base one and never call preprocess(). Then, with preprocess_output_dir, _wrap_harmonize runs preprocess() after it. The override makes its masks first, so the masks still come before the image copies (V-H2-21). A sample_n with no preprocess_output_dir gives a warning in such an override. Since 2026-11-03, the base harmonize() also warns (base code approved by Frank Li). Checked by tests/test_harmonizer_preprocess.py::test_base_harmonize_with_only_sample_n_warns_once. Before, such overrides (for example Montgomery, RAD-ChestCT, ReXGradient and RANZCR) ignored preprocess_output_dir, preprocessor and sample_n with no message. A call with none of these arguments does not change. The wrapper reads only keyword arguments. So in an override that skips the base steps, image-copy arguments given by position do nothing, with no message. No warning for this: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-03). L-022 stops such overrides in the package, so only a user's own harmonizer can hit it. Checked by: tests/test_montgomery_cxr.py::test_harmonize_runs_the_preprocessor, the test_own_harmonize_* tests and ::test_ms_cxr_harmonize_runs_the_preprocessor_once in tests/test_harmonizer_preprocess.py.
  • Notes (preprocess output name): since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li, the copy of a/1.png is <preprocess_output_dir>/a/1.png.nii (V-P-22). The name keeps the file ending, so a/1.png and a/1.jpg give 2 files. Before, both wrote a/1.nii. An image_path with a .. part raises ValueError before any file is written, so every copy stays in the output folder. A copy made before 2026-11-03 keeps its old name. Checked by: tests/test_preprocessor.py::test_run_batch_gives_2_files_for_2_images_with_the_same_stem and ::test_a_path_with_dot_dot_raises_and_writes_nothing.
  • Notes (preprocess output): a second harmonize() with preprocess_output_dir writes every file again. It does not skip a file that is already there. The tutorial notebooks/tutorials/dataset_api_tour.ipynb says so since 2026-11-03. Before, it said that a second call is fast (V-H2-38). Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-H2-38). The other option was a skip of the files that exist, a base-code change in radharmony/preprocessor/base.py. A skip can keep an old file after a change of the preprocessor settings.
  • Notes: on 4f7a98e, 45 of 53 overrides copied the base steps (R-code-8). All 45 copied the base reset step (D-24), and 13 copied the base label sort (D-05).
  • Related: D-05.

docs.title: D-09 Official splits are separate classes
docs.text:
When the dataset authors provide an official split, each split has its own harmonizer class and its own dataset class. A class does not take a split= argument and does not mix splits in one table. For example, ChestX-ray14 has ChestXray14TrainDataset and ChestXray14TestDataset. Each official split class gives only its own rows.

An old class or registry key that mixes splits, or takes split=, stays and works as before, so old code still runs. Its docstring and its wiki page say that it mixes splits and is not for benchmarks. The split classes stand beside it.

Why: a benchmark must use the split that the dataset authors published. With one class for each split, a user cannot mix train and test images by mistake.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-28). On the same day, Frank Li decided to keep the old keys as they are.
  • Checked by: tests/test_official_splits.py, tests/test_save_load.py, and for the datasets with expected_stats, tests/test_dataset_stats.py::test_stat_matches_expected (the image count) and tests/test_dataset_stats.py::test_patients_in_two_splits.
  • MIMIC-CXR-JPG test: mimic_cxr_jpg_test stays the test set of mimic-cxr-2.1.0-test-set-labeled.csv (685 studies with a JPG, radiologist labels). A new key mimic_cxr_jpg_test_chexpert gives the test split of mimic-cxr-2.0.0-split.csv (CheXpert-labeler labels), as the DICOM key mimic_cxr_test does. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other option was no new key.
  • Notes (MIMIC-CXR-JPG test): the test split of the split file has 3,269 studies. With the default drop_uncertain=True, mimic_cxr_jpg_test_chexpert gives 2,216 studies, 3,556 images and 287 patients.
  • App: the app lists the split keys only. A dataset with official splits gets one entry for each split, and the old mixed keys leave the app. They still work in code. A dataset with no official split keeps its one key. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-25 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other options were every registry key, and no rule. Exception: Emory CXR DICOM (emory_cxr_dicom) stays out of the app. The PNG entry shows the same images. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-01, A-17). The other option was its own entry. Checked by: tests/test_app.py::test_app_lists_the_split_keys_and_every_dataset. It reads the old keys from the inventory in docs/wiki/reference/datasets/index.md. Before 2026-11-02, the app had 17 old mixed entries, for example MIMIC-CXR, TAIX-Ray and CT-RATE, and no entry for mimic_cxr_jpg_test_chexpert (Q-25, A-17).
  • Known gaps:
  • MR-RATE has split harmonizers, but no dataset class and no registry key (no ID). Its data is restricted, so a user with access must build and check it.
  • Old saved files: a split class loads a file that the old class saved only when every row is in its own split. Otherwise it raises ValueError with the file name and the split. Example: ChestXDet10TrainDataset(harmonizer_path=<a test file>) raises. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other option was to keep the rows of its own split, which gives 0 rows for a wrong file.
  • Source file of another split: when the file name picks the split, a split class raises ValueError for the file of another split. Examples: RAD-ChestCT img<split>_...csv, and ReXGradient <split>_metadata_view_position.json (since 2026-11-03, V-H2-46). Before, ReXGradientTestHarmonizer with the train JSON gave the 238,968 train rows. Checked by: tests/test_official_splits.py::test_rexgradient_split_class_rejects_the_json_of_another_split.
  • Notes: 5 split classes load old files (_LoadOldFileMixin). An old file never mixes splits. For 3 of them, the old class gives the same table as the split class. A run on 2026-10-30 gave 10,675 rows for SIIM-ACR train, 6,334 for SIIM-COVID19 train and 26,684 for RSNA Pneumonia Kaggle train. The old ChestXDet10 class saves 1 split.
  • Notes (since 2026-11-03, V-H1-49): the 3 Chest ImaGenome silver split classes and the 2 CheXphoto split classes also load old files. Before, they raised ValueError for a file of their own split. The CheXphoto table has no split column, so the saved csv_path names the split (train.csv or valid.csv). Checked by: tests/test_chexphoto.py::test_valid_class_loads_a_valid_file_of_the_old_class and tests/test_chest_imagenome.py::test_silver_split_class_loads_a_file_of_the_old_class.
  • MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA: 3 split keys since 2026-11-01 (V-H1-29), with the split of each patient from patient_metadata.parquet. A split class keeps its own patients before the max_studies cut, so max_studies counts the studies of its split. Decided (Frank Li confirmed on 2026-11-02 the choice of the agent of 2026-11-01). The other option was the cut first, as _KeepSplitMixin does. Then the first 20 studies of the q1M export give 0 test rows. Checked by: tests/test_harmonizer_id_filter.py::test_mimic_ext_qba_split_classes_keep_one_split.
  • Related: D-24, D-25, D-34.

docs.title: D-25 Images with no labels go in a separate test class
docs.text:
D-09 also applies to a split that has no labels. A harmonizer with label columns gives only the rows that the authors labeled. Images that the authors give without labels (for example, a Kaggle test set) go in a separate test class. The test harmonizer has LABEL_COLS = [], and the test dataset class does not give cls. Examples: RSNAPneumoniaKaggleTestHarmonizer, SIIMACRPTXTestHarmonizer and SIIMCOVID19TestHarmonizer.

Why: an unlabeled row in a labeled table can go into train or validation with NaN labels.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-28).
  • Checked by: tests/test_official_splits.py::test_ranzcr_split_classes and tests/test_official_splits.py::test_rsna_bone_age_test_images_have_no_labels.
  • Images with no label row: the label merge leaves them out, and the harmonizer warns with the count. MIMIC-CXR and MIMIC-CXR-JPG share warn_images_without_labels in radharmony/harmonizer/_labels.py. Example: 15 train images in 8 studies have no row in mimic-cxr-2.0.0-chexpert.csv. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-H1-32). The other option was no warning. Notes: before 2026-11-03, only the JPG class warned. Checked by: tests/test_mimic_cxr.py::test_mimic_cxr_dicom_warns_about_images_without_labels and tests/test_harmonizer_data.py::test_mimic_cxr_jpg_warns_about_images_without_labels.
  • Notes:
  • The old key ranzcr_clip still adds the 3,582 unlabeled test images by default (include_test_split=True). D-09 keeps old keys as they are. With output_cls=True, it raises a ValueError (V-H2-25).
  • Kaggle gives only a few sample test files for 2 competitions, so their test classes cannot load the full test set. rsna_abdominal_trauma_2023_test: test_series_meta.csv lists 6 series, but test_images/ has only 3 of them, with 1 slice each. rsna_2022_cervical_spine_test: the 3 studies in test.csv (10197, 10454, 10690) are not in the 3 image folders (22327, 25399, 5876).
