So the class has 3 rows, and ds[0] raises RuntimeError, because no image file exists (checked on 2026-11-04).
  • Kaggle code competitions: rsna_abdominal_trauma_2023_test and rsna_2022_cervical_spine_test stay. Their docstrings and wiki pages say that the public download has only sample test files. Each class is for a Kaggle notebook of the competition, where the hidden test set has the same layout. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other options were to remove both, and a FileNotFoundError when the images are not on disk.
  • Related: D-09.

docs.title: D-10 Our own splits group by patient
docs.text:
get_datasets() and get_folds() split on patient_id, not on rows. All images of one patient are in one split. The split is not stratified by label. A split with no patient raises ValueError. The message names n_splits and the number of patients.

Why: images of one patient in train and test make the test score too high. An empty split always means a wrong call.

  • Status: From the code (docs/wiki/get-started/concepts.md, "Splits"). The empty-split rule: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-21 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other options were a warning, and no check.
  • Checked by: J-02.
  • Checked by (empty split): tests/test_dataset.py::test_an_empty_split_raises and ::test_a_fold_with_no_patient_raises. Before 2026-11-01, split_data and kfold_splits gave an empty split with no error (Q-21). Examples: n_splits=1, and 3 patients with n_splits=10.
  • Related: D-09, D-32.

docs.title: D-34 Official splits stay as published, also when they share patients
docs.text:
A split class gives its split as the authors published it, also when the splits share patients. The class docstring and the wiki page say how many patients the splits share. A user who needs splits with no shared patient removes them in their own code.

Examples:

  • VQA-RAD: 202 of the 203 test images also have train questions. The paper made the test set this way.
  • CheXinstruct VQA: the 2 sources made their splits on their own. The train, val and test splits share 2,007 patients. 497 of the 734 test patients are also in train.
  • MIMIC-CXR-JPG: 3 patients (9 studies, 94 images) of the official validate split are also in the labeled test set of version 2.1.0 (mimic_cxr_jpg_test).

Why: a benchmark must use the split that the authors published (D-09), so that a score can be compared with published scores. A shared patient is a fact of the dataset, so the docs must say it. A score on such a test split can be too high.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-29), option (a). Frank Li chose it over (b), remove the test patients from train and validation in every dataset, and (c), a choice for each dataset.
  • Checked by: tests/test_dataset_stats.py::test_patients_in_two_splits.
  • Notes: since 2026-10-30, mimic_cxr_jpg_validate keeps the 3 patients (62 images in 43 studies after the label filter). Before, it removed them. The MIMIC-CXR DICOM classes follow the official split file, which has no shared patient. No stored result uses the VQA-RAD or CheXinstruct VQA splits.
  • QaTa-COV19 copies: the table keeps one patient_id for each picture (the file stem). The wiki page warns that 2 copies of one picture can have 2 IDs, so they can land in train and val (D-10). It also says that 1 test picture is the same as a train picture. Example: 37 train pairs are near copies under 2 IDs (not pixel-equal), and test sub-S09512 equals train covid_4134 (correlation 0.9999). Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-02, Q-16 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were to group the copies as one patient, and to drop the test picture that is in train.
  • Notes (QaTa-COV19): since 2026-11-03, the wiki page and the 2 docstrings give the copies and the shared test picture. Before, they said that the splits have zero overlap (Q-16).
  • Related: D-09, D-18.

docs.title: D-11 Output flags
docs.text:
ds[i] always has img. Each output_* flag adds only its own keys:

Flag Keys output_cls cls output_mask mask output_bbox bbox, bbox_labels, and bbox_findings if the class supports it output_report report output_reg reg

Only output_mask, output_report and the MS-CXR-T output_previous can also remove rows (D-33). If a class does not support a flag, it gives a warning and does not return the key. It does not raise an error and does not return wrong data.

Why: the same code can request the same outputs from every dataset.

  • Status: From the code (SUPPORTED_OUTPUTS in radharmony/dataset/base.py).
  • Checked by:
  • L-010: tests/test_output_flags.py in CI (all 5 flags since 2026-10-30), and tests/test_dataset_stats.py::test_output_flag_on_a_real_sample in the full run.
  • tests/test_integrity.py::test_requested_output_that_no_sample_has_warns: check_dataset warns when no sample has a requested key.
  • tests/test_output_flags.py::test_a_class_that_supports_reg_names_its_reg_columns.
  • L-013: tests/test_output_flags.py::test_output_bbox_keeps_every_key_of_the_flag. With output_bbox=True, the default transform keeps bbox, bbox_labels and bbox_findings (where supported).
  • The app: tests/test_app.py::test_bbox_checkbox_follows_the_build_default.
  • output_reg: every image key takes it, as the other 4 flags. A dataset with no regression target gives the warning and no reg key. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other option was output_reg only for RSNA Bone Age, with TypeError elsewhere.
  • VQA and caption classes (BaseVQADataset, 21 keys): the 5 flags are for image dataset classes only. A VQA sample has its own keys (question and answer), so a VQA class raises TypeError for these flags. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-24 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other option was to accept the flags with a warning (a base-code change in base_vqa.py).
  • A transform of the user: when a given transform ends with SelectItemsD and drops the key of a flag that the class supports, __init__ warns. Example: output_report=True with RadiologyTransform2D().get_transform(), which keeps only cls and img. No image is loaded for the check. Before, the samples had no report key and there was no message. Base code in radharmony/dataset/base.py, approved by Frank Li on 2026-11-04. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04, found in the 6c rewrite of the how-to pages). The other options were a ValueError, and no change. Checked by: tests/test_output_flags.py::test_a_transform_that_drops_a_requested_key_warns_at_once.
  • VQA output_struct and output_question_type: when the table has no answer_struct or question_type column, get_datasets and get_folds warn once, and the samples have no such key. Example: ROCO, MedPMC and VQA-RAD with output_struct=True. Before, there was no warning. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04). The other options were a ValueError, and no change. Checked by: tests/test_vqa_base.py::test_output_flag_with_no_column_warns_and_adds_no_key.
  • App VQA rows: the app shows the same sample as the VQA dataset class, one row for each question. A row shows only its own question and answer. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-3 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other options were one row for each image with all its questions, and a message with the image count. Checked by: tests/test_app.py::test_gemex_row_shows_only_its_own_question and ::test_vqa_adapter_gives_one_row_per_question. Before 2026-11-02, a GEMeX VQA row showed all questions of its image (Q-3), and so did VQA-RAD, CheXinstruct and MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA. Real data: 80 GEMeX rows and 451 VQA-RAD test rows, each with 1 question now.
  • App: when the user picks a dataset, the "BBox" checkbox takes the output_bbox default of the _build_* function of that dataset in app.py. It is on for NODE21, ChestX-Det10, PadChest-GR and Chest ImaGenome (gold and silver), and off for the others. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, V-A-13). The other options were "BBox" off with a hint in the load message, and no change.
  • MS-CXR-T output_previous: the sample also has previous_img, the prior-visit image. It goes through the same transform as img in a second call, so a random step (for example a flip) draws again for it. Decided (Frank Li confirmed on 2026-11-02 the choice of the agent of 2026-11-01, V-D-31). The other option was one random draw for both images, which needs a base-code change (the base load steps name only img). A row with no previous_image_path is dropped, because a pair needs both images. Only a user table can have such a row, because the harmonizer always gives the path. Decided (Frank Li confirmed on 2026-11-02 the choice of the agent). Checked by: tests/test_output_flags.py::test_ms_cxr_t_previous_image_reaches_the_sample, ::test_ms_cxr_t_previous_image_gets_its_own_random_draw_in_a_worker and ::test_ms_cxr_t_previous_image_needs_its_column.
  • A flag that a class supports, with no data in the table: the class warns and leaves out the keys. This is the same as for a flag that it does not support. Example: RSNA 2024 lumbar with output_bbox=True and no point CSV (no bbox column) gives no bbox and no bbox_labels. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-D-40). The other option was an empty (0, 6) box. At that time, the 3-D box step of the base transform failed on an empty box (fixed on 2026-11-03, V-D-41). Before, the warning promised empty boxes, and ds[0] raised KeyError bbox. Checked by: tests/test_rsna_2024_lumbar_spine.py::test_output_bbox_with_no_point_csv_leaves_out_the_box_keys.
  • Notes: on 2026-10-30, output_reg was added to 49 __init__ methods in 48 dataset files. BRAX now lists only cls in SUPPORTED_OUTPUTS, so output_reg=True gives a warning, not an empty reg.
  • Related: D-33.

docs.title: D-33 An empty mask_path means "not annotated"
docs.text:
An empty mask_path (NaN or "") means that nobody drew a mask for this image. An annotated image with no finding gets an all-zero mask, not an empty mask_path. With output_mask=True, the dataset class drops the rows that are not annotated. It warns with the number of dropped rows. A blank or NaN image_path always drops the row, because the row has no file (V-P-23, checked by tests/test_dataset_outputs.py::test_blank_image_path_drops_the_row).

Why: if an empty mask_path also meant "no finding", output_mask=True drops every negative image. Then the segmentation result is biased. The warning tells the user why the dataset is smaller.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-28).
  • Checked by: tests/test_harmonizer_preprocess.py::test_preprocess_masks_writes_zero_mask_for_annotated_image_with_no_finding, ::test_preprocess_masks_skips_image_that_nobody_annotated, and tests/test_dataset_outputs.py::test_requested_mask_drops_rows_with_no_mask_and_warns, ::test_requested_report_drops_rows_with_no_report_and_warns, ::test_output_not_requested_keeps_every_row and tests/test_harmonizer_preprocess.py::test_shenzhen_tb_image_with_no_mask_file_is_not_annotated.
  • Reports: with output_report=True, the dataset class also drops a row with no report (NaN or ""). It warns with the number of dropped rows. Example: PadChest then has 157,590 of 157,607 rows. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, V-D-9). The other options were "" for a missing report, and NaN with a doc line.
  • Placeholder reports: a text that only says that there is no report counts as no report (NaN). Examples: the Emory CXR blank template (D-03) and the Montgomery text "NO REPORT (same pt as MCUCXR_0162_1)". Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-16 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other option was to keep the text. Checked by: tests/test_harmonizer_data.py::test_montgomery_placeholder_is_no_report (since 2026-11-01).
  • Labeled negatives: an image whose labels say "no finding" for every masked finding is annotated, also when the release has no mask file for it. It gets an all-zero mask. Example: CheXlocalize drew masks only for positive findings, so its images with all 10 labels negative are labeled negatives. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-10 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other option was an empty mask_path for them. Checked by: tests/test_official_splits.py::test_chexlocalize_labeled_negative_gets_an_all_zero_mask (since 2026-11-01).
  • Box findings: when the source annotates the findings of only some images, a bool column findings_annotated tells the annotated images. An empty bbox_findings entry of an image that is not annotated means "not annotated", not "no finding". Example: the Chest ImaGenome gold attribute file has only 500 of the 1,000 images. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-H1-14). The other options were NaN in bbox_findings, which breaks the list of strings in ds[i], and a wiki line only. Checked by: tests/test_chest_imagenome.py::test_gold_tells_an_image_with_no_finding_annotation_from_no_finding.
  • Known gaps:
  • MR-RATE mask_source="nvseg-brain" gives paths to files that exist only for some series (no ID).
  • Notes: since 2026-10-30, the 13 TB-positive Shenzhen images with no finding mask have an empty mask_path. Since 2026-10-29, the base preprocess_masks writes no mask for an image that nobody annotated (V-H2-4). RANZCR CLiP train with output_mask=True has 9,095 images, not 30,083. CheXlocalize has 667 of 668 test rows and 234 of 234 val rows since 2026-11-01 (Q-10). Before, its 168 test and 47 val labeled negatives had no mask. SIIM-ACR (the RLE -1 gives an all-zero mask), MedSeg, QaTa-COV19, Montgomery and RSNA 2022 cervical spine follow this decision (checked on 2026-10-28).
  • Notes (reports): a real run on 2026-10-30 counted the rows with no report. PadChest had 17. MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert Plus, ReXGradient, Emory CXR, Montgomery and Shenzhen had 0. Open-I had 40 rows (25 studies), counted on 2026-11-02 when its folder became readable. Since the D-03 fix, 7 Emory CXR rows (3 studies with only a blank template) have no report.
  • Related: D-11.

docs.title: D-28 The box in a sample matches the image in that sample
docs.text:
In ds[i], the box always matches ds[i]["img"]. Every resize, pad, crop, flip and warp of the image moves the box in the same way. The box keeps the format of D-07, as fractions of the returned image. A sample box is an (N, 4) (2-D) or (N, 6) (3-D) float32 tensor, and (0, 4) or (0, 6) when there is no box.

Example: a 2,000 × 1,000 (H × W) image is resized to 512 × 256. Then it is padded equally on the left and right to 512 × 512. A box with x_min = 0.0 in the table must have x_min = 0.25 in ds[i].

Why: a model and a metric use the box together with the returned image, not with the source file.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-28). Method: exact math on the box corners for resize, pad, crop, the with_spacing resample (since 2026-11-03), flip and transpose. Only the affine and elastic augmentations use the mask round trip. The change to radharmony/dataset/transforms.py (base code) was approved by Frank Li on 2026-10-28. A warning for the encoder box (the known gap below) until a detection evaluator needs it: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31). The other options were exact math now, an error, and no warning.
  • Checked by: J-03, L-011 (tests/test_lessons.py::test_l011_box_stays_on_the_white_rectangle), tests/test_transforms.py, tests/test_dataset.py::test_visualize_samples_draws_every_box, tests/test_encoder_transforms.py::test_encoder_transform_box_is_float32_with_4_columns, ::test_encoder_transform_warns_that_the_box_does_not_follow_the_processor and ::test_encoder_transform_gives_no_box_warning, tests/test_transforms.py::test_an_error_in_the_3d_box_step_is_not_hidden and ::test_a_3d_sample_with_no_box_gives_an_empty_box, L-018 (tests/test_lessons.py::test_l018_3d_box_stays_on_its_cube).
  • Known gaps: RadiologyEncoderTransform does not move the box with the crop or pad of the encoder processor (no ID). It warns when bbox is in output_keys and the processor crops or pads. A custom preprocess with no processor= also warns, because its steps are unknown. A processor that only resizes keeps the box fractions, so it gives no warning. Example: the MedSigLIP recipe gives no warning, and the RAD-DINO and EVA-X recipes warn.
  • Notes: since 2026-10-30, the box of RadiologyEncoderTransform is a float32 (N, 4) tensor, also for no box. Before, it was bfloat16 with shape (0,) for no box, and a JSON string box stayed a string. Since 2026-11-02 (base code approved by Frank Li), an error in the 3-D box step _ReorientBbox stops the run. Before, except Exception: pass hid it, so the image turned and the box kept its old axes (R-code-18). On real cervical spine, lumbar spine and RAD-ChestCT samples, that except caught no error. Since 2026-11-03 (base code approved by Frank Li), a 3-D row with no box gives a (0, 6) box (V-D-41). Before, _ReorientBbox raised IndexError on it. Example: a lumbar series with no labeled point stopped the run. Since 2026-11-03 (base code approved by Frank Li), the box moves with the resample of with_spacing (pixdim) with exact math on its corners (V-D-42). Before, the box kept its fractions, but the output covers a different area than the input. Example: 15 slices of 4 mm resampled to 1 mm put the box 1.2 voxels off the object.
  • Related: D-07, D-12, D-43.

docs.title: D-12 3-D orientation
docs.text:
When base_transpose=True (the default), every 3-D volume is reoriented to the axis code in axcodes (default IPL). Then it is transposed to (D, H, W). The box goes through the same 2 steps. The 2 steps always stay together.

Why: scanners save volumes in different orientations. One orientation makes the box order of D-07 true for every volume.

  • Status: Decided (Judy, 2026-04-26, docs/proposals/orientation_normalization.md).
  • Checked by: J-03.
  • RAD-ChestCT: its .npz arrays have no orientation data, but they are already IPL in (D, H, W) order. The box columns name the axes (sup_axis0min/inf_axis0max, ant_axis1min/pos_axis1max, rig_axis2min/lef_axis2max). So the class passes base_transpose=False, and the image and the box still follow this rule. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31). The other options were code that gives the arrays an orientation, and a known gap with no change.
  • 2-D slices of a 3-D volume are in the usual axial view. Rows go from anterior to posterior. Columns go from patient right to patient left. The mask gets the same step. Example: before 2026-11-03, a MedSeg COVID CT slice was vol[:, :, k] in NIfTI array order, which is the transpose of this view. Now it is vol[:, :, k].T. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-02, Q-11 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were the array order with a wiki line, and a reorientation with the affine.
  • Notes (MedSeg, since 2026-11-03): the slices are in this view, and their folder name has the HU window, for example dataset1_hu-1000_400. Before, a new window used the old PNGs (V-H1-42). Checked by: tests/test_harmonizer_data.py::test_medseg_slices_use_the_usual_axial_view and ::test_medseg_new_hu_window_writes_new_slices.
  • Related: D-07, D-28.

docs.title: D-43 A resample keeps the image centered
docs.text:
A resample to a new voxel spacing covers the same physical area as the input. So the output origin moves by (new spacing - old spacing) / 2 along each axis. This is the usual way to resample with SimpleITK.

Example: an input of 1,000 pixels at 1 mm covers x = -0.5 to 999.5 mm. At 9 mm, the output must cover the same area, not -4.5 to 995.5 mm.

Why: a box stored as fractions of the image (D-07) assumes that the output covers the same area as the input.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-20 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other options were a docstring line about a shift of up to half a pixel, and no change.
  • Checked by: tests/test_preprocessor.py::test_resample_keeps_the_image_centered.
  • Notes: Frank Li approved the base-code change on 2026-11-02 (Q-20). Before it, _resize_isotropic in radharmony/preprocessor/base.py kept the input origin, so the content moved by up to half an output pixel. In the example above, it moved by 4.0 mm. The fix moves the origin in the image direction, so it also works for an oblique 3-D image. It changes CXRPreprocessor and CTPreprocessor output written after 2026-11-02. No dataset class uses them.
  • CT axes (V-P-25, V-P-26): CTPreprocessor first turns the volume to LPS. Then the crop and the resize take L-R and A-P as the axial plane, for a coronal or sagittal volume too. Then it turns the volume to orientation. Before, the long side could land on S-I. A bad orientation code (for example "LIX") raises ValueError. Before, it gave LPS output with no error. Checked by tests/test_preprocessor.py::test_ct_long_side_is_axial_for_a_sagittal_volume and ::test_ct_orientation_with_a_bad_code_raises. No change in radharmony/preprocessor/base.py.
  • Known gaps: with_spacing (MONAI SpacingD) keeps the first voxel center, so its output is not centered (no ID). Since 2026-11-03 (base code approved by Frank Li), the box moves with it (D-28, V-D-42).
  • Related: D-07, D-12, D-28.

docs.title: D-13 CXR pixel values
docs.text:
Every CXR that a dataset class gives has bright bone. A MONOCHROME1 DICOM is inverted one time.

Why: a model must see the same contrast from every dataset.

  • Status: From the code. The inversion by GDCM, with the pydicom test as a guard: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31). The other options were a run-time check in base code and a known gap with no change.
  • Checked by: tests/test_preprocessor.py (the CXRPreprocessor path), tests/test_dataset.py::test_dataset_load_of_signed_monochrome1_dicom_with_window, ::test_dataset_load_uses_the_window_for_any_dicom_file_name and ::test_dataset_load_does_not_read_an_mha_copy_with_pydicom (the dataset load). tests/test_encoder_transforms.py::test_monai_reader_applies_the_dicom_window, ::test_monai_reader_reads_a_palette_png_as_shown and ::test_monai_reader_drops_the_alpha_channel (reader="monai"). ::test_recipe_image_loader_reads_palette_and_alpha_pngs_as_shown (the backbone recipes). ::test_palette_loader_picks_the_reader_by_file_suffix, ::test_palette_loader_gives_a_new_cache_key and L-012 (both).
  • Notes: GDCM in the ITK reader inverts MONOCHROME1, and the dataset load has no inversion step of its own. test_dataset_load_of_signed_monochrome1_dicom_with_window fails if GDCM stops the inversion. Its expected values come from pydicom, not from GDCM. The dataset load and CXRPreprocessor take the GDCM maximum M from one helper, stored_value_sum in radharmony/utils/dicom.py. M is -1 for signed values. Both find a DICOM file by the tag 0028|0004 in the image information, not by its file name (is_dicom in the same file). An .mha, .nrrd or NIfTI copy of a DICOM file keeps this tag, so these endings are not DICOM. The base _fix_monochrome and the unused _convert_monochrome1_to_2 were removed. All 3 changes are from 2026-10-29 (approved by Frank Li). A second inversion gave a negative image (V-P-1). Since 2026-10-30, reader="monai" of the encoder transforms runs the 2 DICOM steps of the dataset load (_fix_missing_highbit and _apply_voi_lut). Since 2026-10-31, reader="monai" and the backbone recipes read a palette PNG as the colors it shows, not as its raw index. Before, 334 of the 662 Shenzhen PNGs were inverted (V-B-11, V-P-19). A palette or RGBA PNG becomes RGB, and an LA PNG becomes gray. The mask loaders of the recipes keep mt.LoadImage, because a palette mask keeps its class numbers in the index. CXRPreprocessor also reads an LA PNG as gray (it falls back to PIL, because SimpleITK cannot read it, V-P-27). Checked by tests/test_preprocessor.py::test_cxr_reads_a_gray_plus_alpha_png.
  • Notes (a window only for MONOCHROME): the DICOM standard applies a VOI window only to a MONOCHROME1 or MONOCHROME2 image. So _apply_voi_lut skips an image of another type, for example RGB, as CXRPreprocessor does. Since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li (V-P-21, V-P-24). Before, an RGB DICOM with window tags raised a ValueError in the dataset load, in reader="monai" and in the recipe loaders (_display_255). Now an 8-bit RGB DICOM with window tags gives its 3 channels as they are, as with no window tags (D-27). The tests use only a synthetic file. We found no real RGB DICOM with window tags. The code of _apply_voi_lut is in the cache key (D-15). So each 2-D cache_dir builds a new cache once. An embedding_cache file from before 2026-11-03 raises ValueError (D-41). The samples of a MONOCHROME image are the same. Checked by tests/test_transforms.py::test_an_rgb_dicom_skips_the_window_in_the_dataset_load and tests/test_encoder_transforms.py::test_an_rgb_dicom_skips_the_window_and_stays_as_it_is.
  • Notes (HighBit step): since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li. _fix_missing_highbit in radharmony/dataset/base.py skips a color DICOM (more than 1 sample per pixel), as CXRPreprocessor does. Before, an RGB DICOM with no HighBit tag crashed the load. The code of the step is in the cache key (D-15). So each 2-D cache_dir builds a new cache once, and an older embedding_cache file raises ValueError (D-41). Checked by tests/test_dataset.py::test_highbit_step_skips_a_color_dicom.
  • Related: D-14, D-27.

docs.title: D-14 Pixel value range
docs.text:
• A 2-D image is scaled to [-1, 1] with the 0.5 and 99.5 percentiles of that image, and clipped to that range.
  • A 3-D volume is clipped to its hu_window when the dataset sets one.

Why: every dataset gives the same value range to the next step.

  • Status: From the code (radharmony/dataset/transforms.py).
  • Checked by: tests/test_preprocessor.py::test_uniform_image_gives_minus_one_not_nan (a uniform image only).
  • Masks: with RadiologyTransform2D, a 2-D mask in ds[i] holds 0 and 1. The transform maps a value above 0 to 1, so mask files with 0 and 255 on disk also give 0 and 1. All 2-D masks have 1 class today. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30), with the base-code change in radharmony/dataset/transforms.py. The other options were 0/1 mask files from the harmonizers, and no change. Checked by tests/test_transforms.py::test_2d_mask_file_with_255_gives_0_and_1.
  • Masks in the segmentation probes: the probes also take masks from other sources. In a binary mask (num_classes=2), any value above 0 is foreground, for example 1 or 255. A mask with K > 2 classes (K = num_classes) holds the class indices 0 to K-1. A value above K-1 raises a ValueError. The probe turns a one-hot mask into indices with argmax. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, V-E-6). The other option was a map of the sorted mask values to 0 to K-1. Checked by tests/test_evaluator.py::test_seg_index_mask_targets_do_not_depend_on_the_batch. Before 2026-11-03, the binary probe divided the mask by the batch maximum. So 0, 1 and 2 gave 0, 0 and 1 (V-E-32).
  • Notes: before 2026-10-30, Montgomery, Shenzhen, SIIM-ACR, CheXlocalize, QaTa-COV19 and the MedSeg slices gave 0 and 255 in ds[i] (V-D-10). The segmentation probes take any value above 0 as foreground, so no stored result is wrong. A backbone transform (RadiologyEncoderTransform) keeps the mask values of the file. So a mask with more classes still works there (V-E-6).
  • Related: D-27.

docs.title: D-42 One channel count for each dataset
docs.text:
Every ds[i]["img"] of one 2-D dataset has the same number of channels. A gray modality (CXR, CT slices) gives 1 channel: an RGB or RGBA file of a gray image becomes gray. A dataset with color figures (MedPMC, ROCO, ROCOv2, VQA-RAD) gives 3 channels: a gray file is repeated to 3 channels. The dataset class sets the count.

Example: ChestX-ray14 has a few RGBA PNGs. Each gives (1, 224, 224), as the gray PNGs do, so a default DataLoader batch works.

Why: a batch needs one shape, and a model for one modality expects one channel count.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-5 and V-D-27 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other options were 1 channel for every image (color figures lose their color), and the channels of the file with a doc line.
  • Checked by: tests/test_transforms.py (test_a_gray_dataset_gives_1_channel_for_any_png, test_a_color_dataset_repeats_a_gray_png_to_3_channels, test_the_channel_count_is_in_the_cache_key and test_the_vqa_datasets_set_their_channel_count).
  • Channel step: the step _SetChannelsD of _base_load_2d drops an alpha channel. With 1 channel, RGB becomes gray with the weights of PIL convert("L"), or channel 0 if R = G = B. RadiologyTransform2D(channels=...) and the class attribute IMG_CHANNELS of the VQA datasets set the count. MedPMC, ROCO, ROCOv2 and VQA-RAD set 3.
  • Notes: Frank Li approved this base-code change on 2026-11-02 (V-D-27). Before it, _base_load_2d kept the channels of the file. ChestX-ray14 gave (4, 224, 224) for 15 of 3,000 sampled train rows, and MedPMC mixed 1 and 3 channels, so a default batch failed. The RGBA ChestX-ray14 files are gray images (R = G = B, alpha 255), so they keep their gray values. A 1-channel file gives the same tensor as before. The new step is in the cached steps, so each cache_dir builds a new cache once. An embedding_cache file from before 2026-11-02 raises ValueError (D-41).
  • Related: D-13, D-14, D-27.

docs.title: D-27 A reader never clips pixel values
docs.text:
A reader is the step that opens the image file. A reader never clips pixel values. Later transform steps can clip (D-14).

Some readers must give an 8-bit image, for example reader="pil" for a Hugging Face processor. Such a reader scales a 16-bit image to 0 to 255 with the minimum and maximum of that image. Then it converts the image to RGB. An 8-bit image stays as it is.

The VOI window of a DICOM file (D-13) is not a clip by the reader. It is the display step that the file defines. The dataset load and reader="monai" apply it to a MONOCHROME image after the file is read.

Why: clipping makes most pixels of a 16-bit CXR white. Scaling with the minimum and maximum of each image also works for a 12-bit image that is stored in a 16-bit file. Division by 257 makes such an image very dark.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-28).
  • Checked by: tests/test_encoder_transforms.py (with ::test_recipe_loader_keeps_an_8_bit_png, ::test_recipe_loader_applies_the_dicom_window, ::test_every_recipe_image_loader_has_the_display_step and ::test_an_rgb_dicom_skips_the_window_and_stays_as_it_is).
  • Notes: since 2026-11-01, the image loader of every backbone recipe follows this rule, with display_255 in backbones/_utils.py. Before, it stretched every image with its minimum and maximum, also an 8-bit image, and it skipped the DICOM window (V-B-12). A real run gave the same RAD-DINO input as reader="monai" for 40 VinDr-CXR DICOMs, 40 SIIM-ACR DICOMs and 30 ChestX-ray14 PNGs.
  • Related: D-13, D-14.

docs.title: D-15 Cache before augmentation
docs.text:
cache_dir stores the loaded and preprocessed tensors, before augmentation. Augmentation runs again for each sample. Each cache folder name has a short key of the cached steps (_transform_key in radharmony/dataset/base.py). So a new load or preprocessing step, for example a new img_size or reader, builds a new cache. A new setting of an augmentation, for example the flip strength, does not, because the augmentation runs after the cache.

Why: augmentation must be random each time, and loading is slow.

  • Status: From the code (MONAI PersistentDataset in radharmony/dataset/base.py). The transform key: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-29, V-D-8). The code in the key: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-02, V-D-37).
  • Checked by: tests/test_dataset.py::test_a_new_image_size_does_not_read_the_old_cache, ::test_the_same_settings_reuse_the_cache_and_augmentation_is_not_in_the_key, ::test_the_transform_key_is_the_same_in_a_new_process, ::test_the_transform_key_has_the_reader_and_takes_a_list, ::test_the_transform_key_ignores_the_train_mode_and_takes_any_tensor, ::test_the_3d_cache_holds_the_preprocessed_volume, ::test_the_transform_key_has_the_code_of_a_function_step, ::test_the_transform_key_has_the_code_of_a_radharmony_step, ::test_the_code_in_the_transform_key_is_the_same_for_any_hash_seed, tests/test_dataset_outputs.py::test_augmentation_differs_across_workers_and_epochs, ::test_torch_manual_seed_repeats_the_augmentation_in_the_main_process, ::test_a_sample_with_no_random_step_takes_no_number_from_the_torch_generator and tests/test_encoder_transforms.py::test_palette_loader_gives_a_new_cache_key.
  • Code in the key: the key has a short hash of code. It covers each function in a cached step, also deep inside it, for example the func of Lambdad. It also covers the __call__ of each RadHarmony step. So a changed lambda or a fixed step gives a new cache. A docstring is not in the hash, so a docstring edit keeps the cache. A new Python version changes the bytecode, so its caches build once again. A fix in a helper that a step calls does not change the key, so delete the cache then.
  • Seed in the main process: torch.manual_seed(...) repeats the random augmentation with any num_workers, also with num_workers=0 and with ds[i]. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-02, Q-3 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were a doc line that the seed works only with num_workers > 0, and to leave the question open. In the main process, _WorkerSeeded seeds the random steps for each sample with a number from the PyTorch random generator. So a second torch.manual_seed(0) with the same dataset repeats the augmentation, and the next ds[0] without a new seed is a new augmentation. Example: torch.manual_seed(0); ds[0] gives the same flip in 2 new processes. A torch DataLoader takes 1 number from the PyTorch random generator first, so its first batch is not ds[0], but it also repeats. A transform with no random step takes no number, so feature extraction keeps the random numbers of the user.
  • Notes (seed in the main process): since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li (Q-3 of the 2026-11-02 review). Before, torch.manual_seed(0); ds[0] gave a different flip in 2 new processes. Each sample with a random step now takes 1 number from the PyTorch random generator. So with num_workers=0, a seeded training run with augmentation (for example its dropout) gives other random numbers than before this change. The draw uses the global generator, not the generator= of a DataLoader. A set_random_state on the transform has no effect on ds[i] now. Use torch.manual_seed.
  • Notes: each DataLoader worker seeds the random steps from its PyTorch worker seed. This seed is new for each worker and each epoch (_WorkerSeeded in radharmony/dataset/base.py, approved by Frank Li on 2026-10-29). Before, the workers of a torch DataLoader repeated the same augmentation in every epoch (V-D-7). BaseVQADataset uses the same step. A dataset does not read a cache folder made before 2026-10-29. Delete these old folders to free the disk. Since 2026-11-02, the 3-D cache holds the preprocessed volume (V-D-28, base code approved by Frank Li). Before, 2 steps of the 3-D load were not MONAI transforms, so the cache stopped after the load. One CT-RATE cache file was 1,053 MB, and now it is 3 MB. The samples are the same. The 3-D cache folders from before 2026-11-02 are not read again, so delete them to free the disk. The code in the key is also from 2026-11-02 (V-D-37, base code approved by Frank Li). Before, 2 lambdas x * 2 and x * 3 gave one key, and the second read the old tensors. This change gives every cache a new key, so no cache folder from before it is read again. Delete them to free the disk.
  • Notes (more steps in the key): Frank Li approved this base-code change on 2026-11-02. The key also sees a functools.partial with its arguments, and the default arguments of a function. It sees a builtin or NumPy ufunc by its name, the object of a bound method, and a staticmethod. The critic of V-D-37 found these 5 gaps. Checked by: tests/test_dataset.py::test_the_transform_key_sees_partials_defaults_builtins_methods_and_staticmethods.
  • Related: D-28.

docs.title: D-49 A val split with random steps warns
docs.text:
get_datasets(n_splits=...) and get_folds() warn when val_transform is None and the dataset transform has a random step. The val split still uses the dataset transform, as api.md says.

Example: ds = CheXpertDataset(..., transform=t_with_random_flip), then ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5). The val images can come out flipped, and the flip changes in each epoch. The warning tells the user to pass val_transform=.

Why: train augmentation must not run on the val split, but the code cannot remove the random steps safely. For example, a random crop to 224 x 224 also sets the image size.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-02, Q-4 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were to remove the random steps from the val transform, a doc line only, and to leave the question open.
  • Checked by: tests/test_dataset.py::test_a_val_split_with_a_random_step_warns, ::test_a_val_split_with_no_random_step_does_not_warn and ::test_a_random_step_is_found_inside_lists_and_compose.
  • Notes: since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li (Q-4 of the 2026-11-02 review). The check is _warn_random_val in radharmony/dataset/base.py. A random step is a MONAI RandomizableTrait, also inside a nested Compose. OneOf, SomeOf and RandomOrder are random steps.
  • Notes (VQA): since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li, the get_datasets and get_folds of BaseVQADataset give the same warning. The default VQA transform has no random step. Checked by tests/test_vqa_base.py::test_a_val_split_with_a_random_step_warns.
  • Notes (official splits): since 2026-11-03, get_datasets_predefined of TAIX-Ray and RANZCR CLiP also warns. A val or test split with no transform of its own gets the dataset transform. The warning names the argument, for example test_transform. Checked by tests/test_official_splits.py::test_taix_ray_predefined_val_and_test_warn_about_a_random_step and ::test_ranzcr_predefined_test_warns_about_a_random_step.
  • Related: D-15, D-18.

docs.title: D-37 A warp fills the empty border with black
docs.text:
with_affine and with_elastic_deformation move the image, so they leave an empty border. The border gets the black value of the image:

  • RadiologyTransform2D and RadiologyTransform3D: -1, because the image is in [-1, 1]. The pad of pad=True also uses -1. Before 2026-11-03, their docstrings said zero (V-D-43, docstring fix approved by Frank Li).
  • RadiologyEncoderTransform: the darkest value of each channel of the image. The encoder has already normalized this image ((pixel - mean) / std), so -1 is a gray there.

Why: the border is outside the body, as the empty area of an X-ray is. A gray border adds an edge that no real image has. Example: for RAD-DINO, black is -2.055, and -1 is a gray of 27% brightness.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, V-P-16). The other options were the exact encoder black (0 - mean) / std, which needs the mean and std, and -1 with a doc line.
  • Checked by: tests/test_encoder_transforms.py::test_with_affine_fills_the_border_with_the_encoder_black and ::test_with_affine_fills_the_border_with_the_darkest_value_of_each_channel.
  • Notes: a real run on 2026-10-30 used 50 Shenzhen CXRs and the RAD-DINO processor. The darkest pixel of 42 images was within 0.05 of black. The worst image had -1.948 (2.7% brightness). For MedSigLIP (mean and std 0.5), -1 is black.
  • Related: D-15.

docs.title: D-16 Backbones match their authors
docs.text:
Each make_<name>() factory gives the same features as the authors' own code. This includes the input size, crop, mean, std and the feature token (CLS token, mean pool or pooled output).

Why: the benchmark compares models. A changed input step changes the score of one model only.

  • Status: From the code.
  • Checked by: J-05, tests/test_eva_x.py for EVA-X (it runs where timm is installed and the weights are cached), and tests/test_backbones.py (it runs in the model venv).
  • Two input steps: when the authors' code has 2 different input steps, the factory uses the one of their downstream (fine-tune) code. For Ark+, this is a bilinear resize to 896 x 896, a center crop of 768 and the ImageNet mean and std. The Ark+ pretraining code uses a PIL bicubic resize instead. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, V-B-2). The other option was the pretraining input.
  • Two features: when the authors' fine-tune code and their linear-probe code use different features, the classification feature follows the linear-probe code. For Ark+, this is the projector output (1376 values, generate_embeddings(x, after_proj=True), emb_dim=1376 in Linearprobing/main_linearprobing.py), not forward_features (1536 values). CheXFound follows the same rule (its 4 CLS tokens). Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-02, Q-2 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were to keep forward_features with a note, and an argument with forward_features as the default. Since 2026-11-03, make_ark_plus loads the projector (one Linear, 1536 to 1376) and gives its output. The segmentation feature map does not change. Checked by tests/test_backbones.py::test_ark_plus_classification_feature_is_the_projector_output (where the checkpoint is on the machine).
  • Notes (CheXFound input): since 2026-11-03, the input follows the authors' eval transform. After the resize and the crop, it clips to [0, 1] and scales each channel with its minimum and maximum (RescaleImage). Before, the input of 4 CheXpert images was in [-0.07, 1.08] (V-B-14). Checked by tests/test_backbones.py::test_chexfound_input_is_rescaled_to_0_1_as_the_authors_do.
  • MedSigLIP resize: the model card gives 2 ways. It recommends tf.image.resize (bilinear, no antialias) to reproduce its evals, and it allows the bicubic resize of the Transformers processor. make_medsiglip keeps the processor. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04, found in the 6c rewrite of the backbone pages). The other options were a bilinear resize with no antialias as the evals, and an argument with the processor as the default.
  • PNG files of a generator: make_chexagent_generator and make_maira2_generator write one PNG for each image. With tmp_dir=None, the folder is new under the system temp folder, and it goes when Python exits. A folder that the user gives stays. Before, the folder stayed in /tmp. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04). The other options were a doc line only, and no change. Checked by: tests/test_backbones.py::test_png_folder_of_a_generator_goes_at_exit_unless_the_user_gave_it.
  • Known gaps (MAIRA-2): the current model card (https://huggingface.co/microsoft/maira-2) differs from make_maira2_generator in 3 points. The card asks for transformers>=4.48.0,<4.52, and the maira2_gen extra pins >=4.46.0,<4.47. The card cleans the output with processor.convert_output_to_plaintext_or_grounded_sequence(), and the recipe uses strip(). And normalize_hypothesis does not remove the box marks of get_grounding=True. No fix yet, because the weights are gated and not on the test machine. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04): record the gap, fix it with the real model (eval/TODO.md). The other options were an untested change, and to get the weights first.
  • Device of a generator: make_chexagent_generator loads with device_map=device, not the "auto" of the model card. So device="cuda:3" puts the whole model on GPU 3, as make_maira2_generator does. The device does not change the output. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-03, V-B-15). The other option was to keep "auto" with a doc line. Checked by tests/test_backbones.py::test_chexagent_generator_puts_the_model_on_device.
  • Notes (Ark+): a real run on 2026-10-30 used Shenzhen (662 images) and a linear probe (5 folds, 3 seeds). The bicubic features had a mean cosine of 0.995 to the bilinear features. The AUROC was 0.9973 (bilinear), 0.9969 (bicubic) and 0.9965 (the v0.1 input, 768 with no crop). Ark+ was pretrained with Shenzhen labels, so these AUROC values only compare the inputs.
  • Notes (CheXFound): since 2026-11-01, the classification feature joins the CLS tokens of the last 4 blocks (4096 values), as the authors' linear probe does. A probe used 234 CheXpert valid images (5 labels, 5 folds). The macro AUROC was 0.774 with the last CLS and 0.803 with the 4 CLS tokens (V-B-13).
  • Notes (Ark+ feature): a probe on 2026-11-02 used 600 SIIM-ACR images (300 with pneumothorax), L2 norm, logistic regression, 5 folds and 3 seeds. The AUROC was 0.9590 ± 0.0121 with forward_features and 0.9573 ± 0.0121 with the projector output.

docs.title: D-17 Frozen-feature probes L2-normalize features
docs.text:
The linear, kNN, SVM and prototype probes and zero-shot use features with L2 norm 1. The feature cache stores raw features, and the probe normalizes them after load. A user can turn it off with l2_normalize=False.

Why: all probes then use the same features, so a score difference comes from the classifier only.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-05-26).
  • Checked by: J-07, tests/test_evaluator.py::test_finetune_frozen_head_sees_l2_normalized_features, tests/test_evaluator.py::test_prototype_obeys_l2_normalize and tests/test_evaluator.py::test_zero_shot_warns_for_l2_normalize_false.
  • Zero-shot: it always uses cosine similarity, as CLIP does. l2_normalize has no effect there, so ZeroShotEvaluator gives a warning for l2_normalize=False. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other options were the doc line only, and a raw dot product for l2_normalize=False.
  • Segmentation heads: they use the raw patch features. The rule of this entry is for the classification probes. A segmentation head trains with a learning rate, and the scale of the features sets which learning rate works. The conv and UPerNet heads normalize inside (LayerNorm2d, BatchNorm). Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, R-code-4). The other options were L2 in the linear head with a default learning rate of 1e-1, and L2 in all 3 heads.
  • Notes: a real run on 2026-10-30 used Montgomery lungs, RAD-DINO and the linear head (5 folds, 20 epochs). The best lung Dice was 0.970 with raw features (lr 1e-2) and 0.969 with L2 (lr 1e-1). At the default lr 1e-3, raw gave 0.959 and L2 gave 0.819.

docs.title: D-18 Test data stays out of training
docs.text:
The code does not use test labels to train, to pick a model, to pick a threshold, to pick a setting or to stop early. Every probe drops rows with a NaN label. Every random step has a seed.

Why: a score that used test labels is too high.

  • Status: From the code.
  • Checked by: J-06, L-009 (tests/test_lessons.py::test_l009_nan_train_labels_equal_rows_with_label) and tests/test_evaluator.py::test_same_base_seed_gives_same_result.
  • Related: D-29.

docs.title: D-29 The threshold comes from validation data
docs.text:
The threshold for F1, accuracy, balanced accuracy, TPR, TNR, PPV, NPV and MCC comes from a validation set. The validation set is part of the training data, split by patient. The probe picks the threshold with threshold_strategy (for example, "youden"). It picks it one time for each seed in fixed-split mode, or one time for each fold in k-fold mode. Then it uses that threshold on the test set and on every bootstrap sample.

Why: a threshold that is picked on the test labels makes every threshold metric too high. AUROC and AUPRC do not use a threshold.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-28). The validation set is 10% of the training patients (val_fraction=0.1, the same default as the fine-tune evaluator and the segmentation probes).
  • Checked by: J-06, tests/test_evaluator.py::test_threshold_comes_from_validation_data, and for zero-shot ::test_zero_shot_threshold_metrics_are_nan_without_a_fixed_threshold and ::test_zero_shot_uses_the_fixed_threshold.
  • Fit part: the 5 probes that train (linear, SVM, kNN, prototype, fine-tune) fit on the other 90% of the training patients. Example: with n_train=100 and one image per patient, a probe fits on 90 patients and picks the threshold on the other 10. D-40 says what n_train counts. A very small n_train can give NaN threshold metrics, because the validation part then has too few patients. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other option was a second model on 100% of the patients for the test scores.
  • Notes: a real run on 2026-10-30 used Shenzhen TB, RAD-DINO and the linear probe (5 folds, 3 seeds). For 50 to 200 patients, the AUROC with a fit on 90% and on 100% was 0.003 or less apart. At n_train=20, F1 was NaN.
  • Zero-shot: ZeroShotEvaluator has no train data, so it has no validation part. Its threshold metrics are NaN, unless threshold_strategy is "fixed:<value>". It gives one warning that says this. With negative prompts, the warning tells the user to pass "fixed:0", which means "closer to the positive prompts". AUROC and AUPRC do not change. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other options were a threshold from 10% of the test patients, and the threshold from the test labels with new metric names.
  • Notes (zero-shot): a real run on 2026-10-30 used MedSigLIP, VinDr-CXR test (3,000 images) and 19 labels with 20 or more positives. The mean balanced accuracy was 0.798 with the threshold from the test labels. It was 0.769 with a threshold from 10% of the test patients, and 0.767 with fixed:0.
  • Examples: each zero-shot example in README.md and in the use-radharmony skill says that the threshold metrics are NaN without threshold_strategy, or it passes threshold_strategy="fixed:0". Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-02, Q-20 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other option was no change, because zero_shot.md already says it.
  • Notes: README.md and the use-radharmony skill now say it in a comment. No V- ID: Q-20.
  • Segmentation: the 3 segmentation evaluators use no threshold. The head gives each pixel the class with the highest score. A threshold_strategy other than "youden" gives a UserWarning (base code in radharmony/evaluator/segmentation/base.py, approved by Frank Li on 2026-11-04). Before, it had no effect and no message. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04). The other options were to remove the argument, and no change. Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_seg_threshold_strategy_warns_that_it_is_not_used.
  • Related: D-18, D-19.

docs.title: D-19 Variance of a result
docs.text:
• Fixed-split mode (train_dataset= and test_dataset=): n_seeds sets the number of train subsamples, each with its own seed. n_bootstrap sets the number of bootstrap samples of the test set.
  • K-fold mode (dataset=): the folds give the variance. The evaluator ignores n_seeds and n_bootstrap, and warns if you set them.
  • A result row with bootstrap = -1 is the point estimate.
  • The save_results() summary takes the mean over the point-estimate rows. It takes the std and the 95% CI over the bootstrap rows. With no bootstrap rows, it takes them over the folds or the seeds. With fewer than 2 values, the std and the CI are NaN: 1 value has no spread (V-E-31).
  • The std is the population std (np.nanstd, ddof=0), as cross_val_score(...).std() of scikit-learn gives. Example: 5 fold AUROCs give 0.043, and the sample std (ddof=1) gives 0.049. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04, found in the 6c rewrite): keep it, and say it in the docs. The other options were the sample std everywhere, and the sample std over folds or seeds only.
  • A metric can be NaN in some folds or seeds, for example a threshold metric of a rare label (D-29). Then the summary gives for each metric the number of runs with a value (<metric>_n, for example f1_n = 4 of 5 folds). The probe warns one time for each such label, with the number of NaN runs.

Why: a result shows how much the score changes with the train sample and the test sample. A mean over fewer runs must be visible in the result file, not only in the log.

  • Status: From the code (radharmony/evaluator/base.py). The summary rule: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-29, V-E-15). The count and the warning for NaN runs: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-8 of the 2026-10-31 review). NaN std and CI for 1 value: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-02, V-E-31). The other options were a warning only, and another threshold rule when the validation part has too few positives.
  • Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_summary_mean_uses_point_rows_and_ci_uses_bootstrap_rows, ::test_summary_std_and_ci_need_2_values and ::test_summary_counts_the_runs_with_a_value_and_warns_once_per_label.
  • Notes: Frank Li approved the count and the warning on 2026-11-02 (Q-8), in _summarize of radharmony/evaluator/base.py. So the warning comes from save_results(), one time per label. Example: Label 'nodule': f1 is NaN in 1 of 5 runs. Their means use the other runs (D-19).
  • Related: D-29, D-32.

docs.title: D-32 The bootstrap draws patients
docs.text:
Each bootstrap sample draws test patients with replacement, and it keeps all images of each drawn patient. The metric is still computed over images. If the test data has no patient_id, the bootstrap draws images.

Example: a patient with 20 follow-up images is drawn as one unit, so the 20 images go in or out together. For a test set with one image per patient (for example, VinDr-CXR), the result is the same as a draw of images.

Why: images of one patient are not independent. A draw of images makes the confidence interval too narrow.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-28).
  • Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_bootstrap_draws_patients, tests/test_evaluator.py::test_bootstrap_uses_test_patients, tests/test_evaluator.py::test_base_has_no_unused_bootstrap_helper and tests/test_evaluator.py::test_a_table_with_no_patient_id_column_draws_images.
  • Missing ID: when some rows have a NaN patient_id, the evaluators raise a ValueError. The message gives the number of these rows and their first image paths. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-02, Q-5 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were to draw each such row as its own patient, to keep the crash, and to leave the question open. A NaN ID is a harmonizer bug (D-01). Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_a_nan_patient_id_raises_with_the_count_and_the_image_paths.
  • Notes (NaN patient_id): since 2026-11-03, in radharmony/evaluator/sampling.py (not base code, Q-5 of the 2026-11-02 review). patient_ids_of raises the ValueError. The classification evaluators and ReportGenerationEvaluator read the ids through it. Before, bootstrap_indices raised TypeError ("'<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'float'"), and GroupKFold raised ValueError ("Input contains NaN").
  • Notes (segmentation): since 2026-11-03 (d596a55), LinearProbeSegEvaluator and its subclasses take their ids from group_ids, as the classification probes do. Before, a table with no patient_id column raised KeyError there. Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_seg_probe_takes_the_patient_ids_of_the_classification_probes.
  • Notes: the 8 evaluators use bootstrap_indices in radharmony/evaluator/sampling.py. The old _bootstrap_metrics, which drew images, was removed on 2026-10-29 (R-code-11).
  • Notes (no patient_id column): since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li (V-E-33). In a table with no patient_id column, each image is its own patient (group_ids in radharmony/evaluator/sampling.py). So the bootstrap draws images, and the k-fold split and the validation part split images. Before, every classification evaluator crashed with KeyError: 'patient_id'.
  • Related: D-01, D-10, D-18, D-19.

docs.title: D-40 n_train counts images or patients
docs.text:
n_train_samples sets the size of the training sample. The argument n_train_unit says what it counts. "image" (the default) draws n_train images. "patient" draws n_train patients and keeps all their images. With one image per patient, both give the same sample.

Example: with 4 images per patient, n_train=100 gives 100 images from about 47 patients with "image", and 100 patients with about 400 images with "patient".

Why: label-efficiency studies usually count images, but a study by patient needs whole patients.

  • Status: Decided, planned (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-7 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other options were images only (with a fix of the D-29 example), and patients only.
  • Checked by: none yet.
  • Notes: today the probes draw image rows (_subsample in each probe, for example radharmony/evaluator/classification/svm_probe.py:111). n_train_unit is not built yet.
  • Related: D-29, D-32.

docs.title: D-41 The embedding cache holds features only
docs.text:
embedding_cache of the classification evaluators stores the raw features of one encoder, one transform, one autocast_dtype and one list of images in one image folder. Each run reads the labels from the dataset, not from the cache. A cache from other images, another image folder, another encoder, another transform or another autocast_dtype raises ValueError.

Example: after a label fix (for example D-05: CheXpert keeps -1), a run with the old cache uses the new labels and the old features. The features do not depend on the labels.

Why: a cache that also returns its labels makes a later run use old labels with no error.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-6 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other options were a hash of the labels that raises ValueError when they differ, and labels from the cache with a doc line. The fingerprint: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-02, V-E-25).
  • Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_embedding_cache_takes_the_labels_of_the_dataset, ::test_embedding_cache_sees_every_change_of_the_features, ::test_the_encoder_fingerprint_is_the_same_in_every_process, ::test_an_embedding_cache_with_no_image_folder_or_autocast_dtype_raises, tests/test_lessons.py::test_l017_the_embedding_cache_raises_when_an_input_of_the_features_changes (L-017), and (labels in float32) tests/test_transforms.py::test_2d_dtype_is_for_the_image_only and ::test_3d_dtype_is_for_the_image_only.
  • Fingerprint: the cache file keeps a fingerprint of the encoder and the transform. It hashes the weights and buffers of each torch model in the encoder. This includes a model in a closure, a functools.partial, a method or a global that a function loads. It also hashes the functions of the encoder, for example its pool function. Of the transform, it hashes the cache key (D-15): the steps before the first random step. A random step keeps its last draw, so it would change the fingerprint in every run. Another fingerprint raises ValueError.
  • Notes: Frank Li approved the base-code change on 2026-11-02 (Q-6). Before it, the cache stored the label matrix and a cache hit returned it, so a label fix was not seen. Now a cache hit reads cls from the samples before the transform, with no image load. On 48 real CheXpert rows with -1 and NaN, these labels equal the labels of a run with no cache. Frank Li also approved the fingerprint on 2026-11-02 (V-E-25). Before it, the check used the model class, the weight count and the sum of the first weight. So another pool, another transform, 2 function encoders or other later weights read old features. A file from before 2026-11-02 raises ValueError once. Delete it to build it again. For 300 million weights, the fingerprint takes about 1 s.
  • Notes (image folder and autocast_dtype): since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li (V-E-34). The cache file also keeps the absolute base_image_dir and the autocast_dtype. Before, a run on TAIX-Ray full size read a cache of TAIX-Ray 512, because the 2 tables have the same image_path list. A run in fp32 also read a cache made in bf16. A file from before 2026-11-03 raises ValueError once. Delete it to build it again.
  • Known gaps:
  • The fingerprint does not see every change of the code. It does not hash the forward of a model class or a helper that the pool function calls. It does not hash a model in a global dict, or the settings of a model from outside RadHarmony. It does not hash a change in a random step of the transform.
  • A cache hit skips the label checks inside a transform, for example the check for NaN labels of RANZCR.
  • Notes (label dtype): the transforms cast only img (and bbox_mask) to dtype. cls, reg and mask stay float32, so a cache hit and a run with no cache give the same labels. The backbone recipes do this since 2026-11-03 (V-B-16, tests/test_encoder_transforms.py::test_encoder_transform_casts_only_the_image). RadiologyTransform2D and RadiologyTransform3D do it since 2026-11-03 (base code approved by Frank Li). Before, they cast the labels to dtype (bf16 by default), so a label 37.3 became 37.25 and a 3-D mask id 257 became 256. Checked by: tests/test_transforms.py::test_2d_dtype_is_for_the_image_only and ::test_3d_dtype_is_for_the_image_only.
  • Random steps: the frozen-feature evaluators warn when the transform has a random step before feature extraction, because the cache keeps one random draw. The evaluator tutorial uses no with_* augmentation in the transform of a frozen-feature probe. Decided by the agent, for Frank Li to confirm (2026-11-02, Q-19 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were the tutorial fix only, and no change with a doc line. Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_a_frozen_feature_evaluator_warns_for_a_random_step and ::test_the_random_step_check_keeps_the_random_state.
  • Notes (random steps): since 2026-11-03, base code approved by Frank Li (Q-19). _load_or_extract in classification/base.py warns when the transform has a MONAI RandomizableTrait step. It opens a nested Compose. The warning names the steps. Fine-tune does not call _load_or_extract, so it does not warn.
  • Notes (tutorial): since 2026-11-04 (6c batch 8), notebooks/tutorials/evaluator_tutorial.ipynb gives a frozen-feature probe a transform with no random step. Before, it had a flip and an intensity jitter.
  • Known gaps (log noise): a second frozen-feature probe in the same Jupyter kernel can print some lines in extract_embeddings (radharmony/evaluator/classification/base.py). They start with Exception ignored in _MultiProcessingDataLoaderIter.__del__. New worker processes copy an old data loader iterator. The results are right. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04): record it, no fix now (eval/TODO.md). The other options were to reproduce and fix it in base code, and no change.
  • Related: D-15, D-17.

docs.title: D-46 A prediction names its image by image_path
docs.text:
Each image gets the id image_path with no image file ending, for example .png, .dcm or .nii.gz. predict() of the segmentation probes and of FinetuneEvaluator uses this id, and so does the sample_id of ReportGenerationEvaluator. A 3-D study folder named by a dotted UID keeps all of its name. save_predictions writes one PNG per image. Its file name is the id with __ for each /. Example: patient1/study1/view1_frontal.jpg gives the id patient1/study1/view1_frontal and the file patient1__study1__view1_frontal.png.

Why: the file name alone is not unique. In CheXlocalize, 668 images had only 4 ids, and the PNGs of one id overwrote each other (V-E-24).

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li confirmed on 2026-11-02 the choice of the agent of 2026-11-01, V-E-24). The other options were the file name only (the old way), and PNGs in sub-folders that copy the image folders.
  • Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_prediction_ids_and_pngs_are_one_per_image, ::test_image_ids_cut_only_an_image_file_ending and ::test_report_sample_id_is_the_image_id.
  • Related: D-04.

docs.title: D-47 Fine-tune loss="ce" needs 2 or more label columns
docs.text:
With loss="ce" and 1 label column, FinetuneEvaluator.fit() and .evaluate() raise ValueError. The message tells the user to take loss="bce".

Why: a softmax over 1 logit is always 1, so the loss is always 0 and the model does not train. A run gave AUROC 0.5 in each fold and the score 1.0 for every image, with no warning (V-E-27).

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li confirmed on 2026-11-02 the choice of the agent of 2026-11-01, V-E-27). The other option was a 2-class softmax for 1 label column.
  • Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_finetune_ce_with_one_label_column_raises.
  • Related: D-18.

docs.title: D-38 A report section falls back to the other section
docs.text:
ReportGenerationEvaluator compares the generated text with one section of the real report (ref_section). When the report has no FINDINGS section, "findings" uses the IMPRESSION text. When it has no IMPRESSION section, "impression" uses the FINDINGS text. When it has neither, "findings" and "impression" use the whole report. "both" joins the 2 sections, or uses the whole report when it has neither. "full" always uses the whole report.

Why: each study with a report gets a reference, so no study is dropped.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, V-E-7). The other option was strict sections: an empty reference, so the evaluator drops the pair.
  • Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_report_parser_headers.
  • Headers: a header is a name, an optional "S", then ":", for example FINDINGS:. It counts at the start of a line in upper or lower case, or inside a line in capitals only. So "new findings: none" in a sentence is not a header. Each section stops at the next header of its stop list in radharmony/evaluator/language/_report_parser.py, also on the same line. The FINDINGS list has IMPRESSION and CONCLUSION. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, V-E-8). The other option was a header at the line start only. Checked by tests/test_evaluator.py::test_report_parser_headers.
  • The fallback for a report with neither section uses the same header rule. So "No new findings: lungs are clear." in a sentence keeps the whole report (V-E-28, since 2026-11-03). Before, the fallback cut the report at that lowercase word. Checked by tests/test_evaluator.py::test_report_parser_headers.
  • The IMPRESSION list also has FINDINGS, so a reference never holds the same text 2 times. Example: for "IMPRESSION: Stable. FINDINGS: Heart is normal.", "impression" gives "Stable." and "both" gives "Heart is normal. Stable.". Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-9 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other option was to keep the old list, because the layout is rare (7 of 20,000 random MIMIC-CXR reports). Checked by tests/test_evaluator.py::test_report_parser_headers (since 2026-11-01). Before, "both" repeated the FINDINGS text in this layout (Q-9).
  • Notes: a real run on 2026-10-30 used the MIMIC-CXR test split (2,216 studies, one report each). 499 reports (22.5%) have IMPRESSION only, and 167 have neither section. So with "findings", 22.5% of the references are IMPRESSION text. The header rule changed 7 references (0.3%) from the old parser. Each one now stops at a header of the stop list.
  • Related: D-32.

docs.title: D-50 Both report scoring paths clean the generated text the same way
docs.text:
ReportGenerationEvaluator.evaluate() and the Stage B script (notebooks/evaluator/score_reports_radeval.py) clean each generated report with one function in radharmony. The function removes the CheXagent grounding tags, the boxes, the ref marks and the bold marks. It is on by default. An argument turns it off.

Example: a CheXagent report with grounding tags around "effusion" gives the same score in both paths.

Why: one set of generations must get one score.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-02, Q-6 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were raw text in both paths, a doc line that the 2 paths differ, and to leave the question open.
  • Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_both_report_scoring_paths_clean_the_hypothesis.
  • Notes: the function is normalize_hypothesis in radharmony/evaluator/language/hypothesis.py. The file imports only re. The Stage B script loads it by its path, so the script still runs with no radharmony install. The argument is normalize_hyp=False in evaluate() and --no-normalize-hyp in Stage B. generate_only() writes the raw text. generations.csv of evaluate() holds the cleaned text that was scored. Before 2026-11-03, evaluate() only removed the white space at the ends (Q-6).
  • Related: D-38.

docs.title: D-52 An evaluator argument that the class does not use warns, and one it cannot take raises at once
docs.text:
Some evaluators take a shared argument that they do not use. A value other than the default gives a UserWarning. The result does not change.

Example: ReportGenerationEvaluator(gen, dataset=ds, device="cpu") warns, because the generator of the backbone recipe sets its own device. Pass device to make_chexagent_generator() or make_maira2_generator().

Why: a user who sets an argument expects an effect. Before, these arguments had no effect and no message.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04, found in the 6c rewrite of the evaluator pages). The other options were to remove the arguments, and no change.
  • The arguments: threshold_strategy of the 3 segmentation evaluators (D-29, base code in radharmony/evaluator/segmentation/base.py, approved by Frank Li on 2026-11-04), and device of ReportGenerationEvaluator. ZeroShotEvaluator already warned for n_seeds other than 1.
  • Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_seg_threshold_strategy_warns_that_it_is_not_used and ::test_report_device_warns_that_it_is_not_used.
  • An encoder that the class cannot take raises TypeError in __init__, not later in evaluate(). FinetuneEvaluator moves the encoder and trains its weights, so it needs an nn.Module, also with freeze_backbone=True. Before, a plain function failed in evaluate() with AttributeError after the data loaded. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04). The other options were to accept a plain function with freeze_backbone=True, and no change. Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_finetune_with_a_plain_function_raises_type_error_at_once.
  • A zero-shot prompt can be longer than the model_max_length of a SigLIP processor (64 tokens for MedSigLIP and SigLIP 2, 256 for XraySigLIP). Then ZeroShotEvaluator cuts it to that length and warns. Before, the text model raised ValueError ("Sequence length must be less than max_position_embeddings"). Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04). The other options were a clear ValueError, and a cut with no warning. Checked by: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_zero_shot_cuts_a_long_siglip_prompt_and_warns.
  • Related: D-29.

docs.title: D-20 Base code needs approval
docs.text:
A change to base code needs approval first. CLAUDE.md lists the base files and the approval steps. Use a subclass override when you can.

Why: every dataset or evaluator shares base code. A small change can change results everywhere.

  • Status: Decided (CLAUDE.md).
  • Checked by: J-01, scripts/evalkit/base_guard.py.

docs.title: D-21 One file for data paths
docs.text:
Data paths are in configs/data_paths.json. Code, tests and docs do not contain NAS paths.

Why: when a folder moves, you change one file.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-27).
  • Checked by: L-002 and L-006 (scripts/evalkit/lessons.py), L-007 (tests/test_data_paths.py), and tests/test_evalkit.py::test_l002_checks_the_skills (L-002 reads .claude/skills/).
  • Skills: L-002 also checks .claude/skills/, because agents read and copy the skills. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other options were every tracked text file, and no change.
  • Checkpoint copies: the local .ipynb_checkpoints copies under docs/ stay. Git ignores them, and every check skips them (blocks.py, ste_lint.py, wiki_audit.py, mkdocs.yml and L-002). So their old NAS paths are not a gap. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-23 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other option was to delete the folders.
  • Known gaps: notebooks/datasets/dataset_integrity_check.ipynb keeps its own NAS paths in a paths cell, and it names 43 of the 128 dataset classes (A-15). scripts/check_datasets.py reads the config and covers every class.
  • Notes: on 2026-10-30, .claude/skills/ had 0 NAS paths, and the MedSeg and QaTa pages lost their last NAS paths.
  • A user's own file (Frank Li, 2026-11-04): configs/data_paths.example.json is committed. A user copies it to configs/data_paths.json (out of git in the public repo), or sets RADHARMONY_DATA_PATHS, and keeps the entries of the datasets to check. A missing file or key raises MissingPathsError with a hint. A check skips such a dataset, a tier=nas claim is skipped, and the tests that need data skip. The dev repo commits a complete file ("complete": true), so only there the tests check every key. The other options were to do it later with the public copy, and no change. Checked by: tests/test_data_paths_public.py.
  • Check names: each DatasetSpec of scripts/check_datasets.py is named by its registry key, or <registry key>_<variant> for a second check of the same class (for example ranzcr_clip_mask). Before 2026-11-04, 16 checks had short names (for example montgomery). The old names still work, with a warning (OLD_NAMES). Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-04). The other options were to accept both names, and no change. Checked by: tests/test_scripts.py::test_each_check_name_is_a_registry_key_or_a_variant_of_one.

docs.title: D-22 Docs do not hide code bugs
docs.text:
If a doc example fails because the code is wrong, fix or report the code. Do not change the doc to match the bug.

Why: a doc that matches a bug hides the bug from users and from the checks.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-27).
  • Checked by: J-09.

docs.title: D-23 Tests get their expected values from the source
docs.text:
A test gets its expected value from the source data or the spec, not from the code under test.

Why: a value from the code under test makes the test pass on the bug.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-27).
  • Checked by: J-08.

docs.title: D-39 check_dataset: wrong values are ERROR, missing outputs are WARN
docs.text:
check_dataset (radharmony/integrity.py) gives ERROR when a value breaks a rule:

  • No sample loads. This includes a dataset with 0 samples.
  • An image has NaN or Inf pixels.
  • A box is not 4 or 6 values in [0, 1] (D-07).
  • A box has a min that is not less than its max, for example a wrong axis order (D-07).

It gives WARN when an output is not complete:

  • Some samples do not load, or a key is missing in some samples.
  • No sample has a requested output.
  • output_bbox=True, and no sample has bbox_labels (D-11).
  • Every label, mask or report is empty.

scripts/check_datasets.py exits with code 1 when a dataset has ERROR.

Why: wrong values break training with no error message, so a script or CI must stop. Missing outputs can be normal data.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, V-A-5). The other option was WARN for bad boxes and NaN or Inf pixels.
  • Checked by: tests/test_integrity.py::test_bad_values_change_the_status (with the 2 examples of "Box order"), ::test_requested_output_that_no_sample_has_warns, ::test_boxes_with_no_labels_warn, ::test_zero_samples_is_an_error. tests/test_scripts.py::test_check_datasets_zero_samples_exits_1 checks the exit code. tests/test_scripts.py::test_check_datasets_covers_dataset checks which script holds which spec.
  • Default run: a spec whose data has "status": "restricted" or "not_on_nas" in configs/data_paths.json gets default=False. It runs only when the user names it with --datasets. So a run with no --datasets can pass for every user. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30). The other options were a run of every spec with a new result BLOCKED, and the default values from before 2026-10-29.
  • Box order: ERROR for a box with min not less than max. Example: [0.6, 0.2, 0.4, 0.1] (a wrong axis order) and [0.5, 0.5, 0.3, 0.3] (no area). Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-1 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other options were WARN, and no check.
  • Box labels: WARN when output_bbox=True and no sample has bbox_labels. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-31, Q-2 of the 2026-10-31 review). The other option was no check, because bbox_labels is an optional table column. Since 2026-11-01, every class that gives boxes also gives bbox_labels (V-D-29, V-H3-23). A real run on 2026-11-01 gave OK with both rules. It checked the 7 readable 2-D box datasets (25 samples each) and the 3 3-D box datasets (5 samples each).
  • Empty dataset: ERROR for a dataset with 0 samples. Each spec of check_datasets.py is a whole dataset with its default arguments, so 0 rows means a broken path, join or filter. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-02, Q-1 of the 2026-11-02 review). The other options were WARN with a line in this entry, and to leave the question open.
  • Check scripts: scripts/check_datasets.py checks every dataset whose class is in the public package. scripts/check_datasets_internal.py adds only the datasets with internal data (Emory CXR). So MS-CXR, MS-CXR-T and MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA are in check_datasets.py. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-10-30, A-6). The other option was to keep them in the internal script.
  • Notes: this rule found the bad boxes of SIIM-COVID19 and RAD-ChestCT, which a fix on 2026-10-29 removed. A real run on 2026-10-30 (50 samples each) gave OK for both. On that day, 35 of the 110 specs had default=False. 24 were restricted and 6 not on the NAS. The other 5 were Chest ImaGenome silver (3, slow) and the 2 Kaggle test classes of D-25.
  • Related: D-07, D-14, D-21.

docs.title: D-45 A known-problems list only gets shorter
docs.text:
run_all.py --check-shrink <ref> fails when a known-problems list has an entry that the list at <ref> did not have, or a higher count. Only a new rule can add its old problems. You name each new rule: --check-shrink origin/main --new-rule L-013.

Why: an old rule with 0 known problems has no entry in the old list, so the check cannot tell it from a new rule. Example: L-002 (no NAS paths in docs) has no entry today. A new NAS path in a doc page must fail, not join the list.

  • Status: Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-01, V-A-38). The other options were to read the rule list of each check at <ref> (RULES.md, pyproject.toml, the STE rules), and no change.
  • Checked by: tests/test_evalkit.py::test_shrink_errors, ::test_shrink_errors_for_an_old_rule_with_no_entry and ::test_new_rules_come_from_the_pr_description.
  • CI: the PR description names each new rule on its own line, for example New rule: L-013. The CI step passes the PR description with --pr-body FILE. run_all.py adds the rule of each line to --new-rule. A line in a code block does not count. Decided (Frank Li, 2026-11-01). The other options were a CI failure that a maintainer merges by hand, and a file of new rules in the PR.
  • Named rules: a named rule that has an entry in the old list is not new, so its entries still may not grow.
  • Notes: a list with no file at <ref> belongs to a new check, so it cannot grow.
  • Related: D-20.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
No entry has the status "Open" now. No decided entry has an open part now.

To add an open question, add a D- entry with the next free number and the status "Open". Put it in the section where it belongs, and add it to the index. A maintainer decides each question. Then the status changes to "Decided", with the name and the date.

docs.title: DICOM loading
docs.text: A DICOM file can store its pixels in several ways. If the loader reads them the wrong way, the image comes out inverted, too dark, washed out or blank, and no error tells you. This page explains how the 2-D pipeline reads a DICOM file, and why each step is there. It also lists the problems that we found and fixed in 2026. The rule is D-13: every chest X-ray that a dataset class gives has bright bone.

docs.title: The 2-D load steps
docs.text:
_base_load_2d in radharmony/dataset/transforms.py gives the load steps of every 2-D pipeline:

Step What it does LoadImageD(reader="ITKReader") Reads the file with ITK. ITK uses GDCM for DICOM files _drop_dicom_axis, TransposeD Gives the image the shape (C, H, W) _fix_missing_highbit Reads the pixels again with pydicom when the file has no HighBit tag _apply_voi_lut Applies the window of a MONOCHROME file (WindowCenter and WindowWidth, or a VOI LUT) _SetChannelsD Sets the channel count of the dataset (D-42) ScaleIntensityRangePercentilesD Scales the 0.5 and 99.5 percentiles to [-1, 1], and clips (D-14)
