The 2 DICOM steps (_fix_missing_highbit and _apply_voi_lut) are in radharmony/dataset/base.py. A backbone recipe with reader="monai" runs the same 2 steps (Backbones). CXRPreprocessor in radharmony/preprocessor/cxr.py has its own copy, with the same rules.

is_dicom in radharmony/utils/dicom.py decides if a file is a DICOM file. It looks for the Photometric Interpretation tag (0028,0004), with any file name. It skips .mha, .nrrd and NIfTI files, because a copy of a DICOM file in these formats keeps the tag. The 2 DICOM steps do nothing for a file that is not DICOM.

docs.title: MONOCHROME1 and MONOCHROME2
docs.text:
A DICOM file stores each pixel as a number. There are 2 conventions:

  • MONOCHROME2: a large number is bright. Bone is bright and air is dark. Most models expect this.
  • MONOCHROME1: a large number is dark.

ITK inverts a MONOCHROME1 image when it reads the file. It gives s * (M - raw) + b, where s and b are RescaleSlope and RescaleIntercept, and M = 2**BitsStored - 1. Example: in a 12-bit file, the stored value 95 becomes 4095 - 95 = 4000. M is the largest plus the smallest stored value (stored_value_sum in radharmony/utils/dicom.py). For signed pixel values (PixelRepresentation 1), this sum is -1. Example for 16 bits: 32767 + (-32768) = -1.

So the pipeline has no MONOCHROME1 inversion step. A second inversion makes the image wrong. The old pipeline had such a step in a comment, so it never ran. We removed it on 2026-10-29.

A review said that MONOCHROME1 images (541 of the 3,000 VinDr-CXR test images) come out inverted. This is not true. On VinDr-CXR test, the ITK pixels and the raw pydicom pixels have a correlation of +1.0 for MONOCHROME2 files and -1.0 for MONOCHROME1 files. A check of 6 VinDr-CXR test files on 2026-11-04 gave the same result. The pipeline output had a correlation of +1.0 with a pydicom reference for both kinds.

docs.title: The window of a MONOCHROME1 file
docs.text:
The window tags (WindowCenter and WindowWidth) refer to the stored values, before the ITK inversion. The old _apply_voi_lut applied them to the values after the inversion.

Example: the header says "show the stored values 0 to 1000". After the ITK inversion, these pixels are 3095 to 4095, but the window still takes 0 to 1000. So it takes the wrong pixels. A window in the center of the range does not move when the image is inverted. So only a window that is not in the center gives a wrong image.

In a sample of CheXpert Plus files, 131 were MONOCHROME1 with window tags, and 10 of them came out wrong. The worst file was almost all white (a mean absolute difference of 0.600 on the [-1, 1] scale). In SIIM-ACR, SIIM-COVID and RSNA Pneumonia, no sampled file has window tags, so the window step does nothing there.

The fix: for a MONOCHROME1 file with window tags, _apply_voi_lut undoes the ITK inversion, applies the window, and inverts the image again. It does not change any other file. After the fix, 131 of 131 MONOCHROME1 files matched a reference image made with pydicom only, and 10 MONOCHROME2 files did not change.

docs.title: JPEG 2000 files
docs.text:
For a JPEG 2000 file (transfer syntax 1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.90), ITK inverts around 2**BitsAllocated - 1 (65535), not 2**BitsStored - 1 (4095). So a 12-bit value of 95 becomes 65440, not 4000. With the wrong M, the window (for example center 2047, width 4095) sees only the values 61440 to 65535. Every pixel is then out of the window, and the image is all black. This happened in the VinDr-CXR JPEG 2000 files.

It is easy to see which case a file is in: an inverted 12-bit JPEG 2000 value is 61440 or more, far above 4095. When a value is above M, _apply_voi_lut uses 2**BitsAllocated - 1. In 20 of 20 VinDr JPEG 2000 files, the values were in 0 to 4095 after the step undid the inversion.

docs.title: Files with no HighBit tag
docs.text:
A pixel is stored in 16 bits (BitsAllocated 16), but often only 12 or 15 of the bits are used (BitsStored). HighBit says where the used bits are. It is almost always BitsStored - 1. Some CheXpert Plus files have no HighBit tag. pydicom then uses BitsStored - 1 and reads the file correctly. ITK reads the wrong bits, and every pixel is 1, so the image is blank.

We tried to sample 400 files from each of 16 DICOM datasets. VinDr-CXR train and VinDr-CXR test count as 2. We could not read 2 of them. Only CheXpert Plus has the problem. About 5% of its files have no HighBit (366 files in a larger sample), and 259 of these loaded blank. These datasets had HighBit in every sampled file:

  • 2-D: MIMIC-CXR, VinDr-CXR (train and test), SIIM-ACR, SIIM-COVID, RSNA Pneumonia, BRAX, Emory CXR and Emory CHORUS.
  • 3-D: RSNA PE, RSNA Cervical Spine, RSNA Abdominal Trauma and RSNA Lumbar Spine.

We could not check VinDr-PCXR and OpenI, because we had no read access to them at that time.

The fix: ITK stays the reader. _fix_missing_highbit reads the header of each DICOM file. When the file has no HighBit tag, it reads the pixels again with pydicom. It writes them in the ITK form (rescale applied, MONOCHROME1 inverted with M), so the next steps do not change.

_fix_missing_highbit does nothing for a file with HighBit, and for a color file (SamplesPerPixel not 1). When pydicom cannot decode the file, it warns and keeps the ITK pixels. The cost is one more header read for each DICOM image.

The other choice was to drop these files in the CheXpert Plus harmonizer. That needs a header read of every file before the first use, and it drops about 5% of the images. After the fix, all 366 sampled files with no HighBit matched the pydicom reference. 58 of 58 files with HighBit did not change.

docs.title: Any file name
docs.text:
At first, _apply_voi_lut ran only on a path that ends in .dcm. The VinDr-CXR and VinDr-PCXR files end in .dicom, so they had no window. About 97% of the VinDr-CXR files have window tags, and no file has a VOI LUT sequence. On 60 VinDr-CXR test files, the window changed 11 images by more than 0.01 (mean absolute difference on [-1, 1]), and one image by 0.36.

The fix first added .dicom to the file name check. Now both DICOM steps find a DICOM file by its Photometric Interpretation tag, with any file name (see The 2-D load steps). This fix needs the JPEG 2000 fix, because many VinDr-CXR files are JPEG 2000.

docs.title: Partial downloads in CheXpert Plus
docs.text: The CheXpert Plus DICOM folder that we downloaded has partial downloads with names like .azDownload-<id>-view1_frontal.dcm (18 in a sample of CheXpert Plus files). They are not valid DICOM files. The harmonizer makes each image_path from the CSV file, so it never reads them. They are still there on 2026-11-04.

docs.title: After an update
docs.text:
The fixes above were made before 2026-11-02. Since 2026-11-02, the key of a cache_dir folder holds the code of each cached step (D-15). So a cache folder from before that date is not read again, and you do not need to delete it for these fixes. Delete it only to free the disk. An embedding cache from before 2026-11-03 raises ValueError (D-41). Delete it and run again.

A fix in a helper that a step calls, for example stored_value_sum, does not change the cache key. After such a fix, delete the cache yourself (Cache the samples).

docs.title: Check it yourself
docs.text: The notebook notebooks/datasets/dicom_monochrome_voi_verify.ipynb runs the checks on this page again. It shows the affected images: the old load, the fixed load and the pydicom reference. Its output has patient images, so clear the output before a commit.

docs.title: Label policy
docs.text:
Each source writes its labels in its own way. One dataset writes 1.0, 0.0, -1.0 and blanks. Another writes a list of finding names, or one grade from 0 to 4. RadHarmony puts the labels of every dataset in one format. So a probe can use the label columns of any dataset with no code for that dataset (D-05).

This page explains the rules and why we chose them. The page of each dataset gives its own label rules (Dataset catalog).

docs.title: The 4 codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning What the probes do 1 Positive: the finding is there Use it 0 Negative: the finding is not there Use it -1 Uncertain: the source says "maybe" Skip it NaN Not mentioned, or not known Skip it

These codes are the CheXpert codes, which many papers use. The probes fit and score each label only on the rows where it is 0 or 1. So a NaN label is not a negative. The project keeps -1 in cls (D-05). Before, -1 became NaN, so cls lost the difference between "uncertain" and "not mentioned".

docs.title: Uncertain labels
docs.text:
The dataset classes of CheXpert, CheXpert Plus, CheXphoto, MIMIC-CXR and MIMIC-CXR-JPG take the argument drop_uncertain. With True, the class drops each row with -1 in any label. With False, the row stays, and cls keeps -1. The default is True in most classes. The labeled MIMIC-CXR-JPG test class keeps -1 by default. The page of each dataset gives its default.

PadChest also has drop_uncertain, but there it drops the rows labeled exclude or suboptimal_study.

docs.title: Blank labels
docs.text:
A CheXpert-style source leaves a label blank when the report does not mention the finding. The argument not_mentioned sets what a blank gives:

  • "negative" (the default) gives 0, as most CheXpert papers do.
  • "nan" keeps NaN, so the probes skip it.

Why 0 is the default: 73% of the CheXpert train label cells are blank. With NaN, each probe trains only on the few rows that mention its finding. For example, Pleural Other is blank in 97% of the CheXpert train rows.

docs.title: A row with no label at all
docs.text: Some rows have no label at all. Examples: a PadChest row whose label list is empty, or a CheXpert-style row where every label is blank. Such a row gets NaN in every label (D-05). This is also true with not_mentioned="negative", because the label is unknown, not negative. Example: 777 PadChest rows have the raw Labels value [''], and their reports name findings such as scoliosis. As negatives, they would teach the probe wrong labels.

docs.title: Other rules
docs.text:
• A class that a source does not annotate gets NaN, not 0. Example: the MedSeg dataset2 masks have no pleural effusion class, so pleural_effusion is NaN in these rows.
  • A blank source value that a harmonizer splits into one-hot columns gives NaN in all of these columns, not
  • Example: a blank RSNA 2024 lumbar severity gives NaN in normal_mild, moderate and severe.
  • A trigger word sets only its own finding. Example: the OpenI term Lung/hypoinflation does not set atelectasis.
  • A harmonizer can keep raw grades, for example the TAIX-Ray grades 0 to 4. Its dataset class maps them to 0 and 1 by default (label_mode="binary"), and "ordinal" keeps the grades (TAIX-Ray).
  • A regression target, for example the bone age, goes in its own columns (REG_COLS) and in reg, not in cls.

docs.title: Label names
docs.text: Label columns have snake case names: pleural_effusion, not Pleural Effusion. The harmonizer sorts them in alphabetical order, and cls uses the same order (D-05). So the names and the order of cls do not depend on the source. Box labels (bbox_labels) use snake case too (D-07).

docs.title: Labels from report text
docs.text: Some labels come from the free text of a report, not from a label file. Then a rule must decide what a phrase means. Example: "stable cardiomegaly" means that the heart is still large, so the finding is present (D-44). MIMIC-CXR label extraction uses such rules.

docs.title: MIMIC-CXR label extraction
docs.text:
TAIX-Ray gives each finding a grade from 0 to 4 (0 to 3 for heart size). Some findings also have a grade for each side (left and right). MIMIC-CXR-JPG gives only the CheXpert codes (1, 0, -1 or blank), with no grade and no side. These codes cannot become TAIX-Ray grades.

But the free-text MIMIC-CXR reports often say how large a finding is and on which side. So a script reads the reports and finds the grade and the side with regular expressions. It runs on the local computer, with no external API, so no report leaves the computer.

The script is extract_mimic_labels.py in the separate phase_grounding project. It is not in this repo. This page explains what it does and where it can be wrong. The numbers on this page come from its output file mimic_taix_labels.parquet, read on 2026-11-04.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The output has one row for each MIMIC-CXR study (version 2.1.0 reports). The script skips a study with no report file. It has 13 columns:

Column Values subject_id, study_id The MIMIC-CXR IDs, as integers atelectasis, pleural_effusion, pulmonary_opacities The grade of the finding: the larger of the left and right grades atelectasis_left, atelectasis_right, pleural_effusion_left, pleural_effusion_right, pulmonary_opacities_left, pulmonary_opacities_right The grade on one side heart_size, pulmonary_congestion The grade of the finding. These findings have no side

The grades:

Grade Words in the sentence 0 no, without, absent, resolved, clear, free of, no evidence of, normal, unremarkable, within normal, stable, unchanged, not enlarged 1 trace, minimal, tiny, subtle, subcentimeter, micro, small 2 mild, slight, early, low-grade, minor. Also the default when the sentence has no grade word 3 moderate, moderate-sized 4 large, severe, massive, extensive, significant, marked, considerable NaN The report does not mention the finding

The TAIX-Ray heart_size has the grades 0 to 3 (TAIX-Ray). The script gives heart_size the grades 0 to 4, so grade 4 has no TAIX-Ray match.

docs.title: How a report becomes grades
docs.text:
The script uses the FINDINGS section of the report. With no FINDINGS section, it uses the IMPRESSION section. With neither, it uses the full text. It splits the text into sentences at each ., ; and new line.

A sentence mentions a finding when it has one of the words of that finding:

Finding Words (and their forms) atelectasis atelectasis, atelectatic pleural_effusion pleural effusion, pleural fluid, hydrothorax, effusion pulmonary_opacities opacity, infiltrate, consolidation, airspace disease heart_size cardiomegaly, enlarged heart, cardiac enlargement, enlargement of the heart, heart size, cardiac silhouette, "heart is ... enlarged" pulmonary_congestion pulmonary edema, interstitial edema, vascular congestion, vascular engorgement, vascular plethora, "vascular markings ... prominent"

For each sentence that mentions the finding, the script finds every grade word of the sentence. When the sentence has a grade word above 0, the highest such grade wins. A word of grade 0 counts only when the sentence has no grade word above 0. A sentence with no grade word gives 2. Over all sentences of the report, the highest grade wins.

The side of a lateral finding (atelectasis, pleural effusion, opacities) comes from the same sentence:

  • "bilateral", "bibasilar", "bibasal", "basal", "both lung" or "both side" give both sides. The plurals "both lungs" and "both sides" do not match.
  • "left" and "right" in one sentence give both sides.
  • Only "left" gives the left side. Only "right" gives the right side.
  • A sentence with no side word gives both sides.

Examples, from a run of the script on 2026-11-04:

Sentence Output "Small bilateral pleural effusions." pleural_effusion 1, left 1, right 1 "IMPRESSION: Moderate pulmonary edema." pulmonary_congestion 3 "Heart size is normal." heart_size 0 "No pleural effusion. Small right pleural effusion." pleural_effusion 1, left 0, right 1

docs.title: What the output looks like
docs.text:
The percent of all studies that mention each finding:

Finding Studies with a grade pleural_effusion 67% pulmonary_opacities 46% heart_size 37% atelectasis 25% pulmonary_congestion 24%

Of the studies that mention atelectasis, 7% have grade 0, 9% grade 1, 78% grade 2, 3% grade 3 and 3% grade 4. In 73% of these studies, the left and right grades are the same. 15% have a grade on the left side only, and 10% on the right side only.

docs.title: Where the output can be wrong
docs.text:
• Grade 2 is too common. A finding with no grade word gets 2, for example "Atelectasis is present". So 78% of the atelectasis grades are 2.
  • The side is often a guess. A sentence with no side word gives the grade to both sides. A sentence with both "left" and "right" gives each finding both sides. Example: "Left lower lobe opacity and right pleural effusion." gives both sides to the opacity and to the effusion. "Basal" gives both sides, so "Mild basal atelectasis on the left." gives both sides. "Opacities in both lungs, worse on the left." gives the left side only.
  • A negation covers the full sentence, not one finding. A grade word above 0 wins over a negation. Example: "No pleural effusion but mild atelectasis." gives pleural_effusion 2, not 0, because "mild" (grade 2) is in the same sentence.
  • A FINDINGS section ends at the first header word, also inside a sentence and in lower case. The header words are FINDINGS, IMPRESSION, TECHNIQUE, COMPARISON, INDICATION, EXAMINATION, HISTORY and PROCEDURE. Example: the report "FINDINGS: In comparison with the study of ___, there is a new large left pleural effusion." gives the section "In". So the report gets no grade.
  • The word "effusion" alone counts as a pleural effusion. Example: "Small pericardial effusion." gives pleural_effusion 1 on both sides.
  • "Prominent vascular markings." gives no grade, because the pattern needs "vascular marking" followed by "prominent", or the singular "prominent vascular marking".
  • Grade 1 has another meaning than in TAIX-Ray. In TAIX-Ray, grade 1 is "Questionable". Here, grade 1 is a small finding, for example "small effusion".
  • "Stable" gives 0. Example: "Stable cardiomegaly." gives heart_size 0. The project decision D-44 says that a stable finding is present, with grade 2. The script does not follow D-44 yet.

docs.title: Use the grades with RadHarmony
docs.text:
subject_id and study_id match the patient_id and study_id of the MIMIC-CXR-JPG harmonized table, after you change the IDs from integers to text. This block adds the grades to the table of the official train split. The prefix taix_ keeps the grade columns apart from the CheXpert label columns with the same names, for example pleural_effusion.

import pandas as pd
from radharmony.dataset import MIMICCXRJPGTrainDataset

ds = MIMICCXRJPGTrainDataset(base_image_dir="/data/mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/files/", output_cls=True)
df = ds.get_harmonized_df()

grades = pd.read_parquet("/data/phase_grounding/mimic_taix_labels.parquet")
grades = grades.astype({"subject_id": str, "study_id": str}).rename(columns={"subject_id": "patient_id"})
grades = grades.set_index(["patient_id", "study_id"]).add_prefix("taix_").reset_index()
merged = df.merge(grades, on=["patient_id", "study_id"], how="left")
print(len(merged) == len(df), merged["taix_pleural_effusion"].notna().mean().round(2))  # True 0.7

The grades are extra columns of the table. A dataset class made with harmonized_df=merged keeps the 14 CheXpert labels in cls, because it takes its label columns from its harmonizer.

The phase_grounding project also has a Gradio app, eval_app.py, on port 7861. Its tabs run the script on a report that you paste, and show the rows of the output file.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Label policy: the label codes of RadHarmony.
  • MIMIC-CXR-JPG and TAIX-Ray.

docs.title: How we test RadHarmony
docs.text: A small change in shared code can change the numbers of every dataset, with no error. Example: the code swaps x and y in a bounding box. Each box then points to the wrong part of the image, but the code still runs. The tests and checks on this page find such problems before a change merges. This page gives an overview, and then the commands to run the tests yourself.

docs.title: What we test
docs.text:
The tests are in tests/, and pytest runs them.

Kind What it checks Data it needs Unit tests One function or class on small made-up inputs. Examples: a transform moves each box with the image, and a metric gives the same value as scikit-learn. None Fake-data tests Some harmonizers on a few rows of fake source files, with the real file names and columns. One shared test (the contract test) checks the output table. Examples: the table is the same after save and load, the label columns are sorted, and image_path is relative to the image folder. None Real-data tests harmonize() on the real source files of each dataset. The numbers of images, patients, positives for each label, and patients of each sex must match expected_stats in configs/datasets/<key>.json. The contract test also runs on each real table. The dataset Lesson tests A real mistake from the past, turned into a test so that it cannot come back. Each test has a row in eval/RULES.md. Some need a dataset Repo tests pyproject.toml lists each package that the code imports. Each registry key gives a class. The config files are valid. The script and app functions work on fake files. None

A test skips when the things it needs are not there. Examples:

  • A data test skips when configs/data_paths.json has no entry for its dataset, or when the folder cannot be read (Data paths for the checks).
  • A test skips when it needs an optional package or a GPU that is not installed.

A skip is not a pass. CI has no data, so it skips all the real-data tests.

docs.title: Other automatic checks
docs.text:
Pytest is one part of the automatic checks. scripts/evalkit/run_all.py runs all of them, in 3 groups:

Group Checks lint ruff, with only the rules that find bugs. A word check (the STE linter) on docs, docstrings and comments, for example no em dashes. docs Each argument table in the docs matches the code. Each import and keyword argument in a doc code block exists, and the blocks marked run=ci run. Each number with a claim note matches its source. Some lesson checks that are scripts, not pytest tests. test Pytest. It also lists the changed files that are base code.

Base code is the code that all datasets or evaluators share, for example radharmony/harmonizer/base.py. A change there can change every result, so it needs the approval of a maintainer.

docs.title: Old problems: the known-problems lists
docs.text:
When a new check starts, the code can already have problems of that kind. We do not fix them all on day one. The lists in eval/known_problems/ hold these old problems.

  • A lint or docs check fails only on a problem that is not on its list. A failing test always fails.
  • Only a new rule may add its old problems to a list. The pull request names the rule on its own line, for example New rule: L-013.
  • No other change may make a list longer. CI checks this on each pull request.
  • When you fix an old problem, remove it from the list. So the lists get shorter.

Example: a new docstring with an em dash fails the lint group. An old docstring with an em dash on the list does not fail.

docs.title: When the checks run
docs.text:
When What runs Data Each commit (commit hook) run_all.py --fast: the lint and docs checks on the staged files only. No pytest, and no doc block runs. A commit that changes base code needs a BASE CODE CHANGE: line in its message. None Before you push The quick run, run_all.py: the 3 groups on all files. With many datasets in your data paths file, it can take more than 1 hour. Only the datasets in your data paths file Each pull request (GitHub CI) tests.yml: pytest. checks.yml: the lint and docs groups, the check that no list got longer, and the check that a base-code change has approval text. None Before a release (maintainers) The full run, run_all.py --full: the quick run, plus every doc code block and the number claims that need the data. A block that cannot run because data, a package or a GPU is missing is "blocked", not failed. All datasets, and a GPU for some blocks

CI installs the newest versions of the packages that pyproject.toml allows, the same way a new user installs them. So CI also finds a problem that comes from a new package release, not only from our code.

docs.title: Run the tests yourself
docs.text:
Run these commands in a clone of the repo, with its venv (Install).

  1. Install the test tools once:

    uv pip install -e . --group dev        # radharmony, pytest, ruff and vulture
git config core.hooksPath .githooks    # turns on the commit hooks

  2. Run the checks:

    .venv/bin/python scripts/evalkit/run_all.py --group lint,docs   # lint and docs only, about 20 seconds
.venv/bin/python scripts/evalkit/run_all.py                     # quick run: lint, docs and pytest

    run_all.py prints a table with one row for each check. A new problem starts with NEW, for example NEW ste: docs/wiki/how-to/cache.md:12: [STE-01] 27 words: .... The last line is automatic checks: PASS or automatic checks: FAIL.

  3. To run only some tests, call pytest:

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_transforms.py -v   # one file
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -k montgomery -rs     # tests with "montgomery" in the name, with skip reasons

  4. To run the real-data tests of a dataset, give its folders in a data paths file (Data paths for the checks):

    cp configs/data_paths.example.json configs/data_paths.json
# Keep the entry of your dataset, for example montgomery_cxr, and give its real folders. Then:
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_dataset_stats.py -k montgomery -v

    If a test still skips, -rs prints the reason. Example: the folder cannot be read.

docs.title: A new test for each fix
docs.text:
• A bug fix starts with a test that fails. Then the fix makes it pass.
  • The expected value comes from the source data or the paper, not from the code. A value copied from the code passes even when the code is wrong. Example: the expected image count comes from the dataset paper, not from a run of harmonize().
  • A mistake that happens 2 times, or one time with a large effect, becomes a rule in eval/RULES.md. If a computer can check the rule, the rule gets a test or a check. A script proves that the test fails on the old mistake and passes on the fix.

docs.title: Review by agents
docs.text: The automatic checks find only the problems that we already know how to check. The /evaluate skill of Claude Code adds a review by agents. Bug hunters must prove each bug with a command and its output. A second agent, the checker, runs each proof again and drops the proofs that do not repeat. A lesson from the review becomes a new rule, as in the section above. The steps are in eval/PIPELINE.md.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Design decisions: the expected behaviors that the tests check.
  • eval/RULES.md: the rules and the check for each rule.
  • CONTRIBUTING.md: the commands, and how to send a pull request.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
RadHarmony has 3 main parts: the harmonizer, the dataset class and the evaluator. Each part passes one thing to the next part.

source files (CSV, JSON, DICOM, PNG, NIfTI, RLE masks, ...)
   │  harmonizer: harmonize()
   ▼
harmonized table (pandas DataFrame, one row for each image)
   │  dataset class + transform
   ▼
samples {"img": Tensor, "cls": Tensor, "mask": ..., "bbox": ..., "report": ...}
   │  evaluator + backbone recipe (transform, encoder)
   ▼
result table (pandas DataFrame) → results.csv, results_summary.csv

docs.title: Harmonizer
docs.text:
A harmonizer reads the source files of one dataset and returns the harmonized table. Each dataset has its own harmonizer class, for example MontgomeryCXRHarmonizer. All of them inherit from BaseHarmonizer. harmonize() runs the same steps for every dataset (_build_patient_id(), _build_image_path(), _build_labels(), _build_bbox(), ...). A harmonizer changes these steps, not harmonize() (D-30).

h.save(path) saves the table. MontgomeryCXRHarmonizer.load_from_saved(path) gives back a harmonizer with the same harmonized_df (D-08). So you harmonize a large dataset only one time (Save and reuse a harmonized table).

docs.title: Harmonized table
docs.text:
The harmonized table is the only input of the rest of the code (D-01). After harmonize(), no class reads the source files again.

  • Required columns: patient_id, study_id and image_path.
  • Optional columns: the label columns, bbox, bbox_labels, mask_path, report, view_position, age_years, sex and more (D-01).
  • One row is one image (D-03). Some datasets use one row for each study, series or volume. Their page says so.
  • image_path is relative to base_image_dir, so the same table works on any computer (D-04).
  • Label columns have snake case names, in alphabetical order. A label is 1, 0, -1 (uncertain) or NaN (Label policy).

docs.title: Dataset class
docs.text:
A dataset class wraps the harmonized table in a MONAI PersistentDataset (a plain MONAI Dataset when cache_dir=None). Give it base_image_dir, and it looks for each source file only at 3 places: the path that you give, base_image_dir/<name> and <parent of base_image_dir>/<name>. It does not search other folders (D-35). Each official split has its own class, for example VinDrCXRTrainDataset and VinDrCXRTestDataset (D-09). Each class also has a registry key, for example vindr_cxr_train. resolve_dataset("vindr_cxr_train") in radharmony.registry gives the class (Dataset catalog).

A sample, ds.get_datasets()[i], is a dict. It always has img. Each output_* flag adds its own key: output_cls adds cls, output_mask adds mask, output_bbox adds bbox and bbox_labels, output_report adds report and output_reg adds reg. output_bbox also adds bbox_findings when the class has it. A flag that the dataset does not support gives a warning and no key (D-11).

The transform loads and prepares each image. The default is RadiologyTransform2D or RadiologyTransform3D (Transforms). A 2-D image is scaled to [-1, 1] (D-14). cache_dir stores the prepared images before the first random step (D-15). So a random step, for example a random flip, runs again each time you read a sample. See Dataset API for all keys and arguments.

docs.title: Evaluator and backbone recipe
docs.text:
A backbone recipe, for example make_raddino(), returns a transform and an encoder. The transform prepares the image as the model authors did (D-16). The encoder turns a batch of images into features (Backbones).

An evaluator takes an encoder and a dataset made with the recipe's transform. It runs the task and returns the result table: one row for each label and run. save_results() writes results.csv and results_summary.csv (Evaluators). The frozen-feature probes L2-normalize the features (D-17).

docs.title: Box order
docs.text:
A box is [dim0_min, dim0_max, dim1_min, dim1_max], row first. For a 2-D image, this is [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max], not [x, y, w, h]. A 3-D box adds dim2_min, dim2_max. The values are fractions in [0, 1] of the image size (D-07). Example: on a 1000 × 2000 (H × W) image, a box from row 100 to row 300 and from column 500 to column 1000 is [0.1, 0.3, 0.25, 0.5]. Why rows first: the first axis of a numpy array is the row, so img[y0:y1, x0:x1] uses the box in its own order.

  • In a sample, the box matches sample["img"]. Each resize, pad, crop, flip and warp of the default transforms moves the box with the image (D-28).
  • bbox is a float32 tensor of shape (N, 4) (2-D) or (N, 6) (3-D). Use radharmony.dataset.bbox_collate to batch samples with different box counts.
  • A harmonizer clips each box to the image, and drops a box with no area (D-07).
  • The model processor of a backbone recipe can crop or pad the image. The box does not move with these steps. The recipe transform warns when bbox is in output_keys and the processor does more than resize.
  • A 3-D volume is reoriented to axcodes (default IPL) and then transposed to (D, H, W). The box goes through the same 2 steps (D-12).

docs.title: Splits
docs.text:
There are 2 kinds of split:

  • Official splits: when the dataset authors publish a split, each split has its own class and registry key, for example mimic_cxr_jpg_train and mimic_cxr_jpg_test (D-09). Images with no labels go in a separate test class (D-25). An official split stays as published, also when 2 splits share patients (D-34).
  • Your own splits: get_datasets(n_splits=5) gives a train and a val split, and get_folds() gives k folds. Both split by patient_id, so all images of a patient are in one split (D-10). They split only the rows of that dataset class, so they never mix 2 official splits (Split data).

An evaluator takes one dataset for k folds (dataset=), or a train and a test dataset for a fixed split (train_dataset=, test_dataset=). Its folds and its bootstrap also group by patient (D-32).

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Load a dataset and pick outputs: load a dataset and choose its outputs.
  • Run a probe: test an encoder with a probe.
  • Dataset catalog: all datasets and their registry keys.

docs.title: Your first benchmark in 10 minutes
docs.text:
In this lesson, you test how good the RAD-DINO features are at finding tuberculosis (TB) on chest X-rays. You download a small dataset, load it, make the encoder, run a linear probe with 5 folds, and read the result table.

You need a computer with an NVIDIA GPU and about 1.5 GB of free disk space. On our server, all steps took about 3 minutes: the download took 81 s and the Python steps took 70 s.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
Follow Install to clone RadHarmony and make a venv. Then add the raddino extra.

uv pip install -e ".[raddino]"
python -c "import rad_dino; print('ok')"  # ok

docs.title: 2. Download Montgomery County CXR
docs.text:
Montgomery County CXR has 138 chest X-rays, 58 with TB and 80 normal. It needs no account. These commands download it (about 600 MB) to MontgomerySet/ in the current folder.

BASE="https://data.lhncbc.nlm.nih.gov/public/Tuberculosis-Chest-X-ray-Datasets/Montgomery-County-CXR-Set"
wget -q -r -np -nH --cut-dirs=3 -e robots=off --reject "index.html*" "${BASE}/MontgomerySet/index.html"
ls MontgomerySet/CXR_png | wc -l  # 138
# set base_image_dir to MontgomerySet/CXR_png/

The images are in MontgomerySet/CXR_png/. In the next steps, replace /data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/ with the full path of this folder. For other datasets, see Get the data.

docs.title: 3. Load the dataset
docs.text:
The dataset class reads the source files and makes the harmonized table: one row for each image.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset

ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
df = ds.get_harmonized_df()
print(len(df), df["patient_id"].nunique())  # 138 135
print(ds.LABEL_COLS)  # ['tuberculosis']
print(int(df["tuberculosis"].sum()), "images with TB")  # 58 images with TB

sample = ds.get_datasets()[0]
print(sample["img"].shape, sample["cls"])  # torch.Size([1, 224, 224]) tensor([0.])

cache_dir=None turns off the image cache, so the class writes no files. The table has 138 images of 135 patients. The label tuberculosis is 1 for TB and 0 for normal. A sample is a dict: img is the image and cls is the label vector.

docs.title: 4. Make the encoder
docs.text:
make_raddino() returns a transform and an encoder. The transform prepares each image as RAD-DINO needs it. The encoder turns a batch of images into one feature for each image. The first call downloads the RAD-DINO weights (331 MB) from Hugging Face. Then make the dataset again with this transform.

from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
print(ds.get_datasets()[0]["img"].shape)  # torch.Size([3, 518, 518])

Now each image has the size and scale that RAD-DINO needs: 3 channels of 518 × 518.

docs.title: 5. Run the linear probe
docs.text:
The linear probe extracts the features of all images one time. Then it fits and tests a probe 5 times, one time for each fold. Each time, it fits a logistic regression on the images of the other 4 folds, and tests it on this fold. It keeps 10% of the train patients apart (the validation part) to pick the threshold of F1 (D-29). The folds group the images by patient, so all images of one patient are in the same fold.

from radharmony.evaluator import LinearProbeEvaluator

ev = LinearProbeEvaluator(encoder, dataset=ds, n_folds=5, output_dir="outputs/first_benchmark")
results = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(results)
print(results[["fold", "label", "auroc", "auprc", "f1"]].round(3).to_string(index=False))
#  fold         label  auroc  auprc    f1
#     0  tuberculosis  1.000  1.000 1.000
#     1  tuberculosis  0.974  0.975 0.909
#     2  tuberculosis  0.995  0.994 0.957
#     3  tuberculosis  1.000  1.000 1.000
#     4  tuberculosis  0.886  0.856 0.533
#     0 macro_average  1.000  1.000 1.000
#     1 macro_average  0.974  0.975 0.909
#     2 macro_average  0.995  0.994 0.957
#     3 macro_average  1.000  1.000 1.000
#     4 macro_average  0.886  0.856 0.533

The result table has one row for each fold and label. macro_average is the mean over the labels. With only 1 label, it is the same as tuberculosis.

docs.title: 6. Read the summary
docs.text:
save_results() wrote 2 files to outputs/first_benchmark/. results.csv is the table above. results_summary.csv gives, for each metric, the mean over the folds. It also gives the standard deviation (std) and the 95% confidence interval (CI).

import pandas as pd

summary = pd.read_csv("outputs/first_benchmark/results_summary.csv")
cols = ["label", "auroc_mean", "auroc_std", "auroc_ci_lo", "auroc_ci_hi"]
print(summary[cols].round(3).to_string(index=False))
#         label  auroc_mean  auroc_std  auroc_ci_lo  auroc_ci_hi
# macro_average       0.971      0.043        0.895          1.0
#  tuberculosis       0.971      0.043        0.895          1.0

RAD-DINO features find TB with a mean AUROC of 0.971 over the 5 folds.

The AUROC is noisy, because the dataset has only 138 images. Each test fold has about 28 images, so one wrong image changes the AUROC a lot. Here, the AUROC of one fold is 0.886, and the AUROC of 2 other folds is 1.000. Use this dataset to learn the steps. Do not use it to compare encoders. For a real benchmark, use a larger dataset with an official test split.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: RadHarmony needs Python 3.10 or newer. The base install gives the harmonizers, the dataset classes, the evaluators and PyTorch. An extra adds the packages of one backbone, the app or the notebooks.

docs.title: Install with uv
docs.text:
We recommend uv. These commands make a venv and install RadHarmony from the source files.

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh  # only if you do not have uv
git clone https://github.com/f10409/RadHarmony.git
cd RadHarmony
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e .

To add an extra, put its name in brackets. You can give more than one extra.

uv pip install -e ".[raddino]"
uv pip install -e ".[model,app]"

docs.title: Install with pip
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/f10409/RadHarmony.git
cd RadHarmony
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .

Add an extra in the same way, for example pip install -e ".[raddino]".

docs.title: Extras
docs.text:
These are all the extras in pyproject.toml.

Extra What it adds Use it for model torchvision, transformers 5.6 or newer, and the NVIDIA CUDA libraries (cuDNN, cuSPARSELt, NCCL, NVSHMEM) Models in your own code notebook ipykernel, ipywidgets The notebooks in notebooks/ app gradio The app (Use the app) all model, notebook and app All 3 extras above raddino rad-dino RAD-DINO biomed open-clip-torch, transformers, torchvision BiomedCLIP chexagent transformers, sentencepiece, protobuf CheXagent (the vision encoder) medsiglip transformers, sentencepiece, protobuf MedSigLIP siglip2 transformers, sentencepiece, protobuf SigLIP 2 dinov3 transformers DINOv3 medimageinsights mup, fvcore, timm, transformers and 8 more MedImageInsights chexfound omegaconf, torchvision CheXFound eva_x timm, huggingface_hub, torchvision EVA-X ark_plus torchvision Ark+ medical_mae torchvision Medical MAE chexagent_gen transformers 4.40.0, torch 2.7.1, torchvision 0.22.1 and more CheXagent report generator, in its own venv maira2_gen transformers 4.46, huggingface-hub older than 1.0, and more MAIRA-2 report generator, in its own venv medgemma_gen transformers 5.6 or newer, torch 2.7.1, torchvision 0.22.1 and more MedGemma report generator and VQA recipes, in its own venv. Accept the MedGemma license on Hugging Face and log in first radeval RadEval from GitHub (radeval[api]) The report metrics (Run report generation). It needs Python 3.11 or newer

Some backbones also need a clone of the authors' code or a checkpoint. The page of each backbone says what to get (Backbones).

docs.title: More than one venv
docs.text:
The 3 generator extras need versions of transformers and torch that differ from the other extras. So these extras cannot share a venv with the other extras:

  • chexagent_gen: its own venv. It can share a venv only with notebook, app and raddino.
  • maira2_gen: its own venv. It cannot share a venv with chexagent_gen, medgemma_gen, radeval, model, all, biomed, chexagent, medsiglip, dinov3, siglip2 or medimageinsights.
  • medgemma_gen: its own venv. It can share a venv only with notebook, app, raddino and radeval.
  • radeval: it can go in your main venv when that venv has Python 3.11 or newer. On Python 3.10, the extra installs nothing and gives no error. It cannot share a venv with chexagent_gen or maira2_gen.

The [tool.uv] conflicts list in pyproject.toml gives each pair that cannot share a venv. A report generation run uses 2 venvs: the generator venv makes the reports, and the radeval venv scores them. Run report generation makes the 2 venvs.

docs.title: Data paths for the checks
docs.text:
You give the data folders to each dataset class as arguments, so RadHarmony needs no data paths file. The integrity check (scripts/check_datasets.py) and the tests on real data read the folders from configs/data_paths.json. To run them for some datasets, make this file once:

cp configs/data_paths.example.json configs/data_paths.json

Then keep the entries of the datasets that you want to check, and give their real folders. Your copy stays out of git. To keep the file in another place, set RADHARMONY_DATA_PATHS to its path. A dataset with no entry is skipped, and a check of it gives a message that names this file.

docs.title: Claude Code skills
docs.text:
The repo has skills for Claude Code in .claude/skills/: use-radharmony (use the package), add-dataset, add-backbone, evaluate (review the code and docs) and fix. In a clone of the repo, Claude Code loads them with no step. To use a skill in another project, copy its folder to your skills folder:

cp -r .claude/skills/use-radharmony ~/.claude/skills/

add-dataset, add-backbone, evaluate and fix change the repo, so use them in a clone.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
from radharmony.registry import list_datasets

print("montgomery_cxr" in list_datasets())  # True

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Your first benchmark in 10 minutes: run your first benchmark, step by step.
  • Concepts: the parts of RadHarmony and how they work together.

docs.title: Add a backbone
docs.text:
An evaluator needs 2 pieces from a backbone: a dataset transform and an encoder. This page wraps a Hugging Face model in these 2 pieces and runs a probe with them. Then it shows how to make a reusable backbone recipe, a make_<name>() function. To add a recipe to the repo with all its files, use the add-backbone skill.

Before you start, install the raddino extra, and get the Montgomery County CXR data for step 3.

docs.title: 1. Wrap the model
docs.text:
The 2 pieces have separate jobs:

Piece Where it runs What it does Transform (RadiologyEncoderTransform) CPU, in the DataLoader workers Reads the image file, resizes and normalizes it, and gives Tensor[C, H, W] Encoder (ImageEncoderWrapper) device (GPU) Runs the model and gives the feature, Tensor[B, D] (Encoder contract)

So each model reads and normalizes its images with its own code. No other step normalizes them again (D-16). This step makes the encoder, and step 2 makes the transform.

ImageEncoderWrapper is an nn.Module that holds the model. So .to("cuda"), state_dict(), parameters() and copy.deepcopy() see the model weights. A plain function around a model does not. FinetuneEvaluator raises TypeError for an encoder that is not an nn.Module.

For a Hugging Face model, from_huggingface calls model(pixel_values=x). pool picks the feature: "cls" (the default, the first token), "mean" (the mean of the tokens), "pooler" (pooler_output) or a function (output) -> Tensor[B, D].

from transformers import AutoModel

from radharmony.evaluator import ImageEncoderWrapper

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("microsoft/rad-dino")
encoder = ImageEncoderWrapper.from_huggingface(model, pool="cls").to("cuda")

For other models, from_custom takes model_call(model, x) and pool(output). Both are optional.

import timm

# timm with num_classes=0 gives (B, D), so it needs no function.
encoder = ImageEncoderWrapper.from_custom(timm.create_model("resnet50", pretrained=True, num_classes=0))

# OpenCLIP or BiomedCLIP
encoder = ImageEncoderWrapper.from_custom(clip_model, model_call=lambda m, x: m.encode_image(x))

# Any model: model_call runs it, and pool takes the feature from its output.
encoder = ImageEncoderWrapper.from_custom(
    my_model,
    model_call=lambda m, x: m(x, return_dict=True),
    pool=lambda out: out["features"][:, 0, :],
)

Common model_call functions:

Model family model_call Hugging Face ViT (CLS token) lambda m, x: m(pixel_values=x).last_hidden_state[:, 0] Hugging Face SigLIP or CLIP lambda m, x: m(pixel_values=x).pooler_output OpenCLIP or BiomedCLIP lambda m, x: m.encode_image(x) timm (num_classes=0) None, the model gives (B, D) RAD-DINO (rad-dino package) lambda m, x: m.encode(BatchFeature({"pixel_values": x}))[0]

docs.title: 2. Build the transform
docs.text:
EncoderPreprocessTransform.from_huggingface runs the Hugging Face image processor of the model on each image. reader sets how it opens the image file:

reader What it does "pil" (default) PIL.Image.open(path) as RGB, as in most Hugging Face pretraining. PIL cannot open DICOM "monai" MONAI LoadImage and a transpose to (C, H, W). It reads DICOM and NIfTI. Only for 2-D images a function Your own (path) -> image None No read. A step before it has loaded the image

Both readers give values from 0 to 255, because the processor divides by 255. An 8-bit image keeps its values. A reader scales a 12-bit or 16-bit image with its minimum and maximum, for example a 16-bit PadChest PNG. A reader never clips (D-27). "monai" gives a DICOM file the HighBit fix and the window (VOI LUT) of a MONOCHROME image (D-13). It reads a palette or RGBA PNG as the RGB image it shows, and an LA PNG as gray.

RadiologyEncoderTransform puts this step in a MONAI transform for the dataset. output_keys sets the keys of each sample. It has the same augmentation steps as RadiologyTransform2D, for example .with_flip(spatial_axis=1).

from radharmony.evaluator import EncoderPreprocessTransform, RadiologyEncoderTransform

pp = EncoderPreprocessTransform.from_huggingface(keys=["img"], processor="microsoft/rad-dino", reader="pil")
transform = RadiologyEncoderTransform(preprocess=pp, output_keys={"img", "cls"}).get_transform()

For a model with no Hugging Face processor, write a function that does all steps, from the path to Tensor[C, H, W]:

pp = EncoderPreprocessTransform.from_custom(keys=["img"], preprocess=my_preprocess)

Notes on the transform:

  • The image tensor is torch.bfloat16 by default. The evaluators run the encoder under autocast, so an encoder with float32 weights takes the bfloat16 image. For an encoder that cannot autocast, pass RadiologyEncoderTransform(..., dtype=torch.float32). Each built-in encoder recipe also takes dtype=. The labels (cls, reg, mask) are always float32.
  • A box ("bbox" in output_keys) does not follow the crop or the pad of the processor (D-28). So the transform warns when the processor does more than resize. A custom preprocess always warns, unless you pass the Hugging Face processor that it calls: from_custom(..., processor=processor).

docs.title: 3. Run a probe with the 2 pieces
docs.text:
Give the transform to the dataset and the encoder to the evaluator. This block uses the encoder and the transform of steps 1 and 2, on Montgomery.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import LinearProbeEvaluator

ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
df = LinearProbeEvaluator(encoder, dataset=ds, n_folds=5).evaluate()
print(round(df.loc[df["label"] == "macro_average", "auroc"].mean(), 3))  # 0.972

The make_raddino recipe gives 0.971 on the same folds (Run a probe). It loads the same Hugging Face weights with the rad-dino package.

docs.title: 4. Make a reusable recipe
docs.text:
A recipe is one file in radharmony/evaluator/backbones/. Start from _template.py. Follow 3 rules:

  1. Import the model packages inside the function. Then import radharmony works without the extra.
  2. Load the model one time. The transform and the encoder share it.
  3. Do all image steps in the transform. The encoder only runs the model.
# radharmony/evaluator/backbones/my_model.py
import monai.transforms as mt
import torch

from radharmony.evaluator.backbones._utils import (
    display_255, load_image, squeeze_frame_dim, to_3channel, to_uint8,
)
from radharmony.evaluator.transforms import EncoderPreprocessTransform, RadiologyEncoderTransform
from radharmony.evaluator.wrappers import ImageEncoderWrapper

_MODEL_HUB = "org/my-model"


def make_my_model(device: str = "cuda"):
    """Return (transform, encoder) for MyModel."""
    from transformers import AutoImageProcessor, AutoModel  # inside the function (rule 1)

    _model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(_MODEL_HUB)
    _processor = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained(_MODEL_HUB)

    _loader = mt.Compose([
        load_image(),  # a palette or alpha PNG reads as shown (D-13)
        mt.Lambda(squeeze_frame_dim),
        mt.Transpose(indices=[0, 2, 1]),
        mt.Lambda(display_255),  # DICOM window, 8-bit kept, others scaled to 0..255 (D-13, D-27)
        mt.Lambda(to_3channel),
        mt.Lambda(to_uint8),
    ])

    def _preprocess(path) -> torch.Tensor:
        return _processor(images=_loader(str(path)), return_tensors="pt")["pixel_values"][0]

    def _model_call(m, x):
        return m(pixel_values=x).last_hidden_state[:, 0]  # CLS token

    pp = EncoderPreprocessTransform.from_custom(keys=["img"], preprocess=_preprocess, processor=_processor)
    transform = RadiologyEncoderTransform(preprocess=pp, output_keys={"img", "cls"}).get_transform()
    encoder = ImageEncoderWrapper.from_custom(_model, model_call=_model_call).to(device)
    return transform, encoder

The loader functions of backbones/_utils.py, which all built-in recipes use:

Function What it does load_image() The MONAI image loader. A palette or alpha PNG reads as the image it shows squeeze_frame_dim (C, W, H, 1) to (C, W, H): removes the frame dimension of MONAI display_255 The image as the dataset load shows it, float in 0 to 255 (D-13, D-27) to_3channel (1, H, W) to (3, H, W) to_uint8 0 to 255 to uint8, rounded, with no stretch patches_to_spatial [B, N, D] to [B, D, H, W]: ViT patch tokens to a feature map to_pil_rgb (C, H, W) float to a PIL RGB image, for a PIL processor

Two more cases:

  • Segmentation: when output_keys has "mask", the encoder gives patch features (use patches_to_spatial), and the transform needs mask_preprocess. It gives the mask the same resize and crop as the image, with nearest-neighbor interpolation and no normalization. _template.py shows both.
  • Text and image: return (transform, image_encoder, text_encoder, tokenizer). Then ZeroShotEvaluator can use the recipe. See chexagent.py.

docs.title: 5. Register the recipe
docs.text:
Add the recipe to radharmony/evaluator/backbones/__init__.py:

from .my_model import make_my_model
__all__ = [..., "make_my_model"]

A recipe in the repo also needs these changes. The add-backbone skill lists each step.

  • An install extra in pyproject.toml.
  • A page in docs/wiki/reference/backbones/, and a line in the mkdocs.yml nav.
  • A row in the Backbones table, and in the Extras table.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
• The probe of step 3 gives a result table with an AUROC above 0.5.
  • The feature has the size that the model card gives. A shape check is not enough: a wrong crop or mean still gives the right shape. Run the recipe and the authors' own code on a few real images. The cosine similarity between the 2 features must be near 1 (D-16).

docs.title: Add a dataset
docs.text:
A new dataset needs a harmonizer, a dataset class, an entry in the app, its paths, an integrity check and a wiki page. The add-dataset skill does all the steps with you in Claude Code. Ask it to "add a dataset", and give it the paths of the source files. This page lists the files to make, and shows how to add the dataset to the app.

Before you start, have the source files of the new dataset on your disk, and the list of its labels.

docs.title: 1. Make the files
docs.text:
Do not change base code, for example BaseHarmonizer or BaseRadiologicalDataset. Put the new logic in the files of the new dataset. A base code change needs approval first (D-20).

In this list, <name> is the folder name and <key> is the registry key. For Montgomery County CXR, both are montgomery_cxr.

File What it holds configs/datasets/<name>.json The facts of the dataset: the source files, the ID columns, the labels, the outputs, and expected_stats radharmony/harmonizer/<name>/<name>.py and __init__.py The harmonizer: it reads the source files and gives the harmonized table radharmony/dataset/<name>/<name>.py and __init__.py The dataset class, with @register_dataset("<key>"), LABEL_COLS, SUPPORTED_OUTPUTS and _HARMONIZER_CLS radharmony/harmonizer/__init__.py and radharmony/dataset/__init__.py An import line and an __all__ entry each app.py An import, a build function and a DATASET_REGISTRY entry (see step 2) scripts/check_datasets.py and notebooks/datasets/dataset_integrity_check.ipynb The integrity check: a DatasetSpec in get_specs() of the script, and a cell in the notebook docs/wiki/reference/datasets/<group>/<name>.md The dataset page, a row in the dataset catalog, and a line in the mkdocs.yml nav docs/wiki/how-to/get-the-data.md The download steps of the dataset tests/test_<name>.py and tests/fixtures/fake_datasets.py The tests, and a fake-data builder so that CI runs the dataset with no real data The data paths file An entry for <key>, so that the checks on real data find the folders (Install: data paths)

base_image_dir is the deepest folder that all image files share (D-04). For a dataset with official splits, each split is its own class with its own base_image_dir (D-09).

docs.title: 2. Show the dataset in the app
docs.text:
The app needs a build function and a DatasetConfig entry in DATASET_REGISTRY, both in app.py. The dropdown, the textboxes and the load step use them, so the rest of the app needs no change.

The build function takes the values of the textboxes and the output checkboxes. It returns (dataset, None), or (None, "<message>") to show an error in the app.

def _build_my_dataset(base_dir, csv_path, extra_field, extra_field2, cache_dir, **flags):
    csv = _infer(base_dir, "metadata.csv", user_path=csv_path)  # finds the file next to the images
    if not csv:
        return None, "metadata.csv is required."
    return (
        MyDataset(
            base_image_dir=base_dir,
            csv_path=csv,
            label_csv_path=extra_field or None,  # the first extra textbox
            cache_dir=cache_dir or None,
            output_cls=flags.get("output_cls", False),
            output_mask=flags.get("output_mask", False),
            output_report=flags.get("output_report", False),
            output_bbox=flags.get("output_bbox", False),
        ),
        None,
    )
Argument Textbox or checkbox in the app base_dir "Base image directory". The app checks that the folder exists before it calls the function csv_path "CSV path" extra_field The first extra textbox. The app shows it when extra_field_label or extra_placeholder is not empty extra_field2 The second extra textbox. The app shows it when extra_field2_label or extra_placeholder2 is not empty cache_dir "Cache dir" **flags The output checkboxes: output_cls, output_mask, output_report, output_bbox and output_reg

_infer is radharmony.utils.infer.infer_path, with another name in app.py. It looks for the file only in base_dir and its parent folder (D-35). An empty textbox gives an empty string, not None, except an empty cache_dir, which gives None. A required field that depends on a checkbox goes in the build function too, for example if flags.get("output_mask") and not extra_field: return None, "...".

Then add the entry. The app groups the dropdown by modality and then by dataset family. A family header is a row that starts a family, made with _header("<modality>"). Put each entry after a family header of the same modality. An entry with no header before it raises ValueError when the app starts.

    "── My Dataset ──": _header("CXR"),
    "My Dataset": DatasetConfig(
        is_3d=False,
        extra_field_label="Label CSV (optional)",
        build=_build_my_dataset,
        modality="CXR",
        base_dir_placeholder="e.g. /data/my_dataset/images/",
        csv_placeholder="auto: metadata.csv",
        extra_placeholder="auto: labels.csv",
    ),

An official split gets its own entry, for example "CheXpert (Train)" and "CheXpert (Valid)" (D-09).

The fields of DatasetConfig:

Field Type Default Description is_3d bool required True uses the 3-D transform and shows the HU window controls extra_field_label str required The label of the first extra textbox. "" with no extra_placeholder hides it build callable required The build function modality str required One of SUPPORTED_MODALITIES: "CXR", "Radiograph", "CT", "CT (2D)", "MRI", "VQA" or "Other". Another value raises ValueError. It sets only the group in the dropdown, not the transform extra_field2_label str "" The label of the second extra textbox. "" with no extra_placeholder2 hides it csv_label str "CSV path (optional)" The label of the CSV textbox base_dir_placeholder str "" The gray hint text in the base folder textbox csv_placeholder str "" The gray hint text in the CSV textbox extra_placeholder str "" The gray hint text in the first extra textbox extra_placeholder2 str "" The gray hint text in the second extra textbox extra_dropdown_label str "" The label of an extra dropdown for the dataset. "" hides it extra_dropdown_choices tuple () The choices of the extra dropdown. "(all)" or an empty choice gives None extra_dropdown_kwarg str "" The name of the build function argument that gets the dropdown value is_group_header bool False True for a family header. _header() sets it bbox_default bool False The start value of the BBox checkbox for this entry (D-11)

To add datasets to the app with no edit of app.py, write a module with a function register_app_datasets(registry, DatasetConfig, _header, app_dtype) that adds entries to registry. Then start the app with RADHARMONY_APP_PLUGINS=<module> python app.py. A module that raises an error, or adds an entry with no family header, is not loaded. The app prints a message and starts without it.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
The new registry key is in the registry. This block uses montgomery_cxr. Use your own key.

from radharmony.registry import list_datasets, resolve_dataset

print("montgomery_cxr" in list_datasets())  # True
print(resolve_dataset("montgomery_cxr").__name__)  # MontgomeryCXRDataset

The integrity check of the dataset passes (exit code 0). Name its DatasetSpec by the registry key, or <registry key>_<variant> for a second check of the same class. --list prints all names.

python scripts/check_datasets.py --datasets <key> --max-samples 30

In the app (python app.py), the dataset is in the dropdown, and a load shows the first sample.

docs.title: Cache the samples
docs.text:
Each sample needs a load step and preprocessing steps. These steps are slow. The cache keeps their result on the disk, so the next epochs and the next runs read it back. Fill the cache before training to make the first epoch as fast as the others. The examples use Montgomery County CXR.

Before you start, get the Montgomery data.

docs.title: 1. Pick the cache folder
docs.text:
cache_dir is the cache folder. The default is "./cache". cache_dir=None gives no cache, so each access loads the image again.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset

ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir="./cache",  # a fast local disk is best
)
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)

The cache is a MONAI PersistentDataset. It writes a sample to the disk the first time that the code reads the sample. The cache keeps the tensors before the first random step, so each epoch gets a new augmentation. A new load or preprocessing step, for example a new img_size, gives a new cache folder. Dataset API: Cache gives the folder layout and when to delete it.

docs.title: 2. Fill the cache before training
docs.text:
pre_cache() reads each sample one time, before the training starts. It uses a DataLoader with batch_size=1 and shows a progress bar. num_workers is the number of processes that load the samples.

ds.pre_cache(train_ds, num_workers=4)
ds.pre_cache(val_ds, num_workers=4)
# Pre-caching: 100%|██████████| 110/110
# Pre-caching: 100%|██████████| 28/28

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
The cache folder has one folder for each split, and each split folder holds one key folder:

import os

print(sorted(os.listdir("./cache")))
# ['train', 'val']
print(len(os.listdir(os.path.join("./cache/train", os.listdir("./cache/train")[0]))))
# 110

docs.text:

  • D-15 and D-49 in Design decisions.

docs.title: Compare backbones
docs.text:
To compare 2 or more encoders, run the same probe on the same dataset with each backbone recipe. Then put the results in one table. This page compares RAD-DINO, DINOv3 and BiomedCLIP with the linear probe on Montgomery County CXR (138 images).

Before you start, install the extras of the recipes, and get the Montgomery data.

uv pip install -e ".[raddino,dinov3,biomed]"

docs.title: 1. Run the probe with each recipe
docs.text:
Each recipe has its own transform, so each recipe gets its own dataset object. Each recipe also gets its own embedding_cache path, named after the recipe, for example montgomery_raddino. A cache file from a different encoder raises ValueError. Keep the dataset, n_folds and base_seed the same for all recipes. Then all recipes get the same folds and the same validation part.

import gc

import torch

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import LinearProbeEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_biomed_clip, make_dinov3, make_raddino

recipes = {"raddino": make_raddino, "dinov3": make_dinov3, "biomed_clip": make_biomed_clip}
for name, make in recipes.items():
    transform, encoder = make(device="cuda")[:2]  # a text-and-image recipe also gives a text encoder
    ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
        base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
        transform=transform,
        output_cls=True,
        cache_dir=None,
    )
    ev = LinearProbeEvaluator(
        encoder,
        dataset=ds,
        n_folds=5,
        embedding_cache=f"outputs/cache/montgomery_{name}",
        output_dir=f"outputs/compare/{name}",
    )
    ev.save_results(ev.evaluate())  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
    del transform, encoder, ds, ev  # the transform also holds the model: free the GPU memory
    gc.collect()
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()

In a real run on a shared GPU, the 3 recipes took about 2 minutes. For DINOv3, save_results() warns that ppv (the positive predictive value) is NaN in 1 of the 5 folds (D-19).

docs.title: 2. Make one table
docs.text:
Read the results_summary.csv of each backbone, and keep the macro_average row. The summary gives the mean, the std and the 95% CI over the 5 folds (Result table).

import pandas as pd

summary = pd.concat(
    pd.read_csv(f"outputs/compare/{name}/results_summary.csv").assign(backbone=name) for name in recipes
)
table = summary[summary["label"] == "macro_average"].set_index("backbone")
print(table[["auroc_mean", "auroc_std", "auroc_ci_lo", "auroc_ci_hi", "f1_mean"]].round(3))
#              auroc_mean  auroc_std  auroc_ci_lo  auroc_ci_hi  f1_mean
# backbone
# raddino           0.971      0.043        0.895        1.000    0.880
# dinov3            0.869      0.082        0.747        0.964    0.575
# biomed_clip       0.932      0.084        0.786        0.997    0.701
table.to_csv("outputs/compare/table.csv")

With 138 images and 5 folds, the std is large. A difference between 2 backbones that is smaller than the std can come from the split only. For a real comparison, use a larger dataset, or the fixed-split mode with n_bootstrap (Split modes).

A second run with the same embedding_cache path reads the features from the file. It still builds the recipe, but it does not run the encoder on the images. So you can add a probe, for example KNNProbeEvaluator, at a low cost. Run a probe writes the same montgomery_raddino file, so a run of both pages extracts the RAD-DINO features one time. To add a recipe, add it to recipes and run step 1 again.

docs.text:

  • outputs/cache/ has one .pkl file for each backbone.
  • outputs/compare/table.csv has one row for each backbone.

docs.title: Montgomery County CXR
docs.text:
The server has no zip file. These commands copy the MontgomerySet/ folder (about 600 MB) to the current folder.

BASE="https://data.lhncbc.nlm.nih.gov/public/Tuberculosis-Chest-X-ray-Datasets/Montgomery-County-CXR-Set"
wget -q -r -np -nH --cut-dirs=3 -e robots=off --reject "index.html*" "${BASE}/MontgomerySet/index.html"
ls MontgomerySet/CXR_png | wc -l  # 138
# set base_image_dir to MontgomerySet/CXR_png/

docs.title: Shenzhen Hospital CXR
docs.text:
The NLM server does not list the files of the root folder. So copy each subfolder on its own. These commands get the images, the clinical readings and the top-level files:

BASE="https://data.lhncbc.nlm.nih.gov/public/Tuberculosis-Chest-X-ray-Datasets/Shenzhen-Hospital-CXR-Set"
DEST="./Shenzhen-Hospital-CXR-Set"

# Images and clinical readings
wget --mirror --no-parent --no-host-directories --cut-dirs=3 \
     --reject='index.html*' -e robots=off -P "$DEST" \
     "${BASE}/CXR_png/" "${BASE}/ClinicalReadings/"

# Top-level metadata
wget -P "$DEST" \
     "${BASE}/NLM-ChinaCXRSet-ReadMe.docx" \
     "${BASE}/shenzhen_consensus_roi.csv"

The annotation files (polygon JSON and binary masks) are only for segmentation. To get them, use this Python script. It reads the index pages in Annotations/ to find the file names.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Download Shenzhen supplemental annotation files."""
import os, re, time, urllib.request, urllib.error
from pathlib import Path

BASE = "https://data.lhncbc.nlm.nih.gov/public/Tuberculosis-Chest-X-ray-Datasets/Shenzhen-Hospital-CXR-Set"
DEST = Path("./Shenzhen-Hospital-CXR-Set")
HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"}
CRAWL = ["Annotations/", "Annotations-2/"]

def fetch(url):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=HEADERS)
    for _ in range(3):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
                return r.read()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            if e.code == 404:
                return None
            time.sleep(2)
    return None

def list_dir(url):
    data = fetch(url.rstrip("/") + "/index.html")
    if not data:
        return []
    links = re.findall(r"href='([^']+)'", data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
    out = []
    for l in links:
        if l.startswith("?") or l.startswith("/"):
            continue
        if l.endswith("/index.html"):
            l = l[:-len("index.html")]
        out.append(l)
    return out

def crawl(rel):
    if rel.endswith("/"):
        for child in list_dir(f"{BASE}/{rel.rstrip('/')}"):
            crawl(rel + child)
    else:
        dest = DEST / rel
        if dest.exists() and dest.stat().st_size > 0:
            return
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        data = fetch(f"{BASE}/{rel}")
        if data:
            dest.write_bytes(data)
            print(rel)

for path in CRAWL:
    crawl(path)

# ViewPosition tag, to correct the view. The images always come from the PNG files.
wget -P "$DEST" "${BASE}/NLMCXR_dcm.tgz"
tar -xzf "$DEST/NLMCXR_dcm.tgz" -C "$DEST"

docs.text:
PadChest-GR (grounded reports on PadChest images) is on the BIMCV b2drop share.

The PadChest-GR page gives the layout and the overlap with PadChest.

docs.title: Load a dataset and pick outputs
docs.text:
This page shows how to make a dataset object, pick the keys of each sample and check the image files. The examples use Montgomery County CXR.

Before you start, get the Montgomery data.

docs.title: 1. Make the dataset
docs.text:
Give the class the image folder and the output flags. The class reads the source files and makes the harmonized table.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset

ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_report=True,
    transform=None,  # None gives the default image steps
    cache_dir=None,  # no disk cache
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
data = ds.get_datasets()  # one dataset with all the rows
# UserWarning: 1 of 138 rows have no 'report', so the dataset drops them (D-33).
sample = data[0]
print(sorted(sample))
# ['cls', 'img', 'report']
print(sample["img"].shape, sample["img"].dtype)
# torch.Size([1, 224, 224]) torch.float32
  • base_image_dir is the image folder. The dataset page says which folder it is.
  • Other file arguments, for example csv_path, are on the dataset page.
  • transform=None gives the default transform. It keeps img and the keys of the flags that you set. To change the image size or to add augmentation, give your own transform (Transforms). Set its output_keys to all the keys that you need. If it drops the key of a flag, the dataset class warns (D-11).
  • dtype is the type of img (Transforms: dtype).
  • cache_dir is the cache folder (Cache the samples).

docs.title: 2. Pick the outputs
docs.text:
img is always in the sample. Each output_* flag adds its own keys (Data dict keys). A flag that the class does not support gives a warning and no key:

ds_box = MontgomeryCXRDataset(base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/", output_bbox=True)
# UserWarning: output_bbox=True is not supported by MontgomeryCXRDataset; the 'bbox' key will be absent
# from samples.

With output_report=True in the first block, the dataset drops the 1 Montgomery image with no report (D-33). So data has 1 row less than the table:

print(len(ds.get_harmonized_df()), len(data))
# 138 137

docs.title: 3. Check the image files
docs.text:
verify_images() checks that the file of each image_path is on the disk. It returns the rows with no file.

missing = ds.verify_images()
# All image files exist.
print(len(missing))
# 0
  • With drop_missing=True (the default), the dataset drops these rows. The splits that you make after the call do not have them.
  • With drop_missing=False, the dataset keeps all rows. You only get the list.
  • A relative image_path with base_image_dir=None raises ValueError (D-04).

docs.title: 4. Look at the harmonized table
docs.text:
get_harmonized_df() returns the harmonized table of the dataset, one row for each image.

df = ds.get_harmonized_df()
print(df.columns.tolist()[:7])
# ['patient_id', 'study_id', 'image_path', 'report', 'age_years', 'sex', 'tuberculosis']

Each dataset also has a harmonizer class that makes this table alone, with no dataset object. The "Harmonizer" section of each dataset page shows it. To save the table, or to filter it before the dataset uses it, see Save and reuse a harmonized table.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
• sorted(sample) gives only img and the keys of the flags that you set.
  • verify_images() prints All image files exist., or the number of rows with no file (Dropped N rows ... or Found N rows ... (not dropped)).

  • Dataset catalog: the class and the outputs of each dataset.
  • Split data: official splits, a train and val split, and folds.
  • Transforms: the default image steps and augmentation.

docs.title: Run a probe
docs.text:
A probe scores the frozen features of an encoder on the labels of a dataset. This page runs the linear probe on Montgomery County CXR (138 images, 1 label: tuberculosis) with RAD-DINO. Then it runs the kNN, SVM and prototype probes and zero-shot on the same features. Your first benchmark explains the same linear probe run step by step.

Before you start, install the raddino and biomed extras, and get the Montgomery data.

docs.title: 1. Build the encoder and the dataset
docs.text:
The backbone recipe gives the transform and the encoder. Give the transform to the dataset. output_cls=True adds the labels to each sample.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
print(len(ds.get_harmonized_df()), ds.LABEL_COLS)  # 138 ['tuberculosis']

docs.title: 2. Run the linear probe
docs.text:
n_folds=5 gives 5 folds, grouped by patient. embedding_cache writes the features to a file, so the next probes do not run the encoder again.

from radharmony.evaluator import LinearProbeEvaluator

ev = LinearProbeEvaluator(
    encoder,
    dataset=ds,
    n_folds=5,
    embedding_cache="outputs/cache/montgomery_raddino",
    output_dir="outputs/linear_probe",
)
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
print(df.shape)  # (10, 16)

docs.title: 3. Read the result table
docs.text:
The table has one row for each label and fold, and a macro_average row for each fold. Montgomery has 1 label, so 5 folds give 10 rows. auroc and auprc use no threshold. f1 and the other threshold metrics use the threshold of the validation part (Threshold).

macro = df[df["label"] == "macro_average"]
print(macro[["fold", "auroc", "f1"]].round(3))
#    fold  auroc     f1
# 5     0  1.000  1.000
# 6     1  0.974  0.909
# 7     2  0.995  0.957
# 8     3  1.000  1.000
# 9     4  0.886  0.533
print(round(macro["auroc"].mean(), 3))  # 0.971, the mean AUROC of the 5 folds

results_summary.csv gives the mean, the std and the 95% CI of each metric over the folds. See Your first benchmark: Read the summary and Result table.

docs.title: 4. Switch to another probe
docs.text:
The kNN, SVM and prototype probes take the same arguments. With the same embedding_cache path, they read the features from the file.

from radharmony.evaluator import KNNProbeEvaluator, PrototypeProbeEvaluator, SVMProbeEvaluator

for probe in (KNNProbeEvaluator, SVMProbeEvaluator, PrototypeProbeEvaluator):
    ev = probe(encoder, dataset=ds, n_folds=5, embedding_cache="outputs/cache/montgomery_raddino")
    df = ev.evaluate()
    macro = df[df["label"] == "macro_average"]
    print(probe.__name__, round(macro["auroc"].mean(), 3))
# KNNProbeEvaluator 0.968
# SVMProbeEvaluator 0.983
# PrototypeProbeEvaluator 0.959

Each probe has its own arguments, for example k of the kNN probe. See the evaluator list.

docs.title: 5. Run zero-shot
docs.text:
Zero-shot needs a text-and-image recipe and one text prompt for each label. It does not train, so it uses test_dataset= and no folds. Give it its own cache path, named after the recipe. A cache file from a different encoder raises ValueError.

from radharmony.evaluator import ZeroShotEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_biomed_clip

transform, encoder, text_encoder, tokenizer = make_biomed_clip(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
ev = ZeroShotEvaluator(
    encoder,
    text_encoder,
    prompts={"tuberculosis": ["a chest X-ray with tuberculosis"]},
    negative_prompts={"tuberculosis": ["a normal chest X-ray"]},
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    test_dataset=ds,
    threshold_strategy="fixed:0",  # without it, F1 and the other threshold metrics are NaN
    embedding_cache="outputs/cache/montgomery_biomed_clip",
)
df = ev.evaluate()
print(df.loc[df["label"] == "macro_average", "auroc"].round(3).tolist())  # [0.9]

Zero-shot has no validation part to pick a threshold. With negative prompts, "fixed:0" takes a score above 0 as positive (Zero-shot).

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
• outputs/linear_probe/ has results.csv and results_summary.csv.
  • outputs/cache/ has montgomery_raddino.pkl and montgomery_biomed_clip.test.pkl. Zero-shot adds .test to the name, because it uses test_dataset=.
  • The AUROC of each probe is above 0.5. Montgomery has only 138 images, so the AUROC changes a lot from one fold to the next.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Evaluators: the split modes, the embedding cache and the result table.
  • Linear probe and the pages of the other probes: all arguments.
  • Compare backbones: run one probe with 2 or more backbone recipes.
  • Run segmentation: the probes for masks.

docs.title: Run report generation
docs.text:
ReportGenerationEvaluator runs a report generator on a dataset and scores each generated report against the real report with RadEval. The generator recipes and RadEval need different package versions, so you usually generate in one venv and score in another. This page does both steps on Montgomery County CXR with CheXagent-2.

Before you start, get the Montgomery data. Step 2 needs a GPU.

docs.title: 1. Make the 2 venvs
docs.text:
The chexagent_gen extra (and the maira2_gen extra) conflicts with the radeval extra (the conflicts list in pyproject.toml, and Report generators). So install each one in its own venv. RadEval needs Python 3.11 or newer.

uv venv .venv-chexagent
uv pip install --python .venv-chexagent/bin/python -e ".[chexagent_gen]"
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv-radeval
uv pip install --python .venv-radeval/bin/python -e ".[radeval]"

For MAIRA-2, make .venv-maira2 with the maira2_gen extra in the same way.

docs.title: 2. Generate the reports
docs.text:
Run this step in .venv-chexagent, for example with .venv-chexagent/bin/python. generate_only() writes the generated reports and the real reports to a parquet file. It does not score. output_report=True keeps only the rows with a report. max_samples=4 makes a short test run.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import ReportGenerationEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_chexagent_generator

transform, report_generator = make_chexagent_generator(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_report=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
ev = ReportGenerationEvaluator(report_generator, dataset=ds, batch_size=2, max_samples=4)
ev.generate_only("outputs/report_generation/pairs.parquet")
