The parquet file has the columns sample_id, reference, hypothesis and patient_id. The hypothesis is the raw generated text. In a real run, the 4 reports took 35 seconds. The first row:

sample_id   MCUCXR_0001_0
reference   normal
hypothesis  FINDINGS: The hilar contours are normal. The lungs are clear. ... IMPRESSION: No acute
            cardiopulmonary process.

docs.title: 3. Score the reports
docs.text:
In the RadEval venv, run the scoring script from its place in the repo, not from a copy. It finds radharmony/evaluator/language/hypothesis.py from its own path, so it cleans the text in the same way as evaluate() (D-50). --light uses the 5 metrics of LIGHT_METRICS. Without it, the script uses all 16 metrics. One metric can give more than one score column, for example radgraph gives 3.

.venv-radeval/bin/python notebooks/evaluator/score_reports_radeval.py \
    --pairs-parquet outputs/report_generation/pairs.parquet \
    --output-dir outputs/report_generation/scores \
    --light --n-bootstrap 10
# n=4  results → outputs/report_generation/scores/

The script writes results.csv to --output-dir, with one row of scores (bootstrap is -1) and one row for each bootstrap sample. It also writes results_summary.json, with the number of pairs and the scores of the first row.

docs.title: 4. Or: generate and score in one venv
docs.text:
When the generator and RadEval run in the same venv, evaluate() generates and scores in one call. Use it in place of steps 2 and 3. This block needs a report_generator and a ds that you build as in step 2, in that venv.

from radharmony.evaluator import ReportGenerationEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.metrics import LIGHT_METRICS

ev = ReportGenerationEvaluator(
    report_generator,
    dataset=ds,
    metrics=LIGHT_METRICS,
    max_samples=4,
    n_bootstrap=10,
    output_dir="outputs/report_generation",
)
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv, results_summary.csv and generations.csv

The report generator is any function from the img batch to a list[str] with one report for each image. With the 2 generator recipes, the img batch is a list of image paths. So you can also score your own model in this way.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
• outputs/report_generation/pairs.parquet has up to max_samples rows.
  • outputs/report_generation/scores/results.csv has 11 rows: the scores (bootstrap is -1) and 10 bootstrap samples. Its columns are label, bootstrap, bleu, rouge1, rouge2, rougeL, bertscore, the 3 radgraph_* scores and the 6 f1chexbert_* scores.
  • Montgomery reports are short, for example "normal". So the scores mean little here. Use a dataset with full reports, for example MIMIC-CXR, for a real comparison.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Report generation: the reference sections (ref_section), the metric lists, the arguments and the output files.
  • CheXagent-2 (generator) and MAIRA-2 (generator): the 2 generator recipes.

docs.title: Run segmentation
docs.text:
A segmentation probe trains a small head on the frozen patch features of an encoder, and scores the predicted masks. This page segments the lungs of Montgomery County CXR (138 images) with RAD-DINO. It runs the linear head first, then the conv and the UPerNet heads. The 3 heads take 2-D images and masks only. So a dataset with 3-D masks, for example RSNA 2022 Cervical Spine, does not fit them.

Before you start, install the raddino extra, and get the Montgomery data.

docs.title: 1. Build the encoder and the dataset
docs.text:
Pass output_keys={"img", "mask"} to the backbone recipe. Then the encoder gives patch features, Tensor[B, D, H', W'], and the transform resizes the mask with the image (Segmentation mode). Montgomery has a left and a right lung mask for each image. The dataset joins them into one mask file in mask_output_dir.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_mask=True,
    mask_output_dir="/data/montgomery_lung_masks/",  # any folder you can write to
    cache_dir=None,
)
sample = ds.get_datasets()[0]
print(sample["img"].shape, sample["mask"].shape)  # torch.Size([3, 518, 518]) torch.Size([1, 518, 518])

docs.title: 2. Run the linear head
docs.text:
num_classes=2 is the background and the lung. A short run uses 2 folds and 3 epochs. num_workers=8 reads the large PNG files faster.

from radharmony.evaluator import LinearProbeSegEvaluator

ev = LinearProbeSegEvaluator(
    encoder,
    dataset=ds,
    num_classes=2,
    n_folds=2,
    epochs=3,
    num_workers=8,
    output_dir="outputs/linear_probe_seg",
)
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
print(df[df["label"] == "macro_average"][["fold", "dice", "iou"]].round(3))
#    fold   dice    iou
# 4     0  0.868  0.769
# 5     1  0.854  0.749

In a real run on a shared GPU, this step took about 4 minutes. With cache_dir=None, the dataset reads and resizes each image again in each epoch.

docs.title: 3. Read the result table
docs.text:
The table has one row for each class and fold. class_0 is the background and class_1 is the lung. macro_average is the mean over the classes other than class_0, so here it is the lung score. Each metric is a mean over the test images (Metrics).

print(df["label"].unique().tolist())  # ['class_0', 'class_1', 'macro_average']
print(round(df.loc[df["label"] == "class_1", "dice"].mean(), 3))  # 0.861, the mean lung Dice of the 2 folds

docs.title: 4. Switch to a larger head
docs.text:
The conv and the UPerNet heads take the same arguments, and some of their own. conv_hidden_size sets the channels of the conv head. upernet_hidden_size and upernet_pool_scales set the UPerNet head.

from radharmony.evaluator import ConvProbeSegEvaluator, UPerNetSegEvaluator

heads = {
    "conv": (ConvProbeSegEvaluator, {"conv_hidden_size": 256}),
    "upernet": (UPerNetSegEvaluator, {"upernet_hidden_size": 256, "upernet_pool_scales": (1, 2, 3, 6)}),
}
for name, (probe, head_args) in heads.items():
    ev = probe(
        encoder,
        dataset=ds,
        num_classes=2,
        n_folds=2,
        epochs=3,
        num_workers=8,
        output_dir=f"outputs/{name}_seg",
        **head_args,
    )
    df = ev.evaluate()
    ev.save_results(df)
    print(name, round(df.loc[df["label"] == "macro_average", "dice"].mean(), 3))
# conv 0.95
# upernet 0.959

In the real run, the 2 heads took about 7 minutes. With 3 epochs, the larger heads give a higher Dice than the linear head.

The UPerNet head needs a feature size D that is a multiple of 32 (UPerNet).

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
• outputs/linear_probe_seg/, outputs/conv_seg/ and outputs/upernet_seg/ each have results.csv and results_summary.csv.
  • The lung Dice is above 0.8 for each head. The lungs are large and easy to find. A small target, for example a pneumothorax, gives a much lower Dice.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Linear probe (segmentation): early stopping, the metrics, and how to save the head and predict masks.
  • Conv probe and UPerNet: the head layers and their arguments.
  • Run a probe: the classification probes.

docs.title: Save and reuse a harmonized table
docs.text:
Harmonizing a big dataset can take minutes. Save the harmonized table once, and give the file to the dataset class in the next runs. You can also filter the table first. The examples use Montgomery County CXR.

Before you start, get the Montgomery data.

docs.title: 1. Harmonize and save
docs.text:
save() writes one pickle file. It holds the harmonized table, the label columns and the arguments of the harmonizer.

from radharmony.harmonizer import MontgomeryCXRHarmonizer

h = MontgomeryCXRHarmonizer(base_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/")
df = h.harmonize()
h.save("montgomery_harmonized.pkl")
print(len(df))
# 138

save() writes h.harmonized_df. This is always the table of the last harmonize() call (D-24).

docs.title: 2. Load the file into a dataset
docs.text:
harmonizer_path= loads the file with the harmonizer class of the dataset. The dataset does not read the source files.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset

ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    harmonizer_path="montgomery_harmonized.pkl",
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)
print(ds.LABEL_COLS)
# ['tuberculosis']
  • The label columns are the labels of the harmonizer that are in the table (D-08). Other columns, for example age and age_years, are not labels.
  • A file from another harmonizer class raises ValueError. The message names the class of the file.
  • A split class can load a file from an old class that mixes the splits. This works only when every row of the file is in the split of the class. Otherwise it raises ValueError (D-09).

docs.title: 3. Load the harmonizer from the file
docs.text:
load_from_saved() gives the harmonizer back, with its table. It does not read the source files.

h2 = MontgomeryCXRHarmonizer.load_from_saved("montgomery_harmonized.pkl")
print(h2.harmonized_df.shape)
# (138, 10)

If you moved the data, give the new paths as keyword arguments. They replace the saved arguments of the harmonizer, for example load_from_saved("montgomery_harmonized.pkl", base_dir="/data/new/CXR_png/").

docs.title: 4. Filter the table and give it to the dataset
docs.text:
Harmonize the full dataset first. Then filter the table with pandas (D-02). Give the result with harmonized_df=.

table = h2.harmonized_df
tb_only = table[table["tuberculosis"] == 1]

ds_tb = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    harmonized_df=tb_only,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
print(len(ds_tb.get_datasets()))
# 58
  • The table can also come from a CSV file: h.harmonize().to_csv(...), then pd.read_csv(...). The transform reads a box column in CSV text (Transforms: Boxes).
  • With harmonized_df=, the dataset keeps the LABEL_COLS of its class. If that list is empty, it takes the labels of its harmonizer class that are in the table (D-08).
  • The filter arguments of a dataset class also filter a given table, for example series_filter of RSNA 2024 lumbar (D-02).

On a big dataset, you can harmonize only some studies or patients. harmonize() then keeps only these rows right after it makes the IDs. It still reads the full source file.

few = MontgomeryCXRHarmonizer(base_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/").harmonize(patient_ids=["MCUCXR_0001"])
print(len(few))
# 1
  • The result is the same as a filter after harmonize() (D-02).
  • All image harmonizers take study_ids= and patient_ids=. Of the VQA harmonizers, only MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA takes them.
  • A harmonizer of your own that does not call super().harmonize() filters after it makes every row, and warns.

docs.title: 5. Give a harmonizer or change the table
docs.text:
Give a harmonizer object with harmonizer=, after its harmonize() or load_from_saved(). set_harmonized_df() gives a dataset a new table. The next get_datasets() and get_folds() calls use it.

ds2 = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/", harmonizer=h, output_cls=True, cache_dir=None
)
ds2.set_harmonized_df(tb_only)
print(len(ds2.get_datasets()))
# 58

If you give more than one table, see the order of the table arguments.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
The table from the file is the same as the table of harmonize() (D-08):

import pandas as pd

pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(ds.get_harmonized_df(), df)  # no error

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Load a dataset and pick outputs
  • Dataset API: the shared arguments, with harmonized_df, harmonizer and harmonizer_path.
  • D-02 and D-08 in Design decisions.

docs.title: Split data
docs.text:
This page shows the 3 ways to split a dataset. Use the official split classes for a benchmark. Use a random train and val split, or k folds, when a dataset has no official split. You can also use them to split an official train split.

Before you start, get the Montgomery County CXR data and the ChestX-Det10 data.

docs.title: 1. Use the official splits
docs.text:
When the dataset authors publish a split, each split has its own class and its own registry key (D-09). Each class gives only the rows of its split. Example: ChestX-Det10 has a train class and a test class.

from radharmony.dataset import ChestXDet10TrainDataset
from radharmony.registry import resolve_dataset

train = ChestXDet10TrainDataset(base_image_dir="/data/ChestX-Det10/", output_cls=True, cache_dir=None)
test_cls = resolve_dataset("chestxdet10_test")  # the class of a registry key
test = test_cls(base_image_dir="/data/ChestX-Det10/", output_cls=True, cache_dir=None)
print(len(train.get_datasets()), len(test.get_datasets()))
# 3001 542
  • The "Splits" section of each dataset page gives its split classes and registry keys.
  • An old class that mixes the splits still works, for example MIMICCXRJPGDataset (key mimic_cxr_jpg). Do not use it for a benchmark.
  • MR-RATE has split harmonizers, but no dataset class and no registry key yet.
  • A split class keeps the split as the authors published it, also when 2 splits share patients (D-34). The dataset page says how many patients they share.

docs.title: 2. Make a train and val split
docs.text:
get_datasets(n_splits=5) puts about 1/5 of the patients in the val split. All images of one patient go to the same split (D-10).

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset

ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/", output_cls=True, cache_dir=None)
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)
print(len(train_ds), len(val_ds))
# 110 28
  • random_state=56 (the default) is the seed of the patient draw. The Methods section of the Dataset API lists all arguments.
  • The split does not keep the label ratio the same in train and val.
  • If the train or the val split gets no patient, the call raises ValueError. Example: n_splits=1 (D-10).

docs.title: 3. Make k folds
docs.text:
get_folds() shuffles the patients one time and puts them in n_splits groups of about the same size. Each fold uses one group as the val split and the other groups as the train split. It takes the same arguments as get_datasets(), but the default of n_splits is 5.

for fold, (fold_train, fold_val) in enumerate(ds.get_folds(n_splits=5)):
    print(fold, len(fold_train), len(fold_val))
# 0 110 28
# 1 111 27
# 2 111 27
# 3 111 27
# 4 109 29

n_splits must be from 2 to the number of patients. Other values raise ValueError (D-10).

docs.title: 4. Augment only the train split
docs.text:
Give the augmentation to the train split only. With val_transform=None, the val split uses the transform of the dataset. If that transform has a random step, get_datasets(n_splits=...) and get_folds() warn (D-49).

from radharmony.dataset.transforms import RadiologyTransform2D

augment = RadiologyTransform2D(img_size=224).with_flip(spatial_axis=1, prob=0.5).get_transform()
plain = RadiologyTransform2D(img_size=224).get_transform()
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5, train_transform=augment, val_transform=plain)

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
No patient is in both splits:

import os

table = ds.get_harmonized_df()
patient_of = dict(zip(table["image_path"], table["patient_id"]))


def patients(split):
    return {patient_of[os.path.relpath(d["img"], ds.base_image_dir)] for d in split.data}


print(patients(train_ds) & patients(val_ds))
# set()

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Load a dataset and pick outputs
  • Cache the samples: each split has its own cache folder.
  • Transforms: the augmentation steps.
  • D-09, D-10 and D-34 in Design decisions.

docs.title: Use the app
docs.text:
The RadHarmony app is a Gradio web page. Use it to look at the samples of a dataset, with the boxes and masks on the image. You can also try the transform steps before you train, and copy their Python code.

Before you start, install the app extra in your venv: uv pip install -e ".[app]".

docs.title: 1. Start the app
docs.text:
python app.py

The app listens on 0.0.0.0:7860 (all network interfaces). Open http://localhost:7860 on the same machine. Other machines on the same network can open http://<host>:7860. For another port, run python app.py --server-port 7861.

docs.title: 2. Load a dataset
docs.text:
1. Pick the tab of the modality: CXR, Radiograph, CT, CT (2D), MRI or VQA.
  2. Pick the Dataset family. A family with more than one class also shows a Variant list, for example the train and test split.
  3. Type the Base image directory. The dataset page says which folder it is.
  4. If the dataset needs other files, type their paths in CSV path and in up to 2 extra fields. An extra field holds, for example, a box CSV or a report CSV. Some datasets also show a drop-down list, for example the label mode of TAIX-Ray.
  5. Type a Cache dir. Leave it blank for no cache.
  6. Pick the Output fields: Labels (output_cls), Mask (output_mask), Report (output_report), BBox (output_bbox) and Reg (output_reg). BBox is on by default for NODE21, ChestX-Det10, PadChest-GR and Chest ImaGenome (D-11).
  7. Click Load Dataset. The Status box shows the number of samples and the keys, for example Loaded 138 samples. Keys: ['cls', 'img'].

docs.title: 3. Set the steps and run
docs.text:
1. Under Preprocessing & Display, set the image size and the pad. A 3-D tab also has the voxel spacing. The CT tab also has the HU window.
  2. Under Augmentations, turn on the steps that you want to see: Flip, Intensity Jitter, Gaussian Noise, Gaussian Smooth, Elastic Deformation, Affine and Transpose. In the app, each step that is on always runs (probability 1.0).
  3. Click Run on random sample. Run on same sample runs the steps again on the last sample.

The gallery shows the Original image first, then each augmentation alone. With 2 or more steps on, the last image (Compound) has all of them. A 3-D tab shows the middle axial, coronal and sagittal slices.

Under the gallery:

  • Labels shows each label with a cls value above 0.5. A value of 2 or more shows as name (N), for example pleural_effusion_left (3) for TAIX-Ray with label_mode="ordinal". name alone means 1. A regression value shows as name=value.
  • Report and Q & A show the text of the sample.
  • Transform code snippet gives the RadiologyTransform2D or RadiologyTransform3D code of your settings. In the code, each step has its normal probability, for example prob=0.5.

docs.title: 4. Open the app from another machine
docs.text:
Do this step when the app runs on a remote machine and a firewall or VPN blocks port 7860, but allows SSH (port 22). If your browser can open http://<remote-host>:7860, you do not need it.

  1. On the remote machine, start the app: python app.py.
  2. On your laptop, in a second terminal, open an SSH tunnel:
ssh -v -N -L 17860:localhost:7860 <user>@<remote-host>
  1. Open http://localhost:17860 in your browser.
  2. To stop the tunnel, press Ctrl+C in its terminal. To stop the app, press Ctrl+C in the terminal of the app.

Notes:

  • -L 17860:localhost:7860 sends laptop port 17860 to port 7860 of the server. Use a free local port. A local app on port 7860 of your laptop blocks the local side of a -L 7860:... tunnel, and your browser then shows the local app.
  • -N opens no remote shell, so the terminal stays silent while the tunnel works. With -v, SSH prints Local connections to LOCALHOST:17860 forwarded to remote address localhost:7860. If it prints bind [127.0.0.1]:17860: Address already in use, pick another local port.
  • An old app on port 7860 stops the new one, or the new one starts on port 7861. ss -lntp | grep -E ':(7860|7861|7862)' shows the process IDs. Stop your own with kill <pid>, or start the app with --server-port.
  • Add -f to run the tunnel in the background. Through a jump host, add -J jumphost. For a tunnel that starts again after a lost connection, use autossh -M 0 -f -N -L 17860:localhost:7860 <user>@<remote-host>.
  • demo.launch(server_name="0.0.0.0", share=True) in app.py gives a public *.gradio.live link that the firewall does not block. Anyone with the link can use your app and see its file paths. The link stops after about 72 hours. Use it only when SSH is not possible, and undo the change before you commit.

docs.title: Check
docs.text: After Load Dataset, the Status box shows Loaded <N> samples. After Run on random sample, the gallery shows the Original image.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Load a dataset and pick outputs: the same steps in Python.
  • Transforms: the steps of the transform code snippet.

docs.title: Dataset API
docs.text:
Every image dataset class shares these facts: the constructor arguments, the keys of a sample and the columns of the harmonized table. Each dataset page lists the arguments of its own class.

For the steps, see the how-to pages:

  • Load a dataset and pick outputs
  • Save and reuse a harmonized table
  • Split data
  • Cache the samples

docs.title: Constructor arguments
docs.text:
Every image dataset class inherits these arguments from BaseRadiologicalDataset.

Argument Type Required Default Description base_image_dir str Yes The folder of the images. image_path in the table is relative to it (D-04) transform MONAI transform No None in each dataset class The image steps. None gives RadiologyTransform2D or RadiologyTransform3D (Transforms) cache_dir str No "./cache" The MONAI cache folder. None gives no cache (Cache the samples) output_cls bool No False Add cls to the sample output_mask bool No False Add mask to the sample. The dataset drops the rows with no mask, and warns (D-33) output_report bool No False Add report to the sample. The dataset drops the rows with no report, and warns (D-33) output_bbox bool No False Add bbox and bbox_labels to the sample, and bbox_findings when the class has it output_reg bool No False Add reg to the sample. A class with no regression target warns (D-11) harmonized_df pd.DataFrame No None Use this harmonized table. The class does not read the source files harmonizer harmonizer No None Use the table of this harmonizer harmonizer_path str No None Use the table of a file from harmonizer.save()
  • A flag that the class does not support gives a warning and no key (D-11). Every image class takes all 5 flags.
  • The dataset classes also take dtype (default torch.bfloat16), the type of img. The class gives it to its default transform (Transforms: dtype).
  • Many classes also take csv_path and other file paths. When you leave out a file path, the class looks for the file in fixed places (D-35). The dataset pages list these arguments.
  • A VQA or caption class (BaseVQADataset) has other arguments and other sample keys. Its dataset page lists them.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
cache_dir holds a MONAI PersistentDataset cache (Cache the samples).

  • The cache keeps the tensors before the first random step. Augmentation runs again for each sample, so each epoch gets a new augmentation (D-15).
  • Each split has its own folder: train and val, fold_0/train and so on. get_datasets() with no n_splits uses cache_dir itself.
  • Inside this folder, the cache is in a folder named by a short key of the cached steps. A new load or preprocessing step, for example a new img_size, gives a new key and a new cache. A new augmentation setting, for example the flip probability, uses the same cache.
  • A changed lambda or a changed RadHarmony step also gives a new key. If you change a helper function that a step calls, the key stays the same. Then delete the cache folder yourself.
  • Old folders stay on the disk until you delete them.
  • torch.manual_seed(...) repeats the random augmentation of a run, with any num_workers (D-15).

docs.title: Order of the table arguments
docs.text:
If you give more than one table argument, the class uses the first of this list (Save and reuse a harmonized table):

Order Argument Gives 1 harmonized_df the table that you give 2 harmonizer_path the table of a file from save() 3 harmonizer harmonized_df of the harmonizer that you give 4 none of them the class harmonizes the source files

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method What it does How-to get_datasets(n_splits=None, num_cores=2, random_state=56, train_transform=None, val_transform=None) One dataset with all rows, or a (train, val) tuple grouped by patient Split data get_folds(n_splits=5, num_cores=2, random_state=56, train_transform=None, val_transform=None) Yields one (train, val) tuple for each fold Split data get_harmonized_df() Returns the harmonized table Load a dataset set_harmonized_df(df) Gives the dataset a new table for the next splits Save and reuse verify_images(drop_missing=True) Returns the rows with no image file, and drops them by default Load a dataset pre_cache(dataset, num_workers=2) Reads each sample of a split one time, to fill the cache Cache the samples

The arguments of get_datasets() and get_folds():

Name Meaning n_splits get_datasets(): the val split gets about 1/n_splits of the patients. None gives one dataset with all rows. get_folds(): the number of folds, from 2 to the number of patients num_cores The number of processes that make the sample list random_state The seed of the patient draw train_transform The transform of the train split. None uses the transform of the dataset val_transform The transform of the val split. None uses the transform of the dataset, and warns if it has a random step (D-49)

docs.title: Data dict keys
docs.text:
Each sample is a Python dict:

Key Shape Type Condition "img" (C, H, W) or (1, D, H, W) dtype Always "cls" (n_labels,) float32 output_cls=True "mask" (1, H, W) or (1, D, H, W) float32 output_mask=True "bbox" (N, 4) (2-D) or (N, 6) (3-D) float32 output_bbox=True "bbox_labels" list of str, one for each box list output_bbox=True "bbox_findings" list, one entry for each box list output_bbox=True, for a class that has it "report" str str output_report=True "reg" (n_targets,) float32 output_reg=True
  • img: values from -1 to 1 (D-14). C is 1 for a gray modality and 3 for the classes with color figures (D-42, channels).
  • cls: one value for each label, in the order of sorted(ds.LABEL_COLS) (the plain Python sort). After get_datasets() or get_folds(), ds.LABEL_COLS is in this order. So ds.LABEL_COLS[i] is the label of cls[i]. For example, ["edema", "atelectasis"] gives cls[0] = atelectasis (D-05).
  • bbox: fractions of the image size, from 0 to 1, in the order [dim0_min, dim0_max, dim1_min, dim1_max] (row first, as in array indexing). An image with no box gives shape (0, 4) or (0, 6). The box matches the returned image (D-28). Transforms: Boxes says how each step moves it.
  • The default DataLoader collate cannot stack boxes when the samples have a different number of boxes. Use collate_fn=bbox_collate (from radharmony.dataset import bbox_collate), for example DataLoader(ds, batch_size=8, collate_fn=bbox_collate). It stacks img, cls and the other keys as usual. bbox, bbox_labels, bbox_findings and bbox_mask become lists with one entry for each sample.

docs.title: Harmonized table columns
docs.text:
The harmonized table has one row for each image (D-03). A few harmonizers give one row for each study, series or volume, and their dataset page says so. The table always has patient_id, study_id, image_path and one column for each label. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04), so os.path.join(base_image_dir, image_path) opens the file. Some datasets also have series_id, view_position, mask_path, bbox, bbox_labels, report and split.

  • view_position of a 2-D dataset uses the names PA, AP and LATERAL. An unknown view is NaN. Other source values are in upper case, for example AP_HORIZONTAL or FRONTAL. A 3-D dataset keeps its plane or series names, for example axial (CT-RATE) or Sagittal T1 (RSNA 2024 lumbar).
  • age_years and sex are in the table when the source has them. age_years is a float, in years (D-06). sex is "M", "F" or NaN. NaN means unknown or other (D-26). sex comes after age_years.
  • The "Harmonizer" section of each dataset page gives its extra columns.

docs.title: Datathon26
docs.text:
Event-specific datasets and evaluators for the datathon26 chest-X-ray benchmark. In this event, model inference does not run locally. Studies go to an external reportbench service, which returns pre-computed results.

The service runs two tasks: embed (per-image feature .npz) and report (per-study text). The radharmony.datathon26 submodule turns those into three scoring tasks: classification and segmentation (both over the embed features) and report generation. It replaces the model forward pass with the returned results. Datasets serve the embeddings / patch maps / reports in place of image tensors. Evaluators score them with the standard RadHarmony probe, segmentation, and generative code, unchanged.

Importing the package registers everything under datathon26_* keys:

import radharmony.datathon26  # registers datasets + evaluators

A runnable, self-contained walkthrough of all paths is in datathon26/demo_datathon_evaluators.ipynb. It makes a tiny fake batch table and result files, so it runs end-to-end without the service: classification (§3), report generation (§4), and segmentation (§4b). Then it shows how to point the same code at a real run (§5) and how to submit one yourself (§6).

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
batch preparation           reportbench service              radharmony.datathon26
─────────────────           ───────────────────              ─────────────────────
sample + anonymize   ──►  submit a run              ──►  point a dataset at the
6 CXR datasets            (embed / report task)          results dir + batch CSV
                                                                    │
dataset_{DS1..DS6}.csv    writes under                             ▼
(labels + reports)        _reportbench_out/<model>/         evaluate() → metrics
mapping.csv (private)       <study>/<model>_<stem>.npz
                            <study>/<model>_report.txt
  1. An internal batch-preparation step samples and anonymizes six harmonized CXR datasets (DS1=MIMIC-CXR, DS2=ReXGradient-160K, DS3=VinDr-CXR, DS4=EmoryCXR v2, DS5=PadChest, DS6=SIIM-ACR-PTX). It puts them into per-study submission folders (DS1_patient_00001_study_00001/). It writes the anonymized batch tables dataset_{DS1..DS6}.csv, with one row per study, the one-hot finding labels and the free-text report ground truth. It also writes a private mapping.csv de-anonymization key (never uploaded). DS6 (SIIM-ACR-PTX) also carries a pneumothorax mask_path, so it is the dataset the segmentation task scores.
  2. The submission folder is sent to the reportbench service, which runs one of two tasks: embed or report. (The embed task submits without a manifest. The report task attaches a study-keyed manifest.json carrying the per-study indication when an indication_col is given.)
  3. The service writes results under <data_dir>/<run>/_reportbench_out/<model>/:
    • embed task → <study>/<model>_<stem>.npz per image: an archive with global [dim] (the pooled image vector), patches [n_patches, dim], and grid (H, W).
    • report task → <study>/<model>_report.txt per study: the generated free-text report.
  4. A datathon26 dataset joins those results to the batch CSV. A datathon26 evaluator scores them. The two outputs (embed and report) feed the three scoring tasks. Classification reads the .npz global vector. Segmentation folds its patches into a dense map. Report generation reads the .txt. Segmentation also needs a ground-truth mask per image (bring your own mask_path), so it applies only to datasets that have masks.

docs.title: Result-file layout
docs.text:
The real reportbench service writes results under a per-model subfolder, with one embedding .npz per image and one report per study:

<results_dir>/<model>/                 # for example .../_reportbench_out/model-a/
  DS1_patient_00018_study_00001/
    model-a_pa.npz       # embed task: one <model>_<stem>.npz per image
    model-a_lateral.npz  #   archive: global [dim] + patches [n, dim] + grid (H, W)
    model-a_report.txt   # report task: one <model>_report.txt per study
  ...

Point the dataset at the <results_dir>/<model> folder and pass a result_path resolver. The viewwise_embedding_path(model) (defaults to .npz) / perstudy_report_path(model) helpers build the names above. (_load_npy also accepts a bare .npy array. With no resolver, the datasets default to the simpler <study>/embedding.npy / <study>/report.txt. The self-contained notebook demo makes files with these names.)

The classification/segmentation datasets read from the same .npz. Classification takes the global vector. Segmentation folds patches back into a dense [dim, H, W] map. It uses the stored grid, or a square √n_patches grid when grid is absent. Embeddings are per-image, so the classification/segmentation frame has one row per image (the stem is read from each row's image_path). The report frame is deduplicated to one row per study.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
Registry key Class Serves Key sample fields datathon26_embedding EmbeddingResultsDataset .npz global (or result_path) img = embedding vector, cls = label vector datathon26_segmentation PatchSegResultsDataset .npz patches → [D, H, W] (or result_path) img = dense feature map, mask = GT mask datathon26_report ReportResultsDataset report.txt (or result_path) img = predicted report, report = reference report

(DatathonEmbeddingDataset / DatathonReportDataset are the one-shot factories that submit a job and return an EmbeddingResultsDataset / ReportResultsDataset. See "raw studies → dataset" below.)

EmbeddingResultsDataset auto-detects label columns as the binary (0/1) numeric columns in the batch frame. So free-text and demographic columns never go into the cls vector. The anonymized patient_id (DS1_patient_00001) is preserved so patient-grouped k-fold never splits one patient's studies across folds.

docs.title: Evaluators
docs.text:
All are thin subclasses of the standard evaluators, so every feature of the originals is preserved:

  • Patient-grouped k-fold, multi-seed, bootstrap, threshold strategies, macro_average, and the embedding cache.
  • For segmentation: early stopping + prediction dumps.
  • For reports: the full RadEval metric suite + generations.csv.
Registry key Class Base Scores datathon26_linear_probe DatathonLinearProbeEvaluator LinearProbeEvaluator embeddings → per-label logistic regression datathon26_knn_probe DatathonKNNProbeEvaluator KNNProbeEvaluator embeddings → k-NN datathon26_svm_probe DatathonSVMProbeEvaluator SVMProbeEvaluator embeddings → SVM datathon26_prototype_probe DatathonPrototypeProbeEvaluator PrototypeProbeEvaluator embeddings → nearest-centroid datathon26_linear_probe_seg DatathonLinearProbeSegEvaluator LinearProbeSegEvaluator patch map → 1×1-conv head → Dice/IoU datathon26_conv_probe_seg DatathonConvProbeSegEvaluator ConvProbeSegEvaluator patch map → conv-block head → Dice/IoU datathon26_upernet_seg DatathonUPerNetSegEvaluator UPerNetSegEvaluator patch map → UPerNet head → Dice/IoU datathon26_report_generation DatathonReportGenerationEvaluator ReportGenerationEvaluator predicted vs reference report → RadEval

The classification and segmentation evaluators default their image_encoder to an IdentityEncoder (pass-through). So the only encoder call returns the pre-extracted vectors / patch maps unchanged. The segmentation head (1×1 conv / conv block / UPerNet) trains straight on the frozen patch features. The report evaluator uses an identity_generator (pass-through) and reads the predicted report from the dataset instead of calling a VLM.

docs.title: Classification (embeddings → probe)
docs.text:
import radharmony.datathon26  # noqa: F401  (registers datathon26_*)
from radharmony.datathon26 import (
    EmbeddingResultsDataset, viewwise_embedding_path, DatathonLinearProbeEvaluator,
)

ds = EmbeddingResultsDataset(
    embeddings_dir="/path/to/_reportbench_out/model-a",  # <study>/model-a_<stem>.npz
    csv_path="dataset_DS1.csv",                          # one row per image (labels)
    result_path=viewwise_embedding_path("model-a"),
)

ev = DatathonLinearProbeEvaluator(dataset=ds, n_folds=5)
results = ev.evaluate()   # DataFrame: per-label + macro_average rows (auroc, auprc, f1, ...)

Swap in DatathonKNNProbeEvaluator, DatathonSVMProbeEvaluator, or DatathonPrototypeProbeEvaluator. They have the same call shape.

docs.title: Segmentation (patch features → Dice/IoU)
docs.text:
import radharmony.datathon26  # noqa: F401
from radharmony.datathon26 import (
    PatchSegResultsDataset, viewwise_embedding_path, DatathonLinearProbeSegEvaluator,
)

ds = PatchSegResultsDataset(
    embeddings_dir="/path/to/_reportbench_out/model-a",  # <study>/model-a_<stem>.npz
    csv_path="dataset_DS6.csv",                          # one row per image (DS6 has masks)
    result_path=viewwise_embedding_path("model-a"),      # reads the .npz `patches`
    mask_col="mask_path",                                # GT mask per image
    mask_size=224,                                       # output resolution
)

ev = DatathonLinearProbeSegEvaluator(dataset=ds, num_classes=2, n_folds=5)
results = ev.evaluate()   # DataFrame: per-class + macro_average rows (dice, iou, ...)

PatchSegResultsDataset folds the .npz patches [n, dim] into a dense [dim, H, W] map (via the stored grid), and the evaluator puts a frozen-feature segmentation head on it. Swap in DatathonConvProbeSegEvaluator or DatathonUPerNetSegEvaluator for heavier heads (same call shape). Pass feat_size= if the patch grid varies per image.

docs.title: Report generation (reference + predicted → RadEval)
docs.text:
import radharmony.datathon26  # noqa: F401
from radharmony.datathon26 import (
    ReportResultsDataset, perstudy_report_path, DatathonReportGenerationEvaluator,
)
from radharmony.evaluator.metrics.language import LIGHT_METRICS

ds = ReportResultsDataset(
    results_dir="/path/to/_reportbench_out/model-a",  # <study>/model-a_report.txt
    csv_path="dataset_DS1.csv",                       # one row per study; 'report' = reference
    result_path=perstudy_report_path("model-a"),
)

ev = DatathonReportGenerationEvaluator(
    dataset=ds,
    metrics=LIGHT_METRICS,               # or the default full 16-metric suite
    ref_section="findings",              # both reference and prediction parsed to this section
)
results = ev.evaluate()                  # DataFrame with the RadEval metric panel

Both the reference and the predicted report are parsed to the same ref_section so the comparison is symmetric (findings-vs-findings by default). Studies with a blank reference or empty generation are dropped before scoring.

docs.title: One-shot: raw studies → dataset (ReportBenchClient)
docs.text:
The usage above assumes you have already run the studies through the service and have a results folder. The DatathonEmbeddingDataset / DatathonReportDataset factories (+ ReportBenchClient) do that submission step for you. You can go straight from a harmonized frame and the raw image root to a ready dataset object. The frame and the root are the same two inputs that an ordinary RadHarmony dataset takes. The factories wrap the rbclient.py CLI (config → prepare → submit → watch, with an optional check) via subprocess.

import radharmony.datathon26  # noqa: F401
from radharmony.datathon26 import ReportBenchClient, DatathonEmbeddingDataset

client = ReportBenchClient(
    rbclient_path="/path/to/datathon/skill/rbclient.py",
    data_dir="/path/to/datathon/data_deposition/<team_id>",
    api_key="rb_...",                    # from your team INSTRUCTIONS.md
)

ds = DatathonEmbeddingDataset(
    harmonized_df=df,                    # one row per image (labels)
    base_image_dir="/data/mimic",        # where the raw images live
    client=client,
    model="model-a",                     # see client.models()
)
# ds is an EmbeddingResultsDataset pointed at
# <data_dir>/run_embed/_reportbench_out/model-a/<study>/model-a_<stem>.npz

DatathonEmbeddingDataset here is a factory function, not the result class. It does 3 steps:

  1. It stages every study in harmonized_df into the per-study folder layout that the service expects (<study_id>/<view files>). It groups multiple views per study and uses symlinks by default.
  2. It drives rbclient.py to submit the embed task and watch it to the end.
  3. It checks that every image produced its .npz (if not, it raises with the missing ids). Then it returns an EmbeddingResultsDataset pointed at the _reportbench_out/<model> results.

DatathonReportDataset(harmonized_df, base_image_dir, client=..., model=...) is the report-task counterpart. It has the same call shape, submits the report task and returns a ReportResultsDataset. Pass indication_col= to attach a per-study indication via the job's study-keyed manifest.json.

Pass skip_submit=True with an existing results_dir= to re-score a finished run without resubmitting. You can configure every path (client script, interpreter, staging / results dirs) and the run name / task. You can also configure the .npz key + extension (emb_key, emb_ext) and the column names (study_col, image_col, view_col).

docs.title: Transforms
docs.text: RadHarmony has 2 transform builders: RadiologyTransform2D and RadiologyTransform3D. Each one makes a MONAI Compose with the load and preprocessing steps. The with_* methods add augmentation steps. get_transform() returns the Compose. A dataset class with transform=None uses one of them.

docs.title: Default 2-D steps
docs.text:
_ParseBboxD → LoadImageD (ITKReader) → EnsureChannelFirstD → drop the DICOM axis →
TransposeD [0, 2, 1] (if base_transpose) → fix the missing high bit → VOI LUT →
set channels (D-42) → ScaleIntensityRangePercentilesD (0.5 and 99.5 to [-1, 1]) →
mask values above 0 to 1 (if "mask") → ResizeD (longest edge) → SpatialPadD (if pad) →
[augmentation] → box to tensor → ToTensorD → SelectItemsD
  • A 2-D mask in a sample holds 0 and 1, also when the mask file holds 0 and 255 (D-14).
  • The pad value is -1 (black) for the image and 0 for the mask.
import torch
from radharmony.dataset.transforms import RadiologyTransform2D

t = RadiologyTransform2D(img_size=224, dtype=torch.float32).get_transform()
print(len(t.transforms))
# 15

docs.title: Default 3-D steps
docs.text:
_ParseBboxD → LoadImageD (ITKReader) → EnsureChannelFirstD →
_ReorientBbox (if base_transpose) → _SITKOrientD (axcodes, if base_transpose) →
SpacingD (if pixdim, moves the box) → TransposeD [0, 3, 2, 1] (if base_transpose) →
ScaleIntensityRangeD (HU clip, if hu_window) → ScaleIntensityRangePercentilesD (0.5 and 99.5 to [-1, 1]) →
ResizeD (longest edge) → SpatialPadD (if pad) → [augmentation] → box to tensor → ToTensorD → SelectItemsD

from radharmony.dataset.transforms import RadiologyTransform3D

t = RadiologyTransform3D(
    img_size=112,
    hu_window=(-1000, 400),  # a CT lung window
    pixdim=(1.5, 1.5, 1.5),
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_transform()
print(len(t.transforms))
# 15

docs.title: RadiologyTransform2D
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description img_size int 224 The size of the longest edge after the resize, in pixels. With pad=True, the output is img_size × img_size output_keys set[str] None The keys to keep in the sample. None gives {"img", "cls"}. The default transform of a dataset class sets the keys of its flags. A transform of your own must list them, or the dataset class warns (D-11) pad bool True After the resize, pad to a square with -1 (black). A mask gets 0. False keeps the aspect ratio base_transpose bool True Add the [0, 2, 1] transpose after the load. It corrects the axis order of the ITK reader dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The type of img and bbox_mask. cls, reg, mask and bbox are always float32 channels int 1 The channel count of img: 1 or 3 (D-42). With 1, an RGB or RGBA file becomes gray. With 3, a gray file repeats to 3 channels

docs.title: RadiologyTransform3D
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description img_size int 112 The size of the longest edge after the resize, in voxels. With pad=True, the output is a cube output_keys set[str] None The keys to keep in the sample. None gives {"img", "cls"} hu_window tuple[float, float] None The HU clip range, for example (-1000, 400). None gives no clip. Use None for MRI pad bool True After the resize, pad to a cube with -1 (black). A mask gets 0 base_transpose bool True Add the orientation step and the [0, 3, 2, 1] transpose. The boxes need both (3-D orientation) pixdim tuple[float, float, float] None The voxel spacing to resample to, in mm. None gives no resample axcodes str "IPL" The orientation of the volume, for example "RAS", "LPS" or "IPL". _SITKOrientD and _ReorientBbox both use it dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The type of img and bbox_mask. cls, reg, mask and bbox are always float32

docs.title: Augmentation methods
docs.text:
Call the with_* methods before get_transform(). Each method returns the builder, so you can chain them. The steps run in the order of the calls, after the preprocessing steps.

t = (
    RadiologyTransform2D(img_size=224, dtype=torch.float32)
    .with_flip(spatial_axis=0, prob=0.5)
    .with_affine(translate_range=(10.0, 10.0), rotate_range=(0.175,), prob=0.5)
    .with_intensity_jitter(shift=0.1, scale=0.1, prob=0.5)
    .with_gaussian_noise(mean=0.0, std=0.05, prob=0.5)
    .get_transform()
)
print(len(t.transforms))
# 20
Method Defaults Notes with_flip(spatial_axis, prob) 0, 0.5 A random flip. In 2-D, axis 0 is up-down and axis 1 is left-right with_affine(translate_range, rotate_range, scale_range, shear_range, prob) (10.0, 10.0), (0.175,), (0.1, 0.1), (0.05,), 0.5 One random affine step. The translation is in pixels. The rotation is in radians (0.175 is about 10 degrees) with_intensity_jitter(shift, scale, prob) 0.1, 0.1, 0.5 A random shift and a random scale of the values. Each one runs with prob with_gaussian_noise(mean, std, prob) 0.0, 0.05, 0.5 Adds random Gaussian noise with_gaussian_smooth(sigma_range, prob) (0.5, 1.5), 0.2 A random Gaussian blur with_elastic_deformation(magnitude_range, spacing, prob) (50.0, 150.0), 20, 0.2 2-D only. A random grid warp. spacing is the grid step in pixels with_elastic_deformation(sigma_range, magnitude_range, prob) (5.0, 7.0), (50.0, 150.0), 0.2 3-D only. A random elastic warp with_bbox_as_mask(keep_mask) False With keep_mask=True, the sample also has bbox_mask, one channel for each box. The box also moves without this call with_transpose(indices, keys) no default, None Adds a transpose, for example [0, 2, 1] for 2-D. None gives img, and mask when it is in output_keys with_spacing(pixdim) (1.0, 1.0, 1.0) 3-D only. Sets pixdim add_transform(t) Adds any MONAI transform. It does not move the box

with_affine and with_elastic_deformation fill the empty border with black (D-37). For RadiologyTransform2D and RadiologyTransform3D, this is -1. For RadiologyEncoderTransform, it is the darkest value of each channel of the image, because the encoder has already normalized the image.

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
When "bbox" is in output_keys, the box in the sample always matches the returned image (D-28). Each step moves the box in the same way as the image:

Step How the box moves Resize No change. A box is a fraction of the image size, and the resize stretches the whole image with_spacing or pixdim (3-D resample) Exact math. MONAI keeps the first voxel center and rounds the output size, so the output covers a different area than the input. Each box corner goes through the voxel map of the input and output affines. Then the box is clipped to [0, 1] Pad (pad=True) Exact math. Example: a 200 × 100 (H × W) image becomes 64 × 32, then 64 × 64 with 16 pixels on the left and right. dim1_min = 0.0 becomes 0.25 with_flip Exact math: [lo, hi] becomes [1 - hi, 1 - lo] on each flipped axis with_transpose Exact math: the coordinate pairs change places as the axes do with_affine, with_elastic_deformation Mask round trip. Each box gets its own mask channel, and the warp moves the masks with the image. The new box is the box around the warped mask. The round trip moves an edge by 0.5 pixel or less. The step drops a box that leaves the image, with its label add_transform No change. A custom step does not move the box
  • In the sample, bbox is a float32 tensor of shape (N, 4) for 2-D or (N, 6) for 3-D, also when img is bfloat16. An image with no box gives shape (0, 4) or (0, 6).
  • bbox_labels and bbox_findings are lists with one entry for each box.
  • The table can keep the boxes as a list, as a JSON string, or as the Python list text that to_csv writes (for example "['nodule', 'mass']"). The transform reads all 3.
  • RadiologyEncoderTransform does not move the box with the crop or pad of the encoder processor (a known gap of D-28). It warns when "bbox" is in output_keys and the processor does more than resize.
  • To batch samples with a different number of boxes, use bbox_collate (Data dict keys).

docs.title: HU windows
docs.text:
hu_window clips the CT values before the percentile scaling. Use it only for CT. For MRI, use hu_window=None. Common windows:

Body part Window Lung (-1000, 400) Abdomen (-150, 250) Brain (0, 80) Bone (-500, 1500) Soft tissue (-160, 240)

RAD-ChestCT and MedSeg COVID-19 CT use the lung window (-1000, 400).

docs.title: dtype
docs.text: dtype sets the type of img. torch.bfloat16 (the default) is for a GPU that supports it. Use torch.float32 on a CPU or an older GPU. The dtype argument of a dataset class goes to its default transform.

docs.title: A transform of your own
docs.text:
A dataset class takes any MONAI transform as transform. The transform gets a dict with the path of the image in img. It must load the image. It has none of the default steps, so it does not scale the values and does not move a box.

import monai.transforms as mn
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset

my_transform = mn.Compose([
    mn.LoadImageD(keys=["img"]),
    mn.EnsureChannelFirstD(keys=["img"]),
    mn.ResizeD(keys=["img"], spatial_size=(512, 512)),
    mn.ToTensorD(keys=["img", "cls"], dtype=torch.float32, track_meta=False),
    mn.SelectItemsD(keys=["img", "cls"]),
])
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/", transform=my_transform, output_cls=True, cache_dir=None
)
sample = ds.get_datasets()[0]
print(sample["img"].shape, sample["img"].max().item())
# torch.Size([1, 512, 512]) 255.0

To keep the default steps and add a step of your own, use add_transform().

docs.title: 3-D orientation and axis order
docs.text:
The 3-D transform has 2 linked steps before the value scaling (D-12):

  1. Orientation. _SITKOrientD(axcodes=...) turns each volume to one axis code (default "IPL") with the SimpleITK DICOMOrientImageFilter. _ReorientBbox runs before it and changes the order of the box coordinate pairs, so the box stays on the turned image.
  2. Axis transpose. TransposeD([0, 3, 2, 1]) changes the ITK axis order (W, H, D) to the RadHarmony order (D, H, W). This order matches the box order [dim0_min, dim0_max, dim1_min, dim1_max, ...].

Keep both steps. base_transpose=True turns on both. If you remove one step, or use another axcodes for the image and the box, the 3-D boxes do not match the image.

docs.title: Backbones
docs.text:
A backbone recipe is a make_<name>() function in radharmony.evaluator.backbones. It loads one foundation model and returns a dataset transform and an encoder. Give the transform to the dataset and the encoder to an evaluator. Each recipe follows the input steps and the feature of the authors' own code (D-16). This page lists the 16 recipes and the facts that they share.

A recipe of an image-only model returns (transform, encoder). A recipe of a text-and-image model also returns a text encoder and its tokenizer or processor, for zero-shot. For make_medimageinsights, the 4th value is None. A recipe of a report model returns (transform, report_generator). A recipe of a visual question answering (VQA) model returns (transform, vqa_answerer), for VQAEvaluator.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
Recipe Model Feature size Input size Zero-shot Install extra Page make_raddino RAD-DINO 768 518 × 518 no raddino RAD-DINO make_dinov3 DINOv3 ViT-B/16 768 224 × 224 no dinov3 DINOv3 make_eva_x EVA-X 768 (base), 384 (small), 192 (tiny) 224 × 224 no eva_x EVA-X make_medical_mae Medical MAE 768 (base), 384 (small) 224 × 224 no medical_mae Medical MAE make_ark_plus Ark+ 1376 768 × 768 no ark_plus Ark+ make_chexfound CheXFound 4096 512 × 512 no chexfound CheXFound make_biomed_clip BiomedCLIP 512 224 × 224 yes biomed BiomedCLIP make_chexagent XraySigLIP 1024 512 × 512 yes chexagent CheXagent (XraySigLIP) make_medsiglip MedSigLIP 1152 448 × 448 yes medsiglip MedSigLIP make_medimageinsights MedImageInsight 1024 480 × 480 yes medimageinsights MedImageInsight make_siglip2 SigLIP 2 so400m 1152 384 × 384 yes siglip2 SigLIP 2 make_chexagent_generator CheXagent-2-3b a report (text) 512 × 512 (in the model code) no chexagent_gen CheXagent-2 (generator) make_maira2_generator MAIRA-2 a report (text) set by the MAIRA-2 processor no maira2_gen MAIRA-2 (generator) make_medgemma_generator MedGemma 4B (google/medgemma-4b-it, gated) a report (text) set by the MedGemma processor no medgemma_gen no page yet make_medgemma_vqa MedGemma 4B (google/medgemma-4b-it, gated) an answer (text) set by the MedGemma processor no medgemma_gen no page yet. See VQA make_chexagent_vqa CheXagent-2-3b an answer (text) 512 × 512 (in the model code) no chexagent_gen no page yet. See VQA

Feature size is the length of the feature in classification mode. Each page gives the shape of the patch features in segmentation mode. Install the extra of a recipe before you use it:

uv pip install -e ".[raddino]"

docs.title: How a recipe loads an image
docs.text:
All recipes start with the same loader (load_image() and display_255() in radharmony/evaluator/backbones/_utils.py):

  1. MONAI LoadImage reads the file. PNG, JPEG, DICOM and NIfTI files work.
  2. The image is transposed to (C, H, W).
  3. The values go to 0 to 255, in the same way as in the dataset load (D-13, D-27). A DICOM file gets its VOI window. An 8-bit image keeps its values. Any other image is scaled with its minimum and maximum.
  4. A 1-channel image is repeated to 3 channels.
  5. The values are rounded to uint8. BiomedCLIP and MedImageInsight make a PIL RGB image instead. The transform of a report or VQA recipe saves a PNG file.

The model's own steps (resize, crop, mean and std) come after this. Each page lists them. The transform runs on the CPU, in the DataLoader workers. The encoder and the text encoder run on device. The text encoder gives its output on the CPU.

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text:
Pass output_keys={"img", "mask"} (or {"img", "cls", "mask"}) to an encoder recipe. Then the encoder returns patch features, Tensor[B, D, H', W'], for the segmentation evaluators (linear, conv and UPerNet). Without "mask", the encoder returns the feature, Tensor[B, D]. One encoder gives the feature or the patch features, not both. To get the other output, call the recipe again.

  • The patch grid follows from the input size: H' = W' = input size / patch size. For a hierarchical model (the Swin of Ark+), divide by the stride of the last stage.
  • The transform gives the mask the same resize and crop as the image, with nearest-neighbor interpolation and no scaling.
  • The mask keeps the values of the file, for example 0 and 255. The segmentation probes take each value above 0 as foreground in a binary mask (D-14).
  • The report and VQA recipes do not take output_keys.

docs.title: Output dtype
docs.text:
dtype (default torch.bfloat16) is the dtype of the image tensor that the transform gives. The labels (cls, reg, mask) are always float32. The evaluators run the encoder under autocast (autocast_dtype, default torch.bfloat16), so the float32 weights take the bfloat16 image.

When you call an encoder yourself, use torch.autocast, as on each page in Quick use. Or pass dtype=torch.float32 to the recipe. The report and VQA recipes use dtype for the model weights instead.

docs.title: Weights and code locations
docs.text:
Four recipes need files that do not come from Hugging Face. They need a clone of the authors' repo, a checkpoint that you download by hand, or both. By default, the recipe looks in third_party_models/ at the repo root. The arguments in this table point to other folders, for example shared storage.

Recipe Clone Checkpoint Arguments make_eva_x third_party_models/EVA-X/ from Hugging Face repo_path make_medical_mae third_party_models/medical_mae/ <mae_dir>/<variant file>.pth mae_dir, checkpoint_path, legacy_timm_dir make_ark_plus not needed third_party_models/Ark/Ark_Plus/Ark6_swinLarge768_ep50.pth.tar checkpoint_path, legacy_timm_dir make_chexfound third_party_models/CheXFound/ <chexfound_dir>/weights/teacher_checkpoint.pth chexfound_dir, checkpoint_path

make_ark_plus and make_medical_mae need an old timm to build the model. On the first call, they install it into legacy_timm_dir with uv pip install --target --no-deps. This step needs uv and the network. The old timm is on sys.path only while the recipe builds the model. The rest of the session keeps the timm of the venv.

Point legacy_timm_dir to a fast local folder that all users can read. Then the install runs one time, and it stays after a cleanup of third_party_models/.

from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_ark_plus

transform, encoder = make_ark_plus(
    checkpoint_path="/data/models/Ark_Plus/Ark6_swinLarge768_ep50.pth.tar",
    legacy_timm_dir="/data/cache/ark-timm-054",
    device="cuda",
)

docs.title: Report generators
docs.text:
make_chexagent_generator and make_maira2_generator wrap a model that writes a report. They do not give a feature.

  • transform: a function from a sample dict to a sample dict. It writes the image of the sample to a temporary PNG file and puts the path (a str) in img. The report stays as it is.
  • report_generator: a function from a list[str] of image paths to a list[str] of reports. Give it to ReportGenerationEvaluator.

The chexagent_gen extra pins transformers==4.40.0 (from the model card). The maira2_gen extra pins transformers>=4.46.0,<4.47, and the MAIRA-2 model card asks for transformers>=4.48.0,<4.52. So pyproject.toml declares both extras as conflicting with each other and with most other extras. Install each one in its own venv.

docs.title: Authoring a new recipe
docs.text: See Add a backbone.

docs.title: Ark+
docs.text:
Recipe make_ark_plus(), returns (transform, encoder) Model card jlianglab/Ark (folder Ark_Plus) Input size 768 × 768 (bilinear resize to 896 × 896, then center crop) Normalization ImageNet mean (0.485, 0.456, 0.406) and std (0.229, 0.224, 0.225), from the authors' fine-tune code Feature Projector output of the pooled Swin-L feature, 1376 values Install extra ark_plus and a checkpoint that you request from the authors Segmentation features Tensor[B, 1536, 24, 24]

Ark+ is a Swin-L chest X-ray model from the jlianglab group (Ma et al., Nature 2025). It learned from the labels of 6 public chest X-ray datasets: MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert, ChestX-ray14, RSNA Pneumonia, VinDr-CXR and Shenzhen. The training is cyclic multi-task learning with a student and a teacher. Use it as a chest X-ray encoder trained with expert labels.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block encodes one Montgomery image.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_ark_plus

transform, encoder = make_ark_plus(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
img = ds.get_datasets()[0]["img"]  # Tensor[3, 768, 768], torch.bfloat16
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    feature = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))
print(feature.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1376])

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
1. Load: the shared loader gives a 3-channel uint8 image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. Scale: the values are divided by 255.
  3. Resize: the whole image goes to 896 × 896 with bilinear interpolation (the torchvision default). The resize does not keep the aspect ratio.
  4. Crop: a center crop of 768 × 768.
  5. Mean and std: the ImageNet values.
  6. Dtype: the transform casts the image to dtype.

Steps 3 to 5 are the "valid" mode of build_transform_classification() in Finetuning/dataloader.py, with --img_size 896 --input_size 768 from the Ark+ README. The authors' pretraining code resizes with PIL (bicubic) instead. The recipe uses the fine-tune steps (D-16). The "test" mode of the authors averages 10 crops. The recipe uses the one center crop.

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text:
transform, encoder = make_ark_plus(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    patches = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))  # img from Quick use
print(patches.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1536, 24, 24])

Swin is a hierarchical model. A forward hook on the final model.norm takes the feature map before the pool. The last stage has a stride of 32, so the grid is 768 / 32 = 24 on each side. The patch features do not use the projector. See Segmentation mode for the shared rules.

docs.title: Feature
docs.text: The classification feature is the output of the projector (one Linear layer, 1536 to 1376) on the pooled forward_features() output. The authors' linear probe uses this feature: generate_embeddings(x, after_proj=True) in Pretraining/models.py, and emb_dim=1376 in Linearprobing/main_linearprobing.py (D-16). The recipe loads the projector from the checkpoint. A checkpoint with no projector raises KeyError.

docs.title: Weights
docs.text:
The weights do not download by themselves:

  1. Request them with the Google Form or the WeChat form.
  2. Put Ark6_swinLarge768_ep50.pth.tar at third_party_models/Ark/Ark_Plus/Ark6_swinLarge768_ep50.pth.tar, or pass checkpoint_path.

The recipe does not import code from the Ark repo, so a clone is optional. The checkpoint was saved with timm==0.5.4, and the Swin layout of a newer timm is different (downsample is one layer index off). So on the first call, the recipe installs timm==0.5.4 into legacy_timm_dir (Weights and code locations).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description checkpoint_path str None The checkpoint file. None gives third_party_models/Ark/Ark_Plus/Ark6_swinLarge768_ep50.pth.tar at the repo root. A missing file raises FileNotFoundError legacy_timm_dir str None The folder for timm==0.5.4. None gives third_party_models/Ark/timm-054/ at the repo root device str "cuda" The device of the encoder, for example "cuda:1" or "cpu" output_keys set[str] None The keys of each sample. None gives {"img", "cls"}. With "mask", the encoder gives patch features (Segmentation mode) dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The dtype of the image tensor (Output dtype)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Ark+ learned from the labels of its 6 training datasets. So a score on one of these datasets is not a test on new data. For example, Ark+ saw the Shenzhen TB labels.
  • The recipe builds a plain timm SwinTransformer (patch 4, window 12, embed size 192, depths 2, 2, 18, 2). It loads checkpoint["teacher"] with strict=False. It drops the attn_mask buffers and the task heads.
  • Before 2026-11-03, the feature was forward_features() (1536 values). An embedding_cache file from before that date raises ValueError (D-41). Delete the file. The next run makes a new one.
  • Before 2026-10-28, the recipe resized to 768 × 768 with no crop. So results from before that date used another input.
  • Under autocast, the feature is torch.bfloat16, because the last step is a Linear layer.

docs.title: BiomedCLIP
docs.text:
Recipe make_biomed_clip(), returns (transform, encoder, text_encoder, tokenizer) Model card microsoft/BiomedCLIP-PubMedBERT_256-vit_base_patch16_224 Input size 224 × 224 (bicubic resize of the short side to 224, then center crop) Normalization CLIP mean (0.48145466, 0.4578275, 0.40821073) and std (0.26862954, 0.26130258, 0.27577711), from open_clip_config.json of the model Feature CLS token after the linear projection, 512 values Install extra biomed Segmentation features Tensor[B, 768, 14, 14]

BiomedCLIP is a CLIP model from Microsoft, with a ViT-B/16 image encoder and a PubMedBERT text encoder. Microsoft trained it on PMC-15M, 15 million figure and caption pairs from PubMed Central articles. The data covers many kinds of biomedical images, not only chest X-rays. Use it for zero-shot classification and as a general biomedical image encoder.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block encodes one Montgomery image and one prompt.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_biomed_clip

transform, encoder, text_encoder, tokenizer = make_biomed_clip(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
img = ds.get_datasets()[0]["img"]  # Tensor[3, 224, 224], torch.bfloat16
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    feature = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))
print(feature.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 512])

tokens = tokenizer(["this is a photo of chest X-ray with tuberculosis"])  # Tensor[1, 256]
print(text_encoder(tokens).shape)  # torch.Size([1, 512]), float32 on the CPU

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
1. Load: the shared loader gives a PIL RGB image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. Resize: the short side goes to 224 with bicubic interpolation.
  3. Crop: a center crop of 224 × 224.
  4. Scale: the values are divided by 255.
  5. Mean and std: the CLIP values of open_clip_config.json (see At a glance).
  6. Dtype: the transform casts the image to dtype.

Steps 2 to 5 are the OpenCLIP preprocess_val of the model. It is the same transform that open_clip.create_model_from_pretrained gives on the model card (D-16).

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text:
transform, encoder, *_ = make_biomed_clip(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    patches = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))  # img from Quick use
print(patches.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 768, 14, 14])

The patch features are the patch tokens of the last ViT block, with no CLS token and no projection. So they have 768 values (the ViT width), not 512. The patch size is 16, so the grid is 224 / 16 = 14 on each side. See Segmentation mode for the shared rules.

docs.title: Text encoder
docs.text:
• Output: text_encoder(tokens) gives Tensor[T, 512], float32, on the CPU. It is encode_text of the model: the CLS token of PubMedBERT and an MLP projection. The features are not L2-normalized. ZeroShotEvaluator normalizes them.
  • Tokenizer: the OpenCLIP tokenizer of the model, with the BiomedBERT WordPiece vocabulary. It makes the text lowercase. It pads and cuts each prompt to 256 tokens, so it gives Tensor[T, 256].
  • Prompt form: the model card puts "this is a photo of " before each label, for example "this is a photo of chest X-ray".

Give both to the evaluator: ZeroShotEvaluator(encoder, text_encoder, tokenizer=tokenizer, ...). See Zero-shot.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description device str "cuda" The device of the encoder and the text encoder, for example "cuda:1" or "cpu" hub str "hf-hub:microsoft/BiomedCLIP-PubMedBERT_256-vit_base_patch16_224" The OpenCLIP name of the model, with the hf-hub: prefix output_keys set[str] None The keys of each sample. None gives {"img", "cls"}. With "mask", the encoder gives patch features (Segmentation mode) dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The dtype of the image tensor (Output dtype)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The first call downloads the weights from Hugging Face.
  • One model gives the image encoder and the text encoder. The recipe does not load the weights 2 times.
  • Vision-only evaluators use only the transform and the encoder.

docs.title: CheXagent (XraySigLIP)
docs.text:
Recipe make_chexagent(), returns (transform, encoder, text_encoder, processor) Model card StanfordAIMI/XraySigLIP__vit-l-16-siglip-384__webli Input size 512 × 512 (bicubic resize of the whole image, no crop) Normalization mean 0.5 and std 0.5 on each channel, from the XraySigLIP processor Feature Pooled output of the attention-pool head (pooler_output), 1024 values Install extra chexagent Segmentation features Tensor[B, 1024, 32, 32]

XraySigLIP is a SigLIP image and text model for chest X-rays from Stanford AIMI. It is the image encoder of the CheXagent-2 report generator (Chen et al., arXiv 2024). The name says that it is a SigLIP ViT-L/16 that started from WebLI weights at 384 × 384. Use it for zero-shot classification and probes on chest X-rays.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block encodes one Montgomery image and one prompt.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_chexagent

transform, encoder, text_encoder, processor = make_chexagent(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
img = ds.get_datasets()[0]["img"]  # Tensor[3, 512, 512], torch.bfloat16
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    feature = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))
print(feature.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1024])

tokens = processor(text=["tuberculosis"], padding="max_length", return_tensors="pt")  # 256 tokens
print(text_encoder(tokens).shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1024]), float32 on the CPU

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
1. Load: the shared loader gives a 3-channel uint8 image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. Resize: the whole image goes to 512 × 512 with bicubic interpolation (resample=3). There is no crop, so the resize changes the aspect ratio of the image.
  3. Scale: the values are divided by 255.
  4. Mean and std: 0.5 and 0.5 on each channel, so the values go to -1 to 1.
  5. Dtype: the transform casts the image to dtype.

Steps 2 to 4 are the AutoProcessor of the model (preprocessor_config.json).

The name of the model says 384, but its processor resizes to 512. The CheXagent-2 model code also resizes to 512 × 512 (bicubic) with the mean and std of this processor (D-16).

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text:
transform, encoder, *_ = make_chexagent(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    patches = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))  # img from Quick use
print(patches.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1024, 32, 32])

The patch features are the last hidden state of the vision model. SigLIP has no CLS token, so all tokens are patch tokens. The patch size is 16, so the grid is 512 / 16 = 32 on each side. See Segmentation mode for the shared rules.

docs.title: Text encoder
docs.text:
• Output: text_encoder(tokens) gives Tensor[T, 1024], float32, on the CPU. It is the pooler_output of the text model, the same as get_text_features of Transformers. The features are not L2-normalized. ZeroShotEvaluator normalizes them.
  • Tokenizer: the returned processor (a SiglipProcessor). Its SentencePiece tokenizer makes the text lowercase.
  • Text length: the tokenizer of the model pads to 64 tokens, but the text model has 256 positions. The recipe sets the tokenizer length to 256. SigLIP takes the feature from the last position, so the padding length changes the feature. Pad each prompt with padding="max_length". ZeroShotEvaluator does this for a SigLIP processor.
  • Prompt form: the model card gives no template. Its example passes plain labels to the Transformers zero-shot pipeline, and this pipeline uses the template "This is a photo of {}.".

Give both to the evaluator: ZeroShotEvaluator(encoder, text_encoder, tokenizer=processor, ...). See Zero-shot.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description device str "cuda" The device of the encoder and the text encoder, for example "cuda:1" or "cpu" hub str "StanfordAIMI/XraySigLIP__vit-l-16-siglip-384__webli" The Hugging Face name of the model output_keys set[str] None The keys of each sample. None gives {"img", "cls"}. With "mask", the encoder gives patch features (Segmentation mode) dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The dtype of the image tensor (Output dtype)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The first call downloads the weights from Hugging Face.
  • A note in the recipe code gives one VinDr-CXR zero-shot run: the macro AUROC was 0.488 with 64 tokens and 0.772 with 256 tokens.
  • The model card gives no facts about the training data.
  • For report generation, see CheXagent-2 (generator).
  • One model gives the image encoder and the text encoder. The recipe does not load the weights 2 times.
  • The processor does not cut a long prompt. A prompt of more than 256 tokens raises ValueError in the text model. ZeroShotEvaluator cuts it to 256 tokens and warns (D-52).
  • Vision-only evaluators use only the transform and the encoder.

docs.title: CheXagent-2 (generator)
docs.text:
Recipe make_chexagent_generator(), returns (transform, report_generator) Model card StanfordAIMI/CheXagent-2-3b Input size 512 × 512 (bicubic resize of the whole image, no crop, in the model code) Normalization mean 0.5 and std 0.5 on each channel, from the XraySigLIP processor that the model code reads Feature None: it generates a report Install extra chexagent_gen, in its own venv Segmentation features None: it generates a report

CheXagent-2 is a chest X-ray report generator from Stanford AIMI (Chen et al., arXiv 2024). It is a vision-language model with 3B parameters. Its image encoder is XraySigLIP, and a language model writes the text. Use it with ReportGenerationEvaluator to compare report generators.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block writes one report for one Montgomery image.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_chexagent_generator

transform, report_generator = make_chexagent_generator(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_report=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
sample = ds.get_datasets()[0]  # sample["img"] is the path of a temporary PNG
reports = report_generator([sample["img"]])
print(reports[0])
# FINDINGS: The hilar contours are normal. The lungs are clear. ...
#
# IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary process.

The output above is an example of one run. To score many reports, see Report generation.

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
The recipe works with image files, not tensors, because the CheXagent-2 code reads image paths.

  1. Load: the shared loader gives a 3-channel uint8 image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. PNG: the transform writes an RGB PNG to tmp_dir, and puts its path in sample["img"], as a string. The PNG name has a hash of the source path, so 2 images with the same file name get 2 PNG files. When the PNG is already there, the transform uses it again. The transform does not change report.
  3. Resize: the model code opens the PNG as RGB, and the whole image goes to 512 × 512 with bicubic interpolation. There is no crop.
  4. Scale: the values are divided by 255.
  5. Mean and std: 0.5 and 0.5 on each channel, so the values go to -1 to 1.

Steps 3 to 5 are the image transform of the model code (modeling_visual.py of the model).

The transform is a plain function sample -> sample, not a MONAI Compose.

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text: None: CheXagent-2 generates a report and gives no patch features.

docs.title: Generation
docs.text:
report_generator(img_paths, indications=None) takes a list[str] of PNG paths and gives a list[str] of reports, one for each path. Each call is greedy (do_sample=False, num_beams=1), with a system message "You are a helpful assistant.", as on the model card.

With prompt=None (the default), it runs the multi-step "ABCDE" steps of the CheXagent demo (demos/app_demo.py, commit e4f31e6e):

  1. Findings: one call with the image for each of 5 regions. The regions are Airway, Breathing, Cardiac, Diaphragm, and "Everything else" (mediastinal contours, bones, soft tissues, tubes, valves and pacemakers). The prompt is Please provide a detailed description of "<region>" in the chest X-ray. The recipe joins the answers that are not empty with spaces.
  2. Impression: one call with text only: Write the Impression section for the following Findings: <findings>.

The demo first asks for the view of the image and does not use the answer. The recipe skips this call.

The report is "FINDINGS: <findings>\n\nIMPRESSION: <impression>". ReportGenerationEvaluator scores this whole text against the ref_section of the real report. Before it scores, it removes the bold marks (**) that CheXagent-2 can write (D-50).

With a prompt string, the generator makes one call for each image with that prompt. The recipe does not change the answer.

To change the ABCDE steps, keep prompt=None. Then pass findings_prompts (one prompt for each region), or impression_prompt (a template with {findings}):

transform, report_generator = make_chexagent_generator(
    findings_prompts=["Describe the lungs.", "Describe the heart and mediastinum."],
    impression_prompt="Summarize the impression from these findings: {findings}",
)

With use_indication=True in ReportGenerationEvaluator, the generator gets the indication of each image. It puts "Clinical indication: <text>. " before the prompt string, or before each findings prompt. The impression call does not get it.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The model card asks for transformers==4.40.0, torch==2.7.1 and torchvision==0.22.1. These versions do not work with the other extras, so install the chexagent_gen extra in its own venv:

uv venv .venv-chexagent
source .venv-chexagent/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[chexagent_gen]"

RadEval needs other versions too. Generate the reports in this venv with ReportGenerationEvaluator.generate_only(), and score them in the radeval venv. See Report generation.

generate_only(path) writes a parquet file with the columns sample_id, reference and hypothesis, and patient_id when the dataset has patient IDs. It does not import RadEval.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description device str "cuda" The device of the model. The recipe loads with device_map=device, so the whole model is on this device hub str "StanfordAIMI/CheXagent-2-3b" The Hugging Face name of the model prompt str None None runs the ABCDE steps. A string makes one call for each image with that prompt findings_prompts list[str] None The findings prompts of the ABCDE steps, one call for each. None uses the 5 region prompts of the demo impression_prompt str None The template of the impression call. It must have {findings}. None uses the template of the demo max_new_tokens int 512 The maximum number of new tokens of each call dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The dtype of the model weights tmp_dir str None The folder for the PNG files. None makes a new folder under the system temp folder, and deletes it when Python exits. A folder that you give stays (D-16)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The first call downloads the weights from Hugging Face.
