  • The model card loads with device_map="auto", which can spread the model over all GPUs. The device does not change the output (D-16).
  • The Hugging Face model has its own code, so the recipe loads it with trust_remote_code=True.
  • With the default prompt=None, each image needs 6 calls of the model. Use max_samples of the evaluator for a short test.
  • Put tmp_dir on a fast local disk for a large dataset.
  • chexagent_gen and maira2_gen cannot share a venv. See the [tool.uv] conflicts list in pyproject.toml.
  • For the image and text encoder of CheXagent (zero-shot and probes), see CheXagent (XraySigLIP).

docs.title: CheXFound
docs.text:
Recipe make_chexfound(), returns (transform, encoder) Model card RPIDIAL/CheXFound Input size 512 × 512 (bicubic resize of the short side to 512, then center crop) Normalization Each channel goes to [0, 1] with its minimum and maximum. Then the ImageNet mean (0.485, 0.456, 0.406) and std (0.229, 0.224, 0.225), from the authors' eval transform Feature CLS tokens of the last 4 blocks, joined, 4096 values Install extra chexfound, a clone of the authors' repo and a checkpoint Segmentation features Tensor[B, 1024, 32, 32]

CheXFound is a ViT-L/16 with 4 register tokens. It comes from RPIDIAL (Yang et al., IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging 2025). It was trained with iBOT-style self-supervised learning (as in DINOv2) on up to 1 million public chest X-rays, at 512 × 512. Use it as a large chest X-ray ViT that was trained with images only.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block encodes one Montgomery image.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_chexfound

transform, encoder = make_chexfound(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
img = ds.get_datasets()[0]["img"]  # Tensor[3, 512, 512], torch.bfloat16
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    feature = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))
print(feature.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 4096])

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
1. Load: the shared loader gives a 3-channel uint8 image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. Scale: the values are divided by 255.
  3. Resize: the short side goes to 512 with bicubic interpolation.
  4. Crop: a center crop of 512 × 512.
  5. Min-max: the image is clipped to [0, 1]. Then each channel is scaled to [0, 1] with its minimum and maximum.
  6. Mean and std: the ImageNet values.
  7. Dtype: the transform casts the image to dtype.

Steps 3 to 6 are make_classification_eval_transform() in chexfound/data/transforms.py. chexfound/eval/classification/linear_glori.py calls it with resize_size=crop_size=image_size, and the authors' eval commands set --image-size 512 (README and scripts/eval/run_eval_shenzhen.sh). A bicubic resize can give values below 0 or above 255. The authors resize a uint8 PIL image, so PIL clips them to 0 to 255. Step 5 does the same clip, then runs the authors' RescaleImage.

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text:
transform, encoder = make_chexfound(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    patches = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))  # img from Quick use
print(patches.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1024, 32, 32])

The patch features are the patch tokens of the last block, after the final norm. They come from get_intermediate_layers(x, n=1, return_class_token=True), which drops the CLS and register tokens. The patch size is 16, so the grid is 512 / 16 = 32 on each side. See Segmentation mode for the shared rules.

docs.title: Feature
docs.text: The classification feature joins the normed CLS tokens of the last 4 blocks, in block order (4 × 1024 = 4096 values). The authors' linear probe uses this feature: n_last_blocks=[4] and avgpools=[False] in chexfound/eval/classification/linear_glori.py, with create_linear_input() (D-16).

docs.title: Weights and code
docs.text:
Do these 2 steps by hand before the first call:

  1. Clone the authors' repo. The recipe imports the model code from it.
git clone https://github.com/RPIDIAL/CheXFound third_party_models/CheXFound
  1. Download teacher_checkpoint.pth from the Google Drive folder of the authors. Put it at third_party_models/CheXFound/weights/teacher_checkpoint.pth, or pass checkpoint_path.

The checkpoint comes from FSDP training, with the block keys in 4 groups (backbone.blocks.<group>.<index>). The recipe renames them to blocks.<index>, as notebooks/chexfound_example.ipynb of the authors does. It builds the model with LayerScale (init_values=1e-5), so the trained LayerScale weights load.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description chexfound_dir str None The folder of the clone. None gives third_party_models/CheXFound/ at the repo root. A missing folder raises FileNotFoundError checkpoint_path str None The checkpoint file. None gives <chexfound_dir>/weights/teacher_checkpoint.pth. A missing file raises FileNotFoundError device str "cuda" The device of the encoder, for example "cuda:1" or "cpu" output_keys set[str] None The keys of each sample. None gives {"img", "cls"}. With "mask", the encoder gives patch features (Segmentation mode) dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The dtype of the image tensor (Output dtype)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Before 2026-11-01, the feature was the last CLS token (1024 values). Before 2026-11-03, the input had no step 5. An embedding_cache file from before 2026-11-03 raises ValueError (D-41). Delete the file. The next run makes a new one.
  • The plain forward of the model gives only the last CLS token (1024 values). The recipe calls get_intermediate_layers() instead, to get the 4 CLS tokens.

docs.title: DINOv3
docs.text:
Recipe make_dinov3(), returns (transform, encoder) Model card facebook/dinov3-vitb16-pretrain-lvd1689m Input size 224 × 224 (bilinear resize of the whole image, no crop) Normalization ImageNet mean (0.485, 0.456, 0.406) and std (0.229, 0.224, 0.225), from the DINOv3 processor Feature CLS token (pooler_output), 768 values Install extra dinov3 Segmentation features Tensor[B, 768, 14, 14]

DINOv3 is a ViT-B/16 from Meta (Siméoni et al., arXiv 2025), trained with self-supervised learning on LVD-1689M, a set of web images. It is not a medical model. Use it as a strong general-domain baseline next to the chest X-ray models.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block encodes one Montgomery image.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_dinov3

transform, encoder = make_dinov3(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
img = ds.get_datasets()[0]["img"]  # Tensor[3, 224, 224], torch.bfloat16
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    feature = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))
print(feature.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 768])

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
1. Load: the shared loader gives a 3-channel uint8 image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. Resize: the whole image goes to 224 × 224 with bilinear interpolation (size 224 × 224, resample=2 in preprocessor_config.json of the model card). The resize does not keep the aspect ratio. The processor does not crop.
  3. Scale: the values are divided by 255.
  4. Mean and std: the ImageNet values.
  5. Dtype: the transform casts the image to dtype.

Steps 2 to 4 are the AutoImageProcessor of the model card. Its settings come from preprocessor_config.json.

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text:
transform, encoder = make_dinov3(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    patches = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))  # img from Quick use
print(patches.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 768, 14, 14])

The token sequence of DINOv3 is the CLS token, 4 register tokens, then the patch tokens. The recipe drops the CLS and register tokens of last_hidden_state and keeps the patch tokens. It reads the number of register tokens from config.num_register_tokens. The register tokens do not match a patch of the image. The patch size is 16, so the grid is 224 / 16 = 14 on each side. See Segmentation mode for the shared rules.

None gives {"img", "cls"}. With "mask", the encoder gives patch features (Segmentation mode) dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The dtype of the image tensor (Output dtype)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The first call downloads the weights from Hugging Face.
  • The Hugging Face model is gated. Accept its license on the model card, then run hf auth login before the first call.
  • Another DINOv3 ViT model (hub) works with the same recipe. It gives its own feature size.

docs.title: EVA-X
docs.text:
Recipe make_eva_x(), returns (transform, encoder) Model card hustvl/EVA-X (weights: MapleF/eva_x) Input size 224 × 224 (bicubic resize of the short side to 256, then center crop) Normalization mean 0.49185243 and std 0.28509309 on each channel, from build_transform() of the EVA-X repo Feature Mean of the patch tokens, then fc_norm, 768 values (base), 384 (small) or 192 (tiny) Install extra eva_x and a clone of the authors' repo Segmentation features Tensor[B, D, 14, 14], with D = 768, 384 or 192

EVA-X is a family of ViTs from HUST VL (Yao et al., npj Digital Medicine 2025). It was trained with masked image modeling on Merged520k, a merged set of public chest X-ray datasets. It comes in 3 sizes (tiny, small and base). Use it as a chest X-ray ViT that was trained with images only.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block encodes one Montgomery image.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_eva_x

transform, encoder = make_eva_x(variant="base", device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
img = ds.get_datasets()[0]["img"]  # Tensor[3, 224, 224], torch.bfloat16
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    feature = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))
print(feature.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 768])

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
1. Load: the shared loader gives a 3-channel uint8 image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. Resize: the short side goes to 256 with bicubic interpolation (crop_pct = 224 / 256).
  3. Crop: a center crop of 224 × 224.
  4. Scale: the values are divided by 255.
  5. Mean and std: 0.49185243 and 0.28509309 on each channel. These are the EVA-X values, not the ImageNet values.
  6. Dtype: the transform casts the image to dtype.

Steps 2 to 5 are build_transform() in classification/utils/datasets.py of the EVA-X repo. These are its eval steps for an input size of 224.

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text:
transform, encoder = make_eva_x(variant="base", device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    patches = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))  # img from Quick use
print(patches.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 768, 14, 14])

The patch features are the patch tokens of forward_features(), without the CLS token. The patch size is 16, so the grid is 224 / 16 = 14 on each side. The patch features have no final norm. The model moves the pretrained norm weights to fc_norm, and fc_norm acts on the pooled feature only. See Segmentation mode for the shared rules.

docs.title: Feature
docs.text: The feature is the mean of the patch tokens, then the final norm fc_norm (forward_head(forward_features(x), pre_logits=True)). The fine-tune scripts of the authors use this pool (--use_mean_pooling in classification/train_files/eva_x/) (D-16). The model has no final norm for the CLS token, so the recipe does not use the CLS token.

docs.title: Weights and code
docs.text:
The recipe imports the model code from a clone of the EVA-X repo. Clone it before the first call:

git clone https://github.com/hustvl/EVA-X.git third_party_models/EVA-X

The weights are the file eva_x_<variant>_patch16_merged520k_mim.pt of MapleF/eva_x on Hugging Face. The tests used commit f08e647 of the clone.

Variant Feature size Parameters (Yao et al.) tiny 192 6M small 384 22M base 768 86M

docs.text:
• The first call downloads the weights from Hugging Face.

  • Before 2026-10-28, the recipe gave the CLS token. So results from before that date used another feature.

  • When it loads, the model code prints the missing keys head.weight and head.bias. The recipe does not use the head.

docs.title: MAIRA-2 (generator)
docs.text:
Recipe make_maira2_generator(), returns (transform, report_generator) Model card microsoft/maira-2 Input size The MAIRA-2 processor (format_and_preprocess_reporting_input) resizes and crops the PNG. See the model card Normalization The MAIRA-2 processor applies it Feature None: it generates a report Install extra maira2_gen, in its own venv Segmentation features None: it generates a report

MAIRA-2 is a chest X-ray report generator from Microsoft Health Futures (Bannur et al., arXiv 2024). It has 7B parameters: a RAD-DINO-MAIRA-2 image encoder and a Vicuna-7B v1.5 language model. Microsoft trained it on MIMIC-CXR, PadChest and a private US dataset. Use it with ReportGenerationEvaluator to compare report generators.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block writes one report for one Montgomery image.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_maira2_generator

transform, report_generator = make_maira2_generator(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_report=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
sample = ds.get_datasets()[0]  # sample["img"] is the path of a temporary PNG
reports = report_generator([sample["img"]])
print(reports[0])  # the findings text of one report

To score many reports, see Report generation.

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
The recipe works with image files, not tensors, the same as CheXagent-2 (generator).

  1. Load: the shared loader gives a 3-channel uint8 image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. PNG: the transform writes an RGB PNG to tmp_dir, and puts its path in sample["img"], as a string. The PNG name has a hash of the source path, so 2 images with the same file name get 2 PNG files. When the PNG is already there, the transform uses it again. The transform does not change report.
  3. Model input: report_generator opens the PNG as RGB. The MAIRA-2 processor resizes, crops and normalizes it.

The transform is a plain function sample -> sample, not a MONAI Compose.

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text: None: MAIRA-2 generates a report and gives no patch features.

docs.title: Generation
docs.text:
report_generator takes a list[str] of PNG paths and gives a list[str] of reports, one for each path. It follows the single-image report steps of the model card:

  1. Open the PNG as RGB.
  2. Call processor.format_and_preprocess_reporting_input() with the image as current_frontal. The other inputs are None: current_lateral, prior_frontal, indication, technique, comparison and prior_report. RadHarmony datasets give only the image and the real report.
  3. Generate with greedy decoding (do_sample=False, num_beams=1, use_cache=True), with at most max_new_tokens new tokens.
  4. Decode the new tokens with skip_special_tokens=True, and strip the spaces at the start and the end.

The recipe does not change the text of the model. With get_grounding=True, the text also has the grounding marks of the model. ReportGenerationEvaluator does not remove these marks: its cleaning step knows only the CheXagent-2 marks (D-50). So use get_grounding=False for a report that you score.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
MAIRA-2 needs an older transformers than the other extras and RadEval. So install the maira2_gen extra in its own venv:

uv venv .venv-maira2
source .venv-maira2/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[maira2_gen]"

Generate the reports in this venv with ReportGenerationEvaluator.generate_only(), and score them in the radeval venv. See Report generation.

generate_only(path) writes a parquet file with the columns sample_id, reference and hypothesis, and patient_id when the dataset has patient IDs. It does not import RadEval.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description device str "cuda" The device of the model. The recipe moves the whole model to it with .to(device) hub str "microsoft/maira-2" The Hugging Face name of the model max_new_tokens int 300 The maximum number of new tokens of each report dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The dtype of the model weights tmp_dir str None The folder for the PNG files. None makes a new folder under the system temp folder, and deletes it when Python exits. A folder that you give stays (D-16) get_grounding bool False True asks for a grounded report, with a box for each finding

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The first call downloads the weights from Hugging Face.
  • The Hugging Face model is gated. Accept its license on the model card, then run hf auth login before the first call.
  • The maira2_gen extra pins transformers>=4.46.0,<4.47, because transformers 5 breaks the model code. The current model card asks for transformers>=4.48.0,<4.52.
  • For a grounded report, the model card uses max_new_tokens=450. Pass max_new_tokens=450 together with get_grounding=True.
  • The model card turns the decoded text into plain text with processor.convert_output_to_plaintext_or_grounded_sequence(). The recipe does not call it.
  • The Hugging Face model has its own code, so the recipe loads it with trust_remote_code=True.
  • MAIRA-2 can also use a prior image and a prior report. The recipe always gives None for them. To use them, call the processor yourself.
  • maira2_gen and chexagent_gen cannot share a venv. See the [tool.uv] conflicts list in pyproject.toml.

docs.title: Medical MAE
docs.text:
Recipe make_medical_mae(), returns (transform, encoder) Model card lambert-x/medical_mae Input size 224 × 224 (bilinear resize of the short side to 256, then center crop) Normalization mean 0.5056 and std 0.252 on each channel, from the authors' Augmentation(normalize="chestx-ray") Feature CLS token after the final norm, 768 values (base) or 384 (small) Install extra medical_mae, a clone of the authors' repo and a checkpoint Segmentation features Tensor[B, D, 14, 14], with D = 768 or 384

Medical MAE is a ViT trained with a masked autoencoder (MAE) on chest X-rays, from Johns Hopkins University (Xiao et al., WACV 2023). ViT-Small was trained on 266,340 chest X-rays, and ViT-Base on 0.5M (the authors' README). Use it as a chest X-ray ViT that was trained with images only.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block encodes one Montgomery image.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_medical_mae

transform, encoder = make_medical_mae(variant="base", device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
img = ds.get_datasets()[0]["img"]  # Tensor[3, 224, 224], torch.bfloat16
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    feature = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))
print(feature.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 768])

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
1. Load: the shared loader gives a 3-channel uint8 image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. Scale: the values are divided by 255.
  3. Resize: the short side goes to 256 with bilinear interpolation (the torchvision default).
  4. Crop: a center crop of 224 × 224.
  5. Mean and std: 0.5056 and 0.252 on each channel. These are the authors' chest X-ray values, not the ImageNet values.
  6. Dtype: the transform casts the image to dtype.

Steps 3 to 5 are Augmentation(normalize="chestx-ray").get_augmentation("full_224", "val") of the authors (util/dataloader_med.py, used in util/datasets.py).

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text:
transform, encoder = make_medical_mae(variant="base", device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    patches = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))  # img from Quick use
print(patches.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 768, 14, 14])

The patch features are the patch tokens after the final norm (self.norm), without the CLS token. A forward hook on norm takes them. The patch size is 16, so the grid is 224 / 16 = 14 on each side. See Segmentation mode for the shared rules.

docs.title: Feature
docs.text: The feature is the CLS token after the pretrained final norm (norm). The recipe builds the model with global_pool=False, the default of the authors' linear probe (main_linprobe_chestxray.py) (D-16). With global_pool=True, the model uses a new fc_norm with no pretrained weights.

docs.title: Weights and code
docs.text:
Do these 2 steps by hand before the first call:

  1. Clone the authors' repo. The recipe imports models_vit and util.pos_embed from it.
git clone https://github.com/lambert-x/medical_mae third_party_models/medical_mae
  1. Download a pretrained checkpoint from the Google Drive link in the README of the repo. Put it in the clone folder: vit-b_CXR_0.5M_mae.pth (base) or vit_small_patch16_CXR_0.3M_mae_pretrain.pth (small).

The model code of the authors needs timm==0.4.12. Its forward_features(self, x) does not match the newer timm, which calls forward_features(x, attn_mask=..., is_causal=...). On the first call, the recipe installs timm==0.4.12 into legacy_timm_dir (Weights and code locations).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description variant str "base" "base" or "small". Any other value raises ValueError checkpoint_path str None The checkpoint file. None gives the file of variant in mae_dir. A missing file raises FileNotFoundError mae_dir str None The folder of the clone. None gives third_party_models/medical_mae/ at the repo root. A missing folder raises FileNotFoundError legacy_timm_dir str None The folder for timm==0.4.12. None gives <mae_dir>/timm-0412/ device str "cuda" The device of the encoder, for example "cuda:1" or "cpu" output_keys set[str] None The keys of each sample. None gives {"img", "cls"}. With "mask", the encoder gives patch features (Segmentation mode) dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The dtype of the image tensor (Output dtype)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: • The recipe loads the checkpoint as main_linprobe_chestxray.py does. It drops the head weights when their shape does not match the model, and loads with strict=False. The decoder keys of MAE are not used.

docs.title: MedImageInsight
docs.text:
Recipe make_medimageinsights(), returns (transform, encoder, text_encoder, None) Model card lion-ai/MedImageInsights Input size 480 × 480 (bicubic resize of the whole image, no crop) Normalization ImageNet mean (0.485, 0.456, 0.406) and std (0.229, 0.224, 0.225), from config.yaml of the model Feature Mean pool of the last DaViT stage, LayerNorm, projection and L2 normalization, 1024 values Install extra medimageinsights Segmentation features Tensor[B, 2048, 15, 15]

MedImageInsight is an image and text embedding model from Microsoft (Codella et al., arXiv 2024), with a DaViT (Dual Attention Vision Transformer) image encoder. Microsoft trained it with contrastive learning on medical images of many kinds and their text. lion-ai/MedImageInsights (with an "s") is a copy of the Microsoft weights with simpler loading code. Use it for zero-shot classification and as a general medical image encoder.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block encodes one Montgomery image and one prompt.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_medimageinsights

transform, encoder, text_encoder, _ = make_medimageinsights(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
img = ds.get_datasets()[0]["img"]  # Tensor[3, 480, 480], torch.bfloat16
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    feature = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))
print(feature.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1024])

print(text_encoder(["tuberculosis"]).shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1024]), float32 on the CPU

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
1. Load: the shared loader gives a PIL RGB image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. Resize: the whole image goes to 480 × 480 with bicubic interpolation. config.yaml sets TEST.CENTER_CROP: false, so there is no crop, and the resize changes the aspect ratio of the image.
  3. Scale: the values are divided by 255.
  4. Mean and std: the ImageNet values of config.yaml (see At a glance).
  5. Dtype: the transform casts the image to dtype.

Steps 2 to 4 are the preprocess chain of the model (build_transforms of its own code, for test data) (D-16).

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text:
transform, encoder, *_ = make_medimageinsights(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    patches = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))  # img from Quick use
print(patches.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 2048, 15, 15])

The patch features are the tokens of the last DaViT block, before the mean pool and the projection. So they have 2048 values (the width of the last stage), not 1024. A forward hook on image_encoder.blocks[3][0] takes them, and the recipe removes the hook after each call. The 4 DaViT stages reduce the size by 32 in total, so the grid is 480 / 32 = 15 on each side. See Segmentation mode for the shared rules.

docs.title: Text encoder
docs.text:
• Output: text_encoder(texts) takes a list[str] and gives Tensor[T, 1024], float32, on the CPU. It is encode of the model code: the feature of the end token, a projection, and L2 normalization.
  • Tokenizer: the model code has its own CLIP tokenizer (BPE, lowercase). It pads and cuts each prompt to 77 tokens. So the recipe returns None in place of a tokenizer. This keeps the same 4 items as the other image and text recipes.
  • Prompt form: the model card passes plain labels, for example "normal" and "Pneumonia".

Give the text encoder to the evaluator with no tokenizer: ZeroShotEvaluator(encoder, text_encoder, ...). Then the evaluator gives the prompt strings to the text encoder. See Zero-shot.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description device str "cuda" The device of the encoder and the text encoder, for example "cuda:1" or "cpu" hub str "lion-ai/MedImageInsights" The Hugging Face name of the model output_keys set[str] None The keys of each sample. None gives {"img", "cls"}. With "mask", the encoder gives patch features (Segmentation mode) dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The dtype of the image tensor (Output dtype)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The first call downloads the weights from Hugging Face. The recipe adds the downloaded folder to sys.path and imports medimageinsightmodel from it. The weights are in the 2024.09.27 folder.
  • The model code leaves the model in train mode after loading. The recipe sets eval mode, so the drop-path layers are off.
  • The model code prints Model loaded successfully on device: cuda, and PyTorch warns about use_reentrant of torch.utils.checkpoint. Both are harmless.
  • One model gives the image encoder and the text encoder. The recipe does not load the weights 2 times.
  • Vision-only evaluators use only the transform and the encoder.

docs.title: MedSigLIP
docs.text:
Recipe make_medsiglip(), returns (transform, encoder, text_encoder, processor) Model card google/medsiglip-448 Input size 448 × 448 (bicubic resize of the whole image, no crop) Normalization mean 0.5 and std 0.5 on each channel, from the MedSigLIP processor Feature Pooled output of the attention-pool head (pooler_output), 1152 values Install extra medsiglip Segmentation features Tensor[B, 1152, 32, 32]

MedSigLIP is a SigLIP model from Google, based on SigLIP-400M. Google trained it on medical image and text pairs: chest X-rays, skin, eye and pathology images, and CT and MRI slices, with their reports. It is the image encoder of MedGemma (Sellergren et al., arXiv 2025). Use it for zero-shot classification, for probes with little data, and for image search.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block encodes one Montgomery image and one prompt.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_medsiglip

transform, encoder, text_encoder, processor = make_medsiglip(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
img = ds.get_datasets()[0]["img"]  # Tensor[3, 448, 448], torch.bfloat16
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    feature = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))
print(feature.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1152])

tokens = processor(text=["a chest X-ray with tuberculosis"], padding="max_length", return_tensors="pt")
print(text_encoder(tokens).shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1152]), float32 on the CPU

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
1. Load: the shared loader gives a 3-channel uint8 image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. Resize: the whole image goes to 448 × 448 with bicubic interpolation (resample=3). There is no crop, so the resize changes the aspect ratio of the image.
  3. Scale: the values are divided by 255.
  4. Mean and std: 0.5 and 0.5 on each channel, so the values go to -1 to 1.
  5. Dtype: the transform casts the image to dtype.

Steps 2 to 4 are the AutoProcessor of the model (preprocessor_config.json).

The model card gives 2 ways to resize. It recommends tf.image.resize (bilinear, no antialias) to reproduce the results of its evals, as the Big Vision code does. The other way is the resize of the Transformers processor, which the card also allows. The recipe uses the processor (D-16). So a MedSigLIP score can differ a little from the scores of the model card.

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text:
transform, encoder, *_ = make_medsiglip(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    patches = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))  # img from Quick use
print(patches.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1152, 32, 32])

The patch features are the last hidden state of the vision model. SigLIP has no CLS token, so all tokens are patch tokens. The patch size is 14, so the grid is 448 / 14 = 32 on each side. See Segmentation mode for the shared rules.

docs.title: Text encoder
docs.text:
• Output: text_encoder(tokens) gives Tensor[T, 1152], float32, on the CPU. It is the pooler_output of the text model, the same as get_text_features of Transformers. The features are not L2-normalized. ZeroShotEvaluator normalizes them.
  • Tokenizer: the returned processor (a SiglipProcessor). Its SentencePiece tokenizer makes the text lowercase. The model trained with 64 tokens, so pad each prompt to 64 tokens with padding="max_length". ZeroShotEvaluator does this for a SigLIP processor.
  • Prompt form: the model card uses short phrases, for example "a photo of an arm with a rash".

Give both to the evaluator: ZeroShotEvaluator(encoder, text_encoder, tokenizer=processor, ...). See Zero-shot.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description device str "cuda" The device of the encoder and the text encoder, for example "cuda:1" or "cpu" hub str "google/medsiglip-448" The Hugging Face name of the model output_keys set[str] None The keys of each sample. None gives {"img", "cls"}. With "mask", the encoder gives patch features (Segmentation mode) dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The dtype of the image tensor (Output dtype)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The first call downloads the weights from Hugging Face.
  • The Hugging Face model is gated. Accept its license (the Health AI Developer Foundations terms of use) on the model card, then run hf auth login before the first call.
  • One model gives the image encoder and the text encoder. The recipe does not load the weights 2 times.
  • The processor does not cut a long prompt. A prompt of more than 64 tokens raises ValueError in the text model. ZeroShotEvaluator cuts it to 64 tokens and warns (D-52).
  • Vision-only evaluators use only the transform and the encoder.

docs.title: RAD-DINO
docs.text:
Recipe make_raddino(), returns (transform, encoder) Model card microsoft/rad-dino Input size 518 × 518 (bicubic resize of the short side to 518, then center crop) Normalization mean 0.5307 and std 0.2583 on each channel, from the RAD-DINO processor Feature CLS token after the final norm, 768 values Install extra raddino Segmentation features Tensor[B, 768, 37, 37]

RAD-DINO is a ViT-B/14 from Microsoft (Pérez-García et al., Nature Machine Intelligence 2025). It was trained with DINOv2 self-supervised learning on chest X-rays from MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert, NIH-CXR, PadChest and BRAX. It used the images only, with no labels and no text. Use it for frozen features in chest X-ray classification and segmentation.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block encodes one Montgomery image.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
img = ds.get_datasets()[0]["img"]  # Tensor[3, 518, 518], torch.bfloat16
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    feature = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))
print(feature.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 768])

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
1. Load: the shared loader gives a 3-channel uint8 image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. Resize: the short side goes to 518 with bicubic interpolation (size.shortest_edge=518, resample=3 in preprocessor_config.json of microsoft/rad-dino).
  3. Crop: a center crop of 518 × 518.
  4. Scale: the values are divided by 255.
  5. Mean and std: 0.5307 and 0.2583 on each channel. These are the RAD-DINO values, not the ImageNet values.
  6. Dtype: the transform casts the image to dtype.

Steps 2 to 5 are the RAD-DINO processor, as the rad-dino package loads it (use_fast=False, the PIL version of BitImageProcessor).

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text:
transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    patches = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))  # img from Quick use
print(patches.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 768, 37, 37])

The patch features are the patch tokens of the last block, after the final norm. The patch size is 14, so the grid is 518 / 14 = 37 on each side. See Segmentation mode for the shared rules.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description device str "cuda" The device of the encoder, for example "cuda:1" or "cpu" output_keys set[str] None The keys of each sample. None gives {"img", "cls"}. With "mask", the encoder gives patch features (Segmentation mode) dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The dtype of the image tensor (Output dtype)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The first call downloads the weights from Hugging Face. The rad-dino package does the download.
  • The feature is last_hidden_state[:, 0], as in RadDino.encode() of the rad-dino package. The model card example uses this package.

docs.title: SigLIP 2
docs.text:
Recipe make_siglip2(), returns (transform, encoder, text_encoder, processor) Model card google/siglip2-so400m-patch16-384 Input size 384 × 384 (bilinear resize of the whole image, no crop) Normalization mean 0.5 and std 0.5 on each channel, from the SigLIP 2 processor Feature Pooled output of the attention-pool head (pooler_output), 1152 values Install extra siglip2 Segmentation features Tensor[B, 1152, 24, 24]

SigLIP 2 is a general-domain image and text model from Google (Tschannen et al., arXiv 2025). Google trained it on WebLI, a large set of web images with their text, not on medical data. Its text encoder is multilingual. Use it as a general-domain baseline for zero-shot classification and for probes.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block encodes one Montgomery image and one prompt.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_siglip2

transform, encoder, text_encoder, processor = make_siglip2(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)
img = ds.get_datasets()[0]["img"]  # Tensor[3, 384, 384], torch.bfloat16
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    feature = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))
print(feature.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1152])

tokens = processor(text=["This is a photo of a chest X-ray with tuberculosis."], padding="max_length",
                   return_tensors="pt")
print(text_encoder(tokens).shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1152]), float32 on the CPU

docs.title: How the input is prepared
docs.text:
1. Load: the shared loader gives a 3-channel uint8 image in 0 to 255 (How a recipe loads an image).
  2. Resize: the whole image goes to 384 × 384 with bilinear interpolation (resample=2). There is no crop, so the resize changes the aspect ratio of the image.
  3. Scale: the values are divided by 255.
  4. Mean and std: 0.5 and 0.5 on each channel, so the values go to -1 to 1.
  5. Dtype: the transform casts the image to dtype.

Steps 2 to 4 are the AutoProcessor of the model (preprocessor_config.json).

docs.title: Segmentation mode
docs.text:
transform, encoder, *_ = make_siglip2(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    patches = encoder(img[None].to("cuda"))  # img from Quick use
print(patches.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 1152, 24, 24])

The patch features are the last hidden state of the vision model. SigLIP has no CLS token, so all tokens are patch tokens. The patch size is 16, so the grid is 384 / 16 = 24 on each side. See Segmentation mode for the shared rules.

docs.title: Text encoder
docs.text:
• Output: text_encoder(tokens) gives Tensor[T, 1152], float32, on the CPU. It is the pooler_output of the text model, the same as get_text_features of Transformers. The features are not L2-normalized. ZeroShotEvaluator normalizes them.
  • Tokenizer: the returned processor (a SiglipProcessor with a Gemma tokenizer). The model trained with 64 tokens, so pad each prompt to 64 tokens with padding="max_length". ZeroShotEvaluator does this for a SigLIP processor.
  • Lowercase: SigLIP 2 trained with lowercase text. The tokenizer of the Hugging Face model keeps capital letters, so the recipe adds a lowercase step to the processor. The Siglip2Tokenizer of Transformers has the same step.
  • Prompt form: the Transformers docs use "This is a photo of {label}.". The zero-shot pipeline uses the same template.

Give both to the evaluator: ZeroShotEvaluator(encoder, text_encoder, tokenizer=processor, ...). See Zero-shot.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description device str "cuda" The device of the encoder and the text encoder, for example "cuda:1" or "cpu" hub str "google/siglip2-so400m-patch16-384" The Hugging Face name of the model output_keys set[str] None The keys of each sample. None gives {"img", "cls"}. With "mask", the encoder gives patch features (Segmentation mode) dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The dtype of the image tensor (Output dtype)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The first call downloads the weights from Hugging Face.
  • One model gives the image encoder and the text encoder. The recipe does not load the weights 2 times.
  • Another hub model gives other sizes. The feature size is vision_config.hidden_size, for example 768 for google/siglip2-base-patch16-224. The patch grid is the input size divided by the patch size.
  • Before 2026-10-28, the recipe did not make the text lowercase. Zero-shot results made before that date have different text features. The image features did not change. In one run on 202 frontal images of the CheXpert validation split (5 labels), the zero-shot macro AUROC went from 0.717 to 0.727.
  • The processor does not cut a long prompt. A prompt of more than 64 tokens raises ValueError in the text model. ZeroShotEvaluator cuts it to 64 tokens and warns (D-52).
  • Vision-only evaluators use only the transform and the encoder.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
RadHarmony has 132 dataset registry keys. Each row of the inventory is one dataset configuration. The Registry keys column gives the keys for resolve_dataset(). list_datasets() in radharmony.registry lists every key (import radharmony.dataset first). The Page column links to the page of the dataset (constructor arguments, harmonizer notes, label columns).

When a row has split keys and one key without a split name (for example chexpert), use the split keys. The key without a split name is the old class. A row that says "not for benchmarks" is an old class. It mixes the official splits, or a folder or file that you give picks the split (D-09).

docs.title: Finding a dataset's label columns
docs.text:
Every image dataset class has LABEL_COLS and REG_COLS as class attributes. The VQA and captioning classes (VQA-RAD, CheXinstruct VQA, GEMeX-VQA, MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA, ROCO, ROCOv2 and MedPMC) do not have them. An example for image classes:

from radharmony.dataset import CheXpertDataset, RSNABoneAgeDataset

print(CheXpertDataset.LABEL_COLS)   # ['atelectasis', 'cardiomegaly', ...]
print(RSNABoneAgeDataset.REG_COLS)  # ['age_months']

The cls tensor in a data dict has one value for each entry in LABEL_COLS, in the order of sorted(LABEL_COLS) (the plain Python sort). This order can differ from the order in the class definition. See Dataset API → Data dict keys.

docs.title: Output flags
docs.text:
Each image dataset supports a subset of output flags. Passing a flag that the dataset does not support raises a warning and the key is absent from the data dict. The VQA and caption classes take none of these flags. They raise TypeError for an unknown argument (D-11).

Flag Data dict key Description output_cls=True "cls" Multi-label classification tensor output_mask=True "mask" Segmentation mask tensor output_bbox=True "bbox", "bbox_labels" Float32 tensor (N, 4) (2-D) or (N, 6) (3-D) of fractional boxes, and a list of labels in snake case (see Transforms → Boxes) output_report=True "report" Free-text radiology report string output_reg=True "reg" Regression target tensor

docs.title: base_image_dir convention
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the deepest common ancestor directory shared by all images in the dataset — not the competition root. image_path values are relative to it and may include subdirectory components (e.g. patient_id/study_id/image.dcm for datasets with patient/study folder structure). For each dataset, the wiki page above documents the exact expected layout and an example path.

For datasets with separate train/test splits, each split takes its own image directory:

Dataset Train base Test base CheXpert train/ valid/ ChestX-ray14 CXR14 root (images_001/ … images_012/ siblings) same VinDr-CXR train/ test/ SIIM-ACR-PTX dicom-images-train/ dicom-images-test/ SIIM COVID-19 train/ test/ RSNA Pneumonia (Kaggle) stage_2_train_images/ stage_2_test_images/ RSNA PE Detection train/ test/ RSNA Cervical Spine train_images/ test_images/ RSNA Abdominal Trauma train_images/ test_images/ RSNA Lumbar Spine train_images/ test_images/ RSNA Bone Age boneage-training-dataset/ boneage-test-dataset/ (validation: Bone Age Validation Set/) RANZCR CLiP Kaggle root (images in train/) Kaggle root (images in test/) QaTa-COV19 v2 QaTa-COV19-v2/Train Set/Images/ QaTa-COV19-v2/Test Set/Images/ ReXGradient-160K deid_png/ (train split) deid_png/ (test split — JSON differs per split, image tree shared)

Structural exceptions — some datasets have images split across multiple sibling subdirs inside base_image_dir, where image_path carries the subdir name. Examples:

  • MIMIC-CXR (DICOM) and MIMIC-CXR-JPG: base_image_dir is the files/ directory; images are grouped under p10/, p11/, … patient-group subdirectories, so image_path takes the form p{group}/p{patient_id}/s{study_id}/{image}.dcm (or .jpg).
  • ChestX-ray14: base_image_dir is the CXR14 root; images are split across its images_001/ … images_012/ sibling children.
  • PadChest: base_image_dir is the images/ directory; images are split across its 0/, 1/, …, 50/, 54/ sibling children (slots 51/52/53 don't exist in the official distribution).
  • RSNA Bone Age (val): base_image_dir is Bone Age Validation Set/; images are split across its boneage-validation-dataset-1/ and -2/ sibling children. (Train has no exception — its base_image_dir is the flat image directory.)

When adding a new dataset, follow the base_image_dir convention: no hardcoded subdirectory prefix in image_path that could be folded into base_image_dir instead.

docs.title: CT-RATE
docs.text:
Registry keys ct_rate_train, ct_rate_valid Task and outputs Classification, 18 labels (cls) Images in the table train 47,149 volumes (20,000 patients), valid 3,039 volumes (1,304 patients) Modality Chest CT, 3-D, NIfTI. One row is one volume License CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Accept the terms on Hugging Face before the download Download Get the data: CT-RATE

CT-RATE is a chest CT dataset with radiology reports (Hamamci et al., arXiv:2403.17834). The CT scans have no contrast. A scan can have more than 1 volume, one for each reconstruction. A text model read each report and gave 18 labels. The 2 splits have 50,188 volumes of 25,692 scans from 21,304 patients, as the paper says. The source also has the reports, but the harmonizer does not read them.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the train_fixed/ or valid_fixed/ folder. The class finds the label CSV and the metadata CSV in tables/, next to that folder. The Hugging Face download has these CSVs in multi_abnormality_labels/ and metadata/. Move them to tables/, or pass csv_path and view_position_csv_path.

CT-RATE/dataset/
  tables/train_predicted_labels.csv
  tables/train_metadata.csv
  tables/valid_predicted_labels.csv
  tables/validation_metadata.csv
  train_fixed/train_1/train_1_a/train_1_a_1.nii.gz
  valid_fixed/valid_1/valid_1_a/valid_1_a_1.nii.gz

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import CTRATETrainDataset, CTRATEValidDataset

train = CTRATETrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/CT-RATE/dataset/train_fixed/",
    output_cls=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 112, 112, 112), 1 channel, then (D, H, W)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(18,)

test_ds = CTRATEValidDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/CT-RATE/dataset/valid_fixed/",
    output_cls=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()

The image steps: the class keeps the default base_transpose=True. So the transform turns each volume to the axis code IPL and then to (D, H, W) (D-12). It clips the values to hu_window (default (-1000, 1000)) (D-14). Then it scales the 0.5 and 99.5 percentiles to -1 and 1. It resizes the longest side to 112, and pads the volume with -1 to 112 x 112 x 112 (D x H x W).

A volume file is large, so the first run is slow. The first run also writes a MONAI cache to ./cache. cache_dir=None gives no cache.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: train_predicted_labels.csv or valid_predicted_labels.csv. One row is one volume.
  • IDs: the VolumeName valid_1_a_1.nii.gz gives patient_id valid_1, study_id valid_1_a, and image_path valid_1/valid_1_a/valid_1_a_1.nii.gz. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Labels (D-05): the source has only 0 and 1. It has no uncertain or blank label.
  • View (D-01): view_position is the nearest plane ("axial", "coronal" or "sagittal") of ImageOrientationPatient in the metadata CSV. The vector goes to the extra column image_orientation, in one form: a whole number becomes an int, and the other numbers keep all their digits. The train split has 19 coronal and 14 sagittal volumes, and the others are axial. All valid volumes are axial.
  • Age and sex: they also come from the metadata CSV. age_years comes from PatientAge, in years (D-06). For example, 036Y gives 36. sex is M, F or NaN, from PatientSex (D-26). Without the metadata CSV, the harmonized table has no view_position, image_orientation, age_years or sex.
  • Split: the train class keeps only the volumes whose name starts with train_, and the valid class keeps the valid_ volumes. A label CSV with no such volume raises ValueError.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Orientation text: the metadata writes the same axial orientation in 2 forms. In the train metadata, 45,013 volumes have [1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0] and 2,084 have [1.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000, 1.000000, -0.000000] (D-01).
  • Tilted volumes: 12 train volumes are tilted more than 8° from the nearest plane (D-01).
  • Age in months: 7 train volumes have an age in months, for example 018M (1.5 years) (D-06).
  • Missing values: in the train metadata, 6 volumes have no sex and 12 have no age. In the valid metadata, 2 volumes have no age.
  • Volumes with no chest: some copies of CT-RATE have the lists no_chest_train.txt (752 volumes) and no_chest_valid.txt (37 volumes) in tables/. The harmonizer does not read them, so the harmonized table keeps these volumes (D-02). To remove them, filter the harmonized table by the file name:
with open("/data/CT-RATE/dataset/tables/no_chest_train.txt") as f:
    no_chest = {line.strip().rsplit("/", 1)[-1] for line in f if line.strip()}
df = df[~df["image_path"].str.rsplit("/", n=1).str[-1].isin(no_chest)]

docs.title: MedSeg COVID-19 CT
docs.text:
Registry keys medseg_covid_ct, medseg_covid_ct_val Task and outputs Segmentation of COVID-19 lesions: lesion masks (mask) and 4 slice labels (cls). medseg_covid_ct_val has images only Images in the table dataset1 100 slices, dataset2 829 slices (9 volumes), val 10 slices Modality Chest CT, 2-D axial slices of 3-D NIfTI volumes. One row is one slice License CC0 (the figshare records) Download Get the data: other datasets

MedSeg (medicalsegmentation.com) published 2 COVID-19 chest CT sets on figshare. "MedSeg Covid Dataset 1" (figshare 13521488) has 100 axial slices from 43 patients. "MedSeg Covid Dataset 2" (figshare 13521509) has 9 whole volumes. The argument subset picks one of them: "dataset1" or "dataset2".

The masks mark ground-glass opacity, consolidation and pleural effusion. It is like QaTa-COV19, but on CT. Its labels are not all 1: many slices have no lesion.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
The download needs no account. This script gets the files of both records from figshare:

import json
import urllib.request

for aid in (13521488, 13521509):
    det = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/{aid}"))
    for f in det["files"]:
        urllib.request.urlretrieve(f["download_url"], f["name"])

Put the files of each record in its own folder. Unzip rp_im.zip and rp_msk.zip of dataset2 in that folder. base_image_dir is the folder of one record.

MedSeg-COVID-CT/
  figshare_13521488/tr_im.nii.gz
  figshare_13521488/tr_mask.nii.gz
  figshare_13521488/val_im.nii.gz
  figshare_13521509/rp_im/1.nii.gz
  figshare_13521509/rp_msk/1.nii.gz

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MedSegCOVIDCTDataset, MedSegCOVIDCTValDataset

ds = MedSegCOVIDCTDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MedSeg-COVID-CT/figshare_13521509/",
    slice_output_dir="/data/medseg_slices/",  # any folder you can write to
    subset="dataset2",
    output_cls=True,
    output_mask=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the volumes go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(4,), pleural_effusion is NaN in dataset2
# sample["mask"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224), 1 is lesion and 0 is background

test_ds = MedSegCOVIDCTValDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MedSeg-COVID-CT/figshare_13521488/",
    slice_output_dir="/data/medseg_slices/",
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
# test_ds[0] has only "img": 10 slices with no labels, to look at predictions

The first run writes 1 image PNG and 1 mask PNG for each slice to <slice_output_dir>/<subset>_hu<low>_<high>/, for example dataset2_hu-1000_400/. The harmonizer does not write a PNG again when the file exists. The first run also writes a MONAI cache to ./cache. cache_dir=None gives no cache.

hu_window (default (-1000.0, 400.0), a lung window) acts in the harmonizer. It clips each slice to the window and saves it as an 8-bit PNG. The raw HU values stay only in the .nii.gz files. The window is in the folder name, so a new window writes new PNGs. Then the transform scales the 0.5 and 99.5 percentiles of the PNG to -1 and 1 (D-14).

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: in dataset1, tr_im.nii.gz and tr_mask.nii.gz hold 100 slices of 512 x 512 (H x W). In dataset2, rp_im/<n>.nii.gz and rp_msk/<n>.nii.gz hold the 9 volumes, with slices of 630 x 630 (H x W). One row is one axial slice. In dataset1, the harmonizer also reads Test-Images-Clinical-Details.csv. It holds the SIRM case, the age and the sex of each tr_im slice.
  • Slices (D-12): the harmonizer writes each slice in the usual axial view. Rows go from anterior to posterior, and columns go from patient right to patient left. The mask gets the same step.
  • IDs: in dataset2, slice 7 of rp_im/1.nii.gz gives patient_id 1, study_id dataset2_1_0007 and image_path dataset2_1_0007.png. In dataset1, slice 0 gives study_id dataset1_tr_0000, and its SIRM case gives patient_id 42. The class sets base_image_dir to the images/ folder of the slices, and image_path is relative to it (D-04).
  • Patients (D-10): in dataset2, one volume is one patient. In dataset1, patient_id is the SIRM case from Test-Images-Clinical-Details.csv, so the 100 slices are 43 patients. Without this file, the harmonizer raises FileNotFoundError. The val_im slices are not in the file, so each val slice is its own patient.
  • Labels (D-05): they come from the class values in the mask slice: 1 ground-glass opacity, 2 consolidation and 3 pleural effusion. A label is 1 when the slice has its value. Else it is 0. any_lesion is 1 when the slice has a value above 0. The dataset2 masks have only 0, 1 and 2, so pleural_effusion is NaN in each dataset2 row.
  • View (D-01): the source has no view, so the harmonized table has no view_position.
  • Age and sex (D-06, D-26): in dataset1, they come from Test-Images-Clinical-Details.csv. Only the first row of a case has them, and they apply to all slices of the case. Sex 0 gives "M" and 1 gives "F". The dataset2 volumes and the val slices have no age or sex. So their harmonized tables have no age_years or sex.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row.

docs.text:
The 4 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Meaning any_lesion The slice has a lesion of any class consolidation The slice has consolidation (mask value 2) ground_glass The slice has ground-glass opacity (mask value 1) pleural_effusion The slice has pleural effusion (mask value 3). NaN in dataset2

The slices with each label:

Subset any_lesion consolidation ground_glass pleural_effusion dataset1 (100 slices) 99 78 96 25 dataset2 (829 slices) 373 233 298 NaN

docs.title: Masks
docs.text:
• Source: tr_mask.nii.gz and rp_msk/<n>.nii.gz hold one class value for each voxel: 0 background, 1 ground-glass opacity, 2 consolidation and 3 pleural effusion (dataset1 only). The harmonizer does not read the lung masks in rp_lung_msk/.
  • The harmonizer writes 1 binary mask PNG for each slice to the masks/ folder of the slices. A pixel is 255 when its class value is above 0. Else it is 0. So the mask joins the 3 classes. The labels tell the classes apart.
  • mask_path is the full path of that PNG, for example /data/medseg_slices/dataset2_hu-1000_400/masks/dataset2_1_0007.png. The extra column lesion_pixels holds the number of lesion pixels in the slice.
  • An empty mask_path means "not annotated" (D-33). With output_mask=True, the class drops these rows and warns. Every slice has a mask, so no row is dropped. A slice with no lesion has an all-zero mask: 1 slice in dataset1 and 456 slices in dataset2.
  • The sample: mask is a float32 tensor (1, 224, 224) with the values 0 and 1 (D-14). The transform resizes it with the image.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• dataset1 age and sex: in Test-Images-Clinical-Details.csv, SIRM cases 16, 18 and 19 have no age or sex, and cases 17 and 45 have no sex. The last row, "Not used", lists SIRM cases, not slices.
  • dataset2 volume sizes: the 9 volumes have 39 to 418 slices, and volume 3 has 418 of the 829 slices. So a split by volume can give splits of very different sizes.
  • dataset2 slice order: volume 1 has the orientation code LPI, and the other volumes have LPS. The view of a slice is the same, but slice_index 0 is at the other end of the chest.
  • val slices: val_im.nii.gz has no masks.

docs.title: RAD-ChestCT
docs.text:
Registry keys radchestct_train, radchestct_valid, radchestct_test Task and outputs Classification, 84 labels (cls). One lung box for each volume (bbox) Images in the table train 2,286 volumes (2,114 patients), valid 984 volumes (616 patients), test 360 volumes (342 patients) Modality Chest CT, 3-D, NumPy .npz. One row is one scan, which is one volume License Duke University owns the data. CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, or a separate license from Duke. Ask for access on Zenodo before the download Download Get the data: RAD-ChestCT

RAD-ChestCT is a chest CT dataset from Duke University (Draelos et al., Medical Image Analysis 2021). A text tool read each report and marked 84 findings at 52 locations. The metadata file lists 35,747 scans. The Zenodo record has only the first release, about 10% of the scans. It has 3,630 volumes with labels, in 3 label CSVs. The record does not say how to get the other scans.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the images/ folder, with one <NoteAcc_DEID>.npz file for each volume. The class finds the CSV files in base_image_dir or in the folder above it, also in their tables/ folders.

RAD-ChestCT/
  tables/CT_Scan_Metadata_Complete_35747.csv
  tables/Extrema_35747.csv
  tables/imgtrain_Abnormality_and_Location_Labels.csv
  tables/imgvalid_Abnormality_and_Location_Labels.csv
  tables/imgtest_Abnormality_and_Location_Labels.csv
  images/trn00022.npz

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import RadChestCTTrainDataset, RadChestCTTestDataset

train = RadChestCTTrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/RAD-ChestCT/images/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 112, 112, 112), 1 channel, then (D, H, W)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(84,)
# sample["bbox"]: Tensor(N, 6), the lung box. N is 1, or 0 for a volume with no box
# sample["bbox_labels"]: a list of N names, ['lung'] or []

test_ds = RadChestCTTestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/RAD-ChestCT/images/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()

The image steps: the .npz arrays have no orientation data, but they are already in the IPL orientation and in (D, H, W) order. So the class passes base_transpose=False, and the transform does not turn the volume (D-12). The transform clips the values to the fixed window (-1000, 400) (D-14). Then it scales the 0.5 and 99.5 percentiles to -1 and 1. It resizes the longest side to 112, and pads the volume with -1 to 112 x 112 x 112 (D x H x W).

The class has no argument for the window, so pass your own transform for another window. The files we checked hold int16 HU values from -1000 to 1000.

The first run writes a MONAI cache to ./cache. cache_dir=None gives no cache.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: one label CSV, img<split>_Abnormality_and_Location_Labels.csv. One row is one volume.
  • IDs: the NoteAcc_DEID tst29112 gives study_id tst29112 and image_path tst29112.npz. The metadata CSV holds its MRN_DEID mrn16164, which gives patient_id mrn16164. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04). One study is one volume.
  • Labels (D-05): a source column is <finding>*<location>, for example nodule*left_upper. A finding is 1 when one of its locations is 1. Else it is 0. The source has no uncertain or blank label.
  • View (D-01): the metadata CSV has orig_orientation, but the harmonizer does not read it. So the harmonized table has no view_position.
  • Age and sex: the source has no age or sex, so the harmonized table has no age_years or sex (D-06, D-26).
  • Split: a split class needs the label CSV of its split. A label CSV of another split raises ValueError.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops a volume with no .npz file in base_image_dir. Every volume of the label CSVs has a file.

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: Extrema_35747.csv has one lung box for each of its 35,747 volumes. 6 columns hold the voxel index of the first and last lung voxel on each axis: sup_axis0min and inf_axis0max, ant_axis1min and pos_axis1max, rig_axis2min and lef_axis2max. The columns shape0, shape1 and shape2 hold the size of the volume.
  • The harmonizer divides the 2 axis 0 values by shape0, the axis 1 values by shape1, and the axis 2 values by shape2. The volume is (D, H, W) in IPL order, so axis 0 goes from superior to inferior.
  • The box is [dim0_min, dim0_max, dim1_min, dim1_max, dim2_min, dim2_max], in fractions of the volume size (D-07).
  • Example: tst29112 has the values 33, 362, 145, 363, 68 and 408, and the size (406, 470, 470) (D, H, W). It gives bbox [0.0812807881773399, 0.8916256157635468, 0.30851063829787234, 0.7723404255319148, 0.14468085106382977, 0.8680851063829788] and bbox_labels ["lung"].
  • bbox_labels: ["lung"] for each box (D-07).
  • Readers (D-36): the source has one box for each volume, so the harmonizer does not group boxes.
  • No box: a volume with an inf value in the source gets bbox [] and bbox_labels []. Box counts: train 2,272 boxes on 2,286 volumes, valid 983 on 984, and test 360 on 360.
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 6), in fractions of the returned volume (D-28). bbox_labels is a list of N names. Example: tst29112 gives (1, 6) and ['lung']. The pad to a cube moves the box on axis 0, so its first 2 values are 0.1329 and 0.8347. A volume with no box gives (0, 6) and [].
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box to the volume. It drops a box with no area after the clip, and warns (D-07). The source files have no such box.

docs.title: RSNA 2022 Cervical Spine
docs.text:
Registry keys rsna_2022_cervical_spine_train, rsna_2022_cervical_spine_bbox, rsna_2022_cervical_spine_test Task and outputs Classification, 8 labels (cls). Vertebra masks (mask) on 87 studies. 3-D fracture boxes (bbox) in the bbox class. The test split has images only Images in the table train 2,019 volumes, bbox 235 volumes, test 3 volumes (sample files only). One study is one patient Modality Neck CT, 3-D, DICOM series. One row is one study, which is one volume License The rules of the Kaggle competition. Accept them before the download Download Get the data: RSNA 2022 Cervical Spine

RSNA 2022 Cervical Spine Fracture Detection is a 2022 Kaggle challenge. The train split has 2,019 CT studies of the neck. Each study has 8 labels: a fracture label for each vertebra from C1 to C7, and patient_overall. 235 studies also have 7,217 fracture boxes, each on one slice. 87 studies have a segmentation of the vertebrae. The test images are hidden (D-25).

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is train_images/ or test_images/. The classes find train.csv, train_bounding_boxes.csv and test.csv in base_image_dir or in the folder above it. The train class finds segmentations/ next to base_image_dir.

rsna-2022-cervical-spine-fracture-detection/
  train.csv
  train_bounding_boxes.csv
  test.csv
  segmentations/<StudyInstanceUID>.nii
  train_images/<StudyInstanceUID>/<slice_number>.dcm
  test_images/<StudyInstanceUID>/<slice_number>.dcm

The bbox class reads the header of each slice file of its 235 studies. This takes about 1 minute. On the public download, test_ds[0] raises RuntimeError (see Splits).

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import (
    RSNA2022CervicalSpineBboxDataset,
    RSNA2022CervicalSpineTestDataset,
    RSNA2022CervicalSpineTrainDataset,
)

train = RSNA2022CervicalSpineTrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/rsna-2022-cervical-spine-fracture-detection/train_images/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_mask=True,  # keeps only the 87 studies with a segmentation
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 112, 112, 112), 1 channel, then (D, H, W)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(8,)
# sample["mask"]: Tensor(1, 112, 112, 112), the vertebra numbers

boxes = RSNA2022CervicalSpineBboxDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/rsna-2022-cervical-spine-fracture-detection/train_images/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
box_train_ds, box_val_ds = boxes.get_datasets(n_splits=5)
# box_train_ds[0]["bbox"]: Tensor(N, 6), one row for each slice box
# box_train_ds[0]["bbox_labels"]: a list of N names, all 'fracture'

test_ds = RSNA2022CervicalSpineTestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/rsna-2022-cervical-spine-fracture-detection/test_images/",
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
# test_ds[0] has only "img", for a Kaggle submission

The image steps: MONAI ITKReader reads all DICOM files of the study folder as one volume. The class keeps the default base_transpose=True. So the transform turns each volume to the axis code IPL and then to (D, H, W) (D-12). It clips the values to hu_window (default (-200, 1800), for bone) (D-14). Then it scales the 0.5 and 99.5 percentiles to -1 and 1. It resizes the longest side to 112, and pads the volume with -1 to 112 x 112 x 112 (D x H x W).

The bbox class has no hu_window argument. Its transform clips the values to (-1000, 1000).

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: train.csv has one row for each study. The folder train_images/<StudyInstanceUID>/ holds one .dcm file for each slice.
  • IDs: the StudyInstanceUID 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.6200 gives patient_id, study_id and image_path 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.6200. image_path is the study folder, relative to base_image_dir (D-04). The source has no patient ID column. The DICOM PatientID is the last part of the StudyInstanceUID (for example 6200), so one study is one patient.
  • Labels (D-05): the columns C1 to C7 become c1 to c7, and patient_overall stays. 1 gives 1 and 0 gives 0. The source has no uncertain or blank label.
  • View (D-01): the DICOM headers have ImageOrientationPatient, but the harmonizer does not read it. So the harmonized table has no view_position. D-01 lists this as a known gap. All 2,019 studies are axial.
  • Age and sex: the source files and the DICOM headers have neither, so the harmonized table has no age_years or sex (D-06, D-26).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row. harmonize() does not check that the study folders exist.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 8 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Meaning c1 A fracture of the C1 vertebra c2 A fracture of the C2 vertebra c3 A fracture of the C3 vertebra c4 A fracture of the C4 vertebra c5 A fracture of the C5 vertebra c6 A fracture of the C6 vertebra c7 A fracture of the C7 vertebra patient_overall A fracture of any cervical vertebra

In the train split, patient_overall is 1 for 961 studies.

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
Only RSNA2022CervicalSpineBboxDataset has boxes. It has one row for each of the 235 studies with a box.

  • Source: train_bounding_boxes.csv has 7,217 rows. Each row is a pixel box on one slice: x, y, width, height and slice_number (the name of the slice file). The source has no finding name or vertebra for a box. All 235 studies have patient_overall 1.
  • The harmonizer reads the header of each slice file, so it needs base_image_dir. It sorts the slices of a study by ImagePositionPatient[2], from low to high, as the 3-D loader does. The rank of the box slice in this order gives the depth: from rank / n_slices to (rank + 1) / n_slices. It divides y and y + height by Rows (the height), and x and x + width by Columns (the width).
  • The box is [dim0_min, dim0_max, dim1_min, dim1_max, dim2_min, dim2_max], in fractions of the volume size (D-07). In the harmonized table, the order is slice, y, x, in the slice order of the 3-D loader. The class turns the box with the volume (D-12, D-28). These series are axial, so the slice is the D axis.
  • Example: study 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.10051 has 272 slices. Its first box has x 219.27715, y 216.71419, width 17.304399999999987, height 20.385169999999988 and slice_number 133. Slice 133 has the rank 139. The box is [0.5110294117647058, 0.5147058823529411, 0.42326990234375, 0.4630846875, 0.42827568359375, 0.46207333984375].
  • bbox_labels: fracture for each box, because the source has no finding name (D-07).
  • Readers (D-36): the source has one set of boxes for each study, so the harmonizer does not group boxes.
  • bbox and bbox_labels are JSON text in the harmonized table, so they stay the same after a CSV save and load.
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 6), in fractions of the returned volume (D-28). bbox_labels is a list of N names. Example: (2, 6) and ['fracture', 'fracture']. A study has 2 to 167 boxes. A fracture on 10 slices gives 10 thin boxes, not one box.
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box to the volume. It drops a box with no area after the clip, and warns (D-07). It also drops a box on a slice with no DICOM file in the study folder, and warns. The source files have no such box.

docs.title: Masks
docs.text:
• Source: segmentations/ has one NIfTI file <StudyInstanceUID>.nii for 87 studies. It covers the whole volume. Its values are the vertebra numbers (Lin et al., Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2023). 0 is the background, 1 to 7 are C1 to C7, and 8 to 19 are T1 to T12. Every mask has C1 to C7, but not every mask has all thoracic vertebrae.
  • mask_path is the full path of the file, for example /data/rsna-2022-cervical-spine-fracture-detection/segmentations/1.2.826.0.1.3680043.10633.nii. Without segmentation_dir, the class looks for segmentations/ next to base_image_dir.
  • An empty mask_path means "not annotated" (D-33). With output_mask=True, the class drops these rows and warns. Only the 87 studies with a file stay.
  • The sample: mask is a float32 tensor (1, 112, 112, 112) with the vertebra numbers of the file. For example, one study has the values 0 to 10. The transform turns and resizes it with the volume. The resize takes the nearest value, so the numbers stay whole. The 0 and 1 rule of D-14 is for 2-D masks only.

docs.text:
Class Registry key Images Source RSNA2022CervicalSpineTrainDataset rsna_2022_cervical_spine_train 2,019 train.csv and train_images/ RSNA2022CervicalSpineBboxDataset rsna_2022_cervical_spine_bbox 235 The train studies in train_bounding_boxes.csv. They are also in the train class RSNA2022CervicalSpineTestDataset rsna_2022_cervical_spine_test 3 test.csv and test_images/, with no labels (D-25). Use it only for a Kaggle submission RSNA2022CervicalSpineDataset rsna_2022_cervical_spine The old key. It reads train.csv, so it has the train studies. Use the split classes for a benchmark (D-09)

The source has no labeled test split. get_datasets(n_splits=5) makes a train and val split from the train class. It groups by patient (D-10). The source has no patient ID, so one study is one patient, and nobody can check that a patient is in only 1 split. The bbox class has train studies only, so do not use it to test a model that you trained on the train class.

This is a Kaggle code competition (D-25). The public download has only sample test files. The 3 studies of test.csv are not in the 3 folders of test_images/. So test_ds has 3 rows, but test_ds[0] raises RuntimeError, because the study folder does not exist. Use the test class in a Kaggle notebook of the competition, where the hidden test set has the same layout.
