docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Test files: the public download has only sample test files (D-25).
  • Slice size: most studies are 512 x 512 (H x W). 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.22678 and 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8858 are 768 x 768, and 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.23400 is 512 x 519 (H x W). Of these 3, only 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.22678 has boxes (see Boxes).
  • Slice order: in about 9 of 10 studies, the slice number goes up as ImagePositionPatient[2] goes down. So the file name order puts a box at the wrong end of the volume (see Boxes).

docs.title: RSNA 2024 Lumbar Spine
docs.text:
Registry keys rsna_2024_lumbar_spine_train, rsna_2024_lumbar_spine_test Task and outputs Classification, 75 labels (cls): 25 targets with 3 severities each. Small boxes around points (bbox). The test split has images only Images in the table train 6,294 volumes (1,975 studies), test 3 volumes (1 study, sample files only). One study is one patient Modality Lower back MRI, 3-D, DICOM series. One row is one series, which is one volume License The rules of the Kaggle competition. Accept them before the download Download Get the data: RSNA 2024 Lumbar Spine

RSNA 2024 Lumbar Spine Degenerative Classification is a 2024 Kaggle challenge. The train split has 1,975 MRI studies of the lower back. Radiologists graded 5 conditions at 5 disc levels (L1/L2 to L5/S1), so a study has 25 targets (LumbarDISC dataset paper, arXiv:2506.09162). Each target is Normal/Mild, Moderate or Severe, or blank in train.csv. A study has about 3 series (Sagittal T1, Sagittal T2/STIR and Axial T2), and RadHarmony makes one row for each series: 6,294 rows.

A point file marks where each target is on one slice. The test images are hidden (D-25).

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is train_images/ or test_images/. The classes find the CSV files in base_image_dir or in the folder above it.

rsna-2024-lumbar-spine-degenerative-classification/
  train.csv
  train_series_descriptions.csv
  train_label_coordinates.csv
  test_series_descriptions.csv
  train_images/<study_id>/<series_id>/<instance_number>.dcm
  test_images/<study_id>/<series_id>/<instance_number>.dcm

When the train class finds train_label_coordinates.csv, it makes the boxes. For this, it reads the header of each slice file. This took about 15 minutes for the 6,294 series in a test run.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import RSNA2024LumbarSpineTestDataset, RSNA2024LumbarSpineTrainDataset

train = RSNA2024LumbarSpineTrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/rsna-2024-lumbar-spine-degenerative-classification/train_images/",
    series_filter="Sagittal T2/STIR",  # keep one series type
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 112, 112, 112), 1 channel, then (D, H, W)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(75,)
# sample["bbox"]: Tensor(N, 6), one small box for each point
# sample["bbox_labels"]: a list of N names, for example ['spinal_canal_stenosis_l1_l2']

test_ds = RSNA2024LumbarSpineTestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/rsna-2024-lumbar-spine-degenerative-classification/test_images/",
    series_filter="Sagittal T2/STIR",
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
# test_ds[0] has only "img", for a Kaggle submission

The image steps: MONAI ITKReader reads all DICOM files of the series folder as one volume. The class keeps the default base_transpose=True. So the transform turns each volume to the axis code IPL and then to (D, H, W) (D-12). MRI has no fixed value scale, so the class uses hu_window=None and clips nothing. Then the transform scales the 0.5 and 99.5 percentiles to -1 and 1. It resizes the longest side to 112, and pads the volume with -1 to 112 x 112 x 112 (D x H x W).

Example: a sagittal series of 15 slices of 640 x 640 (H x W) becomes a volume about 3 voxels thick.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: train.csv has one row for each study, with 25 target columns. train_series_descriptions.csv has one row for each series. The harmonizer joins them on study_id, so one row is one series.
  • IDs: the study_id 4003253 and series_id 702807833 give patient_id 4003253, study_id 4003253, series_id 702807833 and image_path 4003253/702807833. image_path is the series folder, relative to base_image_dir (D-04). The source has no patient ID column. The DICOM PatientID equals study_id, so one study is one patient.
  • Labels (D-05): each target becomes 3 columns, one for each severity. Moderate gives 1 in ..._moderate and 0 in the other 2. A blank target gives NaN in all 3 columns, not 0. The labels of a study repeat on each of its series.
  • View (D-01): view_position holds the series description: Axial T2, Sagittal T1 or Sagittal T2/STIR. D-01 asks for the plane (axial or sagittal) in view_position and the description in a column series_description. D-01 lists this as a known gap. series_filter keeps the rows of one series description.
  • Age and sex: the source files and the DICOM headers have neither, so the harmonized table has no age_years or sex (D-06, D-26).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops a series whose study is not in train.csv. The source files have no such series.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 75 label columns are <condition>_<level>_<severity>, sorted by name, in the order of cls. Example: spinal_canal_stenosis_l1_l2_normal_mild, spinal_canal_stenosis_l1_l2_moderate and spinal_canal_stenosis_l1_l2_severe.

Part Values Meaning Condition spinal_canal_stenosis The spinal canal is narrow left_neural_foraminal_narrowing, right_neural_foraminal_narrowing The opening for a nerve root, on the left or right side, is narrow left_subarticular_stenosis, right_subarticular_stenosis The space below a facet joint, on the left or right side, is narrow Level l1_l2, l2_l3, l3_l4, l4_l5, l5_s1 The disc level Severity normal_mild, moderate, severe The grade of the condition

572 study targets are blank, in 185 studies. Their 3 columns are NaN in cls, so the probes skip them (D-05).

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: train_label_coordinates.csv has 48,692 points on 6,291 series. Each row is one point of one target: instance_number (the slice), condition, level, and x and y in pixels.
  • The harmonizer lists the slice files of each series in the order of the 3-D loader, with itk.GDCMSeriesFileNames, the same call as ITKReader. It reads the header of each slice file, so it needs base_image_dir. The rank of the point slice in this order gives the depth: from rank / n_slices to (rank + 1) / n_slices. It divides y by Rows (the height) and x by Columns (the width). The box goes 0.015 (bbox_epsilon) below and above each of these 2 values.
  • The box is [dim0_min, dim0_max, dim1_min, dim1_max, dim2_min, dim2_max], in fractions of the volume size (D-07). In the harmonized table, the order is slice, y, x, in the slice order of the 3-D loader. The class turns the box with the volume (D-12, D-28). So in ds[i] of a sagittal series, the slice is the last axis (W).
  • Example: series 4003253/702807833 (Sagittal T2/STIR) has 15 slices, and each slice is 640 x 640 (H x W). Its first point has instance_number 8, x 322.83185840707966 and y 227.9646017699115, for Spinal Canal Stenosis at L1/L2. Slice 8 has the rank 7. The box is [0.4666666666666667, 0.5333333333333333, 0.3411946902654867, 0.37119469026548674, 0.48942477876106194, 0.519424778761062].
  • bbox_labels: <condition>_<level> in snake_case, for example spinal_canal_stenosis_l1_l2 (D-07).
  • Readers (D-36): the source has one point for each target on a series, so the harmonizer does not group boxes.
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 6), in fractions of the returned volume (D-28). bbox_labels is a list of N names. Example: (5, 6) and ['spinal_canal_stenosis_l1_l2', ..., 'spinal_canal_stenosis_l5_s1'] for the series above. A series with no point gives (0, 6) and [].
  • Points with no box: some series folders hold 2 GDCM sub-series, and the 3-D loader reads only the first. A point on the second sub-series is not on the loaded volume, so the harmonizer makes no box for it. A point on a series folder or a slice file that cannot be read also has no box. harmonize() warns with the count (D-07). In a test run, 151 points had no box.
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box to the volume. It drops a box with no area after the clip, and warns (D-07). The source files have no such box.
  • Without a point file, the harmonized table has no bbox column. Then output_bbox=True warns and adds no box keys (D-11).

docs.text:
• Series per study: most studies have 3 series, but not all. 335 studies have 2 or more Axial T2 series, and 7 have 2 Sagittal T1 series. 3 studies have only 2 series: 2 have no Sagittal T1, and 1 has no Sagittal T2/STIR.

docs.title: RSNA 2023 Abdominal Trauma
docs.text:
Registry keys rsna_abdominal_trauma_2023_train, rsna_abdominal_trauma_2023_test Task and outputs Classification, 14 injury labels (cls). The test split has images only Images in the table train 4,711 volumes (3,147 patients), test 6 volumes (sample files only) Modality Abdominal CT, 3-D, DICOM series. One row is one series, which is one volume License The rules of the Kaggle competition. Accept them before the download Download Get the data: RSNA 2023 Abdominal Trauma

The RSNA 2023 Abdominal Trauma Detection challenge is a Kaggle competition of the Radiological Society of North America (RSNA). Each patient has 1 or 2 abdominal CT series. train_2024.csv has 3,147 rows, one for each patient, with injury labels for 5 organs. train_series_meta.csv has 4,711 rows, one for each series. The harmonized table has one row for each series, and the labels of the patient repeat on each series of the patient. So a label belongs to the patient, not to one series.

The source also has organ masks for 206 series in segmentations/. It has 15,632 slice labels in image_level_labels_2024.csv: 8,400 of active extravasation and 7,232 of bowel injury. The harmonizer reads neither of them.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the train_images/ folder. The class finds train_2024.csv and train_series_meta.csv in base_image_dir or in the folder above it. The harmonizer finds train_demographics_2024.csv next to train_2024.csv.

rsna-2023-abdominal-trauma-detection/
  train_2024.csv
  train_series_meta.csv
  train_demographics_2024.csv
  test_series_meta.csv
  train_images/<patient_id>/<series_id>/<instance_number>.dcm
  test_images/<patient_id>/<series_id>/<instance_number>.dcm

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import RSNAAbdominalTrauma2023TrainDataset

train = RSNAAbdominalTrauma2023TrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/rsna-2023-abdominal-trauma-detection/train_images/",
    output_cls=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 112, 112, 112), 1 channel, then (D, H, W)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(14,)

The image steps: MONAI ITKReader reads all DICOM files of the series folder as one volume. The class keeps the default base_transpose=True. So the transform turns each volume to the axis code IPL and then to (D, H, W) (D-12). It clips the values to hu_window (default (-150, 250), for the soft tissue of the abdomen) (D-14). Then it scales the 0.5 and 99.5 percentiles to -1 and 1. It resizes the longest side to 112, and pads the volume with -1 to 112 x 112 x 112 (D x H x W).

A series can have hundreds of DICOM files, so the first load of a sample can take more than 30 seconds. The first run writes a MONAI cache to ./cache. cache_dir=None gives no cache.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: train_series_meta.csv (one row for each series) and train_2024.csv (one row for each patient). The harmonizer joins them on patient_id. So one row is one series, a 3-D volume (D-03).
  • IDs: patient_id 10004 and series_id 21057 give study_id 10004 and image_path 10004/21057. image_path is the series folder, relative to base_image_dir (D-04). The source has no study ID, so study_id is patient_id. series_id is a column of the harmonized table.
  • Labels (D-05): the 14 source columns have 0 and 1, and the harmonizer keeps them. Each series of a patient gets the labels of the patient. The source has no uncertain or blank label.
  • Age and sex: they come from train_demographics_2024.csv, next to csv_path. age_years comes from Age, in years (D-06). 90+ gives 90, and Unknown gives NaN. sex is M, F or NaN, from Sex (D-26). With no such file, the harmonizer warns, and the harmonized table has no age_years or sex.
  • View (D-01): the DICOM headers have ImageOrientationPatient, but the harmonizer does not read it. So the harmonized table has no view_position. D-01 lists this as a known gap.
  • Extra columns (D-01): aortic_hu and incomplete_organ come from train_series_meta.csv. aortic_hu is the HU value in the aorta, a sign of the contrast phase. incomplete_organ is 1 when the scan does not hold an organ fully.
  • Test source: test_series_meta.csv, with patient_id, series_id and aortic_hu. The harmonized test table has no labels, no age and no sex (D-25).
  • Dropped rows: the join drops a series whose patient has no label row. The source files have no such series.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 14 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Meaning any_injury An injury of 1 or more of the 5 organs bowel_healthy No bowel injury bowel_injury A bowel injury extravasation_healthy No active extravasation (bleeding) extravasation_injury Active extravasation kidney_healthy No kidney injury kidney_high A high-grade kidney injury kidney_low A low-grade kidney injury liver_healthy No liver injury liver_high A high-grade liver injury liver_low A low-grade liver injury spleen_healthy No spleen injury spleen_high A high-grade spleen injury spleen_low A low-grade spleen injury

Each organ has 1 in exactly 1 of its columns. For example, kidney_low 1 comes with 0 in kidney_healthy and kidney_high. any_injury is 1 when an injury column is 1. In the source, 910 of the 3,147 patients have an injury. The test series have no labels (D-25).

docs.title: RSNA Pediatric Bone Age
docs.text:
Registry keys rsna_bone_age_train, rsna_bone_age_val, rsna_bone_age_test Task and outputs Regression of the bone age in months (reg). The test split has images only Images in the table train 12,611, val 1,425, test 200. One image is one patient Modality Hand X-ray, 2-D, PNG License The terms of the RSNA download page Download Get the data: RSNA Pediatric Bone Age

The RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge (2017) has hand X-rays of children (Halabi et al., Radiology 2019). The task is to predict the bone age (the age of the skeleton) from the image. The target is the bone age in months, a regression target, not a label. The train split has 12,611 images and the val split has 1,425. The 200 test images have no bone age.

docs.text:
Train and val are 2 downloads, and each has its own base_image_dir. The train class finds train.csv in the folder above base_image_dir. The val class finds Validation Dataset.csv in base_image_dir.

    boneage-validation-dataset-2/<id>.png   # 625 images, ids 9727 to 15612

from radharmony.dataset import RSNABoneAgeTrainDataset, RSNABoneAgeValDataset

    base_image_dir="/data/rsna-boneage/boneage-training-dataset/",
    output_reg=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["reg"]: Tensor(1,), the bone age in months, for example tensor([180.])

test_ds = RSNABoneAgeValDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/rsna-boneage/Bone Age Validation Set/",
    output_reg=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: train.csv has the columns id, boneage and male. Validation Dataset.csv has Image ID, Bone Age (months) and male. The harmonizer renames the val columns to the train names. One row is one image.
  • IDs: the train id 1377 gives patient_id 1377, study_id 1377 and image_path 1377.png. A val image path has its subfolder, for example boneage-validation-dataset-1/1386.png. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04). The source has no patient ID, so one image is one patient.
  • Target (D-05): age_months comes from boneage or Bone Age (months), as a whole number. It is in REG_COLS, not in LABEL_COLS.
  • Sex: sex is M or F, from the True or False column male (D-26). The extra column sex_female (1 for a girl and 0 for a boy) stays, because bone-age models use it as a number.
  • Age: the source has no age of the child, so the harmonized table has no age_years (D-06). age_months is the bone age, not the age of the child.
  • View (D-01): the source has no view, so the harmonized table has no view_position.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row. Every id in the 2 CSV files has a PNG.

The test split has images only Images in the table train 7,279 volumes, test 650 volumes. One study is one volume and one patient Modality Chest CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA), 3-D, DICOM series. One row is one study, which is one series and one volume License The rules of the Kaggle competition. Accept them before the download Download Get the data: RSNA PE Detection

The RSNA-STR Pulmonary Embolism (PE) Detection Challenge (2020) is a Kaggle competition. The Radiological Society of North America (RSNA) and the Society of Thoracic Radiology (STR) made it. Each study is one CTPA scan, with one series of slices. 2,211 train studies have PE.

train.csv has one row for each slice: 1,790,594 rows for 7,279 studies. It has labels at 2 levels. The 13 study labels have the same value on every slice of a study. The image label pe_present_on_image says if one slice shows PE.

docs.text:
base_image_dir is the train/ or test/ folder. The class finds train.csv or test.csv in base_image_dir or in the folder above it.

  test.csv

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import RSNAPEDetectionTrainDataset, RSNAPEDetectionTestDataset

train = RSNAPEDetectionTrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/rsna_pe_dataset/train/",
    output_cls=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 112, 112, 112), 1 channel, then (D, H, W)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(13,)

test_ds = RSNAPEDetectionTestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/rsna_pe_dataset/test/",
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
# test_ds[0] has only "img", for a Kaggle submission

The image steps: MONAI ITKReader reads all DICOM files of the series folder as one volume. The class keeps the default base_transpose=True. So the transform turns each volume to the axis code IPL and then to (D, H, W) (D-12). It clips the values to hu_window (default (-1000, 1000), for CTPA soft tissue and lung) (D-14). Then it scales the 0.5 and 99.5 percentiles to -1 and 1. It resizes the longest side to 112, and pads the volume with -1 to 112 x 112 x 112 (D x H x W).

The first run writes a MONAI cache to ./cache. cache_dir=None gives no cache.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: train.csv or test.csv, with one row for each slice. The harmonizer keeps the first row of each StudyInstanceUID. So one row is one study, with one series and one 3-D volume (D-03).
  • IDs: StudyInstanceUID 6897fa9de148 and SeriesInstanceUID 2bfbb7fd2e8b give patient_id and study_id 6897fa9de148, and image_path 6897fa9de148/2bfbb7fd2e8b. image_path is the series folder, relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Labels (D-05): the 13 study columns are already snake_case, with 0 and 1. The harmonizer keeps them. The source has no uncertain or blank label. The harmonizer drops the image label pe_present_on_image, because one row of the harmonized table is a whole volume.
  • View (D-01): the DICOM headers have ImageOrientationPatient, but the harmonizer does not read it. So the harmonized table has no view_position. D-01 lists this as a known gap.
  • Age and sex: the CSV files have no age or sex. The 5 DICOM headers we checked have no PatientAge and no PatientSex tag. So the harmonized table has no age_years or sex (D-06, D-26).
  • Test source: test.csv has only the 3 UID columns, so the harmonized test table has no label columns (D-25).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops only the extra slice rows of each study. It drops no study.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 13 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Meaning acute_and_chronic_pe The PE is both acute and chronic central_pe PE in the central pulmonary arteries chronic_pe The PE is chronic, not acute flow_artifact A flow artifact in the arteries indeterminate The study quality is too low to say if PE is present leftsided_pe PE on the left side negative_exam_for_pe No PE in the study qa_contrast The contrast is not good enough qa_motion Motion makes the images unclear rightsided_pe PE on the right side rv_lv_ratio_gte_1 The right to left ventricle ratio is 1 or more rv_lv_ratio_lt_1 The right to left ventricle ratio is less than 1 true_filling_defect_not_pe A filling defect that is not PE

A study with PE has 0 in negative_exam_for_pe and in indeterminate. In such a study, exactly 1 of rv_lv_ratio_gte_1 and rv_lv_ratio_lt_1 is 1. In the other studies, both are 0.

Acute PE has no column. A study with PE and 0 in chronic_pe and acute_and_chronic_pe has acute PE. Each indeterminate study has 1 in qa_motion or qa_contrast. The test studies have no labels (D-25).

docs.title: Chest ImaGenome
docs.text:
Registry keys chest_imagenome_gold, chest_imagenome_silver_train, chest_imagenome_silver_valid, chest_imagenome_silver_test Task and outputs Boxes of anatomical regions (bbox), with the findings of each region (bbox_findings). No cls Images in the table gold 1,000 (500 patients), silver 237,844 in 3 splits (62,945 patients) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, DICOM from MIMIC-CXR License PhysioNet credentialed access, as for MIMIC-CXR Download Get the data: other datasets. The images come from MIMIC-CXR (DICOM)

Chest ImaGenome (Wu et al., NeurIPS 2021 Datasets and Benchmarks) is a scene graph dataset for the MIMIC-CXR images. For each frontal image, it gives boxes of anatomical regions (for example the right lung or the trachea) and the findings in each region. It has no image files: the images come from the MIMIC-CXR DICOM files. RadHarmony reads 2 sets:

  • Gold: 1,000 images. People checked the boxes. The harmonized table has 25,961 boxes of 26 regions.
  • Silver: the full set, made by an automatic pipeline, with official train, valid and test splits. The harmonized table has 8,497,868 boxes of up to 36 regions.

The findings stay with their boxes. RadHarmony does not make an image label (cls) from them.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the files/ folder of MIMIC-CXR (DICOM), because the harmonizer reads the image size from each DICOM header. annotation_dir is the Chest ImaGenome folder.

MIMIC-CXR-V2-AWS/files/                <- base_image_dir
  p10/p10000935/s50578979/d0b71acc-b5a62046-bbb5f6b8-7b173b85-65cdf738.dcm
CHEST-IMAGENOME/                       <- annotation_dir
  gold_dataset/
    gold_bbox_coordinate_annotations_1000images.csv
    gold_object_attribute_with_coordinates.txt
  silver_dataset/
    scene_graph.zip
    splits/train.csv, valid.csv, test.csv, images_to_avoid.csv
  utils/cxr-record-list_view.csv

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import ChestImaGenomeGoldDataset, ChestImaGenomeSilverValidDataset

gold = ChestImaGenomeGoldDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MIMIC-CXR-V2-AWS/files/",
    annotation_dir="/data/CHEST-IMAGENOME/",
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = gold.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["bbox"]: Tensor(N, 4), one row for each region (N = 26 for most gold images)
# sample["bbox_labels"]: a list of N names
# sample["bbox_findings"]: a list of N strings, one for each box

valid_ds = ChestImaGenomeSilverValidDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MIMIC-CXR-V2-AWS/files/",
    annotation_dir="/data/CHEST-IMAGENOME/",
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
# valid_ds[0]["bbox"]: Tensor(N, 4) (N = 36 for most silver images)

output_bbox is True by default, because the boxes are the only output.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source, gold: gold_bbox_coordinate_annotations_1000images.csv (one row for each image and region) and gold_object_attribute_with_coordinates.txt (the findings). utils/cxr-record-list_view.csv gives the patient, study, path and view of each dicom_id.
  • Source, silver: the split CSV (train.csv, valid.csv or test.csv) gives the patient, study, path and view. scene_graph.zip has one JSON file for each image, with its boxes and findings. The harmonizer leaves out the images in images_to_avoid.csv.
  • IDs: one row is one image (D-03). The dicom_id 00046130-fd952ef0-57f2948d-491a16b4-5db3a18c gives patient_id 15184836, study_id 59382057, and image_path p15/p15184836/s59382057/00046130-fd952ef0-57f2948d-491a16b4-5db3a18c.dcm. The IDs are the MIMIC digits (D-01). image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Findings: the harmonizer keeps a finding of a region when its relation is yes and its category is anatomicalfinding, disease, tubesandlines or device. It leaves out the categories nlp and technicalassessment.
  • View (D-01): AP or PA, from ViewPosition of the record list (gold) or the split CSV (silver).
  • Age and sex: silver only. age_years comes from the scene graph age_decile, in years (D-06). It is the low edge of the group: 50-60 gives 50, and >=90 gives 90. sex is M, F or NaN, from the scene graph gender (D-26). The gold harmonized table has no age and no sex.
  • Extra columns: bbox_findings, image_width and image_height. Gold adds findings_annotated, and silver adds split.
  • Dropped rows: the silver harmonizer drops an image of the split list that has no scene graph file, and warns. The harmonizer also drops an image when it cannot read the size in its DICOM header, and warns with the count (D-07).

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The harmonized table has no label columns and no cls. The labels are in the boxes:

  • bbox_labels: the region of each box. See Boxes.
  • bbox_findings: the findings of each region, joined with |, in the same order as the boxes. An empty string means no finding. In gold, it can also mean "not annotated" (see Boxes). Example: left_hilar_structures with lung opacity|vascular congestion. The full list of findings is in semantics/attribute_relations_v1.txt of annotation_dir.

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: original_x1, original_y1, original_x2 and original_y2, in the pixels of the DICOM image.
  • The harmonizer reads the size of each image file (the DICOM tags Rows and Columns), so it needs base_image_dir. It divides y1 and y2 by the height, and x1 and x2 by the width.
  • The box is [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max], in fractions of the image size (D-07). Example: the image 00046130-fd952ef0-57f2948d-491a16b4-5db3a18c (the IDs example above) is 2544 x 3056 (H x W). Its gold aortic arch box is 1691, 900, 1978, 1173 (x1, y1, x2, y2). It gives [0.3538, 0.4611, 0.5533, 0.6473].
  • bbox_labels: the snake_case name of the region. For example, aortic arch gives aortic_arch (D-07).
  • Readers (D-36): the source has one set of boxes for each image, so the harmonizer does not group boxes.
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 4), in fractions of the returned image (D-28). bbox_labels and bbox_findings are lists of N strings. Example: (26, 4), ['aortic_arch', 'cardiac_silhouette', ...] and ['', '', ...] for a gold image. Most silver images give (36, 4). Every image has at least one box.
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box to the image. It drops a box with no area after the clip, and warns (D-07). It also drops an inverted box (x1 > x2 or y1 > y2), and it does not swap the corners. It drops the label and the findings of a dropped box too. Known data problems gives the counts.
  • Findings with no box (gold): the harmonizer leaves out a finding on a region that has no gold box, and warns (D-07).
  • Images with no finding annotation (gold): the column findings_annotated is True for the gold images that have finding annotations. For the other gold images, an empty bbox_findings entry means "not annotated", not "no finding" (D-33). Filter with df[df["findings_annotated"]] before you count findings.

docs.text:
Class Registry key Images Source ChestImaGenomeGoldDataset chest_imagenome_gold 1,000 The gold box file ChestImaGenomeSilverTrainDataset chest_imagenome_silver_train 166,504 splits/train.csv (166,521 rows) ChestImaGenomeSilverValidDataset chest_imagenome_silver_valid 23,951 splits/valid.csv (23,953 rows) ChestImaGenomeSilverTestDataset chest_imagenome_silver_test 47,389 splits/test.csv (47,393 rows). Use it as the test split ChestImaGenomeSilverDataset chest_imagenome_silver 237,844 All images. It mixes the 3 splits, so do not use it for a benchmark (D-09)

A silver split class drops the images of its split file that have no scene graph file (see Known data problems). In silver, no patient is in 2 splits. Gold has no official split. get_datasets(n_splits=5) makes a train and val split. It groups by patient (D-10).

A silver split class fixes split to its own split. A call with another split value raises ValueError. It also loads a harmonizer that ChestImaGenomeSilverHarmonizer saved, but only when every row is in its split. If not, it raises ValueError (D-09).

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Gold regions: the gold box file has no mediastinum box, but the gold attribute file puts 227 findings on mediastinum (181 images). So the harmonized table does not have them (D-07).
  • Gold box corners: 22 gold boxes are inverted (x1 > x2 or y1 > y2). With the corners swapped, they still do not cover their region (D-07). With the 6 gold boxes that have no area, the harmonizer drops 28 gold boxes.
  • Silver boxes: some silver boxes have no area inside the image, for example 235 in the valid split. No silver box is inverted.
  • Gold findings: the gold attribute file has only 500 of the 1,000 gold images (D-33).
  • Silver age group: the source writes the group 10-20 as 20-Oct, because a spreadsheet read it as a date. The harmonizer reads it as 10 (D-06).
  • Silver scene graphs: 17 train, 2 valid and 4 test images of the split files have no file in scene_graph.zip.

docs.title: ChestX-Det10
docs.text:
Registry keys chestxdet10_train, chestxdet10_test Task and outputs Detection of 10 findings: boxes (bbox) and image labels (cls) Images in the table train 3,001, test 542. One image is one patient Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, PNG License The GitHub repo states no license. Its README asks you to cite the paper Download Get the data: other datasets

ChestX-Det10 is a box dataset from the Deepwise AI Lab (Liu, Lin and Yu, arXiv:2006.10550). The images come from NIH ChestX-ray14, with new file names. 3 radiologists drew boxes of 10 findings. 2 of them drew the boxes of each image, and the third chose among their boxes and could add boxes.

The official metric is the recall at 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2 false positives per image (IoU 0.5), not mAP. The authors' eval.py computes it. RadHarmony does not compute it.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the dataset root. The class finds train.json or test.json in this folder.

ChestX-Det10/
  train.json
  test.json
  eval.py
  train-old/36200.png
  test_data/36199.png

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import ChestXDet10TrainDataset, ChestXDet10TestDataset

train = ChestXDet10TrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/ChestX-Det10/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the images go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(10,)
# sample["bbox"]: Tensor(N, 4), one row for each box. N is 0 for an image with no finding
# sample["bbox_labels"]: a list of N names, for example ['effusion']

test_ds = ChestXDet10TestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/ChestX-Det10/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: train.json or test.json. One record is one image, with file_name, syms (the findings) and boxes.
  • IDs: the source has no patient ID. The record with file_name 36302.png in test.json gives patient_id 36302, study_id 36302 and image_path test_data/36302.png. So one image is one patient. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Image folders: the train images are in train-old/ and the test images are in test_data/. These are the folder names in the source zip files.
  • Labels (D-05): a finding in syms gives 1, and the other labels give 0. The source has no uncertain or blank label.
  • View, age and sex: the source has none of them, so the harmonized table has no view_position, age_years or sex (D-01).
  • Extra columns: split ("train" or "test") and n_boxes (the number of boxes of the image).
  • Dropped rows: none by default. With keep_negatives=False, the harmonizer drops the images with no finding (681 in train and 83 in test).

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 10 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Meaning atelectasis Part of a lung is collapsed calcification A calcification consolidation Airspace consolidation effusion Pleural effusion emphysema Emphysema fibrosis Pulmonary fibrosis fracture A rib or other bone fracture mass A lung mass nodule A lung nodule pneumothorax Pneumothorax

A label is 1 when the image has 1 or more boxes of the finding. The paper counts boxes, so its counts are larger. Example: in the test split, atelectasis is 1 on 48 images, and these images have 51 atelectasis boxes.

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: boxes holds pixel boxes [x1, y1, x2, y2] (top left, bottom right). syms holds one finding for each box, in the same order. Each image is 1024 x 1024 (H x W). The train split has 6,863 boxes on 2,320 images, and the test split has 1,476 boxes on 459 images.
  • The harmonizer reads the size of each image file, so it needs base_image_dir. It divides y1 and y2 by the height, and x1 and x2 by the width.
  • The box is [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max], in fractions of the image size (D-07).
  • Example: 36302.png has boxes [[799, 666, 937, 761]] and syms ["Effusion"]. It gives bbox [[0.650390625, 0.7431640625, 0.7802734375, 0.9150390625]] and bbox_labels ["effusion"].
  • bbox_labels: the snake_case name of the finding, as in the label columns (D-07).
  • Readers (D-36): the source has one final set of boxes for each image, so the harmonizer does not group boxes.
  • bbox and bbox_labels are JSON text in the harmonized table, so they stay the same after a CSV save and load.
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 4), in fractions of the returned image (D-28). bbox_labels is a list of N names. Example: (1, 4) and ['effusion']. An image with no box gives (0, 4) and []. A train image has up to 36 boxes, and a test image has up to 14.
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box to the image. It drops a box with no area after the clip, and warns (D-07). The source files have no such box.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Train folder: the train images unzip to train-old/, not train/.
  • File names: the names are not the NIH ChestX-ray14 names. Example: 36199.png, where NIH uses names such as 00001075_000.png. So a ChestX-ray14 copy does not give the images or the NIH patient IDs.
  • RGBA files: 40 PNG files are RGBA, and the others are gray. The RGBA files are gray images (R = G = B, alpha 255), so the dataset gives 1 channel for every image (D-42).
  • Shared boxes: one box can have 2 or more findings (paper, section 2). Then the source repeats the box with each finding. Example: 36367.png has the box [243, 662, 407, 886] for Fibrosis and for Consolidation.

docs.title: CheXlocalize
docs.text:
Registry keys chexlocalize, chexlocalize_val Task and outputs Classification, 14 labels (cls). Segmentation, one mask for each image (mask) Images in the table test 668 (500 patients), val 234 (200 patients) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, JPEG License Stanford AIMI research use agreement, as for CheXpert Download Get the data: other datasets

CheXlocalize adds segmentation masks to the CheXpert test set and the CheXpert valid set. Radiologists drew the masks of 10 findings. The test split is the official CheXpert test set, so the CheXpert page points here. The mask file of the test split has 499 of the 668 test images. RadHarmony joins the 10 masks of an image into one mask, so a sample has one "any finding" mask.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the test/ or val/ folder. The class finds the label CSV in the folder above it. It finds the mask file in the CheXlocalize/ folder next to the CheXpert/ folder (D-35). The images and the masks are 2 downloads. Put them side by side, as below.

chexlocalize/
  CheXpert/
    test_labels.csv
    val_labels.csv
    test/patient64741/study1/view1_frontal.jpg
    val/patient64541/study1/view1_frontal.jpg
  CheXlocalize/
    gt_segmentations_test.json
    gt_segmentations_val.json

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import CheXlocalizeDataset, CheXlocalizeValDataset

val_ds = CheXlocalizeValDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/chexlocalize/CheXpert/val/",
    mask_output_dir="/data/chexlocalize_masks/val/",  # any folder you can write to
    output_cls=True,
    output_mask=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
sample = val_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(14,)
# sample["mask"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224), values 0 and 1

test_ds = CheXlocalizeDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/chexlocalize/CheXpert/test/",
    mask_output_dir="/data/chexlocalize_masks/test/",  # any folder you can write to
    output_cls=True,
    output_mask=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: test_labels.csv or val_labels.csv. One row is one image.
  • IDs: the Path test/patient64741/study1/view1_frontal.jpg gives patient_id patient64741, study_id patient64741_study1, and image_path patient64741/study1/view1_frontal.jpg. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04). In val_labels.csv, the harmonizer also removes CheXpert-v1.0/valid/ from the start of Path. With a CSV of another split, it raises ValueError.
  • Labels (14 columns, D-05): 1 gives 1 and 0 gives 0. Both CSV files have only 0 and 1.
  • View (D-01): FRONTAL or LATERAL, from the file name. val_labels.csv has AP or PA in its column AP/PA, but the harmonizer does not read it. D-01 lists this as a known gap.
  • Age and sex: only in the val split. age_years comes from Age, in years (D-06). sex is M or F, from Sex (D-26). test_labels.csv has no age and no sex.
  • Masks: only with mask_json_path. See Masks.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row. With output_mask=True, the class drops a row with an empty mask_path, and warns (D-33).

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 14 label columns, in the order of cls. The masks cover the 10 findings with "Yes" in the column Mask.

Column Meaning Mask atelectasis Part of a lung is collapsed Yes cardiomegaly The heart is large Yes consolidation Airspace consolidation Yes edema Pulmonary edema Yes enlarged_cardiomediastinum The mediastinum is wide Yes fracture A rib or other bone fracture No lung_lesion A lung lesion Yes lung_opacity A lung opacity Yes no_finding No finding No pleural_effusion Pleural effusion Yes pleural_other Another pleural finding No pneumonia Pneumonia No pneumothorax Pneumothorax Yes support_devices A tube, line or other device Yes

docs.title: Masks
docs.text:
• Source: gt_segmentations_test.json and gt_segmentations_val.json. The key of an image is <study_id>_<file name without .jpg>, for example patient64744_study1_view1_frontal. Each image in the file has 10 masks in COCO RLE, one for each masked finding. The mask of an absent finding is empty. The test file has 499 images, and the val file has 187.
  • The harmonizer joins the 10 masks of an image with a bitwise OR. So the mask shows the area of any finding. It does not tell the findings apart.
  • mask_path: with output_mask=True, the class passes the mask file to the harmonizer. It then writes the masks as PNG files to mask_output_dir. Each PNG has the size of its image and the values 0 and 255. Example: <mask_output_dir>/patient64541/study1/view1_frontal.png. Without output_mask=True, the class does not read the mask file, so the harmonized table has no mask_path column.
  • An image that is not in the mask file: if all 10 masked findings are 0, the image is a labeled negative. It gets an all-zero mask (D-33). The test split has 168 labeled negatives, and the val split has 47.
  • An empty mask_path means "not annotated" (D-33). With output_mask=True, the class drops these rows and warns. Only 1 test image has an empty mask_path, so 667 test and 234 val samples stay.
  • The sample: mask is a float32 tensor (1, 224, 224) with the values 0 and 1 (D-14). The transform resizes it with the image.

If you need one mask for each finding, read the JSON file with pycocotools. The class does not give them.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Missing masks: 1 test image, patient65086/study1/view1_frontal.jpg, has 5 positive masked findings in test_labels.csv, but it is not in gt_segmentations_test.json. So it has no mask (D-33).

docs.title: Montgomery County CXR
docs.text:
Registry keys montgomery_cxr Task and outputs Classification, 1 label (cls). Lung masks (mask). Report text (report) Images in the table 138 (135 patients) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, PNG License NLM research use. Do not share the data outside your group. Cite Jaeger et al. and Candemir et al., IEEE TMI 2014 Download Get the data: Montgomery County CXR

The Montgomery County CXR Set is a tuberculosis (TB) screening set from the U.S. National Library of Medicine (NLM) and Montgomery County, Maryland. It has 138 chest X-rays: 58 with TB and 80 normal. Each image has a left and a right lung mask, and a clinical reading with the age, the sex and a short report. The download is small and needs no account, so it is a good first dataset. With 138 images, a result can change a lot from one split to the next.

The source also has montgomery_consensus_roi.csv, with 109 TB boxes on 55 images. The harmonizer does not read it.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
Get the data first: Get the data: Montgomery County CXR.

base_image_dir is the CXR_png/ folder, not MontgomerySet/. The class finds ClinicalReadings/ and ManualMask/ next to CXR_png/.

MontgomerySet/
  CXR_png/MCUCXR_0001_0.png
  ClinicalReadings/MCUCXR_0001_0.txt
  ManualMask/leftMask/MCUCXR_0001_0.png
  ManualMask/rightMask/MCUCXR_0001_0.png

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset

ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_mask=True,
    mask_output_dir="/data/montgomery_lung_masks/",  # any folder you can write to
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(1,), 1 is TB and 0 is normal
# sample["mask"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224), 1 is lung and 0 is background

The class makes mask_output_dir and writes 1 lung mask PNG for each image to it. The first run also writes a MONAI cache to ./cache. cache_dir=None gives no cache. For classification only, leave out output_mask and mask_output_dir.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: the PNG files in CXR_png/. One file is one row. The source has no label CSV.
  • IDs: the file MCUCXR_0001_0.png gives patient_id MCUCXR_0001, study_id MCUCXR_0001 and image_path MCUCXR_0001_0.png. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04). One study is one image.
  • Same patient: 3 readings say that the patient is the same as in another image, for example (same pt as MCUCXR_0113_1) in MCUCXR_0117_1.txt. The harmonizer gives each image of the group the smallest ID of the group as patient_id. So the 138 images give 135 patients.
  • Label (D-05): the file name gives tuberculosis. A file name that ends in _1 gives 1 (TB), and _0 gives 0 (normal). Before 2026-11-05, the column was tb. If you saved a harmonized table before then, harmonize it again (Save and reuse a harmonized table).
  • Age and sex: they come from the reading ClinicalReadings/<file name>.txt. age_years comes from Patient's Age, in years (D-06). For example, 027Y gives 27. sex is M, F or NaN, from Patient's Sex (D-26).
  • Report: report holds the other lines of the reading. A text that only says "NO REPORT" gives NaN (D-33).
  • View (D-01): the source has no view, so the harmonized table has no view_position.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: Column Meaning tuberculosis Tuberculosis. 1 is TB, 0 is normal

docs.title: Masks
docs.text:
• Source: ManualMask/leftMask/ and ManualMask/rightMask/ hold 1 binary PNG for each image, with the same file name as the image. People drew them by hand, and a radiologist supervised the work. A mask has the size of its image, 4020 x 4892 or 4892 x 4020 pixels (H x W).
  • When ManualMask/ is there, the harmonized table always has 2 extra columns, mask_path_left and mask_path_right, for example ../ManualMask/leftMask/MCUCXR_0001_0.png. They are relative to base_image_dir. Without mask_output_dir, the harmonized table has no mask_path.
  • With mask_output_dir, the harmonizer joins the left and right masks into 1 lung mask. A pixel is 1 when it is in one of the 2 masks. It writes 1 PNG for each image to mask_output_dir. mask_path is the full path of that PNG. The harmonizer does not write a PNG again when the file exists.
  • An empty mask_path means "not annotated" (D-33). With output_mask=True, the class drops these rows and warns. All 138 images have both masks, so no row is dropped.
  • output_mask=True with no mask_output_dir raises ValueError. With output_mask=True and no ManualMask/ folder, the class raises FileNotFoundError with the folder name (D-35).
  • The sample: mask is a float32 tensor (1, 224, 224) with the values 0 and 1 (D-14). The transform resizes it with the image.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
report holds the free text of the reading, in one line. Every normal image has the text normal. A TB image has a short note, for example MCUCXR_0104_1:

inactive TB scars LUL, unchanged for 2Y, pt previously treated DOT (17Y ago) for pan-sensitive disease

With output_report=True, the class drops the 1 image with no report (MCUCXR_0166_1), and warns (D-33).

Montgomery County CXR has no official split. get_datasets(n_splits=5) makes a train and val split. It groups by patient (D-10). The source has no patient ID. Only 3 readings link the images of one patient, so nobody can check that a patient is in only 1 split.

docs.title: MS-CXR
docs.text:
Registry keys ms_cxr_train, ms_cxr_val, ms_cxr_test Task and outputs Phrase grounding. Boxes of 8 findings (bbox), and 8 labels (cls) Images in the table train 737, val 155, test 155. 1,448 boxes in all Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, JPEG from MIMIC-CXR-JPG 2.0.0 License PhysioNet credentialed access, as for MIMIC-CXR Download Get the data: other datasets. The images come from MIMIC-CXR-JPG

MS-CXR is a phrase grounding benchmark (Boecking et al., ECCV 2022). Radiologists linked a phrase of the report to a box on the image. The source is one CSV file with 1,448 phrase and box pairs on 1,047 MIMIC-CXR images. Each box has one of 8 findings. The source has an official train, val and test split.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the files/ folder of MIMIC-CXR-JPG 2.0.0. The CSV is in its own folder, so pass csv_path.

mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/files/        <- base_image_dir
  p10/p10233088/s54276838/675d792f-a3521e48-5eec8573-1e81d644-e60c34f8.jpg
ms-cxr/
  MS_CXR_Local_Alignment_v1.1.0.csv   <- csv_path

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MSCXRTrainDataset, MSCXRValDataset, MSCXRTestDataset

args = dict(
    base_image_dir="/data/mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/files/",
    csv_path="/data/ms-cxr/MS_CXR_Local_Alignment_v1.1.0.csv",
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds = MSCXRTrainDataset(**args).get_datasets()
val_ds = MSCXRValDataset(**args).get_datasets()
test_ds = MSCXRTestDataset(**args).get_datasets()
sample = val_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(8,)
# sample["bbox"]: Tensor(N, 4), one row for each box
# sample["bbox_labels"]: a list of N names

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: MS_CXR_Local_Alignment_v1.1.0.csv. One row is one phrase and its box. The harmonizer makes one row for each image (dicom_id), with a list of boxes (D-03).
  • IDs: the path files/p10/p10233088/s54276838/675d792f-a3521e48-5eec8573-1e81d644-e60c34f8.jpg gives patient_id 10233088, study_id 54276838, and image_path p10/p10233088/s54276838/675d792f-a3521e48-5eec8573-1e81d644-e60c34f8.jpg. The IDs are the MIMIC digits (D-01). image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • DICOM images: base_image_dir can also be the files/ folder of MIMIC-CXR (DICOM). The harmonizer looks for the first image as .jpg, then as .dcm. If only .dcm exists, every image_path ends in .dcm.
  • Labels (8 columns, D-05): a label is 1 when the image has a box of this finding, and 0 when it has none. So 0 means "no box of this finding", not "no finding".
  • View, age and sex: the source has none of them, so the harmonized table has no view_position, age_years or sex (D-01).
  • Extra columns: split, label_text (one phrase for each box), image_width and image_height.
  • Dropped rows: a split class keeps the rows of its split. The harmonizer drops no other row.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 8 label columns, in the order of cls. The box labels use the same names.

Column Meaning atelectasis Part of a lung is collapsed cardiomegaly The heart is large consolidation Airspace consolidation edema Pulmonary edema lung_opacity A lung opacity pleural_effusion Pleural effusion pneumonia Pneumonia pneumothorax Pneumothorax

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: the CSV columns x, y, w and h, in the pixels of the image. The columns image_width and image_height give the image size, so the harmonizer does not read the image files for it.
  • The harmonizer divides y and h by the height, and x and w by the width.
  • The box is [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max], in fractions of the image size (D-07). Example: the image of the first CSV row is 2021 x 1767 (H x W). Its box x 196, y 1136, w 532, h 315 gives [0.5621, 0.7180, 0.1109, 0.4120].
  • bbox_labels: the snake_case name of category_name. For example, Pleural Effusion gives pleural_effusion (D-07).
  • Readers (D-36): each box has its own phrase, so the harmonizer does not group boxes. The phrases are in label_text, in the order of the boxes. They are in the harmonized table only, not in the sample.
  • Box counts: train has 1,020 boxes, val 212 and test 216. Every image has at least one box.
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 4), in fractions of the returned image (D-28). bbox_labels is a list of N names. Example: (1, 4) and ['pneumonia'].
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box to the image. It drops a box with no area after the clip, and warns (D-07). The source files have no such box.

docs.title: NODE21
docs.text:
Registry keys node21, node21_original Task and outputs Nodule detection: boxes (bbox) and 1 image label (cls) Images in the table 4,882 (1,134 with nodules) in each key. One image is one patient Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, MHA License CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: no commercial use and no changed copies Download Get the data: other datasets

NODE21 is the data of the NODE21 nodule challenge (Sogancioglu et al., arXiv:2401.02192). The frontal chest X-rays come from ChestX-ray14, PadChest, JSRT and Open-I. Radiologists drew 1,476 nodule boxes on 1,134 images. The other images are controls with no nodule. The source has 2 copies of each image: proccessed_data and original_data.

The official metric is a free-response ROC (FROC): the sensitivity at each mean number of false positives per image. It is not mAP. RadHarmony does not compute it. The ct_patches/ folder holds 3-D CT nodule patches for the generation task of the challenge. No class reads them.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the dataset root with cxr_images/. The class finds metadata.csv in the folder of its variant.

NODE21/
  cxr_images/
    proccessed_data/metadata.csv
    proccessed_data/images/n0001.mha
    original_data/metadata.csv
    original_data/filenames_orig_and_new.csv
    original_data/images/n0001.mha
  ct_patches/

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import Node21Dataset

ds = Node21Dataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/NODE21/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the images go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(1,)
# sample["bbox"]: Tensor(N, 4), one row for each box. N is 0 for a control
# sample["bbox_labels"]: a list of N names, for example ['nodule']

Node21OriginalDataset takes the same arguments and reads original_data/.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: metadata.csv of the variant. One row is one box (5,224 rows in proccessed_data). A control has 1 row with label 0 and x, y, width and height 0. The harmonizer makes one row for each image, and a control gets no box.
  • IDs: the source has no patient ID. img_name n0239.mha gives patient_id n0239, study_id n0239 and image_path cxr_images/proccessed_data/images/n0239.mha. So one image is one patient. A name starts with n for an image with nodules and with c for a control. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Variant: variant="processed" (the default) reads proccessed_data/, and variant="original" reads original_data/. The column variant holds the value.
  • Labels (D-05): nodule is 1 when the image has a row with label 1, and 0 if not. The source has no uncertain or blank label.
  • Source dataset: source_dataset comes from original_data/filenames_orig_and_new.csv. It is chestxray14 (617 images), padchest (314), jsrt (149) or openi (54). The file lists only the images with nodules, so a control gets unknown.
  • View, age and sex: the source has none of them, so the harmonized table has no view_position, age_years or sex (D-01).
  • Dropped rows: none by default. With keep_negatives=False, the harmonizer drops the controls.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 1 label column of cls:

Column Meaning nodule The image has 1 or more lung nodules

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: x, y, width and height, in the pixels of the image. The source does not say which corner is the origin. With the top left corner, the boxes fall on nodules in the lungs, so the harmonizer uses that corner.
  • The harmonizer reads the size of each image file (with SimpleITK), so it needs base_image_dir. It divides y and y + height by the height, and x and x + width by the width.
  • The box is [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max], in fractions of the image size (D-07).
  • Example: in proccessed_data, n0239.mha has x 776, y 579, width 92 and height 94, on a 1024 x 1024 (H x W) image. It gives bbox [[0.5654296875, 0.6572265625, 0.7578125, 0.84765625]] and bbox_labels ["nodule"]. In original_data, the same nodule has y 538, so bbox starts with 0.525390625.
  • bbox_labels: nodule for each box (D-07).
  • Readers (D-36): the source has one set of boxes for each image, so the harmonizer does not group boxes.
  • bbox and bbox_labels are JSON text in the harmonized table, so they stay the same after a CSV save and load.
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 4), in fractions of the returned image (D-28). bbox_labels is a list of N names. Example: (1, 4) and ['nodule']. An image with no box gives (0, 4) and []. An image has 0 to 3 boxes.
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box to the image. It drops a box with no area after the clip, and warns (D-07). The source files have no such box, in either variant.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Folder name: the source spells the folder proccessed_data, with 2 c.
  • Variants: every proccessed_data image is 1024 x 1024 (H x W) with 16-bit pixels. The original_data images have many sizes, for example 1024 x 1024 and 2991 x 3000 (H x W). They also have several pixel types: 8-bit, 16-bit and 64-bit float.
  • Box coordinates: a box is valid only on the image of its variant. The processing resized and padded the images, so the coordinates moved (example in Boxes).
  • Source dataset: filenames_orig_and_new.csv lists only the images with nodules. So for a control, you cannot find the same image in ChestX-ray14, PadChest or Open-I. You cannot check that a control is not also in your other data.

docs.title: PadChest-GR
docs.text:
Registry keys padchest_gr_train, padchest_gr_validation, padchest_gr_test Task and outputs Classification, 154 labels (cls). Boxes (bbox) with the sentence of each box. Reports (report) Images in the table The source tables give 4,555 images (1 for each study) of 4,459 patients. The paper is Castro et al., arXiv:2411.05085. The RadHarmony tests cannot read the images, so no test checks the harmonized table Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, PNG License The source has no license file. The terms are on the BIMCV download page Download Get the data: PadChest-GR

PadChest-GR (grounded reports) is a BIMCV release of PadChest images. The authors split each report into sentences. Each sentence is abnormal or not, and it has the PadChest labels of its finding. Radiologists drew boxes for the findings that have a place on the image. Each sentence is in English and in Spanish.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the source folder. Its name ends with a space (see Known data problems). The class finds master_table.csv and grounded_reports_20240819.json in this folder. The images are in PadChest_GR/.

BIMCV-Padchest-GR /
  grounded_reports_20240819.json
  master_table.csv
  PadChest_GR/<ImageID>.png
  PadChest_GR_progression_prior_studies/

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import PadChestGRTrainDataset, PadChestGRTestDataset

train_ds = PadChestGRTrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/PadChest-GR/BIMCV-Padchest-GR /",
    padchest_csv_path="/data/PadChest/PADCHEST_chest_x_ray_images_labels_160K_01.02.19.csv.gz",
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    output_report=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(154,)
# sample["bbox"]: Tensor(N, 4), N is 0 for an image with no box
# sample["bbox_labels"]: a list of N names
# sample["bbox_findings"]: a list of N sentences
# sample["report"]: the report text

test_ds = PadChestGRTestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/PadChest-GR/BIMCV-Padchest-GR /",
    output_cls=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()

PadChestGRValidationDataset loads the validation split.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: grounded_reports_20240819.json has one item for each image, with its sentences, labels and boxes. master_table.csv has one row for each label of an abnormal sentence, and one Normal row for an image with no abnormal sentence. Each row has the patient, split, sex and age. The harmonizer joins them on ImageID. One row is one image (D-03).
  • Checks: the patient, split, sex, age and date must be the same on all rows of an image in master_table.csv. If not, harmonize() raises ValueError.
  • IDs: the ImageID 251488034557732338959601580328898734705_wigcpj.png gives image_path PadChest_GR/251488034557732338959601580328898734705_wigcpj.png, relative to base_image_dir (D-04). The row of this image has a StudyID, which gives study_id 251488034557732338959601580328898734705. It also has a PatientID, which gives patient_id 243089588168270594079245995953840813067. They are the same IDs as in PadChest.
  • Labels (154 columns, D-05): a label of an abnormal sentence gives 1 in its column. All other columns are 0. An image with no abnormal sentence has 0 in all columns. A label that is not in the list of 154 raises ValueError.
  • View (D-01): the PadChest-GR files have no view. With padchest_csv_path, the view comes from the PadChest column Projection. It is PA, AP or AP_HORIZONTAL. An image that is not in that file raises ValueError. Without padchest_csv_path, the harmonized table has no view_position.
  • Age and sex: age_years comes from PatientAge, in years (D-06). sex is M or F, from PatientSex_DICOM (D-26).
  • Report: the harmonizer joins the sentences of an image into one text. The language is English (report_language="en") or Spanish (report_language="es").
  • Dropped rows: a split class keeps only the rows of its split. The harmonizer drops no other row.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 154 label columns are PadChest labels in snake_case, for example apical_pleural_thickening. They are the labels of the abnormal sentences of the source. The list, in the order of cls, is LABEL_COLUMNS in radharmony/harmonizer/padchest_gr/padchest_gr.py.

An image with no box can have a label. Example: a sentence with the label vertebral_fracture never has a box. So n_boxes == 0 does not mean that all labels are 0.

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: each sentence in the JSON file has boxes, a list of [x0, y0, x1, y1] fractions of the image. So x comes first.
  • The source values are already fractions, so the harmonizer only changes the order to [y0, y1, x0, x1]. Example: the sentence "Minimal biapical pleural thickening." has the box [0.27670749, 0.10440252, 0.48518978, 0.18993711]. This gives [0.10440252, 0.18993711, 0.27670749, 0.48518978].
  • The box is [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max], in fractions of the image size (D-07).
  • bbox_labels has the labels of the sentence of each box, in snake_case. A sentence with 2 or 3 labels gives one name with + between the labels, for example suture_material + surgery_breast + metal (D-07).
  • bbox_findings has the English sentence of each box. It has the same order as bbox.
  • The harmonized table holds bbox, bbox_labels and bbox_findings as JSON text, because the lists of the images have different lengths. An image with no box has "[]". n_boxes is the number of boxes.
  • Readers (D-36): the source gives one set of boxes in boxes, and a second set in extra_boxes, so the harmonizer does not group boxes. The extra boxes go to extra_bbox and n_extra_boxes. They are not in the sample.
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 4), in fractions of the returned image (D-28). bbox_labels is a list of N names, and bbox_findings is a list of N sentences. Example: (2, 4) and ['apical_pleural_thickening', 'apical_pleural_thickening']. An image with no box gives (0, 4) and [].
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box and each extra box to the image. It drops a box with no area after the clip, with its label and sentence, and warns (D-07). The source JSON file has no such box.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
• report is the text of all sentences of the image, in the language of report_language. Example: "Minimal biapical pleural thickening. Slight blunting of the posterior left costophrenic angle. No other significant alterations."
  • findings is JSON text with one item for each sentence. An item has sentence_en, sentence_es, abnormal, labels, locations, progression and n_boxes.
  • A normal image also has a report, with sentences that are not abnormal.

docs.title: Splits
docs.text:
Class Registry key Images Source PadChestGRTrainDataset padchest_gr_train 3,185 split is train in master_table.csv PadChestGRValidationDataset padchest_gr_validation 455 split is validation PadChestGRTestDataset padchest_gr_test 915 split is test. Use it as the test split PadChestGRDataset padchest_gr 4,555 All images. It mixes the 3 splits, so do not use it for a benchmark (D-09)

The counts above come from master_table.csv of the source. They match the 70%, 10% and 20% of the paper.

No patient is in 2 splits.

Every PadChest-GR image is also in PadChest, with the same ImageID and PatientID. The PadChest-GR split does not follow PadChest. So a PadChest-GR test patient can be in your PadChest train data. Drop these patients before you train on PadChest and test on PadChest-GR.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Folder name: the source folder BIMCV-Padchest-GR ends with a space.
  • Split zip: the images are in a zip of 37 parts. unzip cannot read it. Use 7z x PadChest_GR.zip.001 (see Get the data).
  • Row count: a count of the master_table.csv rows is not a count of images or of sentences. Each label of an abnormal sentence has its own row. A sentence that is not abnormal has no row.
  • Extra boxes: the JSON file does not say what extra_boxes is. The paper says that each abnormal sentence has up to 2 independent sets of boxes, and that 5,242 findings have extra boxes.
  • Vague labels: some labels are vague or do not name a body part, for example dai, end on vessel, chronic changes, metal, surgery and abnormal foreign body. The harmonizer keeps them.

docs.title: QaTa-COV19
docs.text:
Registry keys qata_cov19_train, qata_cov19_test Task and outputs Segmentation of the COVID-19 infection (mask). 1 label, always 1 (cls) Images in the table train 7,145 (4,607 patient IDs), test 2,113 (474 patients) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, PNG, 8-bit gray, 224 x 224 (H x W) License The source files have no license file. See the Kaggle page of the dataset Download Get the data: other datasets

QaTa-COV19 is a COVID-19 chest X-ray dataset from Qatar University and Tampere University. The papers are Degerli et al., Health Inf Sci Syst 2021 and Yamac et al., Comput Biol Med 2021.

RadHarmony reads version 2 (v2). It has 9,258 COVID-19 images, and each image has a mask of the infected lung region. The first author put the data on Kaggle (aysendegerli/qatacov19-dataset).

The download also has QaTa-COV19-v1/, Control_Group/ and Early-QaTa-COV19/. No class reads them. The v1 images with a mask are the covid_ images of the v2 train split. The control groups hold ChestX-ray14 images (a RadHarmony dataset with its own classes), pediatric pneumonia images and a set of normal images. Early-QaTa-COV19/ is a part of v1.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the Images/ folder of one split. The class finds the masks in the Ground-truths/ folder next to it.

QaTa-COV19/
  readme.txt
  QaTa-COV19-v2/
    Train Set/Images/covid_1000.png
    Train Set/Ground-truths/mask_covid_1000.png
    Test Set/Images/sub-S08047_ses-E16280_run-1_bp-chest_vp-ap_dx.png
    Test Set/Ground-truths/mask_sub-S08047_ses-E16280_run-1_bp-chest_vp-ap_dx.png

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import QaTaCOV19TrainDataset, QaTaCOV19TestDataset

train = QaTaCOV19TrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/QaTa-COV19/QaTa-COV19-v2/Train Set/Images/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_mask=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(1,), always 1
# sample["mask"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224), values 0 and 1

test_ds = QaTaCOV19TestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/QaTa-COV19/QaTa-COV19-v2/Test Set/Images/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_mask=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: the PNG files in base_image_dir. One file is one image. The source has no CSV. All columns come from the file name and the Ground-truths/ folder.
  • IDs: the file sub-S08047_ses-E16280_run-1_bp-chest_vp-ap_dx.png gives patient_id S08047, study_id E16280 and image_path sub-S08047_ses-E16280_run-1_bp-chest_vp-ap_dx.png. A covid_ file has no subject, so covid_1000.png gives patient_id and study_id covid_1000. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Name scheme: filename_scheme is bids for a sub- file and qata for a covid_ file. All covid_ files are in the train split.
  • Labels (D-05): covid is 1 on every row, because every v2 image is COVID-19 positive. It is not a classification task alone. Use it with a dataset of negative images.
  • View (D-01): from the vp- part of a sub- name. vp-ap gives AP, vp-pa gives PA and vp-ll gives LATERAL. A name with no vp- part, and every covid_ name, gives NaN.
  • acquisition: CR (computed radiography) or DX (digital radiography), from the end of a sub- name. A covid_ name gives NaN.
  • Age and sex: the source has neither, so the harmonized table has no age_years or sex.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 1 label column of cls:

Column Meaning covid COVID-19 pneumonia. It is 1 on every image

docs.title: Masks
docs.text:
• Source: the Ground-truths/ folder of each split has one PNG mask for each image, named mask_<image file name>. A mask is 224 x 224 (H x W), with 0 for the background and 255 for the infected region.
  • mask_path is the full path of the mask file, for example /data/QaTa-COV19/QaTa-COV19-v2/Test Set/Ground-truths/mask_sub-S08047_ses-E16280_run-1_bp-chest_vp-ap_dx.png. It is not relative to base_image_dir, because the class adds base_image_dir only to image_path.
  • The masks are PNG files, so they need no decode step. So the class needs no mask_output_dir.
  • An image with no mask file gets an empty mask_path. An empty mask_path means "not annotated" (D-33). With output_mask=True, the class drops these rows and warns. In the source files, every image has a mask.
  • The sample: mask is a float32 tensor (1, 224, 224) with the values 0 and 1 (D-14). The transform resizes it with the image.

No patient is in 2 splits. But 1 test image is also a train image (see Known data problems). The split stays as published (D-34).

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Image source: the source does not document where the sub- images came from. So filename_scheme gives only the name scheme.
  • No subject: a covid_ name has no subject, session or view. So 2 covid_ images of one patient get 2 patient IDs, and our own split can put them in train and val (D-10).
  • Copies in train: 37 pairs of train files look like one picture under 2 names (correlation above 0.99 at 32 x 32 pixels). Example: covid_104.png and covid_2791.png. Each copy has its own patient_id, so our own split can put the 2 copies in train and val (D-10).
  • Copy in test: the test image sub-S09512_ses-E21506_run-1_bp-chest_vp-pa_dx.png is also in train, as covid_4134.png (correlation 0.9999). The split stays as published (D-34).
  • Image size: the v2 images are 224 x 224 (H x W). The source has no larger copy of them.

docs.title: RANZCR CLiP
docs.text:
Registry keys ranzcr_clip_train, ranzcr_clip_test Task and outputs Classification, 11 labels (cls). Line masks (mask) with the train class Images in the table train 30,083 (3,255 patients, 9,095 with line masks), test 3,582 (no labels) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, JPEG License The rules of the Kaggle competition. Accept them before the download Download Get the data: RANZCR CLiP

RANZCR CLiP (Catheter and Line Position) is a Kaggle competition of the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Radiologists. The images show endotracheal tubes (ETT), nasogastric tubes (NGT), central venous catheters (CVC) and Swan-Ganz catheters. Most of the 11 labels say if the position of a tube or line is normal, borderline or abnormal. For some train images, train_annotations.csv has 17,999 polylines that trace the tubes and lines. The harmonizer can draw them as a binary mask. The Kaggle test images have no labels.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the Kaggle folder. The class finds train.csv and train_annotations.csv in it.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import RANZCRClipTrainDataset, RANZCRClipTestDataset

train = RANZCRClipTrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/ranzcr-clip-catheter-line-classification/",
    output_cls=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(11,)

test_ds = RANZCRClipTestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/ranzcr-clip-catheter-line-classification/",

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: train.csv. One row is one image. The test harmonizer lists the .jpg files in test/.
  • IDs: the row with PatientID ec89415d1 gives patient_id ec89415d1. Its StudyInstanceUID 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498.26697628953273228189375557799582420561 gives study_id (the same text). So one study is one image. The StudyInstanceUID also gives image_path train/1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498.26697628953273228189375557799582420561.jpg, relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Test IDs: patient_id is the StudyInstanceUID, because the test rows have no patient ID.
  • Labels (11 columns, D-05): the harmonizer renames each column, for example CVC - Abnormal gives cvc_abnormal. The values stay 0 and 1. The source has no blank and no uncertain label.
  • View, age and sex: the source has none of them, so the harmonized table has no view_position, age_years or sex (D-01).
  • Masks: see Masks.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 11 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Meaning cvc_abnormal A CVC in an abnormal position cvc_borderline A CVC in a borderline position cvc_normal A CVC in a normal position ett_abnormal An ETT in an abnormal position ett_borderline An ETT in a borderline position ett_normal An ETT in a normal position ngt_abnormal An NGT in an abnormal position ngt_borderline An NGT in a borderline position ngt_incompletely_imaged An NGT that the image does not fully show ngt_normal An NGT in a normal position swan_ganz_catheter_present A Swan-Ganz catheter is in the image

An image can have more than 1 label, for example cvc_normal and ett_normal.

docs.title: Masks
docs.text:
With output_mask=True, RANZCRClipTrainDataset adds a line mask to the sample. It needs mask_output_dir, a folder for the mask PNG files.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import RANZCRClipTrainDataset

mask_ds = RANZCRClipTrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/ranzcr-clip-catheter-line-classification/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_mask=True,
    mask_output_dir="/data/ranzcr_masks/",  # any folder you can write to
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
sample = mask_ds[0]
# sample["mask"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224), values 0 and 1
  • Source: train_annotations.csv has one row for each polyline, with StudyInstanceUID, label and data. data is a list of [x, y] points in the pixels of the JPEG, for example [[1487, 1279], [1477, 1168], ...].
  • The harmonizer puts all polylines of an image into one JSON text in mask_path. The line labels are not in the mask. Without mask_output_dir, mask_path keeps this JSON text.
  • harmonize(mask_output_dir=...) draws each polyline with cv2.polylines as a line of mask_line_thickness pixels (default 15) on an image of the JPEG size. It saves one PNG for each image and puts the PNG path in mask_path.
  • An image with no polyline has an empty mask_path. An empty mask_path means "not annotated" (D-33). With output_mask=True, the class drops these rows and warns. So 9,095 images stay.
  • The sample: mask is a float32 tensor (1, 224, 224) with the values 0 and 1 (D-14). The transform resizes it with the image.

Class Registry key Images Source RANZCRClipTrainDataset ranzcr_clip_train 30,083 train.csv RANZCRClipTestDataset ranzcr_clip_test 3,582 test/*.jpg, with no labels and no masks (D-25). Use it only for a Kaggle submission RANZCRClipDataset ranzcr_clip 33,665 All images. It mixes the 2 splits, so do not use it for a benchmark (D-09)

get_datasets(n_splits=5) makes a train and val split from the train class. It groups by patient (D-10).

RANZCRClipDataset adds the test images by default (include_test_split=True), with NaN labels and a split column. With output_cls=True, a test sample raises ValueError when it loads. RANZCRClipDataset(...).get_datasets_predefined() returns the train and test datasets. The split classes hold one split, so their get_datasets_predefined() raises TypeError.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Test patients: the test images have no PatientID. So nobody can check if a test patient is also in train.
  • Lines with no polyline: 24 images have polylines, but one of their positive labels has no polyline. For example, an image has 1 in CVC - Normal, but none of its polylines has the label CVC - Normal. So the mask does not show that line.

docs.title: RSNA Pneumonia
docs.text:
Registry keys rsna_pneumonia Task and outputs Classification, 3 labels (cls). Boxes (bbox) of lung opacities Images in the table Not counted. The RadHarmony tests cannot read the source files, so no test checks the harmonized table Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, DICOM License The terms of the RSNA download page Download Get the data: RSNA Pneumonia (official release)

The RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge (2018) has chest X-rays from ChestX-ray14, with 3 labels and boxes on the lung opacities. This page is about the adjudicated JSON release from the RSNA website. The JSON file puts the annotations in label groups. For example, Team 1 and Team 2 are reader teams, and Calculated is the final consensus. The Kaggle release of the same challenge has its own page: RSNA Pneumonia (Kaggle). The source files are not available to the maintainers, so this page has no real example.

rsna/

from radharmony.dataset import RSNAPneumoniaDataset

ds = RSNAPneumoniaDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/rsna/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
