train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(3,)
# sample["bbox"]: Tensor(N, 4), N is 0 for an image with no box
# sample["bbox_labels"]: a list of N names

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: the JSON file pneumonia-challenge-annotations-adjudicated-kaggle_2018.json. csv_path is this JSON file. The harmonizer keeps the annotations of one label group, by default Calculated (the final consensus). One row is one image (SOPInstanceUID).
  • IDs: patient_id and study_id are the StudyInstanceUID of the annotation. image_path is <StudyInstanceUID>/<SeriesInstanceUID>/<SOPInstanceUID>.dcm, relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Labels (3 columns, D-05): an annotation with a label gives 1 in the column of that label. The other columns stay 0. In Calculated, the label IDs L_v8n, L_yd0 and L_o8w give, in this order, lung_opacity, no_lung_opacity_/_not_normal and normal.
  • View, age and sex: the source has none of them, so the harmonized table has no view_position, age_years or sex (D-01).
  • Boxes: from the annotations with a data field. See Boxes.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops an image with no annotation in the label group.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 3 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Meaning lung_opacity A lung opacity that can be pneumonia. Only these annotations have boxes no_lung_opacity_/_not_normal No lung opacity, but the image is not normal normal A normal chest X-ray

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: an annotation of a lung opacity has data with x, y, width and height of the box, in pixels. The annotation also has width and height of the image.
  • The harmonizer divides data.y and data.height by the image height, and data.x and data.width by the image width. So the box is [data.y / height, (data.y + data.height) / height, data.x / width, (data.x + data.width) / width].
  • The box is [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max], in fractions of the image size (D-07).
  • bbox_labels has the snake_case name of the label of each box, lung_opacity. An image with no box has [] in bbox and in bbox_labels (D-07).
  • Readers (D-36): the harmonizer uses the boxes of 1 label group only, so it does not group the boxes of several teams.
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 4), in fractions of the returned image (D-28). bbox_labels is a list of N names. An image with no box gives (0, 4) and [].
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box to the image. It drops a box with no area after the clip, and warns (D-07).

docs.title: RSNA Pneumonia (Kaggle)
docs.text:
Registry keys rsna_pneumonia_kaggle_train, rsna_pneumonia_kaggle_test Task and outputs Classification, 3 labels (cls). Boxes (bbox) of lung opacities Images in the table train 26,684 (9,555 boxes on 6,012 images), test 3,000 (no labels) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, DICOM License The rules of the Kaggle competition. Accept them before the download Download Get the data: RSNA Pneumonia (Kaggle release)

The RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge (2018) is a Kaggle competition of the Radiological Society of North America. The images come from ChestX-ray14. Each train image has 1 of the 3 labels, and radiologists drew boxes on the lung opacities.

This page is about the Kaggle stage 2 files: 2 CSV files and 2 folders of DICOM files, with no subfolders. Each CSV file has one row for each box, and one row for each image with no box. So each has 30,227 rows. The adjudicated JSON release of the same challenge has its own page: RSNA Pneumonia.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the stage_2_train_images/ or stage_2_test_images/ folder. The train class finds the 2 CSV files in the folder above it.

  stage_2_detailed_class_info.csv
  stage_2_train_labels.csv
  stage_2_train_images/<patientId>.dcm
  stage_2_test_images/<patientId>.dcm

from radharmony.dataset import RSNAPneumoniaKaggleTrainDataset, RSNAPneumoniaKaggleTestDataset

train = RSNAPneumoniaKaggleTrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/rsna-pneumonia-detection-challenge/stage_2_train_images/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(3,)
# sample["bbox"]: Tensor(N, 4), N is 0 for an image with no box
# sample["bbox_labels"]: a list of N names

test_ds = RSNAPneumoniaKaggleTestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/rsna-pneumonia-detection-challenge/stage_2_test_images/",
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
# test_ds[0] has only "img", for a Kaggle submission

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: stage_2_detailed_class_info.csv, with patientId and class. It has one row for each box. The harmonized table has one row for each image (D-03).
  • Test source: the test harmonizer lists the .dcm files in base_image_dir.
  • IDs: the patientId 0004cfab-14fd-4e49-80ba-63a80b6bddd6 gives patient_id and study_id (the same text), and image_path 0004cfab-14fd-4e49-80ba-63a80b6bddd6.dcm. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04). So one patient is one study and one image.
  • Labels (3 columns, D-05): class gives 1 in its own column and 0 in the 2 other columns. For example, Lung Opacity gives lung_opacity 1. The source has no blank and no uncertain label.
  • View (D-01): from the DICOM tag ViewPosition, because the CSV files have no view. It is PA or AP. The D-01 notes have the counts.
  • Age and sex: age_years comes from the DICOM tag PatientAge, in years (D-06). sex is M or F, from the DICOM tag PatientSex (D-26). The harmonizer reads the DICOM headers only when base_image_dir is set.
  • Boxes: from stage_2_train_labels.csv. See Boxes.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops only the extra rows of an image with 2 or more boxes. It drops no image.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 3 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Meaning lung_opacity A lung opacity that can be pneumonia. Only these images have boxes no_lung_opacity_/_not_normal No lung opacity, but the image is not normal normal A normal chest X-ray

Each image has 1 in exactly 1 column. The test images have no labels (D-25).

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: stage_2_train_labels.csv has patientId, x, y, width, height and Target. A box is in the pixels of the DICOM image. A row with Target 0 has no box.
  • The harmonizer divides each value by 1024, because every image is 1024 x 1024 (H x W). Example: patientId 00436515-870c-4b36-a041-de91049b9ab4 has x 264, y 152, width 213 and height 379. This gives [0.1484375, 0.5185546875, 0.2578125, 0.4658203125].
  • The box is [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max], in fractions of the image size (D-07).
  • bbox_labels has the name lung_opacity for each box. An image with no box has the empty list [] in both bbox and bbox_labels (D-07).
  • Readers (D-36): the source has one set of boxes for each image, so the harmonizer does not group boxes.
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 4), in fractions of the returned image (D-28). bbox_labels is a list of N names. Example: (2, 4) and ['lung_opacity', 'lung_opacity']. An image with no box gives (0, 4) and [].
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box to the image. It drops a box with no area after the clip, and warns (D-07). The source files have no such box.

docs.title: Shenzhen Hospital CXR
docs.text:
Registry keys shenzhen_cxr Task and outputs Classification, 1 label (cls). TB region masks (mask), only with the Annotations-2/ download. Report text (report) Images in the table 662 (662 patients) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, PNG License NLM research use. Do not share the data outside your group. Cite Jaeger et al. and Candemir et al., IEEE TMI 2014 Download Get the data: Shenzhen Hospital CXR

The Shenzhen Hospital CXR Set is a tuberculosis (TB) screening set from the U.S. National Library of Medicine (NLM) and Shenzhen No.3 People's Hospital, China. It has 662 chest X-rays from outpatient care: 336 with TB (numbers 0327 to 0662) and 326 normal. A Philips DR system took them, and an image is about 3000 x 3000 pixels (H x W). Each image has a clinical reading with the sex, the age and a short diagnosis. It comes from the same NLM project as Montgomery County CXR, with the same folders and the same form of file name.

A later download, Annotations-2/, adds 19 TB finding columns and masks of the TB regions for 323 of the 336 TB images. It is a separate download: Get the data has a Python script for it. The harmonizer does not read the older Annotations/ folder or shenzhen_consensus_roi.csv (250 TB boxes on 68 images).

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the CXR_png/ folder. The class finds ClinicalReadings/ and Annotations-2/ next to it.

Shenzhen-Hospital-CXR-Set/
  CXR_png/CHNCXR_0001_0.png
  ClinicalReadings/CHNCXR_0001_0.txt
  Annotations-2/Statistics_ShenzhenDataset_US.csv
  Annotations-2/masks/CHNCXR_0327_1_Small_Infiltrate_(non-linear)_1.png

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import ShenzhenCXRDataset

ds = ShenzhenCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/Shenzhen-Hospital-CXR-Set/CXR_png/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_mask=True,  # needs Annotations-2/
    mask_output_dir="/data/shenzhen_tb_masks/",  # any folder you can write to
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(1,), 1 is TB and 0 is normal
# sample["mask"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224), 1 is a TB region and 0 is background

For classification only, leave out output_mask and mask_output_dir. Then the class keeps all 662 images.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: the PNG files in CXR_png/. One file is one row. The source has no label CSV.
  • IDs: the file CHNCXR_0001_0.png gives patient_id 0001, study_id 0001 and image_path CHNCXR_0001_0.png. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04). Each image number is one patient and one study.
  • Label (D-05): the file name gives tuberculosis. A file name that ends in _1 gives 1 (TB), and _0 gives 0 (normal).
  • Age and sex: they come from the first line of ClinicalReadings/<file name>.txt, for example male 45yrs. age_years comes from patient_age, in years (D-06). An age in months or days becomes years, so female 64days gives 0.175. sex is M or F, from patient_sex (D-26).
  • Report: report holds the whole reading, with the first line, for example male 45yrs\nnormal.
  • TB findings: the harmonizer joins the 19 finding columns of Annotations-2/Statistics_ShenzhenDataset_US.csv on the file name. They are NaN for a normal image.
  • View (D-01): the source has no view, so the harmonized table has no view_position.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
Column Meaning tuberculosis Tuberculosis. 1 is TB, 0 is normal

The 19 TB finding columns are extra columns, not labels, so cls does not hold them. They come from Annotations-2/. Each value is the number of regions of that finding on the image (0 to 75), not a 0 or 1 flag. For each column, the table below shows the number of TB images with 1 or more regions and the total number of regions.

Column Images Regions Small_Infiltrate_(non-linear) 145 219 Clustered_Nodule_(2mm-5mm_apart) 113 605 Linear_Density 90 339 Pleural_Thickening_(non-apical) 75 113 Single_Nodule_(non-calcified) 71 193 Apical_Thickening 68 92 Moderate_Infiltrate_(non-linear) 66 97 Calcified_Nodule 42 171 Pleural_Effusion 34 36 Other 29 71 Cavity 22 101 Adenopathy 22 30 Retraction 19 22 Severe_Infiltrate_(Consolidation) 18 20 Miliary 15 27 Unknown 14 19 Thickening_of_interlobar_fissure 8 8 Calcification_(other_than_nodule&lymphnod) 6 6 Calcified_lymph_node 5 8

docs.title: Masks
docs.text:
• Source: Annotations-2/masks/ holds 1 binary PNG for each finding region of a TB image. The file name gives the image, the finding and a region number, for example CHNCXR_0330_1_Pleural_Effusion_3.png. A normal image has no mask file.
  • The extra column finding_masks holds a JSON list of the mask files of each TB image, for example ["../Annotations-2/masks/CHNCXR_0327_1_Small_Infiltrate_(non-linear)_1.png"]. The paths are relative to base_image_dir.
  • With mask_output_dir, the harmonizer joins the masks of each TB image into 1 "TB region" mask. A pixel is 1 when it is in one of the masks. A normal image gets an all-zero mask of the image size. The harmonizer writes 1 PNG for each image to mask_output_dir. mask_path is the full path of that PNG. The harmonizer does not write a PNG again when the file exists.
  • An empty mask_path means "not annotated" (D-33). With output_mask=True, the class drops these rows and warns. 13 TB images have no mask file, so their mask_path is empty, and 649 of the 662 images stay.
  • With mask_output_dir and no Annotations-2/masks/ folder, the class raises FileNotFoundError with the folder name (D-35). Download Annotations-2/ before you use output_mask=True.
  • output_mask=True with no mask_output_dir raises ValueError.
  • The sample: mask is a float32 tensor (1, 224, 224) with the values 0 and 1 (D-14). The transform resizes it with the image.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text: report holds the whole reading. The first line has the sex and the age. The next lines have the diagnosis, for example normal or bilateral PTB (PTB is pulmonary tuberculosis). Every image has a reading, so output_report=True keeps all 662 images.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Age text: the first line of a reading has several forms, for example femal 32yrs (a typo, in 3 files), male35yrs (no space), male 16month and female 64days. CHNCXR_0018_0 says male 42 with no unit, so its age is NaN. The harmonizer does not guess the unit (D-06).
  • PNG type: 635 of the 662 PNGs are palette images and 27 are RGB. All are gray, so img has 1 channel (D-42).

docs.title: SIIM-ACR Pneumothorax
docs.text:
Registry keys siim_acr_ptx_train, siim_acr_ptx_test Task and outputs Classification, 1 label (cls). Pneumothorax masks (mask). The test split has images only Images in the table train 10,675 (10,675 patients), test 1,377 (1,377 patients) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, DICOM License The rules of the Kaggle competition. Accept them before the download Download Get the data: SIIM-ACR Pneumothorax

SIIM-ACR Pneumothorax Segmentation is a 2019 Kaggle challenge. RadHarmony reads the stage 1 files. The train split has 10,675 images, and 2,379 of them have a pneumothorax. train-rle.csv has 11,582 rows, because it has one row for each pneumothorax region. Each row holds one region as a run-length encoded (RLE) mask. The 1,377 test images have no labels and no masks.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is dicom-images-train/ or dicom-images-test/. The class finds train-rle.csv in base_image_dir or in the folder above it.

SIIM_ACR_Pneumothorax/
  train-rle.csv
  dicom-images-train/<StudyInstanceUID>/<SeriesInstanceUID>/<SOPInstanceUID>.dcm
  dicom-images-test/<StudyInstanceUID>/<SeriesInstanceUID>/<SOPInstanceUID>.dcm

The first run with output_mask=True decodes the masks and writes 10,675 PNG files to mask_output_dir. A later run uses these files.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import SIIMACRPTXTrainDataset, SIIMACRPTXTestDataset

train = SIIMACRPTXTrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/SIIM_ACR_Pneumothorax/dicom-images-train/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_mask=True,
    mask_output_dir="/data/siim_acr_ptx_masks/",
    mask_num_cores=8,  # threads that decode the masks
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(1,), 1 is pneumothorax and 0 is no pneumothorax
# sample["mask"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224), 1 is pneumothorax and 0 is background

test_ds = SIIMACRPTXTestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/SIIM_ACR_Pneumothorax/dicom-images-test/",
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
# test_ds[0] has only "img", for a Kaggle submission

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: train-rle.csv and the DICOM files in dicom-images-train/. The CSV has one row for each region. The harmonizer joins the rows of one image into one row (D-03).
  • IDs: the harmonizer finds each DICOM file below base_image_dir and joins it on ImageId. The first folder of the path (the StudyInstanceUID) gives patient_id, for example 1.2.276.0.7230010.3.1.2.8323329.5597.1517875188.959089. The second folder (the SeriesInstanceUID) gives study_id, for example 1.2.276.0.7230010.3.1.3.8323329.5597.1517875188.959088. image_path is the path of the file, relative to base_image_dir (D-04), for example 1.2.276.0.7230010.3.1.2.8323329.5597.1517875188.959089/1.2.276.0.7230010.3.1.3.8323329.5597.1517875188.959088/1.2.276.0.7230010.3.1.4.8323329.5597.1517875188.959090.dcm.
  • Patients: patient_id is the StudyInstanceUID folder, not the DICOM PatientID. Both are different for each image, so the split is the same with either one.
  • Label (D-05): pneumothorax is 0 when the RLE text is -1, and 1 for any other text.
  • View (D-01): the harmonized train table has view_position FRONTAL for every image. The harmonizer does not read the DICOM tag ViewPosition, which is PA or AP for every file. D-01 lists this as a known gap. The harmonized test table has no view_position.
  • Age and sex: they come from the DICOM headers. age_years comes from PatientAge, in years (D-06). sex is M or F, from PatientSex (D-26).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops the 37 train DICOM files that have no row in train-rle.csv.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: Column Meaning pneumothorax Pneumothorax. 1 when the image has a mask, 0 when the RLE text is -1

docs.title: Masks
docs.text:
• Source: the column EncodedPixels of train-rle.csv (the name starts with a space). Each row is the RLE text of one region on the 1024 x 1024 image (H x W), for example 407576 2 1021 7 1015 10 .... The pixels go down each column first. Each start is relative to the end of the run before it. -1 means no pneumothorax.
  • Without mask_output_dir, mask_path holds the RLE text. An image with 2 or more regions joins their texts with |. 624 train images have 2 or more regions.
  • With mask_output_dir, the harmonizer decodes each image into 1 PNG. A pixel is 1 when it is in one of the regions. An image with -1 gets an all-zero PNG, so the negative images stay. The PNG path copies image_path, for example <mask_output_dir>/<StudyInstanceUID>/<SeriesInstanceUID>/<SOPInstanceUID>.png. mask_path is the full path of that PNG. The harmonizer does not write a PNG again when the file exists.
  • An empty mask_path means "not annotated" (D-33). With output_mask=True, the class drops these rows and warns. Every train image has an RLE text or -1, so no mask_path is empty, and no row is dropped.
  • output_mask=True with no mask_output_dir raises ValueError.
  • The sample: mask is a float32 tensor (1, 224, 224) with the values 0 and 1 (D-14). The transform resizes it with the image.

docs.title: SIIM COVID-19 Detection
docs.text:
Registry keys siim_covid19_train, siim_covid19_test Task and outputs Classification, 4 labels for each study (cls). Opacity boxes (bbox). The test split has images only Images in the table train 6,334 (3,261 patients), test 1,263 (652 patients) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, DICOM License The rules of the Kaggle competition. Accept them before the download Download Get the data: SIIM COVID-19

SIIM-FISABIO-RSNA COVID-19 Detection is a 2021 Kaggle challenge. The train split has 6,334 images of 6,054 studies. The 1,263 test images have no labels and no boxes.

The source gives labels at 2 levels. Each study has 1 of 4 study labels, for example "Typical Appearance". Each image has an image label: opacity with 1 or more boxes, or none. 4,294 train images have 7,853 opacity boxes.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the train/ or test/ folder. The train class finds train_study_level.csv and train_image_level.csv in base_image_dir or in the folder above it.

from radharmony.dataset import SIIMCOVID19TrainDataset, SIIMCOVID19TestDataset

train = SIIMCOVID19TrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/siim-covid19-detection/train/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(4,), 1 for the study label and 0 for the other 3
# sample["bbox"]: Tensor(2, 4), one row for each box
# sample["bbox_labels"]: a list of N names, here ['opacity', 'opacity']

test_ds = SIIMCOVID19TestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/siim-covid19-detection/test/",
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
# test_ds[0] has only "img", for a Kaggle submission

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: train_image_level.csv (one row for each image) and train_study_level.csv (one row for each study). One row is one image (D-03). Each image gets the labels of its study.
  • IDs: study_id is the StudyInstanceUID of the image CSV. The harmonizer finds the file of each image in the folders of base_image_dir. patient_id is the DICOM tag PatientID, or study_id when the tag is empty. For example, patient_id dcc3fdf6426a, study_id 5776db0cec75 and image_path 5776db0cec75/81456c9c5423/000a312787f2.dcm. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Labels (D-05): the study CSV has 4 columns with 0 or 1, and each study has exactly one 1. The study id 5776db0cec75_study gives the StudyInstanceUID 5776db0cec75. The column names become snake_case, for example Typical Appearance gives typical_appearance.
  • Image label: the harmonizer does not keep the column label. An image with the label none has no box, so its bbox is an empty list.
  • View (D-01): the source has no view, so the harmonized table has no view_position.
  • Age and sex: sex is M or F, from the DICOM tag PatientSex (D-26). The DICOM files have no PatientAge, so the harmonized table has no age_years (D-06).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops a row of the image CSV with no DICOM file, and prints the count. With the source files, it drops no row.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 4 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Meaning atypical_appearance Atypical appearance for COVID-19 pneumonia indeterminate_appearance Indeterminate appearance for COVID-19 pneumonia negative_for_pneumonia No pneumonia typical_appearance Typical appearance for COVID-19 pneumonia

The labels are study labels. All images of one study have the same cls. No image of a negative_for_pneumonia study has a box. 304 images of the other studies have no box either.

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: the column boxes of train_image_level.csv. It is the text of a Python list of {x, y, width, height} dicts, in the pixels of the DICOM image. It is empty for an image with no box.
  • The harmonizer reads Rows and Columns of each DICOM header, so it needs base_image_dir. It divides y and height by Rows (the height), and x and width by Columns (the width).
  • The box is [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max], in fractions of the image size (D-07).
  • For example, image 000a312787f2 is 3488 x 4256 pixels (H x W). The source box {'x': 789.28836, 'y': 582.43035, 'width': 1026.65662, 'height': 1917.30292} gives [0.167, 0.717, 0.185, 0.427].
  • bbox_labels has opacity for each box (D-07).
  • Readers (D-36): the source has one set of boxes for each image, so the harmonizer does not group boxes.
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 4), in fractions of the returned image (D-28). bbox_labels is a list of N names. Example: (2, 4) and ['opacity', 'opacity']. An image with no box gives (0, 4) and [].
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box to the image. It drops a box with no area after the clip, and warns (D-07). The source files have no such box.

VinDr-CXR is a chest X-ray dataset from Vietnam, with 15,000 train and 3,000 test images. All images are PA. In train, 3 radiologists labeled each image on their own and drew boxes. In test, 5 radiologists agreed on one set of labels and boxes. The source has no patient ID.

    image_labels_test.csv
    annotations_test.csv

# sample["bbox"]: Tensor(N, 4), and Tensor(0, 4) for an image with no box
# sample["bbox_labels"]: a list of N names

    base_image_dir="/data/vindr-cxr/1.0.0/test/",

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: image_labels_train.csv or image_labels_test.csv. The train CSV has 3 rows for each image, one for each radiologist (rad_id). The test CSV has one row for each image. The harmonized table has one row for each image.
  • IDs: the source has no patient or study. The image_id e0dc2e79105ad93532484e956ef8a71a gives patient_id and study_id e0dc2e79105ad93532484e956ef8a71a, and image_path e0dc2e79105ad93532484e956ef8a71a.dicom. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Labels (28 columns, D-05): train uses a majority vote. A label is 1 when 2 or more of the 3 radiologists gave 1. The test labels are 0 or 1 as in the CSV. The harmonizer renames the test column Other disease to other_diseases, as in train.
  • View (D-01): all images are PA, so the harmonized table has no view_position.
  • Age and sex: from the DICOM headers, only with base_image_dir. age_years comes from PatientAge, in years (D-06). An age of 0 gives NaN (see Known data problems). sex is M, F or NaN, from PatientSex (D-26).
  • Boxes: see Boxes.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row.

Column Meaning Box aortic_enlargement The aorta is wide Yes atelectasis Part of a lung is collapsed Yes calcification A calcification Yes cardiomegaly The heart is large Yes clavicle_fracture A clavicle fracture Yes consolidation Airspace consolidation Yes copd Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease No edema Pulmonary edema Yes emphysema Emphysema Yes enlarged_pa The pulmonary artery is wide Yes ild Interstitial lung disease Yes infiltration Infiltration Yes lung_cavity A cavity in a lung Yes lung_cyst A cyst in a lung Yes lung_opacity A lung opacity Yes lung_tumor A lung tumor No mediastinal_shift The mediastinum moved to one side Yes no_finding No finding No nodule/mass A nodule or a mass Yes other_diseases Another disease No other_lesion Another lesion Yes pleural_effusion Pleural effusion Yes pleural_thickening Pleural thickening Yes pneumonia Pneumonia No pneumothorax Pneumothorax Yes pulmonary_fibrosis Pulmonary fibrosis Yes rib_fracture A rib fracture Yes tuberculosis Tuberculosis No

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: annotations_train.csv and annotations_test.csv. One row is one box: image_id, class_name and x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max in the pixels of the DICOM image. The train file also has rad_id. A No finding row has no box.
  • The harmonizer reads the size of each image file (the DICOM tags Rows and Columns), so it needs base_image_dir. It divides y_min and y_max by the height, and x_min and x_max by the width.
  • The box is [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max], in fractions of the image size (D-07). Example: the test image e0dc2e79105ad93532484e956ef8a71a is 2420 x 2148 (H x W). Its Calcification box x_min 1221.6, y_min 661.6, x_max 1343.3, y_max 783.3 gives [0.2734, 0.3237, 0.5687, 0.6254].
  • bbox_labels: the snake_case name of class_name. For example, Nodule/Mass gives nodule/mass (D-07).
  • Readers (D-36), train only: 3 radiologists drew boxes on each image. The harmonizer groups the boxes of one image and one finding that overlap (IoU > 0.5). A group with boxes of 2 or more radiologists is one lesion, and its box is the mean of the boxes in the group. The harmonizer drops a group with boxes of only 1 radiologist. So train has 8,328 boxes on 4,167 images.
  • Readers (D-36), test: the test file has one agreed set of boxes, so the harmonizer does not group boxes. Test has 2,697 boxes on 949 images, and no Edema box.
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 4), in fractions of the returned image (D-28). bbox_labels is a list of N names. Example: (8, 4) and ['calcification', 'cardiomegaly', 'ild', ...]. An image with no box gives (0, 4) and [].
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box to the image. It drops a box with no area after the clip, and warns (D-07). The source files have no such box. When the harmonizer cannot read the DICOM file of an image, the image gets no box, and the harmonizer warns. Without base_image_dir, every image gets no box, and harmonize() warns.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Sex: many headers have PatientSex O or an empty tag. These give NaN (D-26). Only 7,354 of the train images and 1,254 of the test images have M or F.
  • Age: many headers have no PatientAge tag, an empty tag, or a bad value such as Y. These give NaN (D-06). 905 train and 269 test images have the age 0 (000Y or 000D), which means unknown. One train age is 238Y, above 130, so it gives NaN. 4 test ages have no unit letter (for example 39), so they give NaN.
  • Column name: the test CSV writes Other disease, but the train CSV writes Other diseases.
  • Box counts: some train radiologists drew several boxes of one finding on one image (D-36). Example: on the train image 03e6ecfa6f6fb33dfeac6ca4f9b459c9, 3 radiologists drew 55 Nodule/Mass boxes, and the harmonized table keeps 14.

One image is one patient Modality Chest X-ray of children, 2-D, DICOM License PhysioNet Restricted Health Data License 1.5.0. Restricted access: a PhysioNet account and a signed data use agreement Download Get the data: other datasets

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: image_labels_train.csv or image_labels_test.csv. One row is one image. The boxes come from annotations_train.csv or annotations_test.csv. The image size, age and sex come from the DICOM header.
  • IDs: the source and the DICOM headers have no patient ID and no study ID. The image_id d7e71a052a753c3f2f3e317d60177bec of image_labels_test.csv gives the same patient_id and study_id, and image_path test/d7e71a052a753c3f2f3e317d60177bec.dicom. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Labels (D-05): the 15 label columns of the source hold 0 or 1. The source has no uncertain or blank label.
  • View (D-01): the source has no view, so the harmonized table has no view_position.
  • Age and sex: age_years comes from the DICOM tag PatientAge, in years (D-06). The tag has a unit: 005Y gives 5, 006M gives 0.5 and 000D gives 0. sex is M, F or NaN, from PatientSex (D-26).
  • Extra columns: split ("train" or "test"), image_width and image_height (from the DICOM header).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row.

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: annotations_train.csv and annotations_test.csv have one row for each box, with image_id, rad_ID (the radiologist), class_name and x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max in pixels. A No finding row has empty coordinates, so it gives no box.
  • The harmonizer reads the size of each image file (Rows and Columns of the DICOM header), so it needs base_image_dir. It divides y_min and y_max by the height, and x_min and x_max by the width.
  • The box is [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max], in fractions of the image size (D-07).
  • Example: the test image d7e71a052a753c3f2f3e317d60177bec is 1692 x 1255 (H x W). Its first row is Reticulonodular opacity with x_min 157.3, y_min 426.9, x_max 487.9 and y_max 914.6. It gives the box [0.2523, 0.5405, 0.1254, 0.3887] (rounded) with the label reticulonodular_opacity.
  • bbox_labels: the snake_case name of class_name (D-07). The train split has 36 box labels (the list below), and the test split has 23 of them.
  • Readers (D-36): one radiologist read each image, so the harmonizer does not group boxes.
  • bbox and bbox_labels are JSON text in the harmonized table. An image with only a No finding row gets [].
  • The sample: bbox is a float32 tensor (N, 4), in fractions of the returned image (D-28). bbox_labels is a list of N names. Example: (2, 4) and ['reticulonodular_opacity', 'reticulonodular_opacity']. An image with no box gives (0, 4) and []. A train image has up to 10 boxes, and a test image has up to 6.
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer clips each box to the image. It drops a box with no area after the clip, and warns (D-07). The source files have no such box. Also, an image with boxes and a DICOM file that the harmonizer cannot read gets no box, and a warning gives the count.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Age over 10: the PhysioNet page says that every patient is under 10. But PatientAge gives 72 train and 14 test images an age over 10, for example 011Y, 019Y and 035Y. The harmonized table keeps the tag value (D-06).
  • No age: 294 train and 59 test images have no age. The tag is missing (185 images), empty (167) or Y with no number (1).
  • Age 0: 150 images have 000D, which gives 0. A newborn is a real patient, so the harmonized table keeps it (D-06).
  • Sex O: 46 train and 16 test images have the sex O, which gives NaN (D-26).
  • Spelling: the source spells some names wrong, for example Brocho-pneumonia, Diagphramatic hernia, Bronchectasis and Paraveterbral mass. The harmonized names keep the source spelling.

docs.title: BRAX
docs.text:
Registry keys brax (DICOM), brax_png (PNG) Task and outputs Classification, 14 labels (cls) Images in the table 40,967 (18,442 patients, 23,276 studies) in each key Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, DICOM or PNG License PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0 Download Get the data: BRAX

BRAX (Brazilian Chest X-Ray) v1.1.0 is a chest X-ray dataset from a hospital network in Brazil. The original CheXpert labeler read the Portuguese reports and gave the 14 CheXpert labels. The source has no reports. One download has the DICOM and the PNG images. BRAXDataset reads the DICOM files, and BRAXPNGDataset reads the PNG files. Both use one harmonizer, so both keys have the same rows.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the BRAX root. The class finds master_spreadsheet.csv or master_spreadsheet_update.csv in this folder or in the folder above it.

brax/1.1.0/
  master_spreadsheet_update.csv
  Anonymized_DICOMs/id_<PatientID>/Study_<UID>/Series_<UID>/image-<UID>.dcm
  images/id_<PatientID>/Study_<UID>/Series_<UID>/image-<UID>.png

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import BRAXDataset

ds = BRAXDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/brax/1.1.0/",
    uncertain_strategy="u_zeros",  # -1 and blank give 0
    output_cls=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(14,)

BRAXPNGDataset takes the same arguments.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: master_spreadsheet.csv or master_spreadsheet_update.csv. One row is one image (D-03).
  • IDs: patient_id is PatientID, for example id_55c25711-75a21898-593e2eea-46007548-5afa539c. study_id is AccessionNumber, for example 79565147 (D-01). series_id is the Series_<UID> folder name in the path.
  • image_path is DicomPath (brax) or PngPath (brax_png), as in the source. It is relative to the BRAX root (D-04). Example (PNG): images/id_55c25711-75a21898-593e2eea-46007548-5afa539c/Study_79565147.82013478.83925914.72078900.07189967/Series_40604671.16381531.63216171.19463495.14134010/image-61667501-86352188-29978958-28578248-00095672.png.
  • Labels (D-05): the source codes are 1 (positive), 0 (negative), -1 (uncertain) and blank (not mentioned). uncertain_strategy="raw" (the default) keeps all 4 codes, so cls can hold -1 and NaN. The other strategies are in Labels.
  • View (D-01): from ViewPosition. L and RL give LATERAL. A blank gives NaN. Other values, such as LT-DECUB or RLO, stay as in the source.
  • Age and sex: age_years comes from PatientAge, in years (D-06). It is the lowest age of the 5-year group. For example, 40 (40 to 44 years) gives 40, and 85 or more gives 85. sex is M or F, from PatientSex (D-26).
  • Size (D-01): rows and columns give the DICOM size from the source, also for brax_png. The PNG files are smaller. Example: 2752 x 2232 in the harmonized table, but the PNG is 1261 x 1024.
  • Dropped rows: none with "raw". With uncertain_strategy="drop", the harmonizer drops each row with a -1 label.

uncertain_strategy sets the values in the harmonized table and in cls:

Strategy -1 gives Blank gives Dropped rows "raw" (default) -1 NaN None "u_zeros" 0 0 None "u_ones" 1 0 None "u_ignore" NaN 0 None "drop" Not in the harmonized table 0 The rows with a -1 label

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Shared study IDs: 2 AccessionNumber values (21498229 and 26826491) belong to 2 patients each, with different study dates. The harmonizer warns. Group by patient_id and study_id together (D-01).
  • Age: the source gives only 5-year age groups, not the exact age (D-06).
  • View: many rows of the source have a blank ViewPosition (D-01).
  • Size: the source gives only the DICOM size. The PNG files are smaller (D-01).
  • Counts: the source CSV has 18,442 PatientID values and 23,276 AccessionNumber values. The BRAX paper (Reis et al., Scientific Data 2022) gives 19,351 patients and 24,959 studies. The image count is the same.

docs.title: ChestX-ray14
docs.text:

Cite Wang et al., CVPR 2017 Download Get the data: ChestX-ray14

ChestX-ray14 (NIH Chest X-ray Dataset) has 112,120 frontal chest X-rays of 30,805 patients from the NIH Clinical Center. A text-mining tool read each report and gave 14 findings or "No Finding". The official split puts each patient in train or in test. Radiologists drew 984 boxes of 8 findings on 880 test images.

train = ChestXray14TrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/NIH_CXR/CXR14/",

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: Data_Entry_2017.csv. One row is one image (D-03). A split class keeps only the images in its list, train_val_list.txt or test_list.txt (D-09).
  • IDs: the row with Image Index 00000003_000.png, Patient ID 3 and Follow-up # 0 gives patient_id 3 and study_id 3_0. So one study is one image (D-01).
  • image_path: the harmonizer looks for the file in the 12 image folders. Example: images_001/images/00000003_000.png. It is relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Labels (15 columns, D-05): Finding Labels holds names with a | between them, for example Atelectasis|Effusion. A name in the list gives 1, and all other labels give 0. The source has no uncertain or blank label.
  • View (D-01): from View Position. It is PA or AP for every image.
  • Age and sex: age_years comes from Patient Age, in years (D-06). sex is M or F, from Patient Gender (D-26).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops the rows that are not in the split list. It drops no row for its labels.

docs.text:
The 15 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Meaning atelectasis Part of a lung is collapsed cardiomegaly The heart is large consolidation Airspace consolidation edema Pulmonary edema effusion Pleural effusion emphysema Emphysema fibrosis Pulmonary fibrosis hernia Hernia infiltration Infiltration mass A lung mass no_finding No finding nodule A lung nodule pleural_thickening Pleural thickening pneumonia Pneumonia pneumothorax Pneumothorax

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
ChestXray14BboxDataset gives the 880 images with boxes. Each image has 1 or more boxes.

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import ChestXray14BboxDataset

bbox_ds = ChestXray14BboxDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/NIH_CXR/CXR14/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_bbox=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
sample = bbox_ds[0]
# sample["bbox"]: Tensor(1, 4), one row for each box
# sample["bbox_labels"]: ['infiltration']
  • Source: BBox_List_2017.csv. A box is x, y, w, h in the pixels of the 1024 x 1024 PNG.
  • The harmonizer divides x and w by the PNG width, and y and h by the PNG height. So ChestXray14BboxHarmonizer needs base_image_dir, and without it harmonize() raises ValueError.
  • The box is [dim0_min, dim0_max, dim1_min, dim1_max], so [y_min, y_max, x_min, x_max]. The harmonizer clips each box to the image (D-07).
  • A box label uses the snake_case name of its label column (D-07). For example, Infiltrate gives infiltration. The 8 box labels are atelectasis, cardiomegaly, effusion, infiltration, mass, nodule, pneumonia and pneumothorax.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Age: 16 source ages are above 130 (148 to 414), so they are errors (D-06). Example: patient 5567 is 412 at the first visit and 53 at the next.
  • RGBA files: some PNGs are RGBA, but the image is gray (D-42).
  • Box labels: BBox_List_2017.csv writes Infiltrate, but Data_Entry_2017.csv writes Infiltration.
  • Box CSV header: the header has the commas of Bbox [x,y,w,h] inside it, and it ends with 3 empty fields. So the header has 9 fields, but each data row has 6.
  • Image size: OriginalImage[Width and Height] in Data_Entry_2017.csv give the size before the authors resized the image to the PNG. The boxes use the PNG size, so these columns do not match the boxes.

CheXpert is a chest X-ray dataset from Stanford. For train.csv, the CheXpert labeler (a rule-based tool) read each report and gave 14 labels. For valid.csv, 3 radiologists gave the labels. train.csv has 223,414 images. The default drop_uncertain=True drops each row with a -1 label, so 138,358 train images stay. The official test set is in CheXlocalize.

CheXphoto (Phillips et al., ML4H 2020) tests a model on photos of chest X-rays. It takes CheXpert X-rays and gives phone photos of a screen (natural) and synthetic copies (synthetic). The 14 labels are the CheXpert labels, with no change. So you can train on CheXpert and test here. train.csv has 32,521 images. The default drop_uncertain=True drops each row with a -1 label, so 20,034 train images stay.

The authors keep the test split for their CodaLab competition, so there is no test class. Redivis gives train and valid as 2 file index tables. Download both.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Path starts with CheXphoto-v1.0/<split>/, but the download has no such folders (D-04).
  • In Path, the patient folder is not at the same position as in CheXpert, because of the 2 extra folders <subset>/<capture method>.
  • The CSV column names have _ where the CheXpert names have a space or /.
  • The paper describes a film subset in valid, but version 1.0 has no film images.

docs.title: Emory CHoRUS (X-ray subset)
docs.text:
Registry keys emory_chorus Task and outputs Images only (img). No labels, masks, boxes or reports Images in the table 10,290 chest images, 4,889 studies and 1,397 patients (chest_only=True) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, DICOM (all images are DX) License Internal Emory data. It is not public, and you must not share it Download No download. The data paths are in configs/data_paths.json

Emory CHoRUS is an internal dataset of Emory. It links a clinical database with DICOM images of many modalities. RadHarmony reads only the X-ray subset: 13,611 images of 1,496 patients. By default, the class keeps only the chest X-rays. The other images show the abdomen, the spine, the skull or the limbs.

The database uses OMOP CDM, a standard format for clinical tables, with the patients, conditions, measurements, procedures and visits. The class names write the dataset name as CHORUS.

The subset has no labels, masks, boxes or reports. Use it for image-only work, for example to extract features or to look at the images of a patient. The page is in the label group only because the dataset has chest X-rays.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the images_dicom_xray/ folder. The source has no table of the images. So the first run reads the header of each DICOM file and writes a manifest CSV to manifest_csv_path. The manifest CSV is a table with one row for each DICOM file. The next runs read the manifest.

Emory_CHORUS/
  images_dicom_xray/<person_id>/Images/<StudyInstanceUID>/<SeriesInstanceUID>/<file>.dcm
  chorus_xray_manifest.csv   # the first run writes it

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import EmoryCHORUSDataset

ds = EmoryCHORUSDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/Emory_CHORUS/images_dicom_xray/",
    manifest_csv_path="/data/Emory_CHORUS/chorus_xray_manifest.csv",
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample keys: img
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: the manifest CSV. One row is one DICOM file. The scan reads each header with pydicom, with num_workers processes. It skips a file that pydicom cannot read. Without manifest_csv_path, each run scans the folder again, and this is slow.
  • Chest filter: with chest_only=True (the default), the harmonizer keeps a row when Modality is DX or CR, and BodyPartExamined or StudyDescription contains CHEST. See Known data problems.
  • IDs: the file <person_id>/Images/<StudyInstanceUID>/<SeriesInstanceUID>/<file>.dcm gives patient_id <person_id> (the name of the patient folder), study_id <StudyInstanceUID> and series_id <SeriesInstanceUID>. image_path is the whole path, relative to base_image_dir (D-04). A study can have more than one image.
  • View (D-01): from the DICOM ViewPosition. AP and PA stay. LL, LAT and LATERAL give LATERAL. Oblique views, for example LAO, keep their source value.
  • Age and sex: age_years comes from the DICOM PatientAge, in whole years (D-06). sex is M, F or NaN, from PatientSex (D-26).
  • Dropped rows: only the chest filter drops rows. With chest_only=False, the table has all rows of the manifest.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: The subset has no label columns, so LABEL_COLS is empty. The OMOP tables have the condition codes of each patient, but RadHarmony does not read them.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Manufacturer: one maker has more than one spelling, for example CARESTREAM HEALTH and Carestream Health, or GE Healthcare with and without quote marks. The table keeps the source text.
  • Study date: study_date has the form 2020-01-31 00:00:00, not the DICOM form 20200131. The DICOM headers of this subset store the date in this form, and the harmonizer does not change it.
  • Chest filter: the filter reads the header text, not the image. So an image with the body part ABDOMEN or RIB stays when its study description names the chest.

docs.title: Emory CXR v2
docs.text:
Registry keys emory_cxr (PNG), emory_cxr_dicom (DICOM) Task and outputs Classification, 14 labels (cls), and the report text (report) Images in the table 2,430,209 images, 1,214,535 studies and 402,809 patients (manifest 08152025) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D. 16-bit PNG (emory_cxr) or 8-bit DICOM (emory_cxr_dicom) License Internal Emory data. It is not public, and you must not share it Download No download. The data paths are in configs/data_paths.json

Emory CXR v2 is an internal chest X-ray dataset of Emory. The images are from 2008 to 2021, from 11 institutions. The institution names are de-identified.

Almost every study has a de-identified free-text report. The reports are the main reason to use this dataset, for example as a report-generation target. The 14 labels follow CheXpert. Most label cells are blank, and a blank means "not mentioned", not "absent".

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is DEID_PNG/. The class finds the 3 tables in TABLES/, next to DEID_PNG/. It reads the label table only with output_cls=True, and the report table only with output_report=True.

EmoryCXRv2/
  DEID_PNG/<empi_anon>/<AccessionNumber_anon>/<SOP>.png
  DEID_DICOM/B1/ ... DEID_DICOM/B5/
  TABLES/
    EmoryCXR_v2_Metadata_08152025.csv
    EmoryCXR_v2_FindingLabel_10162024.csv
    EmoryCXR_v2_Report_05102026.csv
    mapping_deid_dcm_sopid.csv

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import EmoryCXRDataset, EmoryCXRDicomDataset

ds = EmoryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/EmoryCXRv2/DEID_PNG/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_report=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(14,), with 1, 0, -1 and NaN
# sample["report"]: str

# The DICOM tree. The class finds TABLES/mapping_deid_dcm_sopid.csv.
dicom_ds = EmoryCXRDicomDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/EmoryCXRv2/DEID_DICOM/",
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
# dicom_ds[0]["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: 3 tables, joined on AccessionNumber_anon as a string. The metadata manifest has one row for each image. One row of the harmonized table is one image (D-03).
  • IDs: patient_id is empi_anon. study_id and accession_number are AccessionNumber_anon. image_path is ImagePath, relative to DEID_PNG/ (D-04). Example: image_path 84269073/3739633430788944/1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498.11539031758371223425771024448750240761.png has patient_id 84269073 and study_id 3739633430788944.
  • Labels (D-05): the labels are for each study. A left join gives them to each image of the study. The 14 columns get snake_case names. An image whose study has no label row gets NaN in every label.
  • Uncertain and blank labels: -1 stays in cls, and a blank stays NaN. There is no drop_uncertain and no not_mentioned argument. A study can have 2 label rows. If one row has only No Finding = 1, the harmonizer keeps the other row (D-03).
  • View (D-01): the PNG class uses Frontal first, and ViewPosition second:
  • Frontal 1 with AP or PA keeps AP or PA.
  • Frontal 1 with Lateral or a blank gives NaN, because AP or PA is unknown.
  • Frontal 1 with Other gives OTHER.
  • Frontal 0 with AP gives NaN.
  • Frontal 0 with any other value (PA, Lateral, Other or a blank) gives LATERAL.
  • The DICOM class keeps ViewPosition as in the source.
  • Age and sex: age_years comes from Age, in years (D-06). sex is M, F or NaN, from Sex (D-26). The raw values stay in patient_age and patient_sex.
  • Dropped rows: none in the PNG class. The DICOM class joins mapping_deid_dcm_sopid.csv on the SOP column, and drops an image with no mapping row. Its image_path starts at the batch folder, for example B2/mdai_emory_project_..._part01of10/<UID>/<UID>/<UID>.dcm. <UID> is a new MD.ai UID, not the SOP. Only the mapping CSV links the two.

The 14 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Source column Meaning atelectasis Atelectasis Part of a lung is collapsed cardiomegaly Cardiomegaly The heart is large consolidation Consolidation Airspace consolidation edema Edema Pulmonary edema enlarged_cardiomediastinum Enlarged Cardiomediastinum The mediastinum is wide fracture Fracture A rib or other bone fracture lung_lesion Lung Lesion A lung lesion lung_opacity Lung Opacity A lung opacity no_finding No Finding No finding pleural_effusion Pleural Effusion Pleural effusion pleural_other Pleural Other Another pleural finding pneumonia Pneumonia Pneumonia pneumothorax Pneumothorax Pneumothorax support_devices Support Devices A tube, line or other device

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
The report table has the text in the column deid_report. The harmonized table gives it in report. A report has 66 words on average. 98.9% of the reports have an IMPRESSION section, and 86.5% have a FINDINGS section.

A blank template (only "REPORT", spaces and underscores) counts as no report. When a study has a blank template and a real report, the harmonizer keeps the real report (D-03). With output_report=True, the dataset drops the images with no report (D-33).

Emory CXR v2 has no official split. get_datasets(n_splits=5) makes a train and val split. It groups by patient (D-10). Do not split by study: 42.7% of the patients have more than one study (up to 296). The app lists only emory_cxr, because emory_cxr_dicom shows the same images (D-09).

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• View: for some images, Frontal and ViewPosition do not agree. In a manual check of some images, Frontal was right (D-01).
  • View: most images with Frontal 0 and ViewPosition AP are upright frontal or decubitus images, not lateral images (D-01).
  • Repeated rows: some studies have 2 or more rows in the label or report table. The report table has 151 such studies, and the label table has 75. Most of them have a blank report template and a real report. 8 label and 17 report conflicts have 2 real rows that do not agree (D-03).
  • Reports: 3 studies (7 images) have only a blank report template, so they have no report (D-03, D-33).
  • Labels: most label cells are blank, and No Finding has no 0. So a blank as 0 gives false negatives.
  • Manifests: the dated metadata manifests are not the same cohort. 08112025 has 2,486,502 images of 410,449 patients. 08152025 keeps only an age of 18 or more, and has 2,430,209 images of 402,809 patients.
  • Pixels: each PNG is min-max scaled to the full 16-bit range, with no VOI LUT. So pixel values do not compare across images. ORIGINAL_PNG/ has a different scaling. Do not mix it with DEID_PNG/.
  • DICOM tree: the files are an 8-bit MD.ai export, not the source DICOM files. AccessionNumber is blank, and PatientID is different in each file. Only mapping_deid_dcm_sopid.csv links a file to a patient. The MD.ai manifests name 3 files that were never delivered.

docs.title: MIMIC-CXR (DICOM)
docs.text:
Registry keys mimic_cxr_train, mimic_cxr_validate, mimic_cxr_test Task and outputs Classification, 14 labels (cls), and the report text (report) Images in the table train 291,240 (171,373 studies, 60,024 patients), validate 2,320 (1,355 studies, 459 patients), test 3,556 (2,216 studies, 287 patients) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, DICOM License PhysioNet credentialed access (CITI training and a signed DUA) Download Get the data: MIMIC-CXR

MIMIC-CXR has chest X-rays and their reports from the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. cxr-record-list.csv.gz has 377,110 images in 227,835 studies of 65,379 patients. The 14 labels come from the CheXpert labeler, which read each report. The default drop_uncertain=True drops each study with a -1 label, so 291,240 train images stay. For the JPEG copy of the same images, see MIMIC-CXR-JPG.

base_image_dir is the files/ folder. The class finds cxr-record-list.csv.gz and cxr-study-list.csv.gz in base_image_dir or in the folder above it. The label file and the split file are in the MIMIC-CXR-JPG release, so give their paths.

  cxr-record-list.csv.gz
  cxr-study-list.csv.gz
  files/p10/p10000032/s50414267.txt
  files/p10/p10000032/s50414267/02aa804e-bde0afdd-112c0b34-7bc16630-4e384014.dcm

from radharmony.dataset import MIMICCXRTestDataset, MIMICCXRTrainDataset, MIMICCXRValidateDataset

    label_csv_path="/data/mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/mimic-cxr-2.0.0-chexpert.csv",
    split_csv_path="/data/mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/mimic-cxr-2.0.0-split.csv",
    output_cls=True,
    output_report=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds = MIMICCXRTrainDataset(**kw).get_datasets()
val_ds = MIMICCXRValidateDataset(**kw).get_datasets()
test_ds = MIMICCXRTestDataset(**kw).get_datasets()
sample = val_ds[0]

# sample["cls"]: Tensor(14,)

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: cxr-record-list.csv.gz. One row is one DICOM image. A split class keeps the images of its split in mimic-cxr-2.0.0-split.csv, by dicom_id (D-09).
  • IDs: subject_id 10000032 gives patient_id 10000032, and study_id 50414267 gives 50414267. The path files/p10/p10000032/s50414267/02aa804e-bde0afdd-112c0b34-7bc16630-4e384014.dcm gives image_path p10/p10000032/s50414267/02aa804e-bde0afdd-112c0b34-7bc16630-4e384014.dcm, relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Labels (D-05): mimic-cxr-2.0.0-chexpert.csv has one row for each study. The harmonizer joins it on patient_id and study_id, so all images of one study get the same labels. 1 gives 1 and 0 gives
  • A blank gives 0 (not_mentioned="negative") or NaN (not_mentioned="nan"). A study with every label blank gets NaN in every label.
  • View (D-01): only with dicom_base_dir. The harmonizer reads the DICOM tag ViewPosition of each file. A shared step maps the values to AP, PA and LATERAL. A rare value keeps its name in upper case. Without dicom_base_dir, the harmonized table has no view_position.
  • Age and sex: the source has no age and no sex.
  • Dropped rows: with drop_uncertain=True (the default), the harmonizer drops a study with -1 in any label, with all its images. With False, -1 stays in cls. The harmonizer also drops an image whose study has no row in the label file, and warns with the count (D-25).

docs.text: With output_report=True, sample["report"] is the text of the report file of the study. cxr-study-list.csv.gz lists 227,835 report files. Its path, for example files/p10/p10000032/s50414267.txt, gives the file p10/p10000032/s50414267.txt in base_image_dir. All images of one study get the same report. The report generation evaluator finds the FINDINGS and IMPRESSION sections from the headers in the text (D-38).

from radharmony.harmonizer import MIMICCXRValidateHarmonizer

docs.title: MIMIC-CXR-JPG
docs.text:
Registry keys mimic_cxr_jpg_train, mimic_cxr_jpg_validate, mimic_cxr_jpg_test, mimic_cxr_jpg_test_chexpert Task and outputs Classification, 14 labels (cls) Images in the table train 291,240 (60,024 patients), validate 2,320 (459 patients), test 1,029 (296 patients), test_chexpert 3,556 (287 patients) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, JPEG License PhysioNet credentialed access (CITI training and a signed DUA) Download Get the data: MIMIC-CXR-JPG

MIMIC-CXR-JPG is the JPEG copy of MIMIC-CXR. It is faster to load than the DICOM files. mimic-cxr-2.0.0-metadata.csv has 377,110 images in 227,835 studies of 65,379 patients. The source has no report text, so use MIMIC-CXR for reports.

The labels of mimic_cxr_jpg_train, mimic_cxr_jpg_validate and mimic_cxr_jpg_test_chexpert come from the CheXpert labeler. The labels of mimic_cxr_jpg_test come from radiologists. The counts above use the default drop_uncertain of each class.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the files/ folder. The class finds mimic-cxr-2.0.0-metadata.csv, mimic-cxr-2.0.0-chexpert.csv and mimic-cxr-2.1.0-test-set-labeled.csv in base_image_dir or in the folder above it. A split class finds mimic-cxr-2.0.0-split.csv next to the metadata file.

mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/
  mimic-cxr-2.0.0-metadata.csv
  mimic-cxr-2.0.0-chexpert.csv
  mimic-cxr-2.0.0-split.csv
  mimic-cxr-2.1.0-test-set-labeled.csv
  files/p10/p10000032/s50414267/02aa804e-bde0afdd-112c0b34-7bc16630-4e384014.jpg

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import (
    MIMICCXRJPGTestDataset,
    MIMICCXRJPGTrainDataset,
    MIMICCXRJPGValidateDataset,
)

kw = dict(base_image_dir="/data/mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/files/", output_cls=True, dtype=torch.float32)
train_ds = MIMICCXRJPGTrainDataset(**kw).get_datasets()
val_ds = MIMICCXRJPGValidateDataset(**kw).get_datasets()
test_ds = MIMICCXRJPGTestDataset(**kw).get_datasets()  # the labeled test set, -1 stays
sample = test_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(14,)

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: mimic-cxr-2.0.0-metadata.csv. One row is one JPEG image. A split class keeps the images of its split in mimic-cxr-2.0.0-split.csv, by dicom_id (D-09).
  • IDs: subject_id 10000032 gives patient_id 10000032, and study_id 50414267 gives 50414267. With the dicom_id, they give image_path p10/p10000032/s50414267/02aa804e-bde0afdd-112c0b34-7bc16630-4e384014.jpg, relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Labels (D-05): mimic-cxr-2.0.0-chexpert.csv has one row for each study. The harmonizer joins it on patient_id and study_id, so all images of one study get the same labels. 1 gives 1 and 0 gives
  • A blank gives 0 (not_mentioned="negative") or NaN (not_mentioned="nan"). A study with every label blank gets NaN in every label.
  • Labeled test set: mimic-cxr-2.1.0-test-set-labeled.csv has no subject_id, and it names Lung Opacity Airspace Opacity. So the harmonizer joins it on study_id only, and renames the column to lung_opacity.
  • View (D-01): from the column ViewPosition. A shared step maps the values to AP, PA and LATERAL. A blank gives NaN. A rare value keeps its name in upper case, for example AP AXIAL or LAO.
  • Age and sex: the source has no age and no sex.
  • Dropped rows: with drop_uncertain=True, the harmonizer drops a study with -1 in any label, with all its images. True is the default for all classes, except MIMICCXRJPGTestDataset. With False, -1 stays in cls. The harmonizer also drops an image whose study has no row in the label file, and warns with the count (D-25). mimic_cxr_jpg_test gives no warning, because it uses this join to keep the test studies only.

docs.text:
The 14 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Meaning atelectasis Part of a lung is collapsed cardiomegaly The heart is large consolidation Airspace consolidation edema Pulmonary edema enlarged_cardiomediastinum The mediastinum is wide fracture A rib or other bone fracture lung_lesion A lung lesion lung_opacity A lung opacity no_finding No finding pleural_effusion Pleural effusion pleural_other Another pleural finding pneumonia Pneumonia pneumothorax Pneumothorax support_devices A tube, line or other device

docs.title: MS-CXR-T
docs.text:
Registry keys ms_cxr_t Task and outputs Change of 5 findings between 2 visits, in the harmonized table only. Image pairs (img and previous_img) Images in the table 1,045 image pairs, with 1,036 current images of 800 patients Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, JPEG from MIMIC-CXR-JPG 2.0.0 License PhysioNet credentialed access, as for MIMIC-CXR Download Get the data: other datasets. The images come from MIMIC-CXR-JPG

MS-CXR-T is a temporal benchmark (Bannur et al., CVPR 2023). Its image task extends the progression labels of Chest ImaGenome. Each row links a current chest X-ray to a prior chest X-ray of the same patient. Experts labeled the change of up to 5 findings: improving, stable or worsening. The labels are in the harmonized table, not in cls. RadHarmony reads only the image classification CSV of the source, not the sentence similarity CSV.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the files/ folder of MIMIC-CXR-JPG 2.0.0, the same folder as for MS-CXR. The CSV is in its own folder, so pass csv_path.

mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/files/        <- base_image_dir
  p10/p10002428/s55758034/3bea0373-0d10dd77-1cac5b90-651be924-d343b184.jpg
ms-cxr-t/
  MS_CXR_T_temporal_image_classification_v1.0.0.csv   <- csv_path

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MSCXRTDataset

ds = MSCXRTDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/files/",
    csv_path="/data/ms-cxr-t/MS_CXR_T_temporal_image_classification_v1.0.0.csv",
    output_previous=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
pairs = ds.get_datasets()
sample = pairs[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224), the current image
# sample["previous_img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224), the prior image

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: MS_CXR_T_temporal_image_classification_v1.0.0.csv. One row is one image pair, not one image (D-03).
  • IDs: patient_id is subject_id. study_id and previous_study_id come from the CSV. image_path is dicom_id plus .jpg, relative to the files/ folder (D-04). Example: the dicom_id p10/p10002428/s55758034/3bea0373-0d10dd77-1cac5b90-651be924-d343b184 gives the image_path p10/p10002428/s55758034/3bea0373-0d10dd77-1cac5b90-651be924-d343b184.jpg, the patient_id 10002428 and the study_id 55758034. previous_image_path comes from previous_dicom_id in the same way.
  • Labels: the class has no LABEL_COLS, so it gives no cls. In each <finding>_progression column, improving gives -1, stable gives 0 and worsening gives 1. Here -1 means "improving", not "uncertain" as in D-05.
  • Blank labels: a finding with no label gets NaN in its progression column and in its quality column.
  • View, age and sex: the CSV has none of them. So the harmonized table has no view_position, age_years or sex.
  • Dropped rows: none from the CSV. With output_previous=True, the class drops a row with no previous_image_path. Only a table that you make yourself can have such a row (D-11).

Column Values Meaning consolidation_progression -1, 0, 1, NaN Change of consolidation: improving, stable, worsening, no label edema_progression -1, 0, 1, NaN Change of edema pleural_effusion_progression -1, 0, 1, NaN Change of pleural effusion pneumonia_progression -1, 0, 1, NaN Change of pneumonia pneumothorax_progression -1, 0, 1, NaN Change of pneumothorax

Each finding also has a column <finding>_label_quality, for example edema_label_quality. Its values are one_expert, multiple_experts, disagreement or NaN, as in the source.

print(df[["study_id", "previous_study_id", "pleural_effusion_progression",

# 1  54394630          57157809                          -1.0               multiple_experts

docs.text:
• Disagreement: for some labels, the experts did not agree. The quality column is then disagreement, but the progression column still has a value. Filter on the quality column if you need clean labels.

docs.title: PadChest
docs.text:
Registry keys padchest Task and outputs Classification, 193 labels (cls). The report text in Spanish (report) Images in the table 157,607 (66,587 patients, 107,439 studies). By default, the harmonizer drops the rows with exclude or suboptimal_study Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, PNG License BIMCV PadChest research use agreement Download Get the data: PadChest

PadChest is a chest X-ray dataset from Hospital San Juan de Alicante, Spain. BIMCV released it. Its 193 labels come from a text-mining tool on the Spanish reports, plus a manual review. The source CSV has 160,861 images of 67,625 patients.

The source CSV also holds the report of each image. The reports are in Spanish. The authors cut each word to its stem, for example hallazg for hallazgo.

Download each numbered zip by itself, because the zip of the whole folder does not resume. Unzip N.zip into images/N/.

docs.text:
base_image_dir is the images/ folder. The class finds the label CSV in this folder or in the folder above it. The PNG files are in 52 folders: 0/ to 50/, and 54/.

  images/
    0/20536686640136348236148679891455886468_k6ga29.png
    1/
    ...
    50/
    54/

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import PadChestDataset

ds = PadChestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/PadChest/images/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_report=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(193,)
# sample["report"]: ' sin hallazg patolog edad pacient .'

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: PADCHEST_chest_x_ray_images_labels_160K_01.02.19.csv.gz (or .csv). One row is one image (D-03).
  • IDs: patient_id is PatientID, for example 839860488694292331637988235681460987. study_id is StudyID, for example 20536686640136348236148679891455886468 (D-01). image_path is <ImageDir>/<ImageID>, for example 0/20536686640136348236148679891455886468_k6ga29.png. It is relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Labels (193 columns, D-05): Labels holds a Python list as text, for example ['cardiomegaly', 'pleural effusion']. A label in the list gives 1, and all other labels give 0. The harmonizer removes a space at the start of a label, so ' pneumonia' and 'pneumonia' give one column. A row with the value [''] gets NaN in all 193 labels, not 0. The probes skip NaN.
  • Uncertain: PadChest has no -1. Two labels mark bad images: exclude and suboptimal_study. With drop_uncertain=True (the default), the harmonizer drops the rows with either label.
  • View (D-01): from Projection. L gives LATERAL, and AP_horizontal gives AP_HORIZONTAL. EXCLUDE and UNK give NaN. COSTAL stays.
  • Age and sex: the source has no age. age_years comes from the year of StudyDate_DICOM minus PatientBirth, in years (D-06). sex is M, F or NaN, from PatientSex_DICOM. The value O gives NaN (D-26).
  • Report: report is the Report column. With output_report=True, the dataset drops the rows with no report, and warns (D-33).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer always drops the 103 rows with a blank Labels value. It also drops a row whose Labels value is not a valid Python list.

print(df.columns.tolist())
# ['patient_id', 'study_id', 'image_path', 'view_position', 'report', 'age_years', 'sex',
#  'abnormal_foreign_body', ..., 'volume_loss']

harmonize(drop_uncertain=False) keeps the rows with exclude or suboptimal_study.

Argument Type Required Default Description csv_path str Yes The label CSV (.csv.gz or .csv) base_image_dir str No None The images/ folder

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Empty label lists: 777 rows have the Labels value ['']. Their reports name findings such as scoliosis, so an empty list does not mean normal (D-05).
  • Shared study ID: 1 StudyID belongs to 2 patients. The harmonizer warns. Group by patient_id and study_id together (D-01).
  • Age: the source has only the birth year, not the birth date. So an age can be 1 year too high. 6 rows have no birth year (D-06).
  • No report: 17 images of the default harmonized table have a blank Report (D-33).
  • Image folders: the folders 51/, 52/ and 53/ do not exist, and folder 50/ holds 1 image. This is the layout of the source, not a download error.

docs.title: ReXGradient-160K
docs.text:
Registry keys rexgradient_train, rexgradient_valid, rexgradient_test Task and outputs The report text (report). Classification, 14 labels (cls), only with labels_csv_path Images in the table train 238,968 (95,716 patients), valid 17,007 (6,964 patients), test 17,029 (6,807 patients) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, PNG License ReXGradient-160K Non-Commercial Data Access and Use Agreement Download Get the data: ReXGradient-160K

ReXGradient-160K is a chest X-ray dataset from 79 sites in the U.S. The Rajpurkar Lab released it on Hugging Face. It has 273,004 images of 160,000 studies and 109,487 patients. Each study has a report in 4 sections: Indication, Comparison, Findings and Impression. The source has no labels.

The PNG width and height are 25% of the original. The ReXrank benchmark keeps a private test set, and this page does not cover it. The source also has interstitial_pattern_bbox.json, with boxes on 398 images. The harmonizer does not read it.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the deid_png/ folder. The class finds the JSON file of its split in this folder, or in download/metadata/ of the folder above it (D-35).

ReXGradient-160K/

    train_metadata_view_position.json
    valid_metadata_view_position.json
    test_metadata_view_position.json

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import ReXGradientTrainDataset, ReXGradientTestDataset

train = ReXGradientTrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/ReXGradient-160K/deid_png/",
    output_report=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["report"]: 'INDICATION:\n...\n\nCOMPARISON:\n...\n\nFINDINGS:\n...\n\nIMPRESSION:\n...'

test_ds = ReXGradientTestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/ReXGradient-160K/deid_png/",
    output_report=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: <split>_metadata_view_position.json. One JSON entry is one study, with a list of its images in ImagePath. One row is one image (D-03). The plain <split>_metadata.csv has no image paths, so a .csv path raises ValueError.
  • IDs: patient_id is PatientID, for example GRDNRZ6LE5QCTQ5A. study_id is StudyInstanceUid, for example 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498.96466585901041020901411755035473531374. AccessionNumber goes in the extra column accession_number (D-01).
  • image_path: ImagePath with the ../deid_png/ at the start removed. It is relative to base_image_dir (D-04). Example: GRDNRZ6LE5QCTQ5A/GRDNZ9W6GFJMI7SO/studies/1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498.96466585901041020901411755035473531374/series/1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498.59425159848405213029298826561879810186/instances/1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498.51759003029321912113312962240139898600.png.
  • Report: the 4 sections in one text. Each section starts with its name, for example FINDINGS:. All images of one study get the same report. See Reports.
  • Labels (D-05): with labels_csv_path, the harmonizer joins 14 CheXpert labels on accession_number. Present gives 1, Absent gives 0, and any other value gives NaN. Without it, the harmonized table has no labels.
  • View (D-01): from ImageViewPosition, one value for each image. LL, RL and LAT give LATERAL, POSTERO_ANTERIOR gives PA, and ANTERO_POSTERIOR gives AP. UNKNOWN, N/A, null and the text None give NaN. Other values, such as LAO, stay as in the source.
  • Age and sex: age_years comes from PatientAge, in years (D-06). PatientAge is a DICOM age text such as 029Y or 002D. sex is M, F or NaN, from PatientSex. The value O gives NaN (D-26).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops a study with no ImagePath. The source has no such study.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The source has no labels. labels_csv_path adds 14 CheXpert labels that the model GPT-OSS-120B gave from the reports. This label CSV is not part of the source, and the code and configs name no download for it. Without it, output_cls=True warns and adds no cls key (D-11).

The 14 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Meaning atelectasis Part of a lung is collapsed cardiomegaly The heart is large consolidation Airspace consolidation edema Pulmonary edema enlarged_cardiomediastinum The mediastinum is wide fracture A rib or other bone fracture lung_lesion A lung lesion lung_opacity A lung opacity no_finding No finding. The label CSV gives Abnormal_response (is the study abnormal?). So the harmonizer flips it: Absent gives 1, and Present gives 0 pleural_effusion Pleural effusion pleural_other Another pleural finding pneumonia Pneumonia pneumothorax Pneumothorax support_devices A tube, line or other device

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
report holds the 4 sections in this order. Each section starts with its name in capital letters:

INDICATION:
Adm

COMPARISON:
Comparison exams: 2/20/2013

FINDINGS:
The lungs are poorly expanded with volume loss at both lung bases. ...

IMPRESSION:
...
  • The harmonizer leaves out a section that is empty, NaN or the text None.
  • A study with all 4 sections empty gets report None. With output_report=True, the dataset drops such rows and warns (D-33).

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• View: many images have the view UNKNOWN, N/A or no view. The train JSON also has values that are not views, such as PICC LINE, ERECT and KUB (D-01).
  • Age: some studies have no PatientAge. The age unit can be days, weeks, months or years (D-06).

docs.title: TAIX-Ray
docs.text:
Registry keys taix_ray_512_train, taix_ray_512_val, taix_ray_512_test, taix_ray_train, taix_ray_val, taix_ray_test Task and outputs Classification, 8 labels (cls), binary or ordinal Images in the table train 137,593 (30,543 patients), val 34,860 (7,636 patients), test 42,928 (9,545 patients) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, 16-bit PNG. One source with 512 pixels on the long side, and one at the original size License CC BY 4.0 Download Get the data: TAIX-Ray

TAIX-Ray is a bedside chest X-ray dataset from the intensive care units of University Hospital RWTH Aachen, Germany. It has 215,381 images of 47,724 patients. During routine work, radiologists graded 8 findings in a structured report. The 512-pixel and the original source have the same annotation.csv content, so the counts above are the same for both. Paper: Truhn et al., Scientific Data 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41597-026-07271-7.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the images/ folder. The class finds annotation.csv in that folder or in the folder above it. The Hugging Face source has parquet files. The notebook notebooks/downloads/download_huggingface.ipynb writes the PNG files and annotation.csv from them.

TAIX-Ray/
  data_512/
    annotation.csv
    images/<UID>.png
  data_original/
    annotation.csv
    images/<UID>.png

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import TAIXRay512TestDataset, TAIXRay512TrainDataset, TAIXRay512ValDataset

kw = dict(
    base_image_dir="/data/TAIX-Ray/data_512/images/",
    label_mode="binary",
    output_cls=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds = TAIXRay512TrainDataset(**kw).get_datasets()
val_ds = TAIXRay512ValDataset(**kw).get_datasets()
test_ds = TAIXRay512TestDataset(**kw).get_datasets()
sample = val_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(8,)

For the original-size images, use TAIXRayTrainDataset, TAIXRayValDataset and TAIXRayTestDataset with data_original/images/.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: annotation.csv. One row is one image (D-03).
  • IDs: patient_id is PatientID. Each UID has one image, so study_id is the UID. image_path is <UID>.png, relative to images/ (D-04). Example: the UID b6c2215aac6e552fa54e483b8e2a66c1d6ef3b481c75125e345ad6c27807bf4f gives the image_path b6c2215aac6e552fa54e483b8e2a66c1d6ef3b481c75125e345ad6c27807bf4f.png. PatientID is also a 64-character code, for example fe59e9dd10af944bac7a83ccfcc1491f40216c5f1c5cf2c6b3eb8d5b5c9c9a56.
  • Labels (D-05): the harmonizer keeps the raw grades, as float32. The dataset class applies label_mode. In "binary" mode, grade 1 or more gives 1, and grade 0 gives 0. "ordinal" keeps the grade.
  • Uncertain and blank labels: the source has no -1 and no blank label. Grade 1 means "Questionable" (or "Borderline Enlarged" for heart_size). In binary mode, grade 1 gives 1.
  • View (D-01): the source has no view column, so the harmonized table has no view_position. All images are bedside AP (Truhn et al. 2026).
  • Age and sex: age_years comes from Age, in days, divided by 365.25 (D-06). sex is M or F, from Sex (D-26).
  • Extra columns: age is the raw Age in days. study_date is the StudyDate (for example 2012-06-25). fold is the source Fold (0 on every row). split is train, val or test. physician_id is the source PhysicianID, a 64-character code. The source does not document it.
  • Dropped rows: none. A split class keeps only the rows of its own Split value (D-09).

docs.text:
The 8 label columns, in the order of cls:

Column Source column Meaning Grades atelectasis_left Atelectasis_Left Atelectasis in the left lung 0 to 4 atelectasis_right Atelectasis_Right Atelectasis in the right lung 0 to 4 heart_size HeartSize The heart is large 0 to 3 pleural_effusion_left PleuralEffusion_Left Left pleural effusion 0 to 4 pleural_effusion_right PleuralEffusion_Right Right pleural effusion 0 to 4 pulmonary_congestion PulmonaryCongestion Pulmonary congestion 0 to 4 pulmonary_opacities_left PulmonaryOpacities_Left Opacities in the left lung 0 to 4 pulmonary_opacities_right PulmonaryOpacities_Right Opacities in the right lung 0 to 4

The grades of heart_size are 0 Normal, 1 Borderline Enlarged, 2 Enlarged and 3 Massively Enlarged. The grades of the other labels are 0 None, 1 Questionable, 2 Mild, 3 Moderate and 4 Severe.
