docs.title: CheXinstruct VQA
docs.text:
Registry keys chexinstruct_vqa_train, chexinstruct_vqa_val, chexinstruct_vqa_test Task and outputs Visual question answering: the question (question) and the answer (answer). question_type with output_question_type=True, and answer_struct with output_struct=True Images in the table train 174,218 images (580,166 questions), val 9,460 images (99,996 questions), test 2,659 images (21,296 questions) Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, JPEG from MIMIC-CXR-JPG License PhysioNet credentialed access (CITI training and a signed data use agreement) for MIMIC-CXR-JPG, MIMIC-CXR-VQA and MIMIC-Diff-VQA. The CheXagent processor code is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 Download Get the data: other datasets, and the compile step in Quick use. The images come from MIMIC-CXR-JPG

CheXinstruct is an instruction-tuning collection from about 28 public chest X-ray datasets (Chen et al., arXiv 2024). For each source, the "processor" code of Stanford-AIMI/CheXagent makes records in one common format. This page covers 2 VQA sources only: MIMIC-CXR-VQA (open-ended and close-ended questions) and MIMIC-Diff-VQA (Difference VQA, named Medical-Diff-VQA on PhysioNet). All their images are MIMIC-CXR-JPG images. The compiled JSON has 701,458 questions.

The other VQA sources of CheXinstruct (VQA-RAD, SLAKE, MedVQA-2019, PMC-VQA and Rad-Restruct) need other image folders, so the class does not read them. VQA-RAD has its own page: VQA-RAD.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
The class reads chexinstruct_vqa.json. You make this file once, from 3 downloads:

  1. The images: MIMIC-CXR-JPG.
  2. The MIMIC-CXR-VQA questions: PhysioNet: MIMIC-Ext-MIMIC-CXR-VQA.
  3. The MIMIC-Diff-VQA questions: PhysioNet: Medical-Diff-VQA.

Then copy 5 files of CheXagent (commit e4f31e6, folder data_chexinstruct/dataset_processors/) to vendor/dataset_processors/, with no change: base_processor.py, templates.py, utils.py, mimic_cxr_vqa.py and mimic_diff_vqa.py. Do not copy its __init__.py. It imports all 28 processors, so the import fails when only these 5 files are there. The CheXagent license allows no changed copies, so RadHarmony does not include these files.

Put the 3 downloads in data/, and make the link vendor/data -> ../data (see the folder tree below). Then make the JSON file:

python scripts/compile_chexinstruct_vqa.py --vendor-dir /data/CheXinstruct/vendor

The script runs the processors in vendor/ and writes compiled/chexinstruct_vqa.json next to vendor/. --out gives another path.

CheXinstruct/
  vendor/
    data -> ../data        # a link: the processors read data/... from vendor/
    dataset_processors/    # the CheXagent files, with no change
  data/
    mimic-cxr/             # the MIMIC-CXR-JPG folder (files/ and the CSV files), or a link to it
    mimic-cxr-vqa/mimiccxrvqa/dataset/train.json, valid.json, test.json
    mimic-diff-vqa/mimic_all.csv, code/temp/mimic_pair_questions_temp.csv
  compiled/chexinstruct_vqa.json

base_image_dir is the files/ folder of MIMIC-CXR-JPG. Pass json_path. Without it, the class looks for the JSON file only in base_image_dir and in the folder above it. It raises FileNotFoundError when the file is not there (D-35).

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import (
    ChexInstructVQATestDataset,
    ChexInstructVQATrainDataset,
    ChexInstructVQAValDataset,
)

kw = dict(
    base_image_dir="/data/mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/files/",
    json_path="/data/CheXinstruct/compiled/chexinstruct_vqa.json",
    output_struct=True,
    output_question_type=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds = ChexInstructVQATrainDataset(**kw).get_datasets()
val_ds = ChexInstructVQAValDataset(**kw).get_datasets()
test_ds = ChexInstructVQATestDataset(**kw).get_datasets()
sample = test_ds[0]
# sample keys: img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id, question_id, answer_struct, question_type
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["question"]: 'Is any technical assessments present within the mediastinum?'
# sample["answer"]: 'Yes'

To batch answer_struct, pass collate_fn=bbox_collate (from radharmony.dataset import bbox_collate) to the DataLoader. answer_struct is a dict for a close-ended question and NaN for the others, so the default DataLoader collate fails.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: the compiled chexinstruct_vqa.json, a list of records. One record is one question. One row of the harmonized table is one question, not one image (D-03). A split class keeps the records with its split value.
  • IDs: the record study_id [mimic-cxr] [56535659] gives study_id 56535659. The records have no patient ID, so patient_id comes from the p<subject_id> folder of the image path, for example 10449873. question_id is unique_id, for example [Open-Ended VQA] [MIMIC-CXR-VQA] [0].
  • image_path: the source path with the data/mimic-cxr/files/ at the start removed, for example p10/p10449873/s56535659/0942432e-6d4664df-1389611d-a70f5cbc-8734b936.jpg. It is relative to base_image_dir (D-04). A MIMIC-Diff-VQA record has a list of 1 path, and the harmonizer takes that path.
  • Text: question comes from text and answer from target_text, with the spaces at the ends removed. question_type comes from task_name, and answer_struct from options. See Questions and answers.
  • Extra columns: data_source, which is MIMIC-CXR-VQA or MIMIC-Diff-VQA.
  • View, age and sex: the source has none of them, so the harmonized table has no view_position, age_years or sex (D-01).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row of its split. question_types and data_sources keep only the types and sources that you name.

docs.title: Questions and answers
docs.text:
The text columns of the harmonized table:

Column Meaning Source question The question text text answer The answer text. It is empty for a close-ended question target_text answer_struct {"yes": bool, "no": bool} for a close-ended question, NaN for the others options question_type Open-Ended VQA, Close-Ended VQA or Difference VQA task_name data_source MIMIC-CXR-VQA or MIMIC-Diff-VQA data_source split train, val or test split, which compile_chexinstruct_vqa.py adds

Answer types:

  • Open-Ended VQA (MIMIC-CXR-VQA): a text answer, for example Mediastinum, Yes or No. An answer with several items is one text with commas, for example Left lung, right lung.
  • Close-Ended VQA (MIMIC-CXR-VQA): the same yes or no questions as the Open-Ended VQA type. answer is empty, and answer_struct holds the answer. So each yes or no question is 2 times in the harmonized table, once for each type.
  • Difference VQA (MIMIC-Diff-VQA): the CheXagent processor keeps only the location, level and type questions of MIMIC-Diff-VQA. Each question is about 1 image, not about a change between 2 studies.

Example rows of chexinstruct_vqa_test (one image):

question answer answer_struct question_type Is any technical assessments present within the mediastinum? Yes NaN Open-Ended VQA Is any technical assessments present within the mediastinum? (empty) {"yes": True, "no": False} Close-Ended VQA

A Difference VQA row: "Where in the image is the pleural effusion located?" with the answer Left upper lung area.

The sample holds img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id and question_id. With output_question_type=True, it also holds question_type. With output_struct=True, it also holds answer_struct. img is (1, 224, 224): chest X-rays are gray, so the class keeps the default IMG_CHANNELS = 1 (D-42).

docs.title: Splits
docs.text:
Class Registry key Images Source ChexInstructVQATrainDataset chexinstruct_vqa_train 174,218 images (580,166 questions) The records with split train ChexInstructVQAValDataset chexinstruct_vqa_val 9,460 images (99,996 questions) The records with split val ChexInstructVQATestDataset chexinstruct_vqa_test 2,659 images (21,296 questions) The records with split test. Use it as the test split ChexInstructVQADataset chexinstruct_vqa All questions. It mixes the 3 splits, so do not use it for a benchmark (D-09)

The train split has 51,530 patients, the val split 3,585 and the test split 734. The splits share 2,007 patients (D-34). 497 of the 734 test patients are also in train.

The 2 sources made their splits on their own. The MIMIC-CXR-VQA split alone puts 663 patients in 2 splits. The MIMIC-Diff-VQA split follows the official MIMIC-CXR split, and alone it shares no patient. For a test with no shared patient, use data_sources=["MIMIC-Diff-VQA"], or remove the shared patients in your own code.

get_datasets(n_splits=5) makes a train and val split from the train class. It groups by patient (D-10).

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• unique_id is unique only in one split. The source starts the count again in each split. So in chexinstruct_vqa (the 3 splits together), a question_id can repeat.
  • The MIMIC-CXR-VQA processor shuffles the train questions before it gives unique_id, and the processors set no seed. So compile_chexinstruct_vqa.py seeds random (--seed, default 0). 2 runs with the same seed give the same file. A file from a run with no seed has other question_id values for the MIMIC-CXR-VQA train rows, in another order. All other ids, and the questions, answers and splits, are the same.

docs.title: GEMeX-VQA
docs.text:
Registry keys gemex_vqa Task and outputs Visual question answering: the question (question) and the answer (answer). question_type with output_question_type=True, and answer_struct with output_struct=True Images in the table 11 images (80 questions). These are the subset files on Hugging Face Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, JPEG from MIMIC-CXR-JPG License The Hugging Face repo states no license. The images need PhysioNet credentialed access, as for MIMIC-CXR-JPG Download Get the data: other datasets. The images come from MIMIC-CXR-JPG

GEMeX is a chest X-ray visual question answering benchmark (Liu et al., arXiv 2024). Each question has an answer, a reason, the report of the study, and the names and boxes of the image regions that the answer uses. The paper has 1,605,575 questions on 151,025 images. The Hugging Face repo BoKelvin/GEMeX-VQA has only a small subset: 4 JSONL files of 20 questions each, one file for each question subtype.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
GEMeX has no images of its own. data_dir is the folder of the 4 JSONL files. base_image_dir is the files/ folder of MIMIC-CXR-JPG 2.0.0.

gemex-vqa/                                 <- data_dir
  open_ended_question.jsonl
  closed_ended_question.jsonl
  single_choice_question.jsonl
  multi_choice_question.jsonl
mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/files/                 <- base_image_dir
  p10/p10046166/s50051329/abea5eb9-b7c32823-3a14c5ca-77868030-69c83139.jpg

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import GEMeXVQADataset

gemex = GEMeXVQADataset(
    data_dir="/data/gemex-vqa/",
    base_image_dir="/data/mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/files/",
    output_question_type=True,
    output_struct=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
ds = gemex.get_datasets()  # all 80 questions. get_datasets(n_splits=5) makes train and val
sample = ds[0]
# sample keys: img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id, question_id, answer_struct, question_type
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["question"]: 'What condition is indicated by the low lung volume in this CXR?'
# sample["answer"]: 'Restrictive lung disease.'

To batch answer_struct, pass collate_fn=bbox_collate (from radharmony.dataset import bbox_collate) to the DataLoader. The answer_struct dicts hold None and lists of different lengths, so the default DataLoader collate fails.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: the 4 JSONL files. One record is one question. One row of the harmonized table is one question, not one image (D-03). question_subtypes picks the files to read.
  • IDs: the image_path p10/p10046166/s50051329/abea5eb9-b7c32823-3a14c5ca-77868030-69c83139.jpg gives patient_id 10046166 and study_id 50051329, the MIMIC IDs as digits. image_path stays as in the source, relative to base_image_dir (D-04). question_id is the question subtype and q_id, for example single_choice_0, because each file starts q_id at 0.
  • Answer: the harmonizer joins the list answer of a multi-choice question with commas. ["A", "B", "D"] gives "A,B,D". The other answers stay as in the source.
  • Question type: question_type comes from type. question_subtype is the question subtype of the file.
  • Extra columns: reason, ori_report, visual_regions, visual_locations and choices, as in the source. answer_struct holds the same 5 values in one dict.
  • View, age and sex: the source has none of them, so the harmonized table has no view_position, age_years or sex (D-01).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row.

docs.title: Questions and answers
docs.text:
The text columns of the harmonized table:

Column Meaning Source question The question text question answer The answer: text, Yes. or No., a letter, or letters joined with commas answer question_type abnormality, disease, location, severity, finding or size type question_subtype open_ended, closed_ended, single_choice or multi_choice The file name reason Why the answer is right reason ori_report The report of the study ori_report visual_regions The names of the image regions that the answer uses, for example ['right hemidiaphragm'] visual_regions visual_locations One box for each region. See Boxes visual_locations choices The options of a choice question, for example A: Left lung. None for the open and closed questions choices answer_struct A dict of reason, visual_regions, visual_locations, ori_report and choices The same keys

Answer types: each file has 20 questions.

question_subtype Answer Example open_ended Free text Restrictive lung disease. closed_ended Yes. or No. (7 and 13 questions) No. single_choice One letter of choices C multi_choice Letters of choices, joined with commas A,B,D

Example row of gemex_vqa:

question_id question answer question_type choices single_choice_0 What is the size of the calcified granuloma observed? C size ['A: 0.5 cm', 'B: 1.0 cm', 'C: 1.2 cm', 'D: 1.5 cm']

The sample holds img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id and question_id. With output_question_type=True, it also holds question_type. With output_struct=True, it also holds answer_struct. img is a tensor (1, 224, 224): chest X-rays are gray, so the class keeps the default IMG_CHANNELS = 1 (D-42).

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
• Source: visual_locations holds one box of 4 whole numbers for each name in visual_regions, in the same order. The 80 questions have 104 boxes, and each question has 1 to 3.
  • Format: the values are [x1, y1, x2, y2] in a 224 x 224 (H x W) image, not in the MIMIC-CXR-JPG image. They are not [x, y, w, h], because x + w would be up to 304. Most boxes (81 of 104) are the region boxes of Chest ImaGenome silver, minus 1 on each value. Example: abea5eb9-... has the right hemidiaphragm box [43, 126, 129, 150], and its Chest ImaGenome scene graph gives [44, 127, 130, 151]. cardiac region matches cardiac silhouette. A region of both sides, for example bilateral lung, has the box around the boxes of the 2 sides. The other 23 boxes differ more. Example: a spine box is [93, 19, 135, 205], and Chest ImaGenome gives [94, 0, 136, 223].
  • The harmonizer copies the boxes with no change to visual_locations and answer_struct. It does not make D-07 boxes, so the harmonized table has no bbox or bbox_labels.
  • Readers (D-36): the source has one box for each region, so the harmonizer does not group boxes.
  • The sample: it has no bbox key. With output_struct=True, answer_struct["visual_locations"] holds the source boxes, for example [[43, 35, 212, 156]] for bilateral lung. The transform does not move these boxes with the image, so D-28 does not apply.
  • Dropped boxes: the harmonizer does not clip or drop a box. All source boxes are inside the 224 x 224 (H x W) image.

docs.title: MedPMC
docs.text:
Registry keys medpmc Task and outputs Image captioning: the caption (answer). question is empty Images in the table 11,123,087 images, with no filter. One image has one caption Modality Medical figures from PubMed Central articles: radiology, pathology, microscopy, clinical photos and more. 2-D, JPEG License CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (the Hugging Face card). Each record also has its own source and license metadata Download Get the data: other datasets

MedPMC (Kim et al., arXiv 2026) pairs medical figures from PubMed Central articles with their captions. It has 3 subsets. multipanel has whole figures with many panels, and singlepanel has figures with one panel. subfigure has the panels cut out of the multipanel figures, with their own captions. The class gives the caption as answer, not as report. ReportGenerationEvaluator reads report, so it cannot score this class.

RadHarmony makes its own tag tables of specialty and modality, so you can filter, for example, to radiology X-ray images. These tags are not labels of the MedPMC authors.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
The source is a Hugging Face snapshot of Yale-BIDS-Chen/medpmc-11m-dataset_jun24_baseline. The images stay in webdataset tar files. Before you use the class:

  1. Build the caption tag table with scripts/build_medpmc_tags.py --base-dir /data/MedPMC/. It reads the caption of each image from the tar files. The answer of the class comes from this table.
  2. For the CLIP filters (modalities, require_tagger_agreement, min_clip_prob), run scripts/build_medpmc_tags_clip.py --subsets singlepanel subfigure. It writes parts to tags/_clip_parts/. Then run scripts/merge_clip_tags.py --base-dir /data/MedPMC/ to make the CLIP tag table.
  3. Extract the images of your subset with scripts/materialize_medpmc_subset.py. Do not extract all images to a network drive. Example: --base-dir /data/MedPMC/ --high-precision-radiology --modalities xray.
MedPMC/
  webdataset/
    metadata/medpmc_index.parquet       # one row for each image
    multipanel/train-000000.tar ...
    singlepanel/train-000000.tar ...
    subfigure/train-000000.tar ...
  tags/medpmc_tags.parquet              # made by scripts/build_medpmc_tags.py
  tags/medpmc_tags_clip.parquet         # made by scripts/merge_clip_tags.py
  images/singlepanel/singlepanel_000000000038.jpg   # made by scripts/materialize_medpmc_subset.py

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MedPMCDataset

ds = MedPMCDataset(
    base_dir="/data/MedPMC/",
    subsets=["singlepanel", "subfigure"],
    radiology_only=True,
    modalities=["xray"],
    require_tagger_agreement=True,
    min_clip_prob=0.9,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
ds.verify_images()  # drop the rows with no extracted image file
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the articles go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample keys: img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id, question_id
# sample["img"]: Tensor(3, 224, 224)
# sample["answer"]: 'Abdomen X-ray of the patient, showed a large urinary calculus in the bladder.'

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: webdataset/metadata/medpmc_index.parquet, with the caption tag table joined on image_id. One row of the harmonized table is one image and its caption (D-03). subsets keeps only those subsets.
  • IDs: the source has no patient ID. patient_id is the article (pmcid), because the figures of one article are not independent. study_id is the figure: parent_image_id for a subfigure, and image_id for the other subsets. question_id is image_id. Example: patient_id PMC4770620, study_id PMC4770620_EUS-5-35-g002 and question_id PMC4770620_EUS-5-35-g002_2.
  • image_path: <source_type>/<key><image_ext>, for example subfigure/subfigure_000000000085.jpg. It is relative to base_image_dir, which is <base_dir>/images by default (D-04).
  • Caption: answer is caption of the caption tag table. With no tag table, answer is None in every row, and the harmonizer warns. question is "".
  • Tags: the caption tag table gives specialty, modality, tag_confidence, tag_source and tag_method. The CLIP tag table gives clip_specialty, clip_modality and clip_prob, only when a CLIP filter (modalities, require_tagger_agreement or min_clip_prob) needs it.
  • View, age and sex: the source has none of them, so the harmonized table has no view_position, age_years or sex (D-01).
  • Dropped rows: by default, the harmonizer drops no row. The filter arguments drop rows (see Arguments). With no caption tag table, radiology_only, specialties, modalities, min_tag_confidence, drop_untagged and require_tagger_agreement raise FileNotFoundError. A CLIP filter with no CLIP tag table also raises FileNotFoundError.

docs.title: Captions
docs.text:
The text columns of the harmonized table:

Column Meaning Source question Always "", because this is a captioning set None answer The caption of the image. A subfigure has its own short caption The caption tag table source_type multipanel, singlepanel or subfigure The index pmcid The PubMed Central article The index image_id, parent_image_id The image, and the multipanel figure of a subfigure The index subfigure_index, figure_label The panel number of a subfigure, and the figure name in the article (for example Fig. 1) The index shard, key The tar file and the name of the image in it The index specialty One of 10 values, for example radiology, pathology or unknown The caption tag table modality The radiology modality: ct, mri, fmri, xray, ultrasound, pet_spect, angiography, mammography or radiology_other The caption tag table tag_confidence high (a specific term matched), low (a general term, or a tag from the parent caption) or None The caption tag table tag_source own (the caption of the image) or parent (the caption of the whole figure). None with no tag The caption tag table tag_method The method that made the tag, for example caption-lexicon-v2 The caption tag table clip_specialty, clip_modality, clip_prob The tag of a zero-shot MedPMC-CLIP model on the pixels, and its probability. Only with a CLIP filter The CLIP tag table

The caption tag table uses word lists on the caption (radharmony/harmonizer/medpmc/tagging.py). The CLIP tag table has rows only for singlepanel and subfigure. On 2026-08-22, a clinician checked 151 images where the 2 taggers disagreed (the docstring of MedPMCHarmonizer). CLIP was right for 72.8% of them, and the caption word lists for 10.6%. So modalities uses the CLIP modality, and the caption modality where CLIP has none.

Example row of medpmc, with radiology_only=True and modalities=["xray"]:

Column Value question_id PMC10009441_gr1 answer Abdomen X-ray of the patient, showed a large urinary calculus in the bladder. source_type singlepanel specialty, modality radiology, xray tag_confidence, tag_source high, own clip_modality, clip_prob xray, 0.964

The sample holds img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id and question_id. img is (3, 224, 224): many figures are in color, so the class sets IMG_CHANNELS = 3 (D-42). A gray file gives 3 equal channels. An answer of None gives "" in the sample. The tag columns are only in the harmonized table, not in the sample.

docs.title: Splits
docs.text:
Class Registry key Images Source MedPMCDataset medpmc 11,123,087 webdataset/metadata/medpmc_index.parquet, all 3 subsets, with no filter

With no filter, the 11,123,087 images come from 3,799,545 figures (study_id) and 1,274,778 articles (patient_id).

MedPMC has no official split. get_datasets(n_splits=5) makes a train and val split. It groups by patient (D-10). Here the patient is the article, so all figures of one article go to one split. For example, a subfigure and its multipanel figure stay in one split.

Every multipanel row goes, because the CLIP tag table has no multipanel row. Without the caption tag table, harmonize() raises FileNotFoundError min_clip_prob float No None Keep only the rows with clip_prob at this value or more modality_source str No "clip" The tagger of modalities. "clip" takes the CLIP modality, and the caption modality where CLIP has none. "caption" takes the caption modality. "either" keeps a row when one of the 2 matches. Another value raises ValueError clip_tags_path str No None The CLIP tag table. None gives <base_dir>/tags/medpmc_tags_clip.parquet include_multipanel bool No True With False, a specialty filter drops the multipanel rows, because their tag comes from the caption of the whole figure. Without a specialty filter, it does nothing tags_path str No None The caption tag table. None gives <base_dir>/tags/medpmc_tags.parquet

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• No specialty or modality: the source has no such field. The paper gives the specialty shares from a check by hand of a sample of images, not a label for each image.
  • Benchmark images: PubMed Central figures include images of MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert, VinDr and other benchmark datasets. If you train on MedPMC and test on these benchmarks, remove these images from the training data first.
  • Same pixels twice: each subfigure is also a panel of its multipanel figure. To count each figure once, count the unique study_id values, or leave out the multipanel subset.

docs.title: MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA
docs.text:
Registry keys mimic_ext_cxr_qba_train, mimic_ext_cxr_qba_validate, mimic_ext_cxr_qba_test Task and outputs Visual question answering: the question (question) and the answer (answer). question_type with output_question_type=True, and answer_struct with output_struct=True Images in the table validate 1,641 images (7,620 questions), test 2,850 images (12,569 questions). The counts are for the A_frontal/metadata/q1M export Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, JPEG from MIMIC-CXR-JPG with image_ext=".jpg", or DICOM from MIMIC-CXR with the default image_ext=".dcm" License PhysioNet credentialed access (CITI training and a signed data use agreement), for the questions and for the MIMIC-CXR images. The license is the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0 Download Get the data: other datasets. The images come from MIMIC-CXR or MIMIC-CXR-JPG

MIMIC-Ext-CXR-QBA is a visual question answering dataset on the studies of MIMIC-CXR (PhysioNet). The questions come from templates. The answers come from the report sentences and the scene graph of each study. Each answer has tags and boxes on the image. The source has parquet files that list the questions, and qa.zip, with one qa.json file of text for each study.

The export folders of the source hold subsets of the questions with a given quality. RadHarmony reads one export folder at a time. The RadHarmony tests use exports/A_frontal/metadata/q1M: a random set of 1 million questions with the quality A, A+ or A++, on frontal images only.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
metadata_dir is an export folder with the parquet files. qa_zip_path is qa.zip. base_image_dir is the files/ folder of the images. The default image_ext=".dcm" reads the DICOM files of MIMIC-CXR. With image_ext=".jpg", use the files/ folder of MIMIC-CXR-JPG 2.0.0.

mimic-ext-cxr-qba/
  qa.zip                                   <- qa_zip_path
  exports/A_frontal/metadata/q1M/          <- metadata_dir
    question_metadata.parquet
    question_image_metadata.parquet
    image_metadata.parquet
    patient_metadata.parquet
mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/files/                 <- base_image_dir
  p17/p17838301/s50037760/0788829b-5419d8e4-5ce8eb81-87a77c03-98c15a1a.jpg

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import MIMICExtCXRQBATestDataset, MIMICExtCXRQBATrainDataset

kw = dict(
    base_image_dir="/data/mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/files/",
    metadata_dir="/data/mimic-ext-cxr-qba/exports/A_frontal/metadata/q1M/",
    qa_zip_path="/data/mimic-ext-cxr-qba/qa.zip",
    image_ext=".jpg",
    output_question_type=True,
    output_struct=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
test_ds = MIMICExtCXRQBATestDataset(**kw).get_datasets()
sample = test_ds[0]
# sample keys: img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id, question_id, answer_struct, question_type
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["question"]: 'Describe the lung opacity.'
# sample["answer"]: 'There is linear opacification in the left mid lung.'

# The full train split reads about 200,000 studies in qa.zip and is slow. Try max_studies first.
train = MIMICExtCXRQBATrainDataset(**kw, max_studies=1000)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val

To batch answer_struct, pass collate_fn=bbox_collate (from radharmony.dataset import bbox_collate) to the DataLoader. The lists of answer dicts have different lengths, so the default collate fails.

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: question_metadata.parquet lists the questions, one row for each question. One row of the harmonized table is one question, not one image (D-03). qa.zip holds the text.
  • One image for each question: question_image_metadata.parquet can list more than 1 image for one question. The harmonizer keeps the first image_id in sort order. In the q1M export, each study then has one image.
  • IDs: p17838301 gives patient_id 17838301 and s50037760 gives study_id 50037760, the MIMIC IDs as digits. image_path is p17/p17838301/s50037760/0788829b-5419d8e4-5ce8eb81-87a77c03-98c15a1a.dcm, relative to base_image_dir (D-04). image_ext sets the extension. question_id is the study and the source question_id, for example 50037760_D01_describe_finding_015, because the source ID is a template name that repeats in each study.
  • Text: question comes from the qa.json file of the study. answer joins the texts of the main_answer dicts with a space (D-51). The details and related_information texts stay only in answer_struct. Without qa_zip_path, question and answer are empty and answer_struct is None.
  • Split: split is the split of the patient in patient_metadata.parquet. A split class first keeps the patients of its split. Then it applies max_studies and reads qa.zip.
  • View: view_position is img.view_position of the question's image in image_metadata.parquet, with the shared names of D-01. The A_frontal exports have frontal images only, so it is AP or PA. Use it to keep only PA images, for example df[df["view_position"] == "PA"]. It is in the table, not in the sample. A question with several images gets the view of its kept image. With no image_metadata.parquet, the harmonizer warns and the table has no view_position.
  • Age and sex: the harmonized table has no age_years or sex (D-01). The source has no age and no sex.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops a question with no image in question_image_metadata.parquet. In q1M, every question has an image, so it drops no row. A question with no text in qa.zip keeps an empty question and answer. The validate and test splits of q1M have no such question.

docs.title: Questions and answers
docs.text:
The text columns of the harmonized table:

Column Meaning Source question The question text question in qa.json answer The main_answer texts, joined with a space (D-51) answers in qa.json answer_struct The list of the top-level answer dicts, with all their tags. answer_type of a dict is main_answer, details or related_information answers in qa.json question_type The template of the question, for example D02_has_finding question.question_type quality The quality of the question: 4_A, 5_A+ or 6_A++ question.quality.rating split train, validate or test split in patient_metadata.parquet

Answer types: the source has no closed or open flag. The template tells the kind of answer. Examples from the test split:

question_type question answer D02_has_finding Is there any indication of pneumothorax? No, there is no indication of pneumothorax. C04_is_normal_region Is the diaphragm normal? No, the diaphragm is associated with the following abnormal findings: There is obscuration of the lateral aspect of the left hemidiaphragm. D01_describe_finding Describe the lung opacity. There is linear opacification in the left mid lung.

A yes or no answer is a full sentence, so compare it as text, not as a yes or no label.

Example row of mimic_ext_cxr_qba_test:

question_id question answer question_type quality 50037760_D01_describe_finding_015 Describe the lung opacity. There is linear opacification in the left mid lung. D01_describe_finding 5_A+

The sample holds img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id and question_id. With output_question_type=True, it also holds question_type. With output_struct=True, it also holds answer_struct, the list of answer dicts. img is a tensor (1, 224, 224): chest X-rays are gray, so the class keeps the default IMG_CHANNELS = 1 (D-42).

Each answer dict has answer_type, text, regions, localization and other tags. localization is a dict with one entry for each image of the study, keyed by image_id. Each entry holds pixel boxes [x1, y1, x2, y2] on that source image in bboxes, for example [[1408.0, 1100.0, 2722.0, 1888.0]]. Use the entry of the image in image_path. The class gives no bbox key. The transform does not move these boxes with the image, so D-28 does not apply.

docs.title: Splits
docs.text:
The official split of each patient is in patient_metadata.parquet. Each split has its own class (D-09).

Class Registry key Images Source MIMICExtCXRQBATrainDataset mimic_ext_cxr_qba_train The train patients of patient_metadata.parquet MIMICExtCXRQBAValidateDataset mimic_ext_cxr_qba_validate 1,641 images (7,620 questions) The validate patients MIMICExtCXRQBATestDataset mimic_ext_cxr_qba_test 2,850 images (12,569 questions) The test patients. Use it as the test split MIMICExtCXRQBADataset mimic_ext_cxr_qba All questions. It mixes the 3 splits, so do not use it for a benchmark (D-09)

The splits share 0 patients (D-34).

The validate split has 481 patients and the test split has 287. The train split has the other questions of q1M. No test counts them, because one harmonize() of the train split takes 30 minutes.

get_datasets(n_splits=5) makes a train and val split from the train class. It groups by patient (D-10).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
The arguments are the same for the 3 split classes and MIMICExtCXRQBADataset.

Argument Type Required Default Description base_image_dir str Yes None The files/ folder of MIMIC-CXR (DICOM) or MIMIC-CXR-JPG 2.0.0. It holds the p10/ to p19/ folders. Not needed with harmonizer_path, which holds it metadata_dir str Yes None An export folder with the parquet files, for example exports/A_frontal/metadata/q1M/. Without it, the class raises ValueError. Not needed with harmonized_df, harmonizer or harmonizer_path qa_zip_path str No None qa.zip. Without it, question and answer are empty image_ext str No ".dcm" The extension in image_path: ".dcm" for MIMIC-CXR or ".jpg" for MIMIC-CXR-JPG max_studies int No None The most studies to read, for a fast run. In a split class, it counts the studies of that split. None reads all

docs.text: Argument Type Required Default Description transform MONAI transform No None The image steps. None gives the VQA steps. They load img with 1 channel (D-42), and resize and pad it to 224 x 224 (H x W). They have no SelectItemsD, so the text keys stay in the sample output_struct bool No False Add the answer_struct list to the sample. To batch it, use collate_fn=bbox_collate output_question_type bool No False Add question_type to the sample cache_dir str No "./cache" The MONAI cache folder. None gives no cache dtype torch.dtype No torch.bfloat16 The type of img. docs.title: Harmonizer
docs.text:
from radharmony.harmonizer import MIMICExtCXRQBATestHarmonizer

h = MIMICExtCXRQBATestHarmonizer(
    metadata_dir="/data/mimic-ext-cxr-qba/exports/A_frontal/metadata/q1M/",
    qa_zip_path="/data/mimic-ext-cxr-qba/qa.zip",
    base_image_dir="/data/mimic-cxr-jpg/2.0.0/files/",
    image_ext=".jpg",
)
df = h.harmonize(study_ids=["50037760"])  # only this study, so the run is fast
print(df.columns.tolist())
# ['patient_id', 'study_id', 'question_id', 'image_path', 'question', 'answer', 'answer_struct',
#  'question_type', 'quality', 'split', 'view_position']

harmonize(study_ids=..., patient_ids=...) keeps only these studies or patients, before the slow qa.zip step. An ID works with or without its s or p. It returns the same rows as a filter after harmonize() (D-02). The other split harmonizers and MIMICExtCXRQBAHarmonizer take the same arguments.

Speed: the harmonizer opens 1 file in qa.zip for each study. The test split took 25 s on 2026-11-04. Use max_studies, study_ids= or patient_ids= for a fast run.

Argument Type Required Default Description metadata_dir str Yes None An export folder with the parquet files. Without it, harmonize() raises ValueError. A split harmonizer with no patient_metadata.parquet raises FileNotFoundError qa_zip_path str No None qa.zip. Without it, question and answer are empty base_image_dir str No None The files/ folder of the images. harmonize() does not read it. verify_images() and a saved harmonizer use it image_ext str No ".dcm" The extension in image_path: ".dcm" or ".jpg" max_studies int No None The most studies to read. In a split harmonizer, it counts the studies of that split

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text: • Empty answer: some questions have an empty main_answer text, so their answer is "" (D-51). This is not a question with no text in qa.zip. In q1M, 12 train questions have an empty answer, and the validate and test splits have none.

docs.title: OpenI Indiana University CXR (IU X-Ray)
docs.text:
Registry keys openi_cxr Task and outputs Classification, 8 labels (cls). The report text (report) Images in the table 7,470 (3,851 reports). One report is one study and one patient Modality Chest X-ray, 2-D, PNG License Open access from the National Library of Medicine (NLM). Read the terms of the Open-i download page Download Get the data: OpenI IU CXR

OpenI IU X-Ray has chest X-rays and radiology reports from the Indiana University hospital network (Demner-Fushman et al., JAMIA 2016). The NLM released it on Open-i. The source has 3,955 XML reports. 104 reports have no image, so 3,851 reports with 7,470 images stay. A report has about 2 images, a frontal and a lateral. The 8 labels come from the MeSH terms of each report.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the dataset root, with ecgen-radiology/ and images/. Put the PNG files of NLMCXR_png.tgz in images/. The DICOM files of NLMCXR_dcm.tgz are optional. The harmonizer reads their ViewPosition tag to correct the view.

OpenI-IU-CXR/
  ecgen-radiology/1.xml ... 3999.xml   # the numbers have gaps
  images/CXR1_1_IM-0001-3001.png
  1/1_IM-0001-3001.dcm          # optional DICOM files, one folder for each report

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import OpenICXRDataset

ds = OpenICXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/OpenI-IU-CXR/",
    output_cls=True,
    output_report=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = ds.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the patients go to val
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample["img"]: Tensor(1, 224, 224)
# sample["cls"]: Tensor(8,)
# sample["report"]: 'The cardiac silhouette and mediastinum size are within normal limits. ...'

img has 1 channel. The PNG files are RGB, and the class makes them gray (D-42).

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: the XML reports ecgen-radiology/<n>.xml. There is no CSV. Each parentImage of a report gives one row, so one row is one image (D-03).
  • IDs: report 1.xml gives patient_id CXR1 (from uId) and study_id 1 (from pmcId). The source has no patient ID, so one report is one patient. image_path is images/<parentImage id>.png, for example images/CXR1_1_IM-0001-3001.png. It is relative to base_image_dir (D-04).
  • Extra columns: dicom_path, findings, impression, indication and mesh_major. For dicom_path, the parentImage id CXR1_1_IM-0001-3001 gives 1/1_IM-0001-3001.dcm, and CXR2_IM-0652-1001 gives 2/2_IM-0652-1001.dcm.
  • Labels (D-05): from the MeSH major terms of the report. See Labels.
  • Report: the FINDINGS and IMPRESSION text of the report. The images of one report get the same text. See Reports.
  • View (D-01): the figure number gives a first view. F1 gives FRONTAL, F2 gives LATERAL, and the others give OTHER. The DICOM tag ViewPosition corrects it. AP gives AP, and LL, RL, LAT, LATERAL or LARGE LATERAL give LATERAL. PA gives PA only on an F1 image, because many lateral images also have the tag PA. Without the DICOM files, the figure number alone gives the view, and the harmonizer warns.
  • Age and sex: the source has neither, so the harmonized table has no age_years or sex (D-01).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops a report with no parentImage (104 reports). It also skips an XML file that it cannot read. The source has no such file.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The 8 label columns, in the order of cls, with the MeSH triggers and the images with label 1:

Column Meaning MeSH triggers Images atelectasis Part of a lung is collapsed "atelectasis", "pulmonary atelectasis" 616 cardiomegaly The heart is large "cardiomegaly" 655 consolidation Airspace consolidation "consolidation", "pneumonia", "airspace disease" 290 edema Pulmonary edema "pulmonary edema", "pulmonary congestion", "edema" 183 no_finding No finding "normal" 2,696 pleural_effusion Pleural effusion "pleural effusion", "effusion/pleural" 286 pneumothorax Pneumothorax "pneumothorax" 44 support_devices A tube, line or other device "catheter", "tube", "medical device", "stent" 425
  • A trigger matches whole words of a MeSH term. The match ignores upper and lower case. Part of a word does not match: tube does not match Tuberculosis, and normal does not match Abnormal. A final s can follow, so tube matches Tubes. A term that matches gives 1, and no match gives 0.
  • support_devices: a pacemaker study has the term "Implanted Medical Device" or "Medical Device". A device term with the word "breast" is a breast implant, so it does not set support_devices.
  • A report with no MeSH term, or with only the term "No Indexing", gets NaN in every label. 172 images have this (D-05).
  • mesh_major keeps the MeSH major terms as JSON text, for example ["normal"].

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
• report is the FINDINGS text and the IMPRESSION text, joined with a space. Example: The cardiac silhouette and mediastinum size are within normal limits. ... Normal chest x-XXXX.
  • The harmonizer leaves out a section that is empty, None or None.. A report with neither section gets report None.
  • findings, impression and indication keep each section alone.
  • 7,430 images have a report. With output_report=True, the class drops the other rows and warns (D-33).

docs.title: Splits
docs.text:
Class Registry key Images Source OpenICXRDataset openi_cxr 7,470 ecgen-radiology/*.xml and images/

OpenI IU X-Ray has no official split. get_datasets(n_splits=5) makes a train and val split. It groups by patient (D-10). The source has no patient ID, so one report is one patient, and nobody can check that a patient is in only 1 split.

from radharmony.harmonizer import OpenICXRHarmonizer

h = OpenICXRHarmonizer(base_dir="/data/OpenI-IU-CXR/")
df = h.harmonize()
print(df.columns.tolist())

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Labels: the MeSH terms do not always list the findings of the report text. Example: report 157.xml has the impression "Chest. Resolving pulmonary interstitial edema and pulmonary venous hypertension." and the only MeSH term "normal". So its images get no_finding 1 and edema 0.
  • View: the figure number is not always right. The DICOM tag shows that 97 F1 images are lateral, and 229 F2 images are AP (D-01).
  • Reports: the source replaced some words with XXXX to remove personal data, for example Normal chest x-XXXX.

docs.title: ROCO and ROCOv2
docs.text:
Registry keys ROCO: roco_train, roco_validation, roco_test. ROCOv2: rocov2_train, rocov2_validation, rocov2_test Task and outputs Image captioning: the caption (answer). question is empty Images in the table ROCOv2: train 59,962 images, validation 9,904 images, test 9,927 images. One image has one caption. ROCO: no count, because the RadHarmony tests cannot read the source files Modality Figures from PubMed Central articles: CT, X-ray, MRI, ultrasound, angiography and more. 2-D, JPEG. With radiology_only=False, ROCO also gives figures that are not radiology License ROCO: the roco-dataset repository states no license. ROCOv2: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 Download Get the data: other datasets

ROCO (Pelka et al., LABELS 2018) and ROCOv2 (Rückert et al., Scientific Data 2024) pair figures from PubMed Central articles with their captions. ROCOv2 is the next version of ROCO. It has only radiology figures, and each image has UMLS concepts (CUIs). The classes give the caption as answer, not as report. ReportGenerationEvaluator reads report, so it cannot score these classes.

docs.title: ROCO
docs.text:
Clone razorx89/roco-dataset and run its scripts/fetch.py. It downloads the images from PubMed Central. base_dir is the folder of the clone.

roco-dataset/
  data/train/radiology/
    captions.txt          # ROCO_00001<TAB><caption>
    keywords.txt          # ROCO_00001<TAB><TAB><keyword><TAB><keyword>...
    images/ROCO_00001.jpg
  data/train/non-radiology/...
  data/validation/...
  data/test/...

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import ROCOTrainDataset, ROCOTestDataset

train_ds = ROCOTrainDataset(base_dir="/data/roco-dataset/", dtype=torch.float32).get_datasets()
test_ds = ROCOTestDataset(base_dir="/data/roco-dataset/", dtype=torch.float32).get_datasets()
sample = train_ds[0]
# sample keys: img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id, question_id
# sample["img"]: Tensor(3, 224, 224)
# sample["question"]: ''

docs.title: ROCOv2
docs.text:
The source stores the images in parquet files. Run scripts/materialize_rocov2.py --base-dir /data/ROCOv2/ once. It writes each image to images/<split>/<image_id>.jpg.

ROCOv2/
  hf/data/train-00000-of-00027.parquet ...   # image, image_id, caption, cui
  hf/data/validation-*.parquet, hf/data/test-*.parquet
  train_concepts_manual.csv, valid_concepts_manual.csv, test_concepts_manual.csv
  images/test/ROCOv2_2023_test_000001.jpg    # made by scripts/materialize_rocov2.py

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import ROCOv2TrainDataset, ROCOv2ValidationDataset, ROCOv2TestDataset

train_ds = ROCOv2TrainDataset(base_dir="/data/ROCOv2/", dtype=torch.float32).get_datasets()
val_ds = ROCOv2ValidationDataset(base_dir="/data/ROCOv2/", dtype=torch.float32).get_datasets()
test_ds = ROCOv2TestDataset(base_dir="/data/ROCOv2/", dtype=torch.float32).get_datasets()
sample = test_ds[0]
# sample keys: img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id, question_id
# sample["img"]: Tensor(3, 224, 224)
# sample["answer"]: 'CT chest axial view showing a huge ascending aortic aneurysm (*).'

docs.title: ROCO
docs.text:
• Source: captions.txt and keywords.txt of each split and subset folder. One row of the harmonized table is one image and its caption (D-03). With radiology_only=True (the default), the harmonizer reads only the radiology/ folders.
  • IDs: the source has no patient or study ID, so patient_id, study_id and question_id are all the ROCO ID, for example ROCO_00002. One image is one patient.
  • image_path: data/<split>/<subset>/<image_subdir>/<ROCO ID>.jpg, for example data/train/radiology/images/ROCO_00002.jpg. It is relative to base_dir (D-04).
  • Caption: answer is the text after the ID. A caption with a tab in it keeps the tab. question is "".
  • Keywords: keywords joins the keywords of keywords.txt with tabs. Use .split("\t") for a list. The harmonizer does not read cuis.txt and semtypes.txt.
  • View, age and sex: the source has none of them, so the harmonized table has no view_position, age_years or sex (D-01).
  • Missing folders (D-35): a split folder with no captions.txt gives no rows and a warning that names it. When no folder has a captions.txt, the harmonizer raises FileNotFoundError.
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops a captions.txt row with no ID or no caption.

docs.title: ROCOv2
docs.text:
• Source: the parquet files hf/data/<split>-*.parquet (columns image_id, caption and cui) and the manual concept file of the split. One row of the harmonized table is one image and its caption (D-03).
  • IDs: the source has no patient ID, so patient_id, study_id and question_id are all image_id, for example ROCOv2_2023_test_000001. One image is one patient. Several figures can come from one article.
  • image_path: <split>/<image_id>.jpg, for example test/ROCOv2_2023_test_000001.jpg. It is relative to base_image_dir, which is <base_dir>/images by default (D-04).
  • Caption: answer is caption. question is "".
  • Concepts: with manual_concepts_only=True (the default), cuis comes from <split>_concepts_manual.csv (valid_ for the validation split). An image that the file does not list takes the CUIs of the parquet. With no file for the split, or with False, every image takes the CUIs of the parquet.
  • Modality: the harmonizer maps 13 CUIs to 7 modalities. modality is the one modality of the CUIs, or None when they name none or more than one.
  • View, age and sex: the source has none of them, so the harmonized table has no view_position, age_years or sex (D-01).
  • Dropped rows: by default, the harmonizer drops no row. The argument modalities keeps only the modalities in its list, and require_modality=True drops the rows with no modality.

docs.title: Captions
docs.text:
The text columns of the harmonized table:

Column Dataset Meaning Source question Both Always "", because this is a captioning set None answer Both The figure caption ROCO: captions.txt. ROCOv2: caption of the parquet split Both train, validation or test The folder (ROCO) or the parquet file name (ROCOv2) keywords ROCO The keywords, joined with tabs. "" when the file has no row for the image keywords.txt subset ROCO radiology or non-radiology The folder cuis ROCOv2 A list of UMLS CUIs The manual concept file, or the parquet cui modality_source ROCOv2 manual when the manual concept file lists the image, else auto The harmonizer modality ROCOv2 ct, mri, xray, ultrasound, angiography, pet_spect or mammography. None when the CUIs name no modality or more than one The harmonizer, from cuis n_modality_cuis ROCOv2 The number of modalities that the CUIs name The harmonizer, from cuis

ROCOv2 modalities: in the source files, no image names 2 modalities and no image has the mammography CUI. In the test split, 105 images get no modality, and 44 get pet_spect.

Example row of rocov2_test:

Column Value question_id ROCOv2_2023_test_000001 answer CT chest axial view showing a huge ascending aortic aneurysm (*). cuis ['C0040405'] modality ct modality_source manual

The sample holds img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id and question_id. img is (3, 224, 224): the figures can be in color, so the classes set IMG_CHANNELS = 3 (D-42). A gray file gives 3 equal channels. The extra columns (keywords, cuis, modality and the others) are only in the harmonized table, not in the sample.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• ROCOv2 train: the paper gives 59,958 train images. The Hugging Face parquet files have 59,962.
  • ROCOv2 validation: the caption of ROCOv2_2023_valid_003902 is only a narrow no-break space (U+202F).
  • ROCOv2 manual concept files: valid_concepts_manual.csv lists 9,945 images and test_concepts_manual.csv lists 9,972, more than the parquet files have. ROCOv2_2023_valid_003902 is not in valid_concepts_manual.csv, so its modality_source is auto.
  • ROCO: none known. The maintainers could not read the source files to check them.

docs.title: VQA-RAD
docs.text:
Registry keys vqa_rad_train, vqa_rad_test Task and outputs Visual question answering: the question (question) and the answer (answer). question_type with output_question_type=True Images in the table train 313 images (1,797 questions), test 203 images (451 questions) Modality X-ray, CT and MRI of the head, chest and abdomen, 2-D, JPEG License CC0 1.0 Download Get the data: other datasets

VQA-RAD is a visual question answering dataset of radiology images from MedPix (Lau et al., Scientific Data 2018). Clinicians wrote questions about the images and gave the answers. VQA_RAD Dataset Public.json has 2,248 questions.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
base_image_dir is the image folder. The class finds VQA_RAD Dataset Public.json in this folder or in the folder above it.

VQA-RAD/
  VQA_RAD Dataset Public.json
  VQA_RAD Image Folder/synpic54610.jpg

import torch
from radharmony.dataset import VQARadTestDataset, VQARadTrainDataset

train = VQARadTrainDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/VQA-RAD/VQA_RAD Image Folder/",
    output_question_type=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
)
train_ds, val_ds = train.get_datasets(n_splits=5)  # 1/5 of the images go to val

test_ds = VQARadTestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/VQA-RAD/VQA_RAD Image Folder/",
    output_question_type=True,
    dtype=torch.float32,
).get_datasets()
sample = test_ds[0]
# sample keys: img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id, question_id, question_type
# sample["img"]: Tensor(3, 224, 224)
# sample["question"]: 'Is there evidence of an aortic aneurysm?'
# sample["answer"]: 'yes'

docs.title: How it is harmonized
docs.text:
• Source: VQA_RAD Dataset Public.json. One record is one question. One row of the harmonized table is one question, not one image (D-03).
  • IDs: the source has no patient or study ID. The image_name synpic54610.jpg gives patient_id synpic54610, study_id synpic54610 and image_path synpic54610.jpg. So one image is one patient. image_path is relative to base_image_dir (D-04). question_id is the source qid, for example 0.
  • Text: question and answer come from the keys of the same name. The harmonizer removes the spaces at both ends. 5 answers are numbers in the source, for example 4 for "How many gallstones are identified?". The harmonizer makes them text.
  • Split: phrase_type test_freeform or test_para gives the split value test. freeform or para gives train.
  • Extra columns: answer_type and image_organ. The harmonizer removes the space at the end of 2 answer_type values ("CLOSED ").
  • View, age and sex: the source has none of them, so the harmonized table has no view_position, age_years or sex (D-01).
  • Dropped rows: the harmonizer drops no row. The image synpic35356.jpg has no question, so the harmonized table has 314 of the 315 images.

docs.title: Questions and answers
docs.text:
The text columns of the harmonized table:

Column Meaning Source question The question text question answer The answer text answer question_type The topic of the question: PRES (presence), POS (position), ABN (abnormality), MODALITY, SIZE, PLANE, ATTRIB (attribute), ORGAN, COLOR, COUNT or OTHER. Some rows have 2 types, for example PRES, POS question_type answer_type CLOSED or OPEN answer_type image_organ HEAD, CHEST or ABD image_organ split train or test phrase_type

Answer types: a closed question has a short answer, mostly yes or no. Some closed questions give a choice, for example "Is the abnormality focal or diffuse?" with the answer "Diffuse". An open question has a free text answer, for example "Where is the abnormality?" with the answer "left temporal lobe". In the test split, 272 questions are closed and 179 are open.

Example row of vqa_rad_test:

question_id image_path question answer question_type answer_type 10 synpic42202.jpg Is there evidence of an aortic aneurysm? yes PRES CLOSED

The sample holds img, question, answer, patient_id, study_id and question_id. With output_question_type=True, it also holds question_type. img is a tensor (3, 224, 224): MedPix has color figures, so the class sets IMG_CHANNELS = 3 (D-42). The VQA steps repeat a gray image to 3 channels.

Use it as the test split VQARadDataset vqa_rad All questions. It mixes the 2 splits, so do not use it for a benchmark (D-09)

The splits share 202 patients (D-34). The paper made the test questions on the same images as the train questions, so 202 of the 203 test images also have train questions. The split is by question, not by image.

get_datasets(n_splits=5) makes a train and val split from the train class. It groups by patient (D-10). The source has no patient ID, so one image is one patient, and nobody can check that a patient is in only 1 split.

docs.title: Known data problems
docs.text:
• Answer case: the closed answers have both Yes and yes, and both No and no. The harmonized table keeps the case of the source. Make the case the same before you compare answers.
  • Question types: a few values have a typo: ATRIB (1 row), PRSE (1 row) and Other (2 rows, where the other rows use OTHER).

docs.title: Evaluators
docs.text:
An evaluator takes a RadHarmony dataset and an encoder, and gives a result table (a pd.DataFrame). It is in radharmony.evaluator. This page lists the 11 evaluators and the facts that they share.

Class Registry key Task Page LinearProbeEvaluator linear_probe Classification, frozen features Linear probe KNNProbeEvaluator knn_probe Classification, frozen features kNN probe SVMProbeEvaluator svm_probe Classification, frozen features SVM probe PrototypeProbeEvaluator prototype_probe Classification, frozen features Prototype probe ZeroShotEvaluator zero_shot Classification with text prompts, no training Zero-shot FinetuneEvaluator finetune Classification, trains the encoder and a head, or the head only Fine-tune LinearProbeSegEvaluator linear_probe_seg Segmentation, frozen patch features, 1×1 convolution head Linear probe (segmentation) ConvProbeSegEvaluator conv_probe_seg Segmentation, frozen patch features, small convolution head Conv probe (segmentation) UPerNetSegEvaluator upernet_seg Segmentation, frozen patch features, UPerNet head UPerNet (segmentation) ReportGenerationEvaluator report_generation Report generation, scores generated reports Report generation VQAEvaluator vqa Visual question answering, scores generated answers Visual question answering

For a walkthrough, see notebooks/tutorials/evaluator_tutorial.ipynb.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: To run your first probe and read its result table, see Run a probe.

docs.title: Encoder contract
docs.text:
The evaluators do not look inside the encoder. They only call it:

Evaluators The encoder gets The encoder returns Classification imgs: Tensor[B, ...] a pooled feature vector, Tensor[B, D] ZeroShotEvaluator (text encoder) the output of tokenizer, or a list[str] with no tokenizer a text feature, Tensor[T, D] Segmentation imgs: Tensor[B, ...] patch features, Tensor[B, D, H', W'] ReportGenerationEvaluator the img batch (a list[str] of image paths with the CheXagent, MAIRA-2 and MedGemma recipes). With use_indication=True, also the indications a list[str] of reports, one for each image VQAEvaluator the img batch and the list[str] of questions a list[str] of answers, one for each image

The input shape is the output of the dataset transform. ImageEncoderWrapper wraps a Hugging Face, timm or OpenCLIP model in this contract. See Add a backbone.

docs.title: Backbone recipes
docs.text: A backbone recipe is a make_<name>() function in radharmony.evaluator.backbones. It returns the dataset transform and the encoder, and a text encoder for a vision-language model. Give the transform to the dataset and the encoder to the evaluator. Pass output_keys={"img", "mask"} to the recipe. Then the encoder gives patch features for the segmentation evaluators. See Backbones for the list of recipes.

docs.title: Split modes
docs.text:
ZeroShotEvaluator, ReportGenerationEvaluator and VQAEvaluator use only test data. The other evaluators need exactly one of 2 split modes. Any other mix raises ValueError.

# k-fold mode: one dataset. GroupKFold makes the folds.
ev = LinearProbeEvaluator(encoder, dataset=ds, n_folds=5)

# fixed-split mode: a train dataset and a test dataset.
ev = LinearProbeEvaluator(encoder, train_dataset=train_ds, test_dataset=test_ds, n_seeds=5, n_bootstrap=100)
  • Patients: the folds, the validation part and the bootstrap group the images by patient_id. All images of a patient go to the same part. With no patient_id column, each image is its own patient. A NaN patient_id raises ValueError (D-32).
  • K-fold mode: the folds give the variance. The evaluator ignores n_seeds and n_bootstrap, and warns if you set them (D-19).
  • Fixed-split mode: the variance comes from n_seeds train samples and n_bootstrap bootstrap samples of the test set. Each bootstrap sample draws test patients with replacement and keeps all their images (D-32).
  • n_train_samples (for example [50, 100]) gives one run for each train size. It counts images (D-40), and it includes the validation part (D-29). A size larger than the train data uses all rows, and the result keeps the size that you asked for.

docs.title: Embedding cache
docs.text:
The frozen-feature evaluators (the linear, kNN, SVM and prototype probes, and zero-shot) extract the features one time, before they fit. With embedding_cache="<path>", they also write the raw features to a file. A later run with the same path reads the file, for any labels= list (D-41).

  • Files: <path>.pkl in k-fold mode. <path>.train.pkl and <path>.test.pkl in fixed-split mode. <path>.test.pkl for zero-shot.
  • Labels: a run always reads the labels from the dataset, not from the file.
  • Checks: a file from other images, another base_image_dir, another encoder, transform or autocast_dtype raises ValueError. A file from before 2026-11-03 raises ValueError too. Delete the file to make it again.
  • Random steps: use a transform with no random step, for example no with_flip. A random step gives one random draw for each image, so these evaluators warn (D-41).
  • L2 norm: the file keeps raw features. The probe normalizes them after it reads them (D-17).

FinetuneEvaluator does not use the cache (Fine-tune).

docs.title: Result table
docs.text:
evaluate() of a classification evaluator returns one row for each label and run, with these columns:

Column Meaning n_train The train size of n_train_samples. -1 when n_train_samples=None (all train rows), and in zero-shot fold The fold, from 0. -1 in fixed-split mode and in zero-shot seed The seed of the train sample, base_seed plus the seed index. -1 in k-fold mode and in zero-shot bootstrap -1 for the point estimate. 0 to n_bootstrap - 1 for a bootstrap sample label The label name, or macro_average auroc, auprc They use no threshold f1, accuracy, balanced_accuracy, tpr, tnr, ppv, npv, mcc They use the threshold. See Threshold threshold The threshold of the label

Each run also gets a macro_average row, also for a dataset with 1 label. It is the mean of the label rows, and it skips NaN values. So a fixed-split run has (labels + 1) * n_seeds * (1 + n_bootstrap) rows for each train size.

A label with fewer than 2 positives or 2 negatives in the test rows of a run gets NaN in all metrics, also in AUROC. Rows with a NaN label are not scored.

save_results(df) writes 2 files to output_dir:

  • results.csv: the result table.
  • results_summary.csv: one row for each label and n_train. For each metric, it gives <metric>_mean (the mean of the point estimates) and <metric>_n (the number of runs with a value). It also gives <metric>_std, <metric>_ci_lo and <metric>_ci_hi (the 95% CI) over the bootstrap rows. With no bootstrap rows, they come from the folds or the seeds. With fewer than 2 values, they are NaN (D-19). <metric>_std is the population std (np.nanstd, which divides by n), as scikit-learn gives. The sample std (pandas .std()) is a little bigger: over 5 folds, about 12%.

When a metric of a label is NaN in some runs, for example the F1 of a rare label, save_results() warns one time.

docs.title: Threshold
docs.text:
threshold_strategy is "youden" (the default), "f1" or "fixed:<float>". The evaluators that train (the linear, kNN, SVM and prototype probes, and fine-tune) pick the threshold on validation data, not on the test labels (D-29):

  1. The probe holds out val_fraction (default 0.1) of the train patients. It does not fit on this validation part.
  2. The probe scores the validation part and picks one threshold for each label with threshold_strategy.
  3. It uses this threshold on the test set and on each bootstrap sample.

So n_train counts the validation part too. The threshold metrics are NaN when the validation part has fewer than 2 positives or 2 negatives of a label, or with val_fraction=0.0. "fixed:<float>" needs no validation data. AUROC and AUPRC use no threshold.

ZeroShotEvaluator has no train data, so its threshold metrics are NaN, except with threshold_strategy="fixed:<float>" (see Zero-shot).

docs.title: Registry
docs.text:
Each evaluator has a registry key. resolve_evaluator gives the class of a key. To add your own evaluator, register it:

from radharmony.evaluator import BaseClsEvaluator, list_evaluators, register_evaluator, resolve_evaluator


@register_evaluator("my_probe")
class MyProbeEvaluator(BaseClsEvaluator):
    def evaluate(self):
        ...


print("my_probe" in list_evaluators())  # True
print(resolve_evaluator("linear_probe").__name__)  # LinearProbeEvaluator

docs.title: ConvProbeSegEvaluator
docs.text:
Registry key conv_probe_seg Task Segmentation, frozen patch features, small convolution head Dataset outputs it needs mask (output_mask=True) Split modes k-fold (dataset=), fixed split (train_dataset=, test_dataset=) Encoder it needs a map of patch features, Tensor[B, D, H', W'], from make_<name>(output_keys={"img", "mask"}) Output The result table, one row for each class and run. See Output

The conv probe is the segmentation linear probe with a larger head. The head mixes the feature channels and the nearby patches before it gives a class score for each patch. Use it when the 1×1 head is too simple and the UPerNet probe head is too large. The training, the scoring and the output are the same as in the linear probe.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block segments the lungs on Montgomery (138 images) with RAD-DINO, 2 folds and 3 epochs.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import ConvProbeSegEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_mask=True,
    mask_output_dir="/data/montgomery_lung_masks/",  # any folder you can write to
    cache_dir=None,
)

ev = ConvProbeSegEvaluator(
    encoder,
    dataset=ds,
    num_classes=2,  # background and lung
    conv_hidden_size=256,
    n_folds=2,
    epochs=3,
    num_workers=8,  # 8 workers read the large PNG files faster
    output_dir="outputs/conv_probe_seg",
)
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
print(df.columns.tolist())
# ['n_train', 'fold', 'seed', 'bootstrap', 'label', 'dice', 'iou', 'pixel_acc', 'tpr', 'tnr', 'ppv', 'npv']

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The head is:

Conv2d(D, hidden, kernel_size=1, bias=False)
LayerNorm2d(hidden)
Conv2d(hidden, hidden, kernel_size=3, padding=1, bias=False)
LayerNorm2d(hidden)
Conv2d(hidden, num_classes, kernel_size=1)
bilinear resize to the mask size
  • Head: hidden is conv_hidden_size. For D=768, hidden=256 and 2 classes, the head has about 0.79 million weights.
  • Norm: LayerNorm2d normalizes the channels at each patch. It works with any batch size.
  • Training: for the training loop, early stopping, the splits, the masks and the metrics, see How it works and Metrics on the linear probe page.

docs.text: fit(), save_head(), load_head(), predict(), inner_val_indices() and store_final_model work as in the linear probe. See Save and reuse. save_head() keeps conv_hidden_size in the file. load_head() warns when the evaluator has another conv_hidden_size.

docs.title: FinetuneEvaluator
docs.text:
Registry key finetune Task Classification, trains the encoder and a head, or the head only Dataset outputs it needs cls (output_cls=True) Split modes k-fold (dataset=), fixed split (train_dataset=, test_dataset=) Encoder it needs a pooled feature vector, Tensor[B, D]. It must be an nn.Module, also with freeze_backbone=True Output The result table, one row for each label and run. See Output

The fine-tune evaluator trains a classification head on the encoder, and by default the encoder too. It uses one GPU, AdamW, a cosine learning-rate schedule and early stopping. It has the same split modes and result table as the probes, so you can compare the results. It has no multi-GPU training and no experiment logger.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block fine-tunes RAD-DINO on Montgomery (138 images), with 3 folds, 3 epochs and a batch of 8 images.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import FinetuneEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)

ev = FinetuneEvaluator(encoder, dataset=ds, n_folds=3, epochs=3, batch_size=8, output_dir="outputs/finetune")
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
print(df.columns.tolist())
# ['n_train', 'fold', 'seed', 'bootstrap', 'label', 'auroc', 'auprc', 'f1', ...]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Model: the head is nn.Linear(D, number of labels), or a copy of head. The evaluator finds D from one batch.
  • Encoder: with freeze_backbone=False, each fold or seed trains its own copy of the encoder, so the runs do not share weights. The encoder learning rate is lr * backbone_lr_scale. With freeze_backbone=True, only the head trains.
  • Training: AdamW with weight_decay, and a cosine schedule over epochs. The loss is one sigmoid cross-entropy for each label (loss="bce"), or a softmax cross-entropy over the labels (loss="ce").
  • Labels: a NaN label adds no loss (D-18). With loss="ce", the evaluator drops a row with a NaN label.
  • Early stopping: the evaluator holds out a validation part of the train patients, and the model does not train on it. After each epoch, the evaluator scores this part with early_stop_metric. It takes the mean over the labels with 2 or more positives and 2 or more negatives in the validation part. It stops after early_stop_patience epochs with no better value, and keeps the weights of the best epoch. An epoch with no value, for example with no positive in the validation part, does not count.
  • Threshold: after training, the evaluator picks the threshold on the same validation part (Threshold, D-29).
  • Bootstrap: the bootstrap samples reuse the test predictions of the trained model. They do not train again.

docs.title: Save and reuse
docs.text:
fit() trains one model on all train data, with no benchmark. save_model() writes it, and predict() runs it. This block uses encoder and ds of Quick use.

ev = FinetuneEvaluator(encoder, dataset=ds, epochs=3, batch_size=8, freeze_backbone=True)
ev.fit()  # trains on all images, minus a validation part for early stopping
path = ev.save_model("outputs/finetune/final_model.pt")

# Later: make the evaluator with the same encoder, head= and freeze_backbone=.
ev2 = FinetuneEvaluator(encoder, dataset=ds, freeze_backbone=True)
ev2.load_model(path)
preds = ev2.predict(ds)
print(sorted(preds[0]))  # ['image_id', 'prob', 'y_true']
Method What it does fit(dataset=None) Trains a model on all of dataset (default: dataset or train_dataset of the evaluator), with the same early stopping as evaluate(). It sets final_encoder_ and final_head_, and returns the head save_model(path=None) Writes the head weights, the labels, freeze_backbone, l2_normalize and loss. It writes the encoder weights only with freeze_backbone=False. The default path is <output_dir>/final_model.pt. It returns the path load_model(path) Builds the head again from the file and loads the weights. It warns when freeze_backbone differs from the file. It takes l2_normalize and loss from the file, with a warning when they differ predict(dataset, *, encoder=None, head=None, indices=None) Runs the model over dataset. It returns one dict for each image, with image_id, y_true and prob. indices limits the run to some rows
  • image_id is the image_path with no file ending (D-46).
  • prob is a sigmoid for each label, or a softmax over the labels with loss="ce".
  • predict() takes the label columns of the dataset by the names in final_labels_. So the dataset can have more labels. A missing label raises ValueError.
  • store_final_model=True runs fit() at the end of evaluate(), on dataset or train_dataset.

evaluate() returns the result table with these columns: n_train, fold, seed, bootstrap, label, auroc, auprc, f1, accuracy, balanced_accuracy, tpr, tnr, ppv, npv, mcc and threshold. save_results(df) writes results.csv and results_summary.csv to output_dir.

With store_final_model=True, the evaluator also sets final_encoder_, final_head_ and final_labels_ (Save and reuse).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Use loss="bce" for a dataset with 1 label column, for example Montgomery or Shenzhen TB. Use loss="ce" only when each image has exactly 1 of 2 or more label columns.
  • The dataset transform is the same for the train, validation and test rows of a k-fold run. So a random step, for example with_flip, also changes the validation and test images. It draws again in each epoch, and the evaluator does not warn.
  • With freeze_backbone=True, the fine-tune evaluator still runs the encoder on each batch of each epoch. A linear probe runs it only one time.

docs.title: KNNProbeEvaluator
docs.text:
Registry key knn_probe Task Classification, frozen features Dataset outputs it needs cls (output_cls=True) Split modes k-fold (dataset=), fixed split (train_dataset=, test_dataset=) Encoder it needs a pooled feature vector, Tensor[B, D] Output The result table, one row for each label and run. See Output

The kNN probe scores each test image by its k nearest train images in feature space. The score of a label is the mean label of these neighbors. The probe has no training loop, only a neighbor search. Use it as a fast check that images with the same label have close features.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block runs the kNN probe on Montgomery (138 images) with RAD-DINO, with 5 folds.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import KNNProbeEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)

ev = KNNProbeEvaluator(encoder, dataset=ds, n_folds=5, k=20, output_dir="outputs/knn_probe")
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
print(df.columns.tolist())
# ['n_train', 'fold', 'seed', 'bootstrap', 'label', 'auroc', 'auprc', 'f1', ...]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Features: the evaluator runs the encoder one time over each dataset. It L2-normalizes the features by default (D-17). So the default metric="cosine" works on unit vectors. The embedding cache keeps the raw features.
  • Neighbors: sklearn.neighbors.NearestNeighbors with metric finds the k nearest train rows. With fewer than k train rows, it uses all of them.
  • Score: the score of a label is the mean of its 0 or 1 values over the k neighbors. For example, 6 positives in 20 neighbors give 0.3. Each label is scored alone.
  • Labels: each label searches only the train rows where it is 0 or 1. A row with a NaN label is not a neighbor for that label (D-18).
  • Threshold: the probe holds out a validation part of the train patients and does not search it. It picks the threshold there (Threshold, D-29).

None uses all train images store_final_model bool False After evaluate(), also fit the neighbor index on all train images. It goes to final_models_, not to a file val_fraction float 0.1 The part of the train patients for the threshold. The probe does not search it. 0.0 gives NaN threshold metrics, except with "fixed:<float>"

docs.text:
evaluate() returns the result table with these columns: n_train, fold, seed, bootstrap, label, auroc, auprc, f1, accuracy, balanced_accuracy, tpr, tnr, ppv, npv, mcc and threshold. save_results(df) writes results.csv and results_summary.csv to output_dir.

With store_final_model=True, final_models_ maps each label to a dict with 2 keys. "nn" is the fitted NearestNeighbors over the rows where the label is 0 or 1. "y_train" holds the labels of these rows. A label with no such row maps to None. The score of new features x is y_train[nn.kneighbors(x)[1]].mean(axis=1).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• With unit vectors, metric="cosine" gives the same neighbors as a largest inner-product search. With l2_normalize=False, metric works on the raw features.
  • The score has only k + 1 possible values, so many test images can have the same score.

docs.title: LinearProbeEvaluator
docs.text:
Registry key linear_probe Task Classification, frozen features Dataset outputs it needs cls (output_cls=True) Split modes k-fold (dataset=), fixed split (train_dataset=, test_dataset=) Encoder it needs a pooled feature vector, Tensor[B, D] Output The result table, one row for each label and run. See Output

The linear probe fits one logistic regression for each label on the frozen features of an encoder. The encoder does not train. Use it as the main test of how good the features of an encoder are. It is the most common protocol for frozen foundation models.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block runs the linear probe on Montgomery (138 images) with RAD-DINO, with 5 folds.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import LinearProbeEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)

ev = LinearProbeEvaluator(encoder, dataset=ds, n_folds=5, output_dir="outputs/linear_probe")
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
print(df.columns.tolist())
# ['n_train', 'fold', 'seed', 'bootstrap', 'label', 'auroc', 'auprc', 'f1', ...]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Features: the evaluator runs the encoder one time over each dataset. It L2-normalizes the features by default (D-17). The embedding cache keeps the raw features.
  • Probe: one LogisticRegression for each label. The default arguments are class_weight="balanced", C=1.0, max_iter=10000 and solver="lbfgs". probe_kwargs changes some of them, and the others stay.
  • Labels: each label fits only on the rows where it is 0 or 1. A NaN label is not a negative (D-18). A label with only one class gets NaN metrics.
  • Threshold: the probe holds out a validation part of the train patients and does not fit on it. It picks the threshold there (Threshold, D-29).
  • Variance: k-fold mode gives one row for each fold. Fixed-split mode gives one row for each seed and bootstrap sample (Split modes).
