docs.title: LinearProbeSegEvaluator
docs.text:
Registry key linear_probe_seg Task Segmentation, frozen patch features, 1×1 convolution head Dataset outputs it needs mask (output_mask=True) Split modes k-fold (dataset=), fixed split (train_dataset=, test_dataset=) Encoder it needs a map of patch features, Tensor[B, D, H', W'], from make_<name>(output_keys={"img", "mask"}) Output The result table, one row for each class and run. See Output

The segmentation linear probe trains a 1×1 convolution on the frozen patch features of an encoder. The head gives a class score for each patch, and a bilinear resize takes the scores to the mask size. The score shows how much location information the patch features hold. This page also has the shared facts of the conv probe and the UPerNet probe. They train and score in the same way, with a larger head.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block segments the lungs on Montgomery (138 images) with RAD-DINO, 2 folds and 3 epochs.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import LinearProbeSegEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_mask=True,
    mask_output_dir="/data/montgomery_lung_masks/",  # any folder you can write to
    cache_dir=None,
)

ev = LinearProbeSegEvaluator(
    encoder,
    dataset=ds,
    num_classes=2,  # background and lung
    n_folds=2,
    epochs=3,
    num_workers=8,  # 8 workers read the large PNG files faster
    output_dir="outputs/linear_probe_seg",
)
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
print(df.columns.tolist())
# ['n_train', 'fold', 'seed', 'bootstrap', 'label', 'dice', 'iou', 'pixel_acc', 'tpr', 'tnr', 'ppv', 'npv']

make_raddino resizes each image and mask to 518×518. With cache_dir=None, the run reads and resizes every image again in each epoch. On a shared GPU, this run took about 5 minutes.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Features: the encoder stays frozen. The head gets the raw patch features, with no L2 norm (D-17). The encoder runs in autocast_dtype, and the head runs in float32.
  • Head: it trains with AdamW, a cosine learning-rate schedule and a cross-entropy loss. class_weights sets a weight for each class in the loss.
  • Splits: the folds, the validation part and the bootstrap group the images by patient (Split modes).
  • Fixed split: it needs 2 datasets with masks, for example QaTaCOV19TrainDataset and QaTaCOV19TestDataset. The SIIM-ACR test split has no masks, so it does not work as test_dataset.
  • Early stopping: the evaluator takes val_fraction of the train patients as a validation part. It never uses the test fold or the test set to train or to stop (D-18). After each epoch, it scores early_stop_metric on the validation part, as a mean over the classes other than background. It keeps the head of the best epoch, and it stops after early_stop_patience epochs with no better score. When the validation part has no foreground pixel, the epoch gets no score and does not count.
  • Train size: n_train_samples sets how many images the evaluator draws from the train part (D-40). It includes the validation part.
  • Masks (D-14): with num_classes=2, every value above 0 is foreground, for example 1 or 255. With more classes, the mask holds the class indices 0 to num_classes - 1, and a larger value raises ValueError. A mask can be [B, 1, H, W], [B, H, W] or one-hot [B, C, H, W]. A one-hot mask gives its class indices with argmax.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The evaluator computes 7 metrics for each class and each test image. Then it takes the mean over the images with np.nanmean.

Metric Meaning dice Dice: 2·TP / (2·TP + FP + FN) iou Intersection over union: TP / (TP + FP + FN) pixel_acc Pixel accuracy: (TP + TN) / N tpr Sensitivity (recall) tnr Specificity ppv Precision npv Negative predictive value

An image with no ground-truth pixel of a class:

  • An empty prediction gives NaN dice and iou, so the image does not count for that class.
  • Any predicted pixel gives dice = iou = 0.

This rule is not an option of MONAI DiceMetric. MONAI gives NaN in both cases (ignore_empty=True), or 1 and 0 (ignore_empty=False). On a dataset with many empty images (for example SIIM-ACR), compare Dice only with results that use the same rule.

docs.title: Save and reuse
docs.text:
fit() trains one head on all images of the dataset, minus the validation part for early stopping. It does not run the folds. save_head() writes only the head, so the file is small. To use it again, build the encoder with the same backbone recipe, and the evaluator with the same head arguments. This block uses ev, encoder and ds of Quick use.

ev.fit()
path = ev.save_head("outputs/linear_probe_seg/head.pt")

ev2 = LinearProbeSegEvaluator(encoder, dataset=ds, num_classes=2)
ev2.load_head(path)
preds = ev2.predict(ds, indices=[0, 1], return_images=True)
print(sorted(preds[0]))  # ['image', 'image_id', 'prob', 'y_pred', 'y_true']
Method What it does fit(dataset=None) Trains a head on all images of dataset (default: dataset or train_dataset of the evaluator), with the same early stopping. It sets final_head_ and returns it save_head(path=None) Writes final_head_ with its shape, num_classes and head settings. The default path is <output_dir>/final_head.pt. It returns the path load_head(path) Builds the head again from the file and loads its weights. It warns when num_classes or the head settings differ from the evaluator predict(dataset, *, head=None, indices=None, return_images=False) Runs the head (default: final_head_) on dataset, or on the rows in indices. It returns one dict for each image: image_id, y_true [H, W], y_pred [H, W] and prob [C, H, W]. return_images=True adds image, a gray [H, W] image in [0, 1] at the mask size, for overlays inner_val_indices(dataset=None) Returns the dataset rows of the validation part that fit() keeps out. It needs no training, so it also works after load_head(). It is empty when val_fraction=0

image_id is the image_path with no file ending (D-46). store_final_model=True runs fit() at the end of evaluate(), so one call gives the result table and the head. The images of inner_val_indices() did not train the head, but they chose the best epoch. So their predictions look a little better than the predictions on new images.

docs.text: Argument Type Default Description n_folds int 5 The number of folds in k-fold mode. Fixed-split mode does not use it n_train_samples list[int] None The train sizes in images, one run for each (Split modes). None uses all train images epochs int 20 The largest number of epochs of one run lr float 0.001 The learning rate of the head weight_decay float 0.05 The AdamW weight decay class_weights list[float] None A weight for each class in the cross-entropy loss, for example for a small foreground. None gives the same weight to all classes save_predictions bool False Write the PNGs GT, Pred and Prob of each test image to <output_dir>/{GT,Pred,Prob}/<run-id>/. The file name is the image_id with __ for each / (D-46). It needs output_dir store_final_model bool False After evaluate(), also run fit() (Save and reuse) early_stop_metric str "dice" The metric of the validation part for early stopping: dice, iou, pixel_acc, tpr, tnr, ppv or npv early_stop_patience int 5 The number of epochs with no better value before the run stops val_fraction float 0.1 The part of the train patients for early stopping. The head does not train on it. 0.0 gives no early stopping

It returns Tensor[B, D, H', W'] (Encoder contract) dataset dataset None K-fold mode: the one dataset (Split modes) train_dataset dataset None Fixed-split mode: the train dataset test_dataset dataset None Fixed-split mode: the test dataset num_classes int 2 The number of classes, with background. 2 is background and one foreground class device str "cuda" "cuda", "cuda:N" or "cpu" batch_size int 8 The batch size of training and of prediction num_workers int 4 The number of DataLoader workers autocast_dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The autocast type of the encoder. None gives no autocast output_dir str None The folder for save_results(), save_head() and the PNGs of save_predictions n_seeds int 1 Fixed-split mode: the number of train samples, each with its own seed (Split modes) base_seed int 0 The first seed of the train samples, the validation part and the training n_bootstrap int 0 Fixed-split mode: the number of bootstrap samples of the test set (Split modes) bootstrap_seed int 0 The first seed of the bootstrap samples threshold_strategy str "youden" Not used. The head gives the class with the highest score for each pixel. A value other than "youden" warns (D-52)

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
evaluate() returns the result table, one row for each class and run. A run is one fold or one seed, for each n_train value. Each run also gets a macro_average row. In fixed-split mode, each bootstrap sample of a run gets its own rows. The columns of the Quick use run:

Column Meaning n_train The train size of n_train_samples. -1 means all train images fold The fold, from 0. -1 in fixed-split mode seed The seed of the train sample. -1 in k-fold mode bootstrap -1 for the point estimate. 0 to n_bootstrap - 1 for a bootstrap sample label class_0 (background), class_1, ..., or macro_average dice, iou, pixel_acc, tpr, tnr, ppv, npv The metrics. See Metrics

macro_average is the mean over the classes other than class_0. save_results(df) writes results.csv and results_summary.csv to output_dir. The summary has one row for each label and n_train. For each metric, it gives <metric>_mean, <metric>_n, <metric>_std, <metric>_ci_lo and <metric>_ci_hi (D-19).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The head is nn.Conv2d(D, num_classes, kernel_size=1) and a bilinear resize to the mask size. For D=768 and 2 classes, it has 1538 weights.
  • An encoder that gives no 4-D map raises ValueError. A dataset with no mask raises KeyError.
  • Each run seeds torch from base_seed, so the same base_seed gives the same result.
  • The evaluator reads the mask size from the last dimension of the first batch. It expects square masks, as the backbone recipes give.
  • The dataset transform is the same for the train, validation and test rows of a k-fold run. So a random step, for example with_flip, also changes the validation and test images. It draws again in each epoch, and the evaluator does not warn.
  • For more examples with SIIM-ACR, Montgomery and Shenzhen, see notebooks/evaluator/fm_comparison_seg.ipynb.

docs.title: PrototypeProbeEvaluator
docs.text:
Registry key prototype_probe Task Classification, frozen features Dataset outputs it needs cls (output_cls=True) Split modes k-fold (dataset=), fixed split (train_dataset=, test_dataset=) Encoder it needs a pooled feature vector, Tensor[B, D] Output The result table, one row for each label and run. See Output

The prototype probe is a nearest-centroid classifier. For each label, it takes the mean feature of the positive train images and of the negative train images. It scores a test image by its cosine to these 2 centroids. It has no optimization and no setting to tune, so it is a fast baseline.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block runs the prototype probe on Montgomery (138 images) with RAD-DINO, with 5 folds.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import PrototypeProbeEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)

ev = PrototypeProbeEvaluator(encoder, dataset=ds, n_folds=5, output_dir="outputs/prototype_probe")
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
print(df.columns.tolist())
# ['n_train', 'fold', 'seed', 'bootstrap', 'label', 'auroc', 'auprc', 'f1', ...]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Features: the evaluator runs the encoder one time over each dataset. It L2-normalizes the features by default (D-17). The embedding cache keeps the raw features.
  • Centroids: for each label, c_pos is the mean feature of the train rows with label 1, and c_neg of the rows with label 0. Both centroids get L2 norm 1. A row with a NaN label is in neither centroid (D-18).
  • Score: cos(x, c_pos) - cos(x, c_neg) for a test feature x. A score above 0 means that x is closer to the positive centroid.
  • Missing class: a label with no positive or no negative train row gets NaN metrics in that run. The macro average leaves it out.
  • Threshold: the probe holds out a validation part of the train patients. The centroids do not use it. The probe picks the threshold there (Threshold, D-29).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description n_folds int 5 The number of folds in k-fold mode. Fixed-split mode does not use it n_train_samples list[int] None The train sizes in images, one run for each (Split modes). None uses all train images store_final_model bool False After evaluate(), also compute the centroids on all train images. They go to final_models_, not to a file val_fraction float 0.1 The part of the train patients for the threshold. The centroids do not use it. 0.0 gives NaN threshold metrics, except with "fixed:<float>"

docs.title: Shared arguments (inherited from BaseClsEvaluator)
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description image_encoder nn.Module or callable required The encoder. It returns Tensor[B, D] (Encoder contract) dataset dataset None K-fold mode: the one dataset (Split modes) train_dataset dataset None Fixed-split mode: the train dataset test_dataset dataset None Fixed-split mode: the test dataset labels list[str] None The labels to evaluate. None gives all labels. The match ignores case. An unknown name raises KeyError device str "cuda" "cuda", "cuda:N" or "cpu" batch_size int 64 The batch size of the feature extraction num_workers int 4 The number of DataLoader workers autocast_dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The autocast type of the encoder. None gives no autocast embedding_cache str None The path of the feature file (Embedding cache) l2_normalize bool False L2-normalize the features before the centroids. This class sets True when you do not pass it (D-17) output_dir str None The folder for save_results() n_seeds int 1 Fixed-split mode: the number of train samples, each with its own seed (Split modes) base_seed int 0 The first seed of the train samples and of the validation part n_bootstrap int 0 Fixed-split mode: the number of bootstrap samples of the test set (Split modes) bootstrap_seed int 0 The first seed of the bootstrap samples threshold_strategy str "youden" "youden", "f1" or "fixed:<float>" (Threshold)

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
evaluate() returns the result table with these columns: n_train, fold, seed, bootstrap, label, auroc, auprc, f1, accuracy, balanced_accuracy, tpr, tnr, ppv, npv, mcc and threshold. save_results(df) writes results.csv and results_summary.csv to output_dir. The score and the threshold are in [-2, 2].

With store_final_model=True, final_models_ maps each label to its (c_pos, c_neg) pair of unit vectors, or to None for a label with only one class.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• With l2_normalize=True (the default), each centroid is the mean of unit vectors. With l2_normalize=False, it is the mean of the raw features. The score is a cosine in both cases.
  • threshold_strategy="fixed:0" means "closer to the positive centroid".

docs.title: ReportGenerationEvaluator
docs.text:
Registry key report_generation Task Report generation, scores generated reports Dataset outputs it needs report (output_report=True) Split modes test only (dataset=) Encoder it needs a report generator, (imgs, indications=None) -> list[str], one report for each image (Encoder contract) Output The result table, one row for the point estimate and one for each bootstrap sample. See Output

The report generation evaluator runs a vision-language model over a dataset and scores each generated report against the real report. The scores come from the RadEval metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, RadGraph, F1-CheXbert and more). Use it to compare report generators on the same images. It does not look inside the model, so any generator works.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
The generator recipes make_chexagent_generator and make_maira2_generator need their own venv (chexagent_gen or maira2_gen extra). RadEval needs other package versions, so you generate and score in 2 steps. In the generator venv, generate_only() writes the generated reports to a parquet file. This block makes 4 reports on Montgomery (138 images) with CheXagent-2, in batches of 2:

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import ReportGenerationEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_chexagent_generator

transform, report_generator = make_chexagent_generator(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_report=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)

ev = ReportGenerationEvaluator(
    report_generator,
    dataset=ds,
    batch_size=2,
    max_samples=4,
    output_dir="outputs/report_generation",
)
ev.generate_only("outputs/report_generation/pairs.parquet")
# pairs.parquet columns: sample_id, reference, hypothesis, patient_id

Then score the parquet file in the RadEval venv (radeval extra). --light uses LIGHT_METRICS (see Metrics). Without it, the script uses all 16 metrics:

python notebooks/evaluator/score_reports_radeval.py \
    --pairs-parquet outputs/report_generation/pairs.parquet \
    --output-dir outputs/report_generation/scores \
    --light --n-bootstrap 10

The script writes results.csv with one row of scores and one row for each bootstrap sample. It also writes results_summary.json with the number of pairs and the scores of the first row. Run the script from the repo, because it loads radharmony/evaluator/language/hypothesis.py by its file path. Montgomery reports are short (for example "normal"). So the scores mean little, and the example only shows the steps.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Generation: the evaluator runs report_generator on each batch of img. It needs one report for each image. With the CheXagent and MAIRA-2 recipes, img is the path of a PNG file, so the batch is a list of path strings.
  • Reference: the evaluator takes the section ref_section of sample["report"] (D-38). See Reference sections.
  • Dropped pairs: the evaluator drops a pair when the reference or the generated report is empty.
  • Cleaning: evaluate() cleans each generated report with normalize_hypothesis before it scores it. The scoring script of step 2 does the same, so both ways give the same score for the same generated reports (D-50).
  • Bootstrap: each bootstrap sample draws patients with replacement and keeps all their pairs (D-32). With no patient_id, the bootstrap draws pairs.
  • IDs: sample_id is the image_path with no file ending (D-46). For example, MCUCXR_0001_0.png gives MCUCXR_0001_0.
  • Splits: the evaluator has no folds and no training (Split modes).

docs.title: Indication
docs.text:
The indication is the reason for the exam, for example "cough". The radiologist has it before they write the report, so it is a fair input. The evaluator never scores it. With use_indication=True, the evaluator takes the section indication_section of sample["report"] and gives it to the generator:

report_generator(imgs, indications) -> list[str]

indications has one string for each image. An entry is None when that report has no indication section. With use_indication=False, the generator gets only imgs. With use_indication=True, a generator that takes only imgs raises TypeError at once (D-52).

The recipes use the indication in different ways:

  • make_maira2_generator puts it in the indication input of MAIRA-2.
  • make_chexagent_generator puts it before each prompt.
  • make_medgemma_generator puts "Indication: <text>. " before its prompt.

docs.title: Reference sections
docs.text:
ref_section picks the part of the real report that is the reference (D-38):

ref_section Reference "findings" The FINDINGS section. With no FINDINGS section, the IMPRESSION section "impression" The IMPRESSION or CONCLUSION section. With neither, the FINDINGS section "both" The FINDINGS text and then the IMPRESSION text, joined with a space "full" The whole report, with single spaces

A report with neither section gives the whole report, with single spaces. A header is a name and a colon, for example FINDINGS:. At the start of a line, it can be in upper or lower case. Inside a line, it must be in capitals. So "No new findings: none." in a sentence is not a header.

The parser and the text cleaning need no data:

from radharmony.evaluator.language import normalize_hypothesis
from radharmony.evaluator.language._report_parser import parse_report_section

report = "INDICATION: cough.\nFINDINGS: Heart is normal. No effusion.\nIMPRESSION: No acute disease."
print(parse_report_section(report, "findings"))  # Heart is normal. No effusion.
print(parse_report_section(report, "both"))  # Heart is normal. No effusion. No acute disease.
print(parse_report_section("IMPRESSION: Stable.", "findings"))  # Stable.
print(normalize_hypothesis("[Lungs: Pleura] **small effusion**."))  # small effusion.

normalize_hypothesis removes the CheXagent grounding tags ([Region: Subregion]), the boxes (<|box|> ... <|/box|>), the ref marks (<|ref|>, <|/ref|>) and the bold marks (**). Then it makes all white space single spaces.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
radharmony.evaluator.metrics has 2 metric lists:

Name Metrics Notes FULL_METRICS (default) bleu, rouge, bertscore, radeval_bertscore, f1chexbert, f1radbert_ct, radgraph, ratescore, radgraph_radcliq, radcliq, srrbert, temporal, green, mammo_green, crimson, radfact_ct 16 metrics. green and mammo_green run a local LLM of about 7B weights. crimson and radfact_ct need an API key LIGHT_METRICS bleu, rouge, bertscore, radgraph, f1chexbert No LLM and no API key

A metric name that RadEval does not know raises ValueError. A metric with a missing model file, API key or package raises the error from RadEval. The evaluator does not skip that metric.

This block scores 2 given texts in the RadEval venv, with no generator:

from radharmony.evaluator.metrics import LIGHT_METRICS, compute_report_metrics

refs = ["Heart size is normal. No pleural effusion.", "Small left pleural effusion."]
hyps = ["The heart is normal. No effusion.", "Left pleural effusion."]
scores = compute_report_metrics(refs, hyps, LIGHT_METRICS)
print(sorted(scores))
# ['bertscore', 'bleu', 'f1chexbert_5_macro_f1', ..., 'radgraph_simple', 'rouge1', 'rouge2', 'rougeL']

docs.title: Score in one call
docs.text:
evaluate() generates and scores in one call. It needs a venv with the generator and RadEval. The chexagent_gen and maira2_gen venvs do not have RadEval, so use the 2 steps of Quick use for them. This block uses ReportGenerationEvaluator, report_generator and ds of Quick use, with a generator that runs in the RadEval venv:

from radharmony.evaluator.metrics import LIGHT_METRICS

ev = ReportGenerationEvaluator(
    report_generator,
    dataset=ds,
    metrics=LIGHT_METRICS,
    n_bootstrap=10,
    output_dir="outputs/report_generation",
)
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv, results_summary.csv and generations.csv

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description report_generator callable required A function (imgs, indications=None) -> list[str]. It returns one report for each image of the batch (Encoder contract) metrics tuple[str, ...] or list[str] ('bleu', 'rouge', 'bertscore', 'radeval_bertscore', 'f1chexbert', 'f1radbert_ct', 'radgraph', 'ratescore', 'radgraph_radcliq', 'radcliq', 'srrbert', 'temporal', 'green', 'mammo_green', 'crimson', 'radfact_ct') The RadEval metric names. The default is FULL_METRICS, all 16 metrics. See Metrics ref_section str "findings" The report section to compare with: "findings", "impression", "both" or "full" use_indication bool False Give the indication section of each report to the generator. See Indication indication_section str "indication" The report section that gives the indication normalize_hyp bool True Clean each generated report with normalize_hypothesis before scoring (D-50). False scores the raw text

docs.title: Shared arguments (inherited from BaseEvaluator)
docs.text:
These arguments have the same names as in the other evaluators. ReportGenerationEvaluator sets them in its own signature. It gives only dataset and output_dir to BaseEvaluator.

Argument Type Default Description dataset dataset required Test only: the one dataset, made with output_report=True (Split modes) device str "cuda" Not used. The generator sets its own device. A value other than "cuda" warns (D-52) batch_size int 8 The batch size of the generator num_workers int 4 The number of DataLoader workers max_samples int None The largest number of pairs to score. Use it for a short test run n_bootstrap int 0 The number of bootstrap samples of the patients (of the pairs when the table has no patient_id) bootstrap_seed int 0 The seed of the bootstrap samples output_dir str None The folder for save_results()

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
evaluate() returns the result table, one row for the point estimate and one row for each bootstrap sample. A real run with LIGHT_METRICS gave these columns:

Column Meaning label Always "report" fold Always -1 seed Always -1 bootstrap -1 for the point estimate. 0 to n_bootstrap - 1 for a bootstrap sample bleu, bertscore One score each rouge1, rouge2, rougeL The scores of rouge radgraph_simple, radgraph_partial, radgraph_complete The scores of radgraph f1chexbert_5_micro_f1, f1chexbert_all_macro_f1, ... The 6 scores of f1chexbert (5 or all labels, and micro, macro or weighted F1)

A metric that gives more than one score gets one column for each score. The column name joins the names with _. A score that is not a number is not in the table.

save_results(df) writes 3 files to output_dir:

  • results.csv: the result table.
  • results_summary.csv: one row. For each metric, it gives <metric>_mean (the point estimate), <metric>_n, and <metric>_std, <metric>_ci_lo and <metric>_ci_hi over the bootstrap samples (D-19). With n_bootstrap below 2, the std and the CI are NaN.
  • generations.csv: the columns sample_id, reference and hypothesis. The hypothesis is the text that the metrics scored, so it is the cleaned text when normalize_hyp=True.

generate_only(path) writes a parquet file with sample_id, reference and hypothesis, and patient_id when the table has it. The hypothesis is the raw text. The scoring script of step 2 cleans it, unless you pass --no-normalize-hyp.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• output_report=True drops the rows with no report (D-33). For MIMIC-CXR, also pass report_csv_path. MIMIC-CXR-JPG has no reports.
  • Each bootstrap sample runs every metric again. With FULL_METRICS this is slow, so keep n_bootstrap small, for example 10 to 50.
  • For a full example, see notebooks/evaluator/report_generation_example.py.
  • For a hands-on notebook with MedGemma and VQA, see datathon26/6_radharmony_hands_on_vqa_report_generation.ipynb.

docs.title: SVMProbeEvaluator
docs.text:
Registry key svm_probe Task Classification, frozen features Dataset outputs it needs cls (output_cls=True) Split modes k-fold (dataset=), fixed split (train_dataset=, test_dataset=) Encoder it needs a pooled feature vector, Tensor[B, D] Output The result table, one row for each label and run. See Output

The SVM probe fits one linear SVM (sklearn.svm.LinearSVC) for each label on the frozen features of an encoder. The score of an image is the SVM decision value, not a probability. Use it as a second linear probe next to the linear probe. It has the squared hinge loss of LinearSVC in place of the logistic loss.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block runs the SVM probe on Montgomery (138 images) with RAD-DINO, with 5 folds.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import SVMProbeEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)

ev = SVMProbeEvaluator(encoder, dataset=ds, n_folds=5, output_dir="outputs/svm_probe")
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
print(df.columns.tolist())
# ['n_train', 'fold', 'seed', 'bootstrap', 'label', 'auroc', 'auprc', 'f1', ...]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Features: the evaluator runs the encoder one time over each dataset. It L2-normalizes the features by default (D-17). The L2 penalty of LinearSVC needs features of the same scale. The embedding cache keeps the raw features.
  • Probe: one LinearSVC for each label. The default arguments are class_weight="balanced", C=1.0, max_iter=10000 and dual=False. svm_kwargs changes some of them, and the others stay. dual=False is the fast form when there are more train rows than feature values.
  • Score: the decision value of the SVM. AUROC and AUPRC need only the order of the scores, so they need no probability.
  • Labels: each label fits only on the rows where it is 0 or 1. A NaN label is not a negative (D-18). A label with only one class gets NaN metrics.
  • Threshold: the probe holds out a validation part of the train patients and does not fit on it. It picks the threshold on the decision values there (Threshold, D-29).

docs.text: Argument Type Default Description n_folds int 5 The number of folds in k-fold mode. Fixed-split mode does not use it n_train_samples list[int] None The train sizes in images, one run for each (Split modes). None uses all train images svm_kwargs dict None Arguments for LinearSVC. Each key replaces the same default key store_final_model bool False After evaluate(), also fit one SVM for each label on all train images. They go to final_models_, not to a file val_fraction float 0.1 The part of the train patients for the threshold. The probe does not fit on it. 0.0 gives NaN threshold metrics, except with "fixed:<float>"

It returns Tensor[B, D] (Encoder contract) dataset dataset None K-fold mode: the one dataset (Split modes) train_dataset dataset None Fixed-split mode: the train dataset test_dataset dataset None Fixed-split mode: the test dataset labels list[str] None The labels to evaluate. None gives all labels. The match ignores case. An unknown name raises KeyError device str "cuda" "cuda", "cuda:N" or "cpu" batch_size int 64 The batch size of the feature extraction num_workers int 4 The number of DataLoader workers autocast_dtype torch.dtype torch.bfloat16 The autocast type of the encoder. None gives no autocast embedding_cache str None The path of the feature file (Embedding cache) l2_normalize bool False L2-normalize the features. This class sets True when you do not pass it (D-17) output_dir str None The folder for save_results() n_seeds int 1 Fixed-split mode: the number of train samples, each with its own seed (Split modes) base_seed int 0 The first seed of the train samples and of the validation part n_bootstrap int 0 Fixed-split mode: the number of bootstrap samples of the test set (Split modes) bootstrap_seed int 0 The first seed of the bootstrap samples threshold_strategy str "youden" "youden", "f1" or "fixed:<float>" (Threshold)

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
evaluate() returns the result table with these columns: n_train, fold, seed, bootstrap, label, auroc, auprc, f1, accuracy, balanced_accuracy, tpr, tnr, ppv, npv, mcc and threshold. save_results(df) writes results.csv and results_summary.csv to output_dir. The threshold column is a decision value, so it can be below 0 or above 1.

With store_final_model=True, final_models_ maps each label to its fitted LinearSVC, or to None for a label with only one class.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• threshold_strategy="fixed:0" is the decision boundary of the SVM: it gives the class of LinearSVC.predict. Another fixed value is a value on the decision scale, not a probability.
  • l2_normalize=False gives the raw features to the SVM. Use it only for features that you scaled yourself.

docs.title: UPerNetSegEvaluator
docs.text:
Registry key upernet_seg Task Segmentation, frozen patch features, UPerNet head Dataset outputs it needs mask (output_mask=True) Split modes k-fold (dataset=), fixed split (train_dataset=, test_dataset=) Encoder it needs a map of patch features, Tensor[B, D, H', W'], from make_<name>(output_keys={"img", "mask"}) Output The result table, one row for each class and run. See Output

The UPerNet probe is the segmentation linear probe with the largest head of the 3 segmentation probes. A small feature pyramid makes 4 feature maps of different sizes from the one patch map. Then the UperNetHead of Hugging Face transformers joins them. Use it when the heads of the linear and the conv probes are too small. The training, the scoring and the output are the same as in the linear probe.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block segments the lungs on Montgomery (138 images) with RAD-DINO, 2 folds and 3 epochs.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import UPerNetSegEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_raddino

transform, encoder = make_raddino(device="cuda", output_keys={"img", "mask"})
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_mask=True,
    mask_output_dir="/data/montgomery_lung_masks/",  # any folder you can write to
    cache_dir=None,
)

ev = UPerNetSegEvaluator(
    encoder,
    dataset=ds,
    num_classes=2,  # background and lung
    upernet_hidden_size=256,
    upernet_pool_scales=(1, 2, 3, 6),
    n_folds=2,
    epochs=3,
    num_workers=8,  # 8 workers read the large PNG files faster
    output_dir="outputs/upernet_seg",
)
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
print(df.columns.tolist())
# ['n_train', 'fold', 'seed', 'bootstrap', 'label', 'dice', 'iou', 'pixel_acc', 'tpr', 'tnr', 'ppv', 'npv']

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Feature pyramid: it takes the patch map (stride 16 for a ViT with 16-pixel patches). It makes 4 maps: stride 4 (2 transposed convolutions), stride 8 (1 transposed convolution), stride 16 (the patch map) and stride 32 (a max pool). Each map keeps the D channels of the encoder.
  • GroupNorm: the stride-4 branch has a GroupNorm(32, D) and a GELU between its 2 transposed convolutions. So D must be a multiple of 32.
  • Head: UperNetHead (a pyramid pooling module and a top-down feature pyramid) joins the 4 maps into class scores. upernet_hidden_size sets its channels, and upernet_pool_scales sets the grid sizes of its pooling module. A bilinear resize takes the scores to the mask size.
  • Weights: the evaluator trains the feature pyramid and UperNetHead. The encoder stays frozen. For D=768, a hidden size of 256 and 2 classes, the head has about 16.7 million weights.
  • Training: for the training loop, early stopping, the splits, the masks and the metrics, see How it works and Metrics on the linear probe page.

docs.title: Save and reuse
docs.text: fit(), save_head(), load_head(), predict(), inner_val_indices() and store_final_model work as in the linear probe. See Save and reuse. save_head() keeps upernet_hidden_size and upernet_pool_scales in the file. load_head() warns when the evaluator has other values.

docs.text: Argument Type Default Description upernet_hidden_size int 256 The number of channels of UperNetHead upernet_pool_scales tuple[int, ...] (1, 2, 3, 6) The grid sizes of the pyramid pooling module

docs.text: evaluate() returns the result table, with the same rows and columns as the linear probe (Output). The Quick use run gave these columns: n_train, fold, seed, bootstrap, label, dice, iou, pixel_acc, tpr, tnr, ppv and npv. save_results(df) writes results.csv and results_summary.csv to output_dir.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The pyramid pooling module has BatchNorm and a branch that pools to 1×1. In training, a batch of 1 image raises ValueError. So use batch_size 2 or more. The evaluator drops a last train batch that is smaller than batch_size. But when all train images fit in one batch, it keeps that batch. So a run with 1 train image fails.
  • The class UperNetHead comes from transformers.models.upernet.modeling_upernet. This module path is not a public import of transformers, so a new transformers version can move it.

docs.title: VQAEvaluator
docs.text:
Registry key vqa Task Visual question answering, scores generated answers Dataset outputs it needs question and answer (every VQA dataset gives them) Split modes test only (dataset=) Encoder it needs a VQA answerer, (imgs, questions) -> list[str], one answer for each image (Encoder contract) Output The result table, one row for each answer group, for the point estimate and for each bootstrap sample. See Output

The VQA evaluator runs a vision-language model over a VQA dataset. The model gets each image and its question, and writes an answer. The evaluator scores each model answer against the reference, with the metrics of the MedGemma technical report (section 3.4, Table 9). The reference is the real answer of the dataset, sample["answer"]. A pair is one question with its reference and its model answer.

Use the evaluator to compare VQA models on the same questions. It does not look inside the model, so any answerer works.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
The recipe make_medgemma_vqa needs its own venv (medgemma_gen extra). google/medgemma-4b-it is a gated Hugging Face model. Accept its license on the model page and run huggingface-cli login first. This block runs MedGemma on the 451 test questions of VQA-RAD, and scores the model answers:

from radharmony.dataset import VQARadTestDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import VQAEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_medgemma_vqa

transform, vqa_answerer = make_medgemma_vqa(device="cuda")
ds = VQARadTestDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/VQA-RAD/VQA_RAD Image Folder/",
    transform=transform,
    cache_dir=None,
)

ev = VQAEvaluator(vqa_answerer, dataset=ds, n_bootstrap=100, output_dir="outputs/vqa")
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv, results_summary.csv and generations.csv
print(df[df["bootstrap"] == -1][["label", "token_f1", "accuracy", "token_recall"]])

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Generation: the evaluator runs vqa_answerer on each batch of img and question. It needs one answer for each image. With the MedGemma and CheXagent recipes, img is the path of a PNG file, so the batch is a list of path strings. An answerer can also take only imgs. Then the evaluator does not give it the questions.
  • Reference: the evaluator uses sample["answer"] as the reference.
  • Dropped pairs: the evaluator drops a pair when the reference or the model answer is empty.
  • Cleaning: the evaluator removes the white space at the start and the end of each model answer.
  • Groups: a pair is closed when its reference is yes or no (is_closed). The other pairs are open. See Metrics.
  • Bootstrap: each bootstrap sample draws pairs with replacement. It does not group them by patient. A bootstrap sample with no closed pair has no closed row. A bootstrap sample with no open pair has no open row.
  • Splits: the evaluator has no folds and no training (Split modes).

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The result table has one row for each group of pairs:

label Metrics Answers overall token_f1 All pairs closed accuracy, token_f1 The pairs with the reference yes or no open token_f1, token_recall The other pairs
  • token_f1: the token F1 that the MedGemma report uses for VQA-RAD and SLAKE. The metric first changes each text to lower case. It changes each character that is not a letter, a digit or a space to a space. It removes the words a, an and the. Then it counts the tokens that the model answer and the reference share. The precision is this count divided by the number of model answer tokens. The recall is this count divided by the number of reference tokens. token_f1 is the F1 of this precision and this recall.
  • accuracy: the part of the closed pairs with a correct model answer. A model answer is correct when its first yes or no token is the reference. So the model answer "Yes, the heart is large." is correct for the reference yes.
  • token_recall: the part of the reference tokens that the model answer has. The MedGemma report gives it for the open SLAKE questions.

radharmony.evaluator.metrics exports the metric functions. They need no data:

from radharmony.evaluator.metrics import extract_yes_no, is_yes_no_answer, token_recall, tokenized_f1

print(tokenized_f1("The left lung.", "left lung"))  # 1.0
print(tokenized_f1("left pleural effusion", "pleural effusion"))  # 0.8
print(round(token_recall("pleural effusion", "left pleural effusion"), 3))  # 0.667
print(extract_yes_no("No, there is no effusion."))  # no
print(is_yes_no_answer(" Yes "), is_yes_no_answer("yes, small"))  # True False

docs.title: Compare with the MedGemma report
docs.text:
Table 9 of the MedGemma report gives the scores of MedGemma. To compare with Table 9, use make_medgemma_vqa. It follows the report in 3 ways:

  • It uses greedy decoding. At each step, it picks the most likely token.
  • Its prompt is the VQA-RAD prompt of Table A7 of the report. The question comes after the prompt.
  • It gives no system message by default (system_message=None). The caption of Table A7 says that MedGemma got no system message.

The VQA-RAD scores of Table 9 use a test split with no overlap with the train data (Yang et al. 2024, Xu et al. 2023). RadHarmony does not have this split. VQARadTestDataset gives the 451 test questions of the VQA-RAD paper.

202 of the 203 images of these questions also have train questions. So your scores can differ from Table 9, because the test questions are not the same.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description vqa_answerer callable required A function (imgs, questions) -> list[str]. It returns one answer for each image of the batch (Encoder contract) is_closed callable is_yes_no_answer A function (reference) -> bool. True puts the answer in the closed group. The default gives True when the reference is yes or no, in any case

docs.title: Shared arguments (inherited from GenerativeEvaluator)
docs.text:
These arguments have the same names as in the other evaluators. VQAEvaluator sets them in its own signature and gives them to GenerativeEvaluator.

Argument Type Default Description dataset dataset required Test only: the one VQA dataset (Split modes) device str "cuda" Not used. The answerer sets its own device batch_size int 8 The batch size of the answerer num_workers int 4 The number of DataLoader workers max_samples int None The largest number of pairs to score. Use it for a short test run n_bootstrap int 0 The number of bootstrap samples of the pairs bootstrap_seed int 0 The seed of the bootstrap samples output_dir str None The folder for save_results()

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
evaluate() returns the result table, one row for each group, for the point estimate and for each bootstrap sample. With n_bootstrap=0, evaluate() gives 3 rows: overall, closed and open.

Column Meaning fold Always -1 seed Always -1 bootstrap -1 for the point estimate. 0 to n_bootstrap - 1 for a bootstrap sample label overall, closed or open token_f1 The mean token F1 of the group accuracy The accuracy of the closed pairs. NaN in the overall and open rows token_recall The mean token recall. NaN in the overall and closed rows

A dataset with no closed pair gives no closed row and no accuracy column. A dataset with no open pair gives no open row and no token_recall column.

save_results(df) writes 3 files to output_dir:

  • results.csv: the result table.
  • results_summary.csv: one row for each group. For each metric, it gives <metric>_mean (the point estimate), <metric>_n, and <metric>_std, <metric>_ci_lo and <metric>_ci_hi over the bootstrap samples (D-19). With n_bootstrap below 2, the std and the CI are NaN. They are also NaN for a group that is in fewer than 2 bootstrap samples.
  • generations.csv: the columns question, reference, hypothesis and closed. hypothesis is the model answer.

generate_only(path) runs the answerer with no scoring. It writes a parquet file with the same 4 columns. You can score the file later with the metric functions of Metrics.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• A transform must keep the question and answer keys. The default transform of a VQA dataset and the VQA recipes keep them. A missing key raises KeyError.
  • save_results() warns that some metrics are NaN in some rows. These are the metrics that do not apply to a group, for example accuracy in the overall row. The summary is correct.
  • The CheXagent recipe make_chexagent_vqa needs the chexagent_gen venv. It puts a short instruction before each question.
  • For a hands-on notebook with MedGemma, see datathon26/6_radharmony_hands_on_vqa_report_generation.ipynb.

docs.title: ZeroShotEvaluator
docs.text:
Registry key zero_shot Task Classification with text prompts, no training Dataset outputs it needs cls (output_cls=True) Split modes test only (test_dataset= or dataset=) Encoder it needs an image encoder and a text encoder with one shared feature space Output The result table, one row for each label, for the point estimate and each bootstrap sample. See Output

The zero-shot evaluator scores each test image against text prompts for each label, with the cosine of the image feature and the prompt feature. It trains nothing and uses only test data. Use it for a vision-language model, for example a CLIP or SigLIP model.

docs.title: Quick use
docs.text:
This block scores Montgomery (138 images) with BiomedCLIP, 1 positive and 1 negative prompt, and 100 bootstrap samples.

from radharmony.dataset import MontgomeryCXRDataset
from radharmony.evaluator import ZeroShotEvaluator
from radharmony.evaluator.backbones import make_biomed_clip

transform, encoder, text_encoder, tokenizer = make_biomed_clip(device="cuda")
ds = MontgomeryCXRDataset(
    base_image_dir="/data/MontgomerySet/CXR_png/",
    transform=transform,
    output_cls=True,
    cache_dir=None,
)

ev = ZeroShotEvaluator(
    encoder,
    text_encoder,
    prompts={"tuberculosis": ["a chest X-ray with tuberculosis"]},
    negative_prompts={"tuberculosis": ["a normal chest X-ray"]},
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    test_dataset=ds,
    n_bootstrap=100,
    threshold_strategy="fixed:0",  # without it, F1 and the other threshold metrics are NaN
    output_dir="outputs/zero_shot",
)
df = ev.evaluate()
ev.save_results(df)  # writes results.csv and results_summary.csv
print(df.columns.tolist())
# ['n_train', 'fold', 'seed', 'bootstrap', 'label', 'auroc', 'auprc', 'f1', ...]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Image features: the evaluator runs the image encoder one time over the test data. It always L2-normalizes the features, as CLIP does (D-17).
  • Prompt features: the text encoder encodes each prompt. The evaluator L2-normalizes each prompt feature, takes the mean over the prompts of a label, and normalizes the mean again.
  • Score: cos(image, positive prompts). When the label has negative prompts, the score is cos(image, positive prompts) - cos(image, negative prompts).
  • Labels: each evaluated label needs positive prompts, or the run raises KeyError. The prompt lookup ignores case. To evaluate only some labels, pass labels=. A label with no negative prompts uses only its positive prompts.
  • Threshold: there is no train data, so there is no validation part. The threshold metrics are NaN, except with threshold_strategy="fixed:<float>" (D-29). The evaluator warns about this. When every label has negative prompts, "fixed:0" means "closer to the positive prompts".
  • Bootstrap: n_bootstrap works with dataset= too (D-32).

docs.text: Argument Type Default Description text_encoder callable required It gets the output of tokenizer, or the list[str] of prompts with no tokenizer. It returns Tensor[T, D] prompts dict[str, list[str]] required The positive prompts of each label negative_prompts dict[str, list[str]] None The negative prompts of each label. A label can have none tokenizer callable None It turns the prompts into the input of text_encoder. None gives the strings to text_encoder

None gives no autocast embedding_cache str None The path of the feature file. The file is <path>.test.pkl (Embedding cache) l2_normalize bool False No effect: the score is always a cosine. A value other than 1 warns base_seed int 0 Not used n_bootstrap int 0 The number of bootstrap samples of the test set bootstrap_seed int 0 The seed of the bootstrap samples threshold_strategy str "youden" Use "fixed:<float>" for the threshold metrics (How it works)

docs.title: Output
docs.text: evaluate() returns the result table with these columns: n_train, fold, seed, bootstrap, label, auroc, auprc, f1, accuracy, balanced_accuracy, tpr, tnr, ppv, npv, mcc and threshold. n_train, fold and seed are always -1. Each label has 1 + n_bootstrap rows: the point estimate (bootstrap = -1) and one row for each bootstrap sample. save_results(df) writes results.csv and results_summary.csv to output_dir.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• A Hugging Face processor (an object with an image_processor) gets the prompts as text=. A SigLIP processor pads to its model_max_length, because SigLIP trains with a fixed text length. Another processor pads to the longest prompt.
  • A longer prompt than the model_max_length of a SigLIP processor is cut to that length, as the Hugging Face zero-shot pipeline does. The class warns with the number of these prompts (D-52).
  • Any callables work in place of a backbone recipe, if they follow the encoder contract. See Add a backbone.
